author: mike-shevchenko
body:
One fix, found with ffemu while testing the 7-segment version display; the bug dates from 839f017c (2019).

Mounting an image puts the 7-segment display in its track state, in which the first button press only switches it back to the image number and is swallowed; it leaves that state after some seconds of inactivity, or when `run_floppy()` returns, which resets it to normal. Pulling the USB drive cancels `run_floppy()` instead, and then `floppy_main()`, so a drive pulled within those seconds of the last activity left the display in the track state, and the first press with no drive was lost: the right button showed no version, both buttons no menu.

The reset now comes after the cancellable call of `run_floppy()` in `floppy_main()`, so that it happens however the call ended, at the same moment as before on a normal return.

Reproduced and checked in ffemu with a 3-digit display, a 720K image mounted and the drive pulled within the 4 s: the right button then showed no version, and does with the fix.

author: el-bri-ga
body:
Closes #1367.

## What changes

- **Boot id** (`felix-storage/src/run_state/boot.rs`). Linux reads `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`. macOS calls `sysctlbyname("kern.bootsessionuuid")`, so no process is spawned. Other platforms: `None`.
- **Decision** (`run_state::begin`, which now takes `boot: Option<BootId>`). On an unclean stop under `periodic`/`none`:
  - same boot: keep the id;
  - different boot: rotate;
  - `None` on either side: rotate.

  `OnCommit`, a clean stop, and the upgrade path are unchanged.
- **Poisoned log.** A failed fsync, or a stop whose flush failed, still rotates on the next crash.
  - `run_state::watch_poison(root)` is registered at startup. The first log poisoned in the process calls `forget_watched()`, which rewrites a v2 record as v1 relaxed with no boot.
  - Shutdown does the same when `!flushed || poisoned`.
  - That rewrite is not synced, on purpose. Only a process crash has to see it, and the page cache keeps it for that. A machine crash rotates anyway, and a sync could fail on the very device that just failed one.
- **Run-state compatibility.**
  - A new **version 2** (44 bytes) adds the 16-byte boot. It is written only for a relaxed run under way with a known boot.
  - Every other record, **a clean stop included**, stays version 1 (28 bytes).
  - **Downgrade after a clean stop** keeps the id: the old decoder sees the v1 STOPPED record.
  - **Downgrade after a crash**: an older build fails to decode v2 and reads it as a relaxed crash, which is what it would have done with its own record of that run. It rotates as before, and nothing extra.
  - **Upgrade**: a v1 relaxed RUNNING record names no boot, so it reads as unknown and rotates.
  - Tested by `only_a_relaxed_run_under_way_uses_the_newer_layout`. The fuzz harness covers both layouts.
- **Cluster harness.**
  - Brokers get `FELIX_STORAGE_BOOT_ID_FILE=<data dir>/boot-id`. Debug builds only: when the file exists, the broker takes its boot id from it.
  - `Cluster::reboot_node` writes a new id, so kill + reboot is a machine crash.
  - `Cluster::power_off` gives every powered-off broker a new boot.
- **Cluster tests** (`failures/wiped.rs`).
  - `Stop::Crash` is split into `Kill` (the id is kept) and `MachineCrash` (kill + `reboot_node`, the id rotates).
  - `a_crashed_follower_is_not_promoted` and both crashed-leader tests now use a machine crash.
  - New: `a_killed_follower_is_promoted_past_the_ttl` and `a_killed_leader_keeps_its_identity_and_serves_again`.
- **TLA+.**
  - `Crash` picks `machine \in BOOLEAN` under `ProcessCrashes`. A process crash keeps the whole log.
  - `CrashRotates(machine)` rotates only on a machine crash under `KeepIdOnSameBoot`, unless `BootCheckBlind`. A leader gives its copy up only when it rotated.
  - New configs:

    | config | expected | weight |
    |---|---|---|
    | `FelixShardProcessCrashKeepsId` (`AckedOnLiveMajority` as a property, as in WipeFull) | pass | 15 |
    | `FelixShardMachineCrashKeepsId` | violates `AckedSurvive` | — |
    | `FelixShardLeaderProcessCrash` | pass | 8 |

  - All have MaxWrites = 1. Weights are guesses until CI measures them.
- **Docs.** `durable-storage.md` "Storage identity" (the boot rule, the write-path audit, downgrade), `storage-format.md` (the v2 layout), `replication-design.md` (rotation passages, failure-model rows, the spec paragraph), `cluster-harness.md`, the docs-site durable-storage page and Leader failover status row, `docs/formal/README.md`, and `changelog.d/1367-…changed.md`.

## Write-path audit (why "keep" is sound)

The question: can an acknowledged byte still be in process memory, rather than handed to the kernel, when it is acknowledged?

- **Segment appends.** `LogInner::append_now` encodes into the staging buffer, then calls `StagedAppend::write`, a `write_all` on the file. It then `finish`es, which errors if the write failed, and only then builds the reply. The ack comes after that reply on the append thread, so every acked byte has been `write()`n.
  - Followers, caches (`LogCache`), counters, consumer groups and dead letters all append through the same `DiskLog::write_batch`.
- **O_DIRECT / mmap.** Neither is used anywhere in felix-storage. I grepped for `O_DIRECT`, `custom_flags`, `mmap` and `memmap`; the only `custom_flags` is the test power-loss model's `O_NONBLOCK`.
- **io_uring** (`io/uring_fsync.rs`). It submits only `opcode::Fsync` and `PollAdd`, never a write. Under `OnCommit` the ack waits for the completion. Under periodic the flush is not tied to the ack.
- **User-space buffers.** The only `BufWriter`s are the sparse index (`segment/index.rs`) and `keys.idx` (`index_snapshot.rs`). Both are derived and rebuilt from the segment, and the index entries are written after the reply. `durable.mark` is a hint written after a sync and only bounds what recovery may call damage.
- **One honest exception: the replicated commit offset.**
  - Under a relaxed mode `DiskLog::advance_commit_offset` writes it at most once per second, so a process crash can read it back behind. Its own doc comment already says so.
  - It is not a record and not what the id vouches for. It only guards a follower against truncating below it. A follower truncates only at the request of a leader at a generation it accepted (ballot and generation are synced in every mode), and such a leader holds every committed record.
  - Before #1284 a periodic process crash had the same stale guard. With rotation on every crash it was moot; now it matters again, as defence in depth.
  - The model abstracts commit-offset persistence for machine crashes too, so I did not change that.
  - **Please check this reasoning.** If you disagree, the fix is a cheap unsynced `pwrite` of the replica state on every advance under periodic, not a rotation.

## Review notes

- **#1343 and #1356 are both still OPEN** (checked just before opening). I branched from main and did not merge either.
  - #1356's `majority_ack` Periodic twin and `under_periodic_a_promotion_waits_for_an_operator_after_its_holders_crash` exist only on #1356, so this PR cannot restore them. Whichever lands second should make two changes there:
    - the process-kill variant asserts the shard resumes without `abandon`;
    - a `reboot_node` variant (kill, then `cluster.reboot_node(..)` before the restart) keeps the wait assertion.
  - Expect conflicts in `node/storage.rs`, `run_state.rs` and the TLA spec.
- **Writeback errors the crashed process never saw.**
  - Linux reports an unseen writeback error to the next opener's `fsync`. In this case the restarted broker keeps the id, its first flush of that file fails, it poisons the log, and the next start rotates.
  - The exposure is the window between the restart and that first flush. That is the same window a live broker under periodic already has between a background writeback failure and its next fsync.
  - I considered syncing the whole data dir before keeping the id (as PostgreSQL does after a crash). I left it out: per-file `F_FULLFSYNC` on macOS makes startup slow on a large directory. Say if you want it.
- **Poison-to-rewrite window.** A process crash in the microseconds between a failed fsync and `forget_watched()` keeps the id.
- **The boot lives in the record itself**, not in a sidecar file. A build that writes no boot (a downgrade to the #1284 release) overwrites the whole record with v1, so a crash under it always rotates on the next start. No stale boot id can outlive the run it described.
- **No unit test for the shutdown `!flushed` path.** It is three lines in `shutdown.rs` calling `forget_boot`, which is tested.
- **TLC has not run** (no Java locally). By eye:
  - the new operators are defined before use;
  - `rotates`, `machine` and `givesUp` shadow nothing;
  - no duplicate definitions (checked by script);
  - all 53 CONSTANTS are set in each new cfg (checked by script against the CONSTANTS block).

  If a passing config finds a counterexample, treat it as a real finding, not a model tweak.
- No inter

body:
Phase 1 of #3469 (plan: the "PR 1: projection package" section of the revised plan comment on #3469).

## What

- New Building-blocks package `@robota-sdk/agent-telemetry-otel`, depending only on `@robota-sdk/agent-interface-analytics`. `projectLivePromptTrace(batch, { mode, agentName })` maps one `ILivePromptTraceBatch` onto content-free span shapes (name, kind, trace/span/parent IDs, start/end, status, attributes) without an OpenTelemetry SDK dependency.
  - `agent`: the CLI exporter's current spans (`live-trace-otlp.ts`), attribute for attribute and in the same order, including the opaque-ID sanitizers and `agent.timing.*` totals.
  - `gen_ai`: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions — `invoke_agent {agent}` (internal), `chat {model}` (client), `execute_tool {tool}` (internal); `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens/output_tokens`, `gen_ai.provider.name`, `gen_ai.agent.name`, `gen_ai.conversation.id`, `gen_ai.tool.name`, `gen_ai.tool.call.id`, and `error.type: _OTHER` on failed spans. Robota-only facts (turn, outcome, timing, omitted counts, usage provenance, total tokens, disposition, provider ID, request ID) keep `agent.*` names. `schemaUrl` is `GEN_AI_SCHEMA_URL`.
  - `gen_ai/dup`: GenAI span names with both attribute sets, for migration.
- Children always take the root's trace ID and the root as parent, as the CLI does.
- `IToolBodyTraceEntry` gains an optional live-only `toolName`; the analytics SPEC sentence is rewritten to cover it. Producers (session permission wrapper and the framework's `projectTool` boundary) fill it in #3465.
- Listings: ARCHITECTURE.md, README.md + its template, content/guide/architecture.md, homepage catalog, architecture diagram; fixed changeset group; changeset.

## Provisional choice (revised from the plan)

**UNRESOLVED — PROVISIONAL CHOICE:** Robota's `gemini` and `google` provider IDs map to `gen_ai.provider.name = gcp.gen_ai`, not `gcp.gemini` as the plan said. The Gemini client can target either the Gemini API or Vertex AI and the trace does not say which; `gcp.gen_ai` is the conventions' name for any Google GenAI endpoint. Provider IDs without a certain GenAI name (`qwen`, `gemma`, gateways) get no `gen_ai.provider.name`; `agent.provider.id` still names them. Reversible in one map; revisit if the trace gains the endpoint kind.

## Not in this PR

The CLI is unchanged; switching its exporter to this package (and deleting its copy of the timing helper) is phase 2 / #3465. No CLI runtime change, so no CLI session run.

## Verification

- New package tests (15): exact `agent`-mode spans and attribute order vs the CLI mapping, gen_ai and dup attribute sets, fallbacks for unknown names, provider-name map, token/ID sanitizing, foreign child trace IDs, timing validation, interrupted vs failed status. They cannot pass before this change (package and `toolName` field did not exist).

- `pr-review-reviewer`: 3 SHOULD findings (child trace ID, analytics SPEC sentence, GenAI `error.type`) fixed in 8b6d1b179. Re-review of the fixes: 0 actionable findings; the reviewer confirmed the four new assertions fail against 00a36db51.

body:
## Stability bug
`createToast(region).destroy()` previously behaved like `dismiss()`: a retired controller could call `show()` after host unmount, recreating UI and scheduling a timer. That contradicts the cleanup semantics of the other experimental controllers.

## Fix
- Make `destroy()` an idempotent, permanent teardown; subsequent `show()` throws before DOM mutation.
- Cancel the active toast and timer; stale dismissal handles and calls to `dismiss()` or `destroy()` remain harmless, even after another controller reuses the same region.
- Preserve region-level ARIA status semantics, and update the experimental API/type documentation.
- Add Node and real Chromium/Firefox regression tests, and record the QA limitations.

## Verified locally
- `npm run check`: 83/83 Node tests, 7,988 sampled opaque color comparisons, token/asset validation and package dry-run (53 files / 14 required exports) passed.
- New browser regression passed in Chromium and Firefox.

## Merge gate
Require **all three GitHub Actions jobs** on this PR to finish successfully, covering the expected 208 automated test executions. This does not imply actual screen-reader certification or production stability. No registry maturity or public API surface was promoted.

body:
## Problem
The first scheduled research-board run (cron `20 */3`, due 00:20 UTC) never started. GitHub delays or drops scheduled runs under load. The model-scan job is scheduled every 10 minutes but started only 3 times in ~7 hours. With a single run every 3 hours, one dropped run leaves a 6-hour gap.

## Fix
- **Workflow:** the cron is now `37 * * * *`, hourly at an off-peak minute. Scheduled runs pass `--scheduled`.
- **`run.ts`:** with `--scheduled`, the script publishes only when no `Research board ·` release has gone out in the last 2.5 hours. Otherwise it reports `skipped_recent_board`.
  - Effective cadence stays about every 3 hours.
  - A delayed or dropped run is retried the next hour.
  - Manual runs always publish.
- **Docs:** `docs/product/research-board.md` is updated.

author: jacksonjray
body: ## Summary Pogo 1.0.1 adds `--allow-short-passphrase`, which skips the 15-character minimum on every passphrase check. A passphrase is still required: empty or whitespace-only is rejected with exit 4. `--min-length` already accepted a floor as low as 1 and warned below 15. The new flag is that same choice without a number. If both are set, `--min-length` is the minimum. The flag prints one warning on stderr (`short passphrases are much easier to guess`) and leaves stdout alone, so `pogo run` output stays the program's output. It applies to `init`, `edit`, `run`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`, `convert`, and `rekey` (current passphrase and the new one), with the interactive prompt, `--key-stdin`, and `--key-env`. Files that already use a passphrase of 15 or more characters decrypt as before. A short passphrase without the flag still exits 4. A wrong passphrase still exits 2. `--key-file` and `--new-key-file` stay rejected with exit 1. The embedded skill tells agents not to pass this flag unless the user explicitly asks for it. ## Tests - `go vet ./...` - `go test ./...` - `go test -race ./...` Unit tests cover acceptance with the flag, exit 4 without it, and rejection of an empty or whitespace-only passphrase even with the flag. The e2e harness has a pty case for the interactive prompt and scripted cases for `--key-env`, `run` stdout, and `rekey`.

author: henrikogaard
body:
Closes OCT-664

`octant agent` now has a child view for the helper agents a harness lead started. Before, a helper showed up in the terminal only as tool calls.

## What changed
- `agentChildren.ts` reads a thread's helpers from the Agents Center list filtered to the thread, and one helper's result and bounded conversation, then replies the way the app does: a working or waiting helper is steered, a finished one gets a follow-up, and a question a helper asked is answered through the session question route. A helper that runs inside its provider, or has failed or stopped, takes no reply and the refusal says so. The host's own refusals (stale version, parent authority gone) are printed as given.
- Line mode: `/agents` lists (number, id, state, role, model, age, brief), `/agent N` shows the brief, what the helper said or reported, blockers and how to reply, and `/agent N <message>` replies. `N` can also be the start of the id.
- Terminal UI: the same commands open a Helper agents panel and a Helper agent panel.
- `octant harness agents <thread-id> [N] [--json]` reads the same list or one helper without starting a turn; with `--json` it prints the host's own rows.
- No route, contract or authority change; every call is authorized by the host against the window the terminal opened the thread in.

## Evidence
- Tests: list order and thread filter, refusal text, picking by number or id, row wording, live text versus reported summary, steering, follow-up, refusals, answering a helper's question; the `harness agents` parse, list, detail and JSON forms; the prompt loop's `/agents`, `/agent 1` and `/agent 1 <message>`.
- Live, on an isolated host with a loopback stand-in endpoint (no paid turn), in a Work thread: a helper listed as working, then done with its reply; `/agent 1 <message>` reached the running helper (its next model request carried the note); the terminal UI panels opened from a pseudo-terminal; `--json` printed the host's rows.
- `packages/cli` typecheck and suite (27 files, 325 tests), `style:check`, `bun run fmt`, `git diff --check`. No rendered web check: nothing in the renderer changed.

## Skipped and limits
- A follow-up on a finished helper after its parent's turn ended was refused live by the host ("The parent execution authority is no longer available."), the same rule the app's route applies; the CLI shows it unchanged. The follow-up success path is covered by the test, not live.

author: hirokazumiyaji
body:
Closes #183

### Summary of Changes
- **Default arguments**:
  - Added support for parameter default expressions in function definitions (`fn f(a, b = 2)`) and anonymous functions (`fn(x, y = 1) { ... }`).
  - Added syntactic and semantic enforcement that parameters without defaults cannot follow parameters with defaults.
  - Defaults are evaluated at call time only when arguments are omitted, in a clean function scope seeing only global variables.
  - Contract validation runs prior to evaluating any defaults to prevent observable side effects on invalid calls.
- **Anonymous functions**:
  - Implemented `Expr::Fn { params, body }` syntax producing first-class `Value::Func(UserFunc { params, body })`.
  - Added arbitrary expression invocation syntax `Expr::Invoke { callee, args, block }` (e.g. `(fn(x) { x + 1 })(2)`, `arr[0](5)`).
  - Preserved Flare static scoping rules (can access globals and parameters; caller locals are not captured).
  - Maintained iterative AST walk for depth limits to protect against parser recursion overflow on deeply nested anonymous functions.
- **Review**:
  - Verified and passed zero actionable comments in `codex review`.

Testing with 1Password exposed another issue: AXRaise can report success while the window remains behind another app. The synthetic title-bar press now waits until the target is exposed at the click point. - Configurable distances from the left and right edges.

author: pcbeingused333
body:
## :bulb: Motivation and Context

Anthropic's `message_delta` usage is cumulative. With server tools (web search, web fetch, code execution), its `input_tokens` and cache counts grow past the `message_start` values during the response. The Anthropic stream accumulator only recorded input and cache counts from `message_start` (it reads `output_tokens` from `message_delta`), so streamed generations under-reported `$ai_input_tokens` and `$ai_cache_creation_input_tokens`.

Example from a recorded web-search stream: `message_start` has input 2247 and cache creation 0, while `message_delta` has input 2254 and cache creation 17269. Before this change the event reported 2247 and 0.

`_AnthropicStreamAccumulator.consume`, shared by the sync and async wrappers, now applies the `message_delta` input and cache counts after the per-event merge. It keeps the larger of the two values, since the totals never shrink, and leaves a field the event omits at the `message_start` value.

## :green_heart: How did you test it?

- New `test_streaming_takes_cumulative_message_delta_usage` and its `_async` twin. They use real `anthropic.types` stream events with the values above and check the captured `$ai_input_tokens`, `$ai_output_tokens` and cache properties. Both fail on main.
- `posthog/test/ai`: 951 passed, 15 skipped; on main, only the two new tests fail.
- `ruff format --check` passes. `ruff check` reports the same findings as on main for the touched files. `mypy … | mypy-baseline filter` reports nothing new.

## :pencil: Checklist

- [x] I reviewed the submitted code.
- [x] I added tests to verify the changes.
- [ ] I updated the docs if needed. (n/a)
- [x] No breaking change or entry added to the changelog.

### If releasing new changes

- [x] Ran `sampo add` to generate a changeset file (added `.sampo/changesets/cumulative-anthropic-stream-usage.md` in the same format)

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

- The bug was found and the fix, tests and description were written by Claude Code; I reviewed the diff and the explanation before submitting.

- Written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5).
- The fix keeps the larger of `message_start` and `message_delta` for each count, rather than switching the merge to "cumulative" mode. That mode would replace the merged `raw_usage` and lose `message_start`'s fields, and `max` also tolerates a delta that omits or under-reports a field.

- Method for gross billed, Direct Consultant and architectural revenue, reconciled against the Office Earnings exports for 2026-06 and 2026-07 (firm, PIC and project level). See docs/BD-REVENUE-METHOD.md and docs/DISCOVERY-HANDOFF.md.

- No real firm amounts, project numbers, credentials or workbooks in this branch (scanned before pushing; tests use made-up numbers).
- .env.vp, vp-findings/ and discovery/data/ are git-ignored.

## Tests
173 pass (npm test), all on synthetic data.

Only two months tested; connection encryption not confirmed; PDF reference import not built.

`actualizar_estaciones.py` lee la lista desde [aramcoestaciones.cl](https://www.aramcoestaciones.cl/estaciones-de-servicio). body:
## What changes

- **Deferred startup data.** Park facilities, the every-park index, Explore trails/places, fresh iNaturalist sightings and page preloading wait for the map's first frame (`onReady`), the first pointer/key press, or 8 s. Pages that need them enable their queries at once (park, trail, place, region, tree, trip pages; Parks, Places, Foliage). The cached sightings still show immediately.
- **Fishing points on demand.** Fetched when the map reaches zoom 7 (`onFishingNear`; pins start at 8) or a `/fishing/` page opens, not on every visit.
- **Parks list in steps.** `useGrowingList` renders 40 rows, then 40 more when a sentinel nears the viewport; resets on search, filter or sort.

## Measured

Production build via `vite preview`, 390 px, 9 Mbps / 60 ms, CPU ×4, cache off:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| kB downloaded before the map's first frame (median of 5) | 1,578 | 1,405 |
| Map library download finished (median of 5) | 1,945 ms | 1,722 ms |
| …slowest of 5 | 3,906 ms | 1,825 ms |
| Total on a first visit | 1,628 kB | 1,580 kB |
| Parks: longest main-thread task | 386 ms | 152 ms |
| Parks: on screen after tap (incl. 250 ms label slide) | 1,488 ms | 1,258 ms |

Map first-frame time itself varies too much under software GL to compare reliably.

Also checked: scrolling Parks to the end reaches all 348 rows; searching "lake" restarts at 40 of 66. Type check, lint (no new warnings) and build pass.

## Trade-off

Before the map has drawn (or the page is touched), search covers report parks, regions and towns only; trails, places and other parks join once data arrives.

The main JS bundle was also checked and left alone: it is mostly react-dom (198 kB minified) and react-router; mapbox-gl (512 kB gzipped) is already split out.

## What Problem This Solves

Desktop rendering still used a controller, host adapter, and update-completion lifecycle after the Solid migration.

## User Impact

No intended visual or behavioral change. Desktop source selection, credential prompts, connection cancellation, dock open intent, fullscreen, and retained viewers keep their existing contracts. No configuration or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the Desktop controller with a synchronous domain factory consumed by a Solid projection. Solid owns controls and cleanup; a native host retains source and dock intent through context remounts. Delete the old controller and registration adapter, and run the existing Desktop tests through the production custom element.

Desktop now hands noVNC its rendered surface by ref. Browser stream sizing and resize/wheel ownership share the existing viewport ref instead of querying the DOM. On first load the page could flash white before the app rendered. The light background applied to any page without the `dark` class, so the page stayed light until the theme script ran, and for good if the script never ran.

body:
## Summary

```diff
 tn/monitoring/
   prometheus/web.sops.yml                    aMadmin: new bcrypt
   alertmanager/web.sops.yml                  aMadmin: new bcrypt
   grafana/provisioning/datasources.sops.yml  basicAuthPassword ×2: new
-  grafana/provisioning/datasources.yml       plaintext twin, committed in #439
 .github/scripts/validate.py
+  secrets: fail if x.sops.yml has a tracked plaintext x.yml
```

The deleted file held the live `aMadmin` passwords for Prometheus and Alertmanager in this public repo. Grafana never read it (it mounts the `.sops.yml`). Both passwords are rotated. History is not rewritten because the old values are dead.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the old passwords returned `200` from `/-/ready` on both. gitleaks passed (the values were too short and low-entropy for its default rules).
- `validate.py secrets` with the plaintext file present: `ERROR: plaintext twin of a SOPS file is tracked`. With it removed: `secrets ok`.
- After deploy: old passwords return `401`, and Grafana's Prometheus and Alertmanager datasources pass their health check.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** Grafana

Grafana reads its datasources only at startup. If it isn't recreated, it keeps the old passwords and shows Prometheus/Alertmanager panels as errors until it restarts.

body:
Closes #179

## Summary

Integrates React 18+ Suspense support into the SDK's React data-fetching hooks (Issue #179).

## Changes

Adds an opt-in `useSuspense?: boolean` option to:

- `useCreator`: `fetchCreator`, `fetchProfile`
- `useUser`: `fetchUser`, `fetchCurrentUser`
- `useWallet`: `listWallets`, `getBalance`

When `useSuspense: true`, hooks throw a promise while fetching (Suspense catches it and shows the fallback), then resolve with cached data once the promise settles. Non-Suspense behavior is fully unchanged: the option defaults to `false`.

## Files

- `src/react/useCreator.ts`: suspense branches + `creatorSuspenseCache` module cache
- `src/react/useUser.ts`: suspense branches + `userSuspenseCache`
- `src/react/useWallet.ts`: suspense branches + `listWalletsSuspenseCache`, `getBalanceSuspenseCache`
- `src/react/index.ts`: exports `UseCreatorOptions`, `UseUserOptions`, `UseWalletOptions`
- `tests/react/suspense.spec.tsx`: 18 tests: promise throwing, promise identity, data availability, error handling, Suspense boundary fallback→data, remount without unmounted-component errors
- `src/react/useCreator.suspense.stories.tsx`: Storybook story documenting the Suspense pattern

## Acceptance

- [x] Hooks with `useSuspense: true` throw promises during fetch
- [x] Suspense boundary catches and displays fallback

The live interviewer previously depended on the paid ElevenLabs connector and could not start with the configured free accounts. Use LiveAvatar FULL mode with a configured stock avatar, voice and rehearsal context, while preserving ElevenLabs voice-only practice.

The backend now retrieves completed transcripts directly from LiveAvatar using the stored session ID. Sessions are capped at two minutes, pending transcripts can retry, and a failed state refresh no longer terminates a connected interview. Browser diagnostics omit raw provider messages and credentials. Background tabs pause polling, and state reads have a separate rate-limit budget from interview controls.

Company context remains explicitly empty; financial-context assembly is not part of this change. Setup and architecture documentation describe the new Doppler fields and transcript flow. Existing connector session history remains readable.

Validation: lint, formatting, typecheck, build, 67 unit tests and 16 PostgreSQL integration tests passed in an isolated checkout based on current main. The production dependency audit reported no known vulnerabilities. A live Chrome test in the development workspace displayed the speaking avatar, captured user speech, and saved the provider transcript. Build retains existing dependency-annotation and bundle-size warnings.

author: skearnes
body:
## Summary The viewer's ask page shows the query as the model wrote it (`same_compound` with `"compound": "ibuprofen"`), and nothing says what structure the name resolved to. `Corpus.search` also resolved each name anew, so a caller without its own cache went back to PubChem on every search naming ibuprofen, even when the match set for its SMILES was cached. This keeps resolutions on the `Corpus` and reports them with each result and in the ask log. ## Changes - `Corpus` caches name → canonical SMILES for the 1024 (`_CACHED_RESOLUTIONS`) most recently used names. Only answers RDKit can read are kept; after a resolver error or an unparseable answer, the next search asks again. - A search whose query names a compound stamps its result with `execute.RESOLVED`, a JSON map from each name to the SMILES it matched, beside `TRUNCATED`; `execute.resolutions(table)` reads it. - `nl.Answer.resolved` carries that map; the query keeps the name. - The ask log records it as `nl_log.Ask.resolved`, for served questions and eval runs alike: a JSON string like `attempts`, empty for a query naming none and null where no search returned. With `translation`, it reproduces what was searched, so redaction keeps it; it is declared `VARCHAR` so months compacted before it existed still bind. - The search README and `nl_log`'s module docstring document the cache, `answer.resolved`, and the log field. ## Testing - `pytest -n auto ord_schema` on the head with main merged: 2090 passed, ORM tests included. - New tests: a name is resolved once across searches; the cache drops the least recently used name and asks again for it; a resolver error and an unparseable answer are each asked again; a result maps each name to its canonical spelling and carries no stamp for a SMILES-only query; `nl.ask` returns the map and records it, including when the description step fails; an eval case records it; the log field round-trips through JSON and compaction, redacted or not, beside records written without it. - Each new guard was mutation-checked, and each mutation fails the test named for it: the cache's lookup, recency refresh, and eviction; the unparseable-answer guard; the stamp; `Answer.resolved`; and the log field's string encoding, column type, presence in every record that follows a search (two in `nl.ask`, one in `nl_eval`), and exclusion from redaction. ## Notes - Once this is released, ord-app reads `execute.resolutions` into each search result for the ask page, and drops its own resolver cache in favor of this one. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge; the evaluation-log omission is fixed.

Summary

 The PR caches compound-name resolutions on each `Corpus` and carries the searched structures through results, answers, and logs. - Compound searches reuse recent name resolutions and report the structures they matched. - Natural-language answers and ask records show what each compound name resolved to.

Diagram

 ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart LR Query[Query naming compounds] --> Cache[Corpus resolution cache] Cache --> Search[Search using resolved structures] Search --> Table[Result with resolved map] Table --> Answer[Answer.resolved] Table --> Eval[Evaluation record] Answer --> Log[Ask log] Eval --> Log ```

## Yang dikerjakan

Kartu **A-15 — Kerangka layout CMS** (Fase 0): kerangka navigasi seluruh area `/cms` yang bisa dipakai semua kartu CMS berikutnya, tanpa isi dashboard (S1).

- `src/lib/rbac.ts` + tes: baris matriks baru `{ path: "/cms/quiz", match: "prefix", minRole: "EDITOR" }` (satu-satunya baris menu yang belum ada di matriks).
- `src/components/cms/cms-nav.ts` (murni, tanpa impor runtime): definisi menu `CMS_MENU` sesuai tabel kartu (grup Ringkasan / KONTEN / PENGIRIMAN / PENERBITAN / PENGATURAN), `getActiveCmsItem(pathname, status, role)` dengan pencocokan batas segmen, `cmsGroupOf`, `roleLabel`.
- `src/components/cms/cms-menu.server.ts`: `getVisibleCmsMenu(user)` — penyaring per peran di **server** (memanggil `pathAllows` dari rbac; tanpa `"use client"`/`"server-only"` supaya Vitest bisa mengimpor fungsi yang sama).
- `src/components/ui/tooltip.tsx` + tes: primitive Tooltip di atas radix-ui (tanpa dependensi baru).
- Kerangka layout: `cms-sidebar.tsx` (≥1024, total 249), `cms-rail.tsx` (640–1023, total 73, tooltip label), `cms-mobile-bar.tsx` (<640, bar 68 + drawer Dialog dengan judul sr-only), `cms-topbar.tsx` (breadcrumb mono), `cms-account-menu.tsx` (DropdownMenu: Lihat situs / Keluar), `cms-pages.tsx` (judul 28/900 + "Segera hadir.").
- `src/app/(cms)/layout.tsx` ditulis ulang: `requireRole("EDITOR")` + `getVisibleCmsMenu` → props serializable; `<main id="konten-utama">` milik layout (target SkipLink). 11 `page.tsx` tipis dengan guard + judul sendiri sesuai matriks; judul `/cms/konten` diturunkan dari `getActiveCmsItem` yang sama dengan breadcrumb.
- **Perbaikan pasca-review** (commit cfca622): ambang 640 (`md:` → `sm:` di 4 tempat), baris ✕ drawer disematkan (pola A-14b), `max-w-content`, `collisionPadding={8}` menu akun.

## Keputusan & asumsi (termasuk yang perlu kamu setujui)

1. **Layout mengirim daftar item tersaring** (`CmsMenuGroup[]`) selain `{ name, role }` — penyimpangan sadar dari kalimat langkah 4 kartu; tetap tanpa objek sesi/profil, dan penyaringan tetap di server lewat `getVisibleCmsMenu`.
2. **ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN + `?status=perlu-revisi` → judul "Persetujuan"**: kartu hanya mendefinisikan perlu-revisi untuk EDITOR; bagi admin nilai itu tak dikenal. Dicakup tes.
3. Ini pemakaian `useSearchParams` pertama di repo — rute tetap dinamis: output build menunjukkan semua `/cms/*` bertanda **ƒ (Dynamic)** **tanpa peringatan Suspense** (lihat "Hasil verifikasi otomatis").
4. Breadcrumb kosong (bukan error) untuk path tak dikenal di bawah `/cms` — tidak ada item aktif, tidak ada judul yang dikarang.
5. Tooltip rel: `delayDuration={300}`; topbar tidak sticky (mengikuti 19a; kartu tidak mensyaratkan sticky).
6. Ukuran di luar baris TOKENS dipakai apa adanya dari desain: mono 10.5 (chip/grup/label peran), item 13.5, judul 28, chip radius 5, baris drawer 15. `Reset attempt` tetap bahasa Inggris persis tabel kartu.
7. Menu akun berisi **Lihat situs** dan **Keluar** — tambahan sadar di luar kalimat kartu (Keluar diperlukan agar akun uji bisa berganti peran; keduanya tanpa ikon, Keluar bergaya danger).
8. Konten kosong di bawah judul disengaja: dashboard adalah S1 dan mengarang data dilarang (CLAUDE.md).
9. `w-[249px]`/`w-[73px]` (bukan 248/72): border-box memakan border 1px dari dalam; nilai ini menghasilkan total terukur persis 249/73.
10. **Ambang tata letak 640, bukan 768** (perbaikan review): rel, topbar, bar ponsel, dan padding isi memakai kelas `sm:` — `--breakpoint-sm` proyek ini **640px** (tokens.css), konsisten dengan komentar dan `matchMedia("(min-width: 640px)")` yang sudah ada di berkas yang sama. Peta akhir: < 640 bar+drawer · 640–1023 rel (73) + topbar 58 · ≥ 1024 sidebar (249) + topbar 62.
11. **Baris ✕ drawer disematkan** (pola drawer akun A-14b): baris sampul ✕+wordmark `flex-none`; hanya nav + blok user yang digulir di dalam panel (`overscroll-contain`, `max-height calc(100dvh - 68px)`). Di 360×640 setelah menggulir sampai Keluar, ✕ tetap sepenuhnya terlihat (probe DOM: y 11,5, 44×44) — penutupan tetap bisa lewat ✕ atau Esc; scrim memang tertutup panel penuh saat drawer terbuka, sama seperti drawer akun A-14b.
12. Kecil: `max-w-content` (token yang sudah ada) menggantikan `max-w-[1200px]` pada pembungkus isi; `collisionPadding={8}` di `DropdownMenuContent` menu akun — di 1280 menu tidak lagi menempel tepi kiri layar (terukur x = 8, dulu x ≈ 1).

## Item checklist §12.6 yang relevan (untuk tugas berisiko tinggi)

Tugas ini tidak menyentuh data pengguna/konten (tanpa query DB baru, tanpa input pengguna) — tidak ada item §12.6 yang relevan. Guard RBAC tetap berlapis: layout `EDITOR+`, tiap `page.tsx` memanggil `requireRole` sesuai matriks (fail-closed catch-all `/cms` SUPER_ADMIN sudah ada di rbac).

- `tsc --noEmit` ✓ · `eslint .` ✓ · `lint:hex` ✓ · grep anotasi desainer `\([A-Z]{1,4}-[0-9]+\)`/`§` pada teks render: bersih ✓

- `next build` ✓ (dijalankan ulang setelah perbaikan review) — semua rute `/cms/*` bertanda ƒ (Dynamic), tanpa peringatan `useSearchParams`/Suspense:
  ```
  ├ ƒ /cms            ├ ƒ /cms/konten       ├ ƒ /cms/pengaturan
  ```

- Matriks rute (curl, server produksi): staf 200 sesuai peran; EDITOR 403 di kategori/pengguna/reset-attempt/pengaturan/audit-log; ADMIN 403 di pengaturan/audit-log; MEMBER 403 semua; tamu 307 → `/masuk?next=…`.

  | Lebar | aside | topbar | bar ponsel | isi (kiri…kanan) | scrollW/clientW |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|

Tinggi topbar diverifikasi dengan probe DOM langsung per lebar (58 pada 640–1023, 62 pada ≥1024) — heuristik "div setinggi 58" di harness keliru menangkap div lain pada ≥1024, jadi kolom topbar memakai hasil probe. body:
## Summary

路由器拉订阅走的是代理，代理挂了就拉不到配置——而更新订阅正是修代理的手段。这是个自锁。

```
路由器(--> sub.judyplan.com) → 匹配 Mine1 → 🌐 国外 → 走代理 → 代理挂了 → 拉不到订阅
```

修法：在 Base YAML 的规则列表里、`RULE-SET,Mine1` **之前**插入一条直连规则。

```yaml
- DOMAIN,sub.judyplan.com,DIRECT   # 订阅地址必须直连
- RULE-SET,Mine1,🌐 国外
```

## 为什么不是改 Mine1.list

第一版我加在 `list/Mine1.list` 里，那是**无效的**：`classical` 类型的 rule-provider 每行只有
"类型,值" 两段，策略由引用它的 `RULE-SET,Mine1,🌐 国外` 统一提供。

日志证实了这一点：

```
[TCP] dial 🌐 国外 (match RuleSet/Mine1) 115.227.210.225 --> sub.judyplan.com:443 error: ...
              ^^^^^^^^ 策略来自 RULE-SET，不是 list 里的行
```

所以规则必须放在引用点之前，而不是 provider 内部。

## 改动

- 三个 Base YAML 各插入一条 `DOMAIN,sub.judyplan.com,DIRECT`（A2 / A3 / A5）
  - A4 复用 `Clash-A2-Base.yaml`，不单独改
- 改了 Base 就要升它自己的 `?v=`，四个 ini 一并升到 `2026-10-17-sub-direct`

author: yohnark
body:
## Scope
Add a repository-local GitHub Actions release workflow, without synchronizing yohn-jp/.github. A semantic version tag triggers independent linux/amd64 Core and Full builds. Each image is started and checked (HTTP/profile/assets, UID, writable /data, graceful SIGTERM) before pushing the same local image to `ghcr.io/yohn-jp/scriptorium/{core,full}:<tag>`.

The workflow uses least-privilege `contents:read` and `packages:write`, no long-lived registry secret, and publishes no `latest` tag. `docs/verification/OCI-RELEASE.md` documents usage, digest pinning, GHCR package visibility and the possibility of a partial release if one matrix leg fails.

## Verification
Inspected latest main (`9942b45679791bc57d83560c687b029187b57dbb`), package manifest, Dockerfile, existing OCI smoke script and GitHub workflow absence. Reviewed generated workflow and corrected the tag matcher to GitHub's `v*` glob with strict Bash semver validation. No release tag was created and no workflow executed, so GHCR permissions and actual release publication remain unverified until first tag. No shared CI changes.

## Release operation
After merging, create/push a new immutable `vX.Y.Z` tag. Set the two GHCR packages public separately if anonymous pulls are desired. Verify both published digests before using them in Praetorium. Do not repoint an existing version tag.

body:
Part b of dual write (#649). Observe now, once per load and only in act mode with planner v2, runs `callum-flow-event --new-path --repo <repo>`. Exit 0 means dual write is on and the new log is read once (a missing file is an empty log; unparseable lines are skipped). An older image (any other exit) means off and nothing else happens. A new `dualWrite` source reports a thrown probe or failed read without blocking anything, and retries at the githubEveryMs cadence. A new pure rule, `dualWriteRules` (H1, in rules-dualwrite.ts, called from stateRules beside heartbeatRules), logs a `transition` event with `via=dual-write` and the record's own seq for every record (closed ones too) whose `<issue>:<life>:<seq>` is not in the log and whose `seqAt` is before the read (the guard that stops a flood). The key is `dual-write:<issue>:<life>:<seq>`, so each stage is logged once. New code: hooks/v2/sources-dualwrite.ts and rules-dualwrite.ts; V2State.dualWrite and the V2Cache field. Docs: SPEC 2.4, 4.1, 7.1; the transition schema's via description; REFERENCE.md regenerated with build:events. One existing test (v2-vocabulary GitHub read order) now leaves the non-GitHub probe out of its log; no assertion was weakened. Hand-built `sources` literals in tests gained dualWrite.

Closes #741

Design brief: https://github.com/cbundy/dev-system/issues/741#issuecomment-6228643871

## Evidence
npm run lint passes (193 files, build:events check included). npm test: first full run 1314 pass, 0 fail. New tests: tests/v2-dual-write.test.ts (planner rule: off, on with empty seen incl. closed record and row/from lookup, closed-only record, seen triple, newer seq, seqAt >= readAt flood guard, done ledger entries; seenIn skipping other device/repo/non-transition/garbage; observe: probe once per load, exit 2, thrown probe, missing file, observe mode and shadow run no probe), v2-record.test.ts (same-seq dual-write re-log rebuilds the same records), tests/factory-loop-v2-events.test.js (via=dual-write through the real callum-flow-event, new line reads back with the same life/seq/via). Later full runs on a host at load average ~18 hit the 5s per-test timeout on a few unrelated CPU-heavy table/driver tests (different ones each run); not related to this change. author: waywardmonkeys
body:
Groundwork for loading and composing on several threads: both intern names and paths into the store as they go, so the interners have to accept new entries from many threads at once. This follows OpenUSD, which interns into global tables split into separately locked parts and never reports anything in the order its ids were created.

**Intern tokens and paths through a shared reference**
- `TokenInterner::intern` and `PathInterner::intern` take `&self`. A new `interning` table splits lookups by value across 64 separately locked hash tables (a `Mutex` with `std`, a `RefCell` without); lookups by id read append-only storage without locking.
- Ids still come from one counter, so they stay dense, as `invalidation::DenseKey` requires. Their order is interning order, which concurrent interning will make vary from run to run.
- `--cfg layerstack_reverse_ids` hands out ids in reverse within runs of 1,024: a diagnostic that turns "is anything ordered by id?" into a test run. The other two commits fix what it found.

**Rank a prim's opinions by node and layer alone**
- `cmp_keys` broke ties between opinions at the same node and layer strength by layer id and spec path id. With reversed ids, that reordered a layer's `clips` and `clipSets`, and a clip query resolved different values. Those opinions now compare equal, as in OpenUSD (`PcpBuildPrimPropertyIndex`).

**Report paths in namespace order**
- `PathInterner::cmp_paths` / `sort_paths` give namespace order (`SdfPath::operator<`).
- `Changes` (put in order where the live stage publishes them), `Applied::recomposed`, `LiveStage::recompose`, and the path queries on `LiveStage` and `Stage` now report in namespace order; the queries take the store to sort by.
- Schema dependency inventories and procedural producer inputs and outputs (which also decide build order) do the same.
- Iterating containers keyed by id stays in id order, documented as such.

**Results**
- Single-threaded cost, built with `std` as a threaded host builds it (15 interleaved rounds): scene A opens 2.9% and composes 7.9% slower, scene B 1.2% and 2.1%. About half of scene A's cost is the locks: built without `std`, where they are `RefCell`s, it composes 3.4% slower. (An earlier version of this description reported numbers from builds without `std`.) #153 cuts this with read locks and stored parent ids, and makes composition faster overall once it runs on threads.
- Scene dumps are byte-identical across #151, this branch, and this branch with reversed ids, on all three scenes.
- C++ comparison corpus: 196 of 198 cases match in every respect, unchanged.
- Gate passes on each commit (2,211 tests); with `--cfg layerstack_reverse_ids` all 2,211 pass too.

author: nima-hs
body:
## What

Debug and test builds keep only line tables for our own crates, still enough for a panic's file and line, and no debug info for dependencies:

```toml
[profile.dev]
debug = "line-tables-only"

[profile.dev.package."*"]
debug = false
```

Release builds are unchanged. The rules that exist only in release builds (`cfg(debug_assertions)`) depend on them, and `debug` is a separate setting from `debug-assertions`. A new CI step reads the compiler's flags from a fresh verbose build of `ubc-vpn-core` and fails if debug builds keep more debug info, or if release builds gain debug info or debug assertions.

Root `Cargo.toml` is normally lead-only; the lead asked for this change.

## Why

Reviewers keep several worktrees, each with its own `target/` of 10-23 GB, on a machine that often has 2-5 GB of free memory. Less debug info means less to write and link.

## Measurements

Windows 11, Rust 1.99.0, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`, a fresh `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` under the worktree for each build, at least 2.5 GB of free memory before each.

| Build | `target/` before | `target/` after | Change | Time before | Time after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `cargo build -p ubc-vpn-core` | 103.9 MB | 84.2 MB | -19% | 12.2 s | 11.8 s |
| `cargo test -p ubc-vpn-platform --features dev-mode --no-run` | 326.9 MB | 223.8 MB | -32% | 25.8 s | 21.1 s |

`cargo build --release -p ubc-vpn-core -v` gives the compiler identical flags for all 19 crates with and without this change (`-C opt-level=3 -C embed-bitcode=no -C strip=debuginfo` for `ubc_vpn_core`).

## Nothing depends on full debug info

Searched the repository for debug info, backtraces, `RUST_BACKTRACE`, `.pdb`, `addr2line`, `split-debuginfo` and profile settings. Nothing reads debug info. The checks that look inside built programs (`platform-windows.yml`, `platform-unix.yml`) read release builds, which do not change. Panics in our own crates still name the file and line.

## Mutations

Each rule broken in `Cargo.toml`, then the new CI step run locally exactly as `ci.yml` has it, then `Cargo.toml` put back.

| Rule | Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Our crates keep line tables only | Removed `debug = "line-tables-only"` | Failed: `ubc_vpn_core in dev.log: expected '-C debuginfo=line-tables-only', got '-C debuginfo=2'` |
| Dependencies keep no debug info | Removed `[profile.dev.package."*"]` | Failed: `serde_json in dev.log: expected '', got '-C debuginfo=line-tables-only'` |
| Release builds keep debug assertions off | Added `[profile.release] debug-assertions = true` | Failed: `ubc_vpn_core in release.log: expected '-C opt-level=3', got '-C debug-assertions=on -C opt-level=3'` |
| Release builds gain no debug info | Added `[profile.release] debug = "line-tables-only"` | Failed: `ubc_vpn_core in release.log: expected '-C opt-level=3', got '-C debuginfo=line-tables-only -C opt-level=3'` |
| (none) | The change as written | Passed |

author: sondrateconsulting-ryan
body:
## Summary

The four audit entrypoints (`orchestrate`, `report`, `export`, `compare`) handled `main()`'s rejection by writing the diagnosis to stderr and calling `process.exit(1)` straight away. `process.exit` throws away anything the runtime still has buffered for a piped stdout or stderr. A consumer reading the JSONL could therefore lose the end of the stream, and on Bun could get a last line cut off mid-way. That contradicted the `scripts/log.ts` header, which promised "the JSONL a consumer parses is always whole lines".

This bug was already on main and has nothing to do with the Bun bump. It came up while reviewing #56.

## Reproduction (outside the repo, macOS)

Write 2,001 JSONL lines of about 230 B each into a consumer that waits 1 s before reading, then exit:

| | Bun 1.4.3 | Node 24 |
|---|---|---|
| `process.exit(1)` straight away | 65,536 B = 284 whole lines **+ the 285th cut mid-line** | 284 whole lines (65,494 B) |
| `process.exitCode = 1`, natural exit | all 2,001 | all 2,001 |
| same, stderr instead of stdout | 299 vs 2,001 | 299 vs 2,001 |

Two fixes that look obvious don't work on Bun:
- **Waiting for `'drain'`.** Right after those writes, Bun 1.4.3's `process.stdout` reports `writableLength 0` and `writableNeedDrain false`, so there is nothing to wait for.
- **An empty-write callback as a barrier.** `process.stdout.write("", cb)` calls back after 6 ms, long before the data is flushed.

## The fix

`exitFatal` in `scripts/cliErrors.ts` does three things:
1. Writes the diagnosis using `renderFatal`, which is unchanged.
2. Sets `process.exitCode = 1` and returns. The event loop then flushes stdout and stderr, and the process exits 1 by itself.
3. Starts an **unref'd** backstop timer. After `FATAL_DRAIN_DEADLINE_MS` (10 s), it hard-exits with code 1 if the loop still hasn't emptied, for example because the consumer stopped reading or a handle was left open. Because the timer is unref'd, it never keeps the process alive by itself.

All four entrypoints now call `main().catch((e) => exitFatal(e, { command, usage }))`.

The divert sink installed by `logLine` needs no flushing. `lifecycle.ts` writes each line with a looped `writeSync` before `logLine` returns, so nothing is left buffered for the exit to throw away.

The `log.ts` header is now scoped accurately:
- `logLine` guarantees only that it hands the active sink whole lines.
- Whether those lines are delivered depends on how the process ends. A normal return keeps every line whole. The fatal path also keeps them whole, provided the consumer catches up within the deadline; both measured on macOS with Bun 1.4.3 and Node 24.
- Other endings can lose the tail, including a partial last line: a consumer still behind at the deadline, a kill signal, or an uncaught exception outside `main()`'s promise chain.

### End-to-end probe with the real `logLine` + `exitFatal` (Bun 1.4.3, macOS)

| Consumer | Result |
|---|---|
| Slow consumer | all 2,001 lines, every one parses as JSON, exit status 1. Node 24 gives the same result. |
| Stalled for 13 s | backstop fires at 10 s, exit status 1, 284 lines. The process waits at most the deadline. |
| Closes the pipe while the fatal path is draining | exit status 1 within about 1 s, then Bun prints an `EPIPE: broken pipe` trace on stderr. A non-fatal run that hits EPIPE prints the same trace. |

On real entrypoints, `bun run scripts/report.ts --bogus` and `bun run scripts/orchestrate.ts --config /nonexistent.json` exit 1 in 0.02–0.11 s. Ordinary fatal errors leave nothing for the loop to wait on, so they never hit the backstop.

## Tests (red → green)

All new tests are in `scripts/cliErrors.test.ts`. None of them spawns a process: the spawn-site allowlist in `github.test.ts` keeps spawn surfaces to the sanctioned sites. The runtime flush itself is therefore covered by the probes above. The tests pin the control flow:

- **No synchronous hard exit.** The fatal flow renders to stderr, sets `exitCode = 1` and starts the backstop, and nothing calls `exit` synchronously.
  - **Red** with the old behaviour extracted unchanged into the seam: `[stderr…, "exit(1)"]`.
- **Only the backstop calls `exit`, with code 1.**
  - **Red** on the old flow: `exit(1)` already happened synchronously.
- **The real backstop timer is unref'd** (`hasRef() === false`).
- **The production host forwards to the real process.** It passes through `stderr`, `exitCode` and `exit` (spied), and its backstop is `armUnrefBackstop`. A mutation that drops `setExitCode` makes this test fail. The test restores `exitCode` with `?? 0`, because Bun 1.4.3 ignores `process.exitCode = undefined`, and restoring the saved `undefined` would leave the test runner itself exiting 1.
- **Source pin.** No non-test script except `cliErrors.ts` calls `process.exit(`, and each audit entrypoint's `import.meta.main` block calls `exitFatal(e, { command: "<name>" …`.
  - **Red** on main: `["compare.ts","report.ts","orchestrate.ts","export.ts"]`.

Results: `bun test` 2,613 pass / 0 fail (exit 0); `bun run typecheck` clean.

## Notes for review

- **Not probed:** Bun on Linux; only Bun 1.4.3 on macOS is installed locally. The claims in the comments are scoped to what was measured. This branch was cut before #56 landed, so its CI runs Bun 1.3.14; updating the branch onto main (which has #56) moves CI to Bun 1.4.3.
- **Source pin limits:** it is a text tripwire. It doesn't catch aliased forms such as `const { exit } = process`.
- **`PROMPT-TUI.md:246` left as is.** It says "renderFatal + exit 1 … is unchanged", a scope statement in the TUI spec. The entrypoint still renders with `renderFatal` and exits 1, now through `exitFatal`, so the line stays accurate and I didn't edit it.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun test` (2,613 pass, exit 0)
- [x] `bun run typecheck`
- [x] Red→green captured for the seam tests and the source pin
- [x] Out-of-repo end-to-end probes: slow, stalled and closed consumers (Bun 1.4.3); slow consumer (Node 24)
- [ ] CI green (Linux; Bun 1.3.14 as branched, 1.4.3 once the branch is updated onto main)

author: harrytwigg
body:
Stacked on #171.

Every icon in the web app is now a Phosphor glyph, duotone by default. Phosphor's React package carries all six weights in each icon, so this generates single-weight modules instead: `scripts/generate-icons.mjs` reads `@phosphor-icons/core`'s duotone SVGs and writes one module per icon name (two path strings each) under `components/ui/icons/`, exposed from `@/components/ui/icon` under the names the app already used. All call sites import from there; `lucide-react` is no longer imported and a lint rule keeps it that way. The output is checked in, and a test fails if it drifts from the generator. The Lucide name → Phosphor glyph map is `scripts/icon-map.mjs` (141 names, each glyph validated to exist).

- Default size 24, decorative unless labelled, `data-icon` names the glyph; spinners animate through their class.
- `filled` raises the 20% layer to full strength where Lucide's `fill` mattered: the radio-item dot, the kept pin, play buttons.
- Lucide's `strokeWidth` has no Phosphor equivalent and is dropped at the call sites.
- Tests that queried Lucide's `.lucide-*` classes now query `data-icon`.

**Size** (gzip, vs #171): initial path 187,779 → 192,529 B (+4,750, budget 195,000); board page 24,570 → 24,600 (+30, budget 25,000); task page 22,464 → 23,384 (+920); all JS +14 KB, mostly lazy routes.

**Regular weight where the duotone layer is a stray shape:** Phosphor's duotone caret is a small outlined triangle, and several glyphs (a tick, a cross, a plus) carry a plain square, rectangle or disc behind the stroke that reads as a box rather than a tint. Those names are generated in Phosphor's regular weight through a per-name override in `scripts/icon-map.mjs`; they keep their shape and still match the set. Names: `Check`, `CheckIcon`, `X`, `XIcon`, `Plus`, `Minus`, `ChevronUp/Down/Left/Right` and their `*Icon` twins, `Ellipsis`, `EllipsisVertical`, `MoreHorizontal`, `GripVertical`, `ArrowRightLeftIcon`, `ListChecks`, `ListTodo`, `ListFilter`, `Download`, `LogOut`, `RefreshCw`, `RotateCw`, `RotateCcw`, `Terminal`, `Minimize2`. A glyph whose layer is its own silhouette (a clock face, a bell, a folder) stays duotone. The published package ships Phosphor's MIT notice in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` (listed in `files`). Lucide stays in `package.json` until the final slice, unused.

Before/after sheets (light and dark, desktop and narrow) for chat, board, todo and settings are attached, plus the fallback chip, the radio dot and the chevrons up close.

author: henrypark133
body:
## GLM-5.3 v7-pdmuxe image recipe: v7 + PD-Multiplexing with EAGLE (draft; do not publish yet)

New recipe `docker/sglang-glm53-hicache-w4afp8-pdmuxe` = the v7 recipe (`218a692`, patches 1-12 byte-identical, no `kda-zero-sync`) plus one patch applied last: `pdmux-eagle.diff`. It adds the publish-workflow variant `hicache-w4afp8-pdmuxe` (tag `glm53-hicache-w4afp8-v7-pdmuxe`). **Without `--enable-pdmux` the patch is inert**, so the image serves exactly like v7.

**Status: draft, do not merge or publish.** The lab gate for its only intended use, a one-replica base canary (stacked PR nearai/cvm-compose-files#362), **fails on long-prompt TTFT**; see below. This PR is open so the recipe can be reviewed. It will be revised with the scheduler fix before anyone publishes it.

### What the patch does (19 files under `python/sglang/srt/`)
- Port of upstream sglang #42411 (GLM PD-Multiplexing): prefill runs in layer slices on its own stream, in a green context capped at 96 of 132 SMs, beside full-device decode, rather than as a pass that freezes every decoding request.
- Port of the single-layer MTP part of #42414. It captures hidden states on the final prefill slice, runs one draft extend on the prefill TP group, and routes verify and mamba state through the per-stream decode backend.
- Per-stream-group EAGLE draft decode CUDA graphs, with eager fallback via `SGLANG_PDMUX_EAGLE_DRAFT_GRAPHS=0`.
- Backlog mode (full-device prefill under queue pressure) is **in the code but off**: the baked YAML has no `backlog_*` keys. It was rejected in the lab, and its uncapped variant deadlocked across TP ranks. Do not enable it.
- `validation_hook.py`: with `--enable-pdmux`, only fixed single-layer EAGLE/NEXTN is accepted. The overlap scheduler and mixed chunking are rejected.
- Config baked read-only at `/etc/glm53/pdmux-ov96-l4.yaml`: `[[96,36,1]]` split, overlap mode, 4 prefill layers per iteration.

### Lab evidence (tee-bench exp 45, nearai/tee-bench#8; bare H200, CC off, n=1)
30-minute soak pair at 1.0 conv/s with the prod base argv, this patch's exact bytes vs v7:

| | v7 | v7-pdmuxe |
|---|---|---|
| streamed time in gaps >300 ms | 71.1% | **0.0%** |
| token-weighted decode rate | 15.1 tok/s | **30.7 tok/s** |
| TPOT p50 / p95 | 64.6 / 99.8 ms | 31.7 / 44.6 ms |
| GSM8K-100 / accept length | n/a / 3.44 | 0.99 / 3.49 |
| smoke gate (tee-bench#7) | 48 / 0 / 0 | 48 / 0 / 0 |
| **TTFT ≥16K prompts, first 300 s (prod-like load)** | p95 9.7 s | **p95 122.6 s, max 144 s** |
| total tok/s; queue-full sheds | 16,007; 404 | 11,917 (−26%); 599 (+48%) |

The freezes go away and decode doubles. But long prompts starve, most likely in split-prefill admission (not traced yet). That has to be fixed before any canary.

### Checks
- `python3 -m unittest scripts.test_glm53_pdmux_recipe`: OK. It checks the hashes, the manifest (42 entries, of which 19 are pdmux files with after = overlay sha256), the COPY list and the workflow pins.
- `git apply --check` of the diff against the v7 sources: clean.
- Overlay CPU tests in the lab: 107 passed. They are the 9 test files that `test-cpu.sh` step 14 runs in the image.
- **Not run:** `apply-patches.py` on the full image, the image build, `test-cpu.sh`. The publish workflow runs all three.

### Rollback
Nothing deploys from this PR. A replica using the image rolls back by redeploying v7 `sha256:fa730e6e…`.

Two of the five `vk::` VkResult accessors disagreed with `include/vulkan/vulkan_core.h` (VK_HEADER_VERSION 365):

| accessor | was | Khronos | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_DRIVER()` | -1000001001 | `VK_ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_DRIVER = -9` | -9 |
| `ERROR_NOT_READY()` | -1000001005 | no `VK_ERROR_NOT_READY`; `VK_NOT_READY = 1` is a **success** code | replaced by `NOT_READY() = 1` |

`SUCCESS()` (0), `INCOMPLETE()` (5) and `ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR()` (-1000001004) already matched the header exactly. `ERROR_NOT_READY` had no Khronos counterpart, so it is mapped to the real code rather than kept under a misleading error name.

## What changed

Adds an interactive annual stability view for four-market liquidity. It summarizes each market-cap bucket using month-weighted ADV20 and ADV20-to-market-cap distributions, with observed-month coverage and monthly P25–P75 ranges. The band is explicitly described as temporal spread, not a confidence interval.

Updates the research notes and page to clarify that the Beijing Stock Exchange minute gap is a known TuShare coverage limitation, that recovered traded-only A-share rows cannot establish a point-in-time listed/suspended denominator, and that actual execution calibration still requires private parent-order, fill, fee and synchronized quote records.

## Validation

- Python: 568 passed, 1 skipped; targeted stability test passed after rebasing.

author: imrans110
body:
## Why

`main` hasn't compiled for a while, so every CI job (Check & Lint, Test, Security Audit) has been failing since February. Nothing Dependabot opened could pass either. This PR gets the workspace building and passing fmt, clippy and tests again. It also fixes two runtime bugs that only showed up once the binary actually ran.

The PR has two commits, so the formatting-only commit can be reviewed separately:

1. **Apply rustfmt across the workspace.** Formatting only, no behavior change.
2. **Fix compile errors, failing tests, lints and two runtime bugs.** All the substantive changes.

## Compile fixes

Most of these come from dependency APIs drifting from what the code expected.

- **avro-kafka**
  - Give `FutureRecord` an explicit key type.
  - Drop the `Debug` derive on `Publisher`, since `FutureProducer` isn't `Debug`.
  - Handle the `Result` that `Writer::into_inner` returns.
  - Add `Publisher::serialize` for a single value, which the tests use.
  - Add a `tokio` dev-dependency for the async integration test.
- **collector-app**
  - Update `histogram!` and `gauge!` calls to the metrics 0.22 macro syntax.
  - Pin the `ctrl_c()` future used in `select!`.
  - Pass a `u32` to `Duration::saturating_mul`.
  - In env overrides, stop moving `Option<String>` fields out from behind `&mut`.

## Test fixes

- **buffer**: the SQLite pool now opens with `create_if_missing(true)`. Before, a fresh buffer path failed with `unable to open database file`. That broke the tests and would also break a first run of the collector. WAL and `synchronous = NORMAL` now live in the connect options, so they apply to every pooled connection. Before, they only applied to whichever connection ran the `PRAGMA`.
- **sunspec-parser**: XML parsing now accepts self-closing `<model ... />` elements. They were skipped silently, so the fixture parsed as 0 models.
- **e2e harness**: the test now builds `PollSample` directly and follows the real pipeline: JSON into the buffer, then Avro on uplink. Before, it stored Avro in the buffer, which the uplink would have discarded as corrupt.

## Runtime fixes

Both were found by running the collector against a local SunSpec Modbus simulator.

- **Modbus reads are capped at 125 registers by default**, the protocol limit for function 0x03. Model discovery reads 200 registers at once, so unless `max_batch_size` was configured, a real device rejects the request with *illegal data value* and no models are ever discovered. A configured `max_batch_size` is still respected but is clamped to that limit.
- **No more hang when no pollers are running.** If discovery finds nothing, or every poller exits, `main` used to leave its loop without sending the shutdown signal. It then waited forever on the buffer task, and Ctrl-C stopped working because the signal future was no longer being polled. It now signals shutdown first and exits cleanly.

## Lint fixes

- `field_reassign_with_default`
- `needless_borrows_for_generic_args`
- redundant `.ok()` matched against `Some`
- an unused assignment in the Modbus retry loop
- an unused import

## Verification

Run locally with Rust 1.99 on macOS:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace -- -D warnings`: 0 findings
- `RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings cargo build --workspace`: ok
- `cargo test --workspace`: 13 passed, 0 failed. The Kafka and diagslave integration tests skip unless their env vars are set.
- End-to-end run against a simulated inverter on localhost:
  - Default settings discovered models 1 and 103.
  - 5 poll cycles produced 10 samples, which went through the SQLite buffer and were Avro-encoded and published. No broker was configured, so this used the mock publisher.
  - `/metrics` served the poller, buffer and uplink metrics.
  - Ctrl-C shut down cleanly.
- With the device offline, the collector now logs `no pollers running, shutting down` and exits instead of hanging.

## Not in this PR

- **Security Audit (`cargo audit`) will still fail.** That needs dependency upgrades (rdkafka, apache-avro and others), several of which have breaking API changes. Those are better handled separately, together with the open Dependabot PRs, once this lands.

author: ethgr0wth
body:
## SI-0 reference runtime — testable, not a spec

Branch `si-0/runtime` → `main`. This is the working `si` runtime the specs
describe: `si init` builds a `.si` bundle, and `si cycle` runs one serial
self-write (PERCEIVE → PROPOSE → GATE → JOURNAL → MATERIALIZE → VERIFY)
with the 5-check ternary gate (ADMIT / REJECT / ESCALATE) in front of every
write. Rollback is a first-class journaled operation.

**Tested and green: 22/22 pytest, verified by the coordinator on this tree**
(`/tmp/prfactory-si0/venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q` → `22 passed`):

- `test_gate.py` (10) — accept; reject isolated per check: constitution,
  safety bounds (3 params), identity continuity, capability floor,
  provenance (2 params); ESCALATE on constitution intents
- `test_journal_ordering.py` (2) — journal-before-materialize (self_edit
  seq strictly precedes the post-materialize checkpoint); rejections journal
  verdicts and move no bytes, no head
- `test_rollback.py` (1) — rollback restores prior head, popped deltas
  marked `rolled_back`, blobs retained on disk as evidence
- `test_bundle.py` (4) — tampered constitution.md, tampered journal doc,
  and unknown major `si_version` all fail closed (`TamperError`); fresh
  init loads clean
- `test_loop.py` (1) — end-to-end self-write on the real numpy `DemoMind`:
  ADMIT, `d0001`, VERIFIED, content-addressed blob on disk
- `test_nedb_backend.py` (4) — same loop against the REAL NEDB engine
  (autostarted `nedbd-v2` daemon): init, cycle, `verify_chain()`,
  rollback, tamper fail-closed

**Real vs stubbed — stated plainly:**

- REAL: the 6-phase loop, the 5-check gate, manifest + SHA-256 hash-chain
  handling, rollback, the hash-chained journal with logical clock, and a
  real CPU machine-learning demo mind (gradient descent learns a rank-2
  LoRA-style adapter; residual ~2.5% of target, identity drift 0.039 vs
  tol 0.25). Deltas are genuine `.safetensors` blobs.
- REAL: the NEDB journal backend (`si/backends/nedb.py`) — the actual
  NEDB engine over pgwire (schemaless collections, native `_seq`/`_hash`,
  real causal edges). The `nedb-engine` wheel ships a prebuilt `nedbd-v2`
  binary, so no Rust toolchain is needed; the backend autostarts it on
  bundle-derived ports with data inside the bundle. Proven with a
  write→read round-trip and daemon-kill durability test.
- STUBBED / DEMO-LABELED: the default journal backend is embedded sqlite
  (zero services; `--journal-backend nedb` selects the real engine), and
  the seed weights from `si init` are RANDOM DATA (`base.source` says
  `"demo:random-seed (not a real model)"` in the manifest itself) — the
  SI-0 seed slot is reserved for the Pocket Spark safetensors master.
  Constitution-amendment intents always ESCALATE (no autonomous
  self-amendment in SI-0, per spec).

**Run the demo loop:**

```bash
python3 -m venv /tmp/si-venv && /tmp/si-venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
/tmp/si-venv/bin/pip install -e .
si init ./sentinel-001.si --name sentinel-001
si cycle ./sentinel-001.si --mind demo   # trains a real adapter, gates it, journals it
si log ./sentinel-001.si
si why ./sentinel-001.si d0001
si rollback ./sentinel-001.si --to base --reason "operator: trim stack"
```

With the real NEDB journal (extra install: `pip install -r requirements-nedb.txt`):

```bash
si init ./sentinel-nedb.si --name sentinel-nedb --journal-backend nedb
si cycle ./sentinel-nedb.si --mind demo
```

Caveats: NEDB's pgwire is simple-query protocol only (`psycopg2`, not
`psycopg3`); pgwire is cleartext, loopback only. Pinned against
`nedb-engine==12.15.16`. No GPU, no network calls in the loop; tests are
deterministic (seeded RNG). Left open for Mark's review — never merged by
Muse.

author: richtera
body:
## Why
universal-relayer prod, 2026-10-16: every transaction from mainnets backend wallet `0xa7d5…777c` on **Arbitrum (42161)** failed at send with `nonce too high: tx: 2 state: 1`, from the moment two sends started in the same second on that wallet's first use on the chain.

## Root cause
- **`acquireNonce`** treated `INCR == 1` as "counter unset → sync from chain → INCR again". Two concurrent first sends: X gets 1 and awaits the onchain read; Y's INCR returns **2** (≠ 1, no sync) and keeps nonce 2; X's sync resets the counter, X gets **0**. Nonce 1 is never issued.
- **`nonceResyncWorker`** only scans `nonce-sent:*` (wallets with an in-flight tx). A wallet whose sends all fail before broadcast has none → the gap is never recycled → stuck until a manual `reset-nonces`.

## Fix
1. **Atomic first use** (`wallet-nonce.ts`): if the last-used counter doesn't exist, read the onchain transaction count and `SET key count-1 NX`, then `INCR`. All concurrent first users read the same count, one write wins, every INCR after it is contiguous. No more `nonce === 1` heuristic.
2. **Self-heal**: the gap logic is extracted to `recycleNonceGaps(chainId, wallet)` (the resync worker now calls it too). On a **`nonce too high`** RPC error the send worker recycles the gap for that wallet, so the BullMQ retry (5 attempts) — and every other queued send — takes the missing nonce first. The catch-block nonce handling moved to `src/worker/tasks/send-error-nonce.ts` so it is unit-tested; other paths unchanged.

Not changed: concurrency of sends per wallet (nonces stay atomic INCRs; serialising per wallet would cap throughput).

## Tests — `tests/unit/wallet-nonce-gap.test.ts`
Real nonce code against a **real Redis** (`REDIS_TEST_URL`, default `redis://localhost:6390/15`, flushed) — only the onchain read is stubbed (with a delay to open the race window).
- 5 concurrent first-use acquires → `[0,1,2,3,4]`; from count 7 → `[7,8,9]`; existing counter → no onchain read. **With the upstream heuristic restored, the first two fail** (`[0,2,3,4,5]` — the prod gap).
- `recycleNonceGaps` on the prod state (onchain last 0, counter 2) → recycles `[1,2]`, next acquires 1, 2, 3; in-flight nonce excluded; no-op when in sync.
- send-error hook: "nonce too high" recycles the gap (`["1","2"]`, next acquire = 1); any other error only recycles its own nonce, no onchain read (fails with the hook disabled).
- `tsc` clean, biome clean. The fork's 9 pre-existing unit failures (auth/kms/chain/webhook/send-worker, env-dependent) are identical on the base commit.

## Rollout
Image `engine:patch-1d3509d9` → dev (`engine_image`, apply, serve) → prod (mirror image, `engine_image`, apply). Once live, the stuck prod wallet heals on its next send attempt (the hourly levelling retry) without a manual reset.

## Task

- Mã task: S-60 — Vận hành viên đổi cấu hình trụ từ xa bằng ChangeConfiguration.
- Phạm vi và checklist: [docs/S60_REMOTE_CONFIGURATION.md](https://github.com/Stephen232980/TTCS_T926_K8S4_N1-CSMS/blob/feature/S-60-remote-configuration/docs/S60_REMOTE_CONFIGURATION.md).

## Thay đổi

- Thêm API operator và giao diện thu gọn trong chi tiết trụ để đọc/đổi HeartbeatInterval (30–600 giây) và MeterValueSampleInterval (5–300 giây). Ẩn điều khiển nếu thiếu quyền.
- Lưu intent UUID/audit trước khi gửi OCPP; chống gửi trùng và dùng GetConfiguration để xác minh. Accepted chưa được coi là thành công; chỉ readback đúng mới cập nhật heartbeat dùng cho liveness.
- RebootRequired cần xác nhận Soft Reset riêng. Chặn khi có phiên/yêu cầu bắt đầu hoặc đầu nối báo đang bận; giữ chặn phiên mới nếu Reset mất phản hồi. Kết quả đọc cũ không được ghi đè xác nhận reset mới.
- Giữ heartbeat qua reconnect, không tự gửi lại ChangeConfiguration/Reset sau timeout hoặc tiến trình khởi động lại. Dùng adapter GetConfiguration chung với phân bổ công suất.
- Thêm migration j240024a2026 và cập nhật simulator để lưu cấu hình bền vững, áp dụng chu kỳ heartbeat/số đo mới. Không đổi giá trị chạy nếu lưu file thất bại.
- Sửa khai báo kiểu trả về truy vấn đối soát để mypy toàn src đạt; không đổi truy vấn hay nghiệp vụ đối soát.

## Lý do

Vận hành viên cần đổi hai chu kỳ từ xa và phân biệt trụ nhận lệnh với cấu hình đã thực sự áp dụng. Yêu cầu khởi động lại và kết quả chưa xác định phải được giữ bền vững để tránh reset tự động, gửi trùng hoặc bắt đầu sạc quá sớm.

## Cách kiểm tra

Trên PostgreSQL thử nghiệm đã áp dụng migration, chạy bộ chức năng riêng với hai kiểm tra latency bắt buộc theo thứ tự CI:

```text
ruff check .
ruff format --check .
mypy src
alembic upgrade head
pytest tests/test_s60_configuration.py tests/test_ocpp_foundation.py tests/test_ocpp_monitoring.py tests/test_ocpp_control.py tests/test_driver_charging.py tests/test_charging_sessions.py tests/test_power.py tests/test_staging_demo_protocol.py tests/test_staging_demo_power.py tests/test_staging_demo_update.py tests/test_charge_points_migration.py tests/test_endpoint_policy_inventory.py -k "not twenty_concurrent_meter_replies"
pytest tests/test_staging_demo_protocol.py tests/test_accounting_reconciliation.py
pytest tests/test_charging_sessions.py::test_committed_replay_and_twenty_concurrent_meter_replies_under_200ms -q -s
pytest tests/test_s19_meter_latency.py::test_twenty_real_sockets_periodic_meter_replies_under_200ms -q -s
```

Trong frontend: `npm run lint`, `npm test -- --maxWorkers=1`, `npm run build`.

## Kết quả

- [x] Ruff và định dạng thành công.
- [x] mypy toàn bộ 159 file src thành công.
- [ ] pytest toàn bộ thành công — **hai kiểm tra latency còn chưa đạt ổn định; không coi PR sẵn sàng merge**.
- [x] Luồng thành công: hai khóa qua WebSocket thật, phản hồi đi qua bộ nhận OCPP và PostgreSQL; readback, audit và giữ cấu hình sau tạo lại simulator.
- [x] Luồng lỗi: timeout/disconnect, mismatch/readonly/unknown, quyền, xác nhận reset, trạng thái trụ bận, race đọc lại/reset, retry cùng UUID, lỗi lưu simulator.
- [ ] Migration tiến/lùi thành công — đã kiểm tra upgrade trên DB mới; chưa kiểm tra downgrade.
- [ ] OpenAPI đã cập nhật hoặc PR không thay đổi API — thêm ba endpoint, schema được sinh từ router; cần review hợp đồng API.
- [x] Không chứa secret, .env hoặc dữ liệu nhạy cảm.
- [x] Tài liệu đã cập nhật.

**Bằng chứng cục bộ:** 327 kiểm tra backend chức năng đạt, gồm 28 trường hợp S-60; 20 kiểm tra bổ sung simulator/đối soát đạt (trùng một phần với bộ trên). Frontend 426/426 đạt khi chạy tuần tự, ESLint/TypeScript/build đạt. Lần chạy frontend mặc định đồng thời có hai ca hết thời gian chờ tải dữ liệu. Build còn cảnh báo bundle >500 kB.

**Hiệu năng chưa đóng:** giữ nguyên ngưỡng 200 ms. S-60 trên DB mới, đo trước chức năng: MeterValues trực tiếp 248 ms và 20 socket thật 287 ms, đều Fail. Develop gốc trong một lần đối chiếu riêng đạt 174 ms và 184/141/185 ms. Đo luân phiên trên cùng DB: develop 225/92/94 ms, S-60 183/245/188 ms; cả hai có biến động. Chạy MeterValues dưới profiler đều đạt ở cả hai bản. Chưa xác định nguyên nhân, chưa chứng minh không có hồi quy; không nới ngưỡng hoặc bỏ hai cổng tốc độ trong CI.

## Phối hợp

- [x] Dependency S-16 có trên develop; nhánh bắt đầu từ develop 82a2794.
- [x] Frontend dùng API được bổ sung cùng PR, có kiểm thử quyền và các trạng thái.
- [x] Hướng dẫn review: ưu tiên UUID xử lý/race reset, giữ chặn khi kết quả Reset chưa xác định, heartbeat qua BootNotification và tác động lên adapter GetConfiguration của power.

## Nghiệm thu / triển khai

Chưa triển khai hay nghiệm thu staging/trụ vật lý. Trình duyệt cục bộ bị tắt nên chưa xác minh UI bằng ảnh. Sau merge cần cập nhật cả script simulator được mount riêng theo quy trình bảo vệ phiên/hold, không seed lại dữ liệu. Checklist nghiệm thu có trong tài liệu S-60.

author: oriontheprogrammer
body:
Agrega el **notification-service**, el consumidor del flujo 2 del EP3: avisa por
correo a quien sigue una prenda cuando **baja de precio**, se **agota** o se **repone**
(tarjetas T08 y T09 del tablero).

## Qué trae

- **Servicio base (T08)**: proyecto .NET 10 con `/health`, Dockerfile y bloque en
  `docker-compose` (red `cep`, puerto 8082 solo en `127.0.0.1`). Esquema propio
  `notification` con la tabla `notificaciones_enviadas` y su migración EF Core
  (`Migrate()` al arrancar).
- **Seguidores y correos**: `GET /internal/personal/seguidores/{productId}` en
  product-service (favoritos = `PersonalItem Kind="deseado"`), y `sub → email` con
  `ListUsers` de Cognito (caché 1 h, salta correos sin verificar). En local, sin AWS,
  un mapa `CorreosPrueba` cumple el mismo rol para demostrar en modo log.
- **Consumo y envío (T09)**: bucle de long polling sobre SQS (`IColaMensajes`),
  deduplicación por `(event_id, owner)`, envío con MailKit (`CORREO_MODO=log|smtp`),
  plantillas HTML/texto por tipo de evento, y DLQ con atributos de diagnóstico.

## Decisiones

Documentadas en **ADR-030**: el servicio **no toca el esquema `product`** (se habla
por HTTP interno); una dirección rechazada por el servidor (SMTP 550/553) se registra
y se salta a esa persona, no manda el evento entero a la DLQ.

## Notas

- Config 100% por variables de entorno (ver `.env.example`); nada de secretos en el repo.
- Compila sin warnings (service + solución). Falta probar `docker compose up` punta a
  punta y confirmar que `LabRole` permite `cognito-idp:ListUsers` en la EC2.
- El lado productor (product-service publicando en SNS, T07) va en su propio PR.
