author: khalilgharbaoui
body:
Nothing bounded what a conversation spends through this plugin. Claude Code's
own `--max-turns` and `--max-budget-usd` are per invocation and the plugin never
set them; opencode's per-agent `steps` counts opencode steps, and a tool Claude
runs itself never ends one; background subagents fanned out with no ceiling,
the running count (h #g231, h #g232) being information only. The plugin is the
one layer that sees every `result` across accounts, respawns and subagents, so
this adds three caps, **all off unless set**:

- **`maxBudgetUsd`** (with `budgetWarnAt`, default `[50, 80]`): a dollar cap on
  one opencode conversation, its subagents included. One `▌ **budget:**` note
  per threshold; once the cap is spent the next message ends **before anything
  is spawned or sent to Claude**, with one note and
  `{unified: "error", raw: "budget_exceeded"}`.
- **Agent `maxTurns` / `maxBudgetUsd`** (and `defaultSubagentMaxTurns`,
  `defaultSubagentMaxBudgetUsd`): passed to the agent's `claude` as
  `--max-turns` / `--max-budget-usd`.
- **`maxBackgroundSubagents`**: a background `task` or `task_batch` that would
  put more subagents to work than the cap allows is refused before it reaches
  opencode.

## What was measured (Claude Code 2.1.293, haiku, `claude -p --input-format stream-json`)

- **`total_cost_usd` is cumulative for the Claude session**, not per turn:
  three messages to one process reported $0.0331, $0.0400, $0.0470. A
  `--resume` restores it ($0.0309 resumed into $0.0359). So the ledger takes
  the delta per Claude session id; summing would count every earlier turn
  again. The interactive transport's synthesized result is per turn and is
  taken as is.
- **`--max-turns` counts API round trips per user message.** Capped at 3,
  three two-call messages in a row all succeeded on one process; capped at 1,
  a tool message ended `error_max_turns` (`terminal_reason: "max_turns"`) and
  the same process answered the next message normally. Safe on any agent.
  `--help` does not list it, so it is version-gated (2.1.280), not probed.
- **`--max-budget-usd` counts over the process's life and restarts on
  resume.** At $0.02 the second message ran, billed, overshot to $0.0250 and
  ended `error_max_budget_usd` (`terminal_reason: "budget_exhausted"`); the
  third and fourth were refused at once with no API call. A resume of a session
  already over $0.03 ran normally under a $0.03 cap. So it is honoured only on
  discovered `mode: subagent` agents (a dispatch has a process of its own) and
  refused with a WARN on a main agent. Both flags are print-only, so the
  interactive transport skips them and says so once.

## Decisions worth a reviewer's eye

- **A turn answering a parked proxy call is never stopped.** A foreground
  subagent's spend can cross the cap while its parent's CLI waits inside the
  `task` call; ending that turn would orphan the call (the model reports a
  denied tool). The stop lands on the next fresh message.
- **A child session never writes a budget note** (its text can become the
  parent's `task` result). A child stopped at the cap gets an `error` part with
  the same sentence instead, so the parent sees why. `doGenerate` gets the
  finish only; compaction is exempt and its spend still counts.
- **The background cap refuses when the count cannot be read** within 2 s,
  because a count that is too low is the harmful direction, and refuses a
  `task_batch` whole. Foreground is never asked about. Wired as an `admit`
  option on `createProxyMcpServer`, registered only with the cap set, so a
  default install's proxy server is unchanged.
- Both CLI caps are session-key elements, appended only when set and named
  (`maxTurns=4`), so a default install's key is byte-identical.

## `turnStats` (h #g109) is affected and deliberately not changed

The footer prints `total_cost_usd`, so on a reused headless process every
footer after the first shows the session's running total beside that turn's
own token counts. Recorded in AGENTS.md and h #g245 as a named follow-up
(print the turn's delta).

## Live

opencode 1.19.0, plugin from this worktree, scratch XDG dirs, a private
`serve`, `claude-haiku-4-5@appical`, `maxBudgetUsd: 0.01`: turn 1 answered and
ended on the cap note ("spent $0.0756 of its $0.0100 ... the next message will
not start a turn"); turn 2 came back `finish: error`, cost 0, carrying only the
stop note, with one spawn for the whole session. opencode's own `cost` for turn
1 was $0.0473: the CLI prices the 37,696 cache-write tokens at the 1-hour rate
and opencode at the 5-minute one. The ledger uses the CLI's figure.

## Not in this PR

`minQuotaRemainingPercent` (a gate on remaining account usage) needs the
account-usage store lane C is building. The ledger is in memory and starts
again on restart, which the docs and the doctor say. Whether a
`--fork-session` child's first total includes its parent's (`forkSessions` is
off by default) is unmeasured.

## Checks

- `npm run typecheck`: exit 0
- `npm test`: exit 0, 1681 tests, 1681 pass
- `npm run build`: exit 0
- `npm run generate:log-messages`: regenerated, drift test green

New tests: `test/budget-ledger.test.ts`, `test/budget.test.ts` (fake CLI
through a real `doStream`), plus additions to `cli-args`, `agent-models`,
`background-subagents`, `doctor` and the marker list in `turn-stats`. Docs: a
new `docs/configuration/budgets.md`, option rows in `options.md` and the skill,
`subagents.md`, `background-subagents.md`, `doctor.md`, AGENTS.md, and history
`g245`.

author: pegasusnotunicorn
body:
This covers the review's load-speed findings: PERF, plus the speed items from the HOME, CAST and TABLE reviews.

## Results
Measured on cold loads, before → after, with a stand-in for Netlify's compression and caching.

**Slow 3G phone:**

| Page | Downloaded | Headline visible | Layout shift |
|---|---|---|---|
| / | 1245 → 956 KB | 10.8 → 7.7 s | ~0 |
| /characters | 2517 → 1251 KB | 7.1 → 5.8 s | **0.99 → 0.001** |
| /digitalartbook | 639 → 396 KB | 5.5 → 4.2 s | 0.19 → 0.001 |
| 404 | 1326 → 250 KB | 5.5 → 4.6 s (largest image 24 → 4.6 s) | ~0 |
| a game room (above the footer) | 369 → 266 KB | 7.3 → 5.8 s | 0.146 → 0 |
| /terms | 330 → 240 KB | 5.4 → 4.2 s | ~0 |

**Desktop downloads:**

| Page | Before → after |
|---|---|
| Home | 3.5 MB → 1.2 MB |
| /characters | 2.5 → 1.2 MB |
| /play | 1.1 MB → 409 KB |
| A game room, before scrolling to the footer | 1.3 MB → 266 KB |

**Rulebook PDF: 17.9 MB → 2.4 MB** at the same `/rulebook.pdf` address. Its pictures are re-encoded at 150 dpi; I compared rendered pages and they read the same. The repo's rulebook is now the web version. The button now says "Rulebook PDF (2.4 MB)".

## What changed
- **Footer 3D cards:**
  - They start only when a quarter of them is on screen, after the page has loaded.
  - Phones get lighter 1000px atlases.
  - Data-saver and slow connections get the flat version.
  - Game rooms keep the site footer as before; its 3D cards just wait until it's scrolled to.
- **No more jumps:** the /characters 3D wall, the artbook mockups, the 404 picture and the game room's top strip all keep their place while they load.
- **Backgrounds:** the site-wide paper texture is 100 → 29 KB and looks the same. The home hero no longer preloads its faint doodle background ahead of real content.
- **Home page:**
  - The headline shows on a short timer instead of waiting for the 3D box to finish spinning.
  - The box's code loads in one go.
  - Swiping across the box no longer loads the YouTube player; only a tap does.
  - The carousel and card wall load when you get near them, with smaller art on phones.
  - The testimonial poster waits until it's scrolled to.
  - Without WebGL, three.js isn't downloaded at all, and there are no more console errors.
- **Right-sized pictures:** the character cards, expansion thumbnails, playtest photos, illustrations, /howtoplay pieces, polaroids (/contact, /thankyou), and the direction and episode card backs now come in smaller copies for where they're shown small. The bottom of the 3D box loads only when it's turned or opened.
- **How to play:** the YouTube video is now a click-to-play poster (no-cookie YouTube), the same as the home page's. It's one shared `VideoPoster`.
- **three.js is 28% smaller** (only the parts used are imported), and the 3D scenes start after the page first paints.
- **Fonts:** the title font is preloaded, there are fallbacks sized to match so there's less jump while loading, and the Rowdies files are 21 → 13 KB each.
- **Analytics** (GTM, MailerLite) load after the page, still only on the live site.
- **react-helmet** is replaced by a tiny hook, so share tags are no longer duplicated.
- **Game lobby:** rulebook pages are fetched only when you go for the Rules button.

## New shared pieces
- `useNearViewport`: the footer, card wall, carousel and polaroid ring.
- `later.ts`: `whenIdle`, `afterPaint`, `afterLoad` and `savingData`.
- `imageCopies.ts`: `srcSet` and `sized`, one list of every picture's smaller copies.
- `VideoPoster`
- `three.ts`

## Worth knowing
- **Slow-3G "largest image" times on two pages look worse, but the pages are faster:**
  - On the home page the metric now lands on the faint background, while the headline appears 3 s sooner.
  - On /howtoplay the poster picture now counts. The YouTube player it replaces didn't count, but it loaded far more.
- **334 new image files (about 6.5 MB)**, in folders named by width under `public/images`. The rulebook alone shrinks by 15.5 MB.
- **Not done:**
  - Splitting the game table's CSS from the lobby's (not a clean split).
  - Switching the remaining ~250 one-off font rules to the new variables. That's coming in the design-tokens PR.
- **package.json** still lists react-helmet. Nothing imports it any more; it will come out in the SEO and ops PR.

author: y0c0ms
body:
## Summary
Step 2 of the team join plan: a machine joins a team with the authenticator code, and renews silently for up to 7 days.

- **Server:** `POST /renew`. A member token renews while its enrolment is within 7 days of the code-confirmed enrolment. The window is stored with the machine, so a restart keeps it. A renewed token never outlives the window. Renewal needs a token for the same machine.
- **Member machine:** `sesync team join <name> --member <m>` prompts for the 6-digit code and saves the token owner-only (mode 600). `sesync team renew <name>` renews it. A credential file readable by others is refused, and errors never show the token.

## Depends on
PR #39 (step 1). This branch is stacked on it.

## Verification
- Team server: 118 tests pass, including the renewal window, renewal over HTTP, and join plus renew against a real server process (Postgres).
- Daemon: 216 tests pass, including the credential file rules.
- Locally against a live server: create, invite, join with the real code, renew. A wrong code is refused.
- `build-test.sh` passes; audit and cargo-deny pass.

## Not in this PR
Step 3, sync in `--watch`.

author: smarthinkerz
body:
## What
A TrustiqLegal pane inside Microsoft Word (desktop and Word on the web):

- **Clauses**: search the firm's clause bank and insert the English or Arabic wording at the cursor (Arabic paragraphs set right to left where Word supports it). Each insert counts a use.
- **Save selection as a clause**: select wording in the document and add it to the clause bank.
- **Save to case**: pick a case and upload the open document as a .docx (text extracted, OCR if needed, same as any upload).
- Signs in with an API key from Settings, API keys. Read-only keys can insert; read and write keys can also save. The key stays in Word on that computer.
- Bilingual: follows Word's display language (English or Arabic, RTL).

## How
- `/api/v1/clauses` now mounts the existing clause routes (same rules and roles as the app).
- `GET /addin/manifest.xml` serves the Office manifest built from `APP_URL`, with a Home tab button. `GET /addin/taskpane` serves the pane (`public/static/addin/`).
- Only `/addin/*` gets a policy that lets Office hosts frame it and load Office.js from Microsoft; the app still sends `frame-ancestors 'none'` and `X-Frame-Options`.
- `/developers` documents the add-in setup and the clause endpoints; Settings, API keys links to it.

## Testing
- New `test/word-addin.test.ts`: manifest, framing policy, clause API with read and write keys, filing a document to a case, no HTML injection in the pane.
- Full suite: 316 tests pass on Postgres and PGlite; typecheck and build pass.
- Browser check of the pane outside Word: connect with a key, clause list, case picker, no script errors besides the blocked Office.js.

## Not done
- Not yet tried inside a real Word install; the first sideload is the remaining check.
- No change to payments, webhooks, orders or subscriptions.

author: prakashuxtech
body:
IT-9a of inspector-timeline: the status pills under the stage, with the frame rate the screen actually shows while playing.

## What changed

- `FlareModel/FlareStatusRead.swift`: `FlareWorkspace.statusPills(measuredFPS:)` returns `StatusPills`. It holds the scene's aspect, reduced by GCD ("16:9", "11:8"), and its size: "1080p" for a 16:9 or 9:16 scene, named by its short side, otherwise "550 × 400". It also holds the document rate ("24 fps"). While playing, it adds the rate actually shown (the measure, capped at the document rate) and whether that rate is under the document rate (dropping, report-only). It adds "Text not shown (n)" when the stage leaves text out. The math is integer on clamped values, so a degenerate scene reads "–" and never traps.
- `FlareApp/PlaybackDriver.swift`: `measuredFPS` is the number of display-link targets over the last second. It stays nil until a full second has passed, and `stop()` clears it. Non-finite or earlier targets are ignored.
- `FlareApp/FlareTransport.swift`: the existing transport controls stay as they are. A `ViewerStatusBar` (SuiteUI) after them shows the pills: aspect, fps, "Showing N fps" (`.warning` when dropping) and the text warning. There is no capsule yet, since `TransportCapsule` waits on SuiteUI #340, and no look-alike control.
- `UITests/FlareJourneyTests+Playback.swift`: J10 `testPlayLoopAndStep` on `bounce`. While paused it checks the fps pill is there and the actual pill is not. It scrubs to 30 and plays: the frame moves and the actual pill appears. Space pauses and the frame holds. Two forward steps give (f+2) mod 48. With loop off, goToEnd → 47 and step back → 46; playing then stops at 47 and stays there. Shots are j10-0…4. The older `testPlayAndStep` is kept, because draw-key-save.wave.json references it.

## Why

This is packet inspector-timeline, IT-9 (the status-bar half): the stage tells the user the scene's format and whether playback keeps up.

## Proof

- `Tests/FlareModelTests/FlareStatusReadTests.swift` (8 tests):
  - HD reads 16:9 / 1080p / 24 fps; bounce reads 11:8 / 550 × 400; portrait reads 9:16 / 1080p.
  - 18 measured at 24 is dropping; 60 caps at 24 with no drop.
  - Paused, nil, NaN or inf shows no actual rate; showcase warns "Text not shown (1)"; degenerate sides never trap.
- `Tests/AppSnapshotTests/PlaybackDriverTests.swift`: 24 ticks per second measure 24, every other tick measures 12, and the measure is nil before a second or after stop. NaN and earlier targets are ignored.
- Snapshots changed: flare-status-playing.png, flare-status-dropping.png, flare-status-text.png, flare-transport-paused.png, flare-transport-playing.png. The two transport PNGs change because the row now ends in the status bar.

## Notes for the lead

- The packet says bounce reads "16:9, 1080p", but the bounce fixture is 550 × 400. The tests use a 1920 × 1080 document for 16:9 / 1080p, and bounce reads 11:8 / "550 × 400".
- The stage's existing `ViewerStatusBar` lives in `FlareStage.swift`, which is outside this task's files. So the new bar in `FlareTransport` repeats the zoom pill, and reads "–" while the stage fits (zoom nil). A follow-up should fold the pills into the stage's bar.
- `measuredFPS` counts display-link ticks, so `statusPills` caps it at the document rate. A 60 Hz link still shows each of the 24 frames once.

Unverified API: none new beyond what the target already uses (`ViewerStatusBar`, `.statusPill`, `.help`, `.accessibilityIdentifier`, `XCUIElement.typeKey`, checked in apple-docs). The SwiftUI side is compiled only by the macOS build.

Refs #1515

author: sparkysolutions10-pixel
body:
### Summary of Changes

This PR resolves several key GraphQL API capabilities and hardening requirements across pair resolution, network scoping, query security, and AMM pool inspection:

1. **Pair Matcher Issuer Preservation (#357)**:
   - Updated `findPair` in `src/api/rest.ts` and `src/api/graphql.ts` to match both asset code and issuer when qualified assets are passed.
   - Canonicalizes `native` asset representation to `XLM` while preserving bare asset code lookup fallback.
   - Prevents cross-issuer misidentification for identically-named assets on the same or different networks.

2. **Network Selection in GraphQL (#359)**:
   - Added optional `network` argument on `getPrice`, `getBestRoute`, `getPriceHistory`, `listPairs`, `pairs`, and `pools`.
   - Respects the `x-network` HTTP header when the argument is omitted.
   - Validates requested network against enabled networks and throws structured `INVALID_INPUT` error if invalid.

3. **Maximum Query Depth Ceiling (#360)**:
   - Implemented AST-level query depth validation rule with configurable `GRAPHQL_MAX_DEPTH` (default: 6).
   - Rejects excessively nested queries before execution to guard against resource exhaustion / DoS attacks.
   - Exempts introspection queries (`__schema` / `__type`) from depth ceiling.

4. **Structured `pairs(network: String)` Query (#365)**:
   - Added `pairs(network: String): [PairInfo!]!` returning structured asset info (`code`, `issuer`), network, and timestamp metadata aligned with REST `/pairs`.
   - Kept legacy `listPairs: [String]!` functional for backward compatibility.

5. **`pools(pair: String, network: String)` Query (#366)**:
   - Added `pools(pair: String, network: String): [PoolInfo!]!` query returning AMM pool reserves, spot prices, and 64-character pool IDs.
   - Integrated shared `queryPools` utility with REST `/pools` endpoint to ensure consistent results.

### Testing & Verification
- Added comprehensive test suite `src/__tests__/graphqlSecurityAndPools.test.ts` covering all 5 features.
- All 52 tests across GraphQL and pair test suites passing cleanly with Vitest.
- Verified TypeScript compilation (`tsc --noEmit`) with zero errors.

Closes #357, Closes #359, Closes #360, Closes #365, Closes #366

body:
## Context
After the FalkorDB volume change the live graph key didn't exist yet. GRAPH.RO_QUERY on a missing key errors with `ERR Invalid graph operation on empty key`, so `seedIfEmpty` failed on boot ("startup seed skipped"), the health check reported FalkorDB down, and every route's probe would 503. The same would hit every new org graph.

## Description
`roQuery` treats the empty-key error as an empty result: a missing graph is an empty graph. One fix in the shared read helper covers the probe, nodeCount, seedIfEmpty and all reads.

## Changes in the codebase
- lib/graph/client.ts: roQuery catches the empty-key error and returns [].
- lib/graph/empty-graph.test.ts: missing graph → [] and nodeCount 0.

## Changes outside the codebase
None. After deploy the web boot seeds the demo graph again.

## How to test
`redis-cli GRAPH.RO_QUERY nokey RETURN 1` errors; the new test shows roQuery returns [] for it.

## Additional information
Found while verifying the live deploy of #110/#115.

Closes #92

## Устойчивые reading routes и list sessions

Эпик опирается на уже вошедшие в `main` исправления интерактивной back-навигации #775 и сохранения выбранной ленты/папки #779. Reader использует native Back, Safari сохраняет общий progress/cancel/commit contract, а временно скрытая фильтром строка Sidebar не меняет выбранную область. Эти задачи закрываются вместе с эпиком, но не представлены как новые изменения текущего diff.

В коммитах `3e22218` и `d6af47c` закреплены устойчивость поиска и фактического viewport при возврате из Reader: query reload не демонтирует search UI, а выбранная статья больше не подменяет scroll anchor. `4c7ee9e` согласовал native back swipe с активным поиском, сохранением запроса для выбранной области и скрытием клавиатуры при прокрутке.

После этого `aa35869` реализовал выбранную в #830 политику минимальной прокрутки вслед за previous/next в Reader. Уже видимая строка сохраняет положение; скрытая появляется у соответствующего края списка до возврата. Накопленные страницы, retained rows и cursor сохраняются, программная прокрутка не запускает загрузку до отсутствующей цели и не создаёт второго позиционирования после Back.

## Согласованные refresh, retention и даты статей

В `183aef2` хранение переведено на absence-based semantics: срок начинается после исчезновения статьи из успешного snapshot, возвращённые и избранные статьи защищены от автоматической очистки. `c9f146f` закрепил семантику дат RSS, Atom и Dublin Core, а `96656a0` провёл единый приоритет `publishedAt ?? updatedAtSource ?? fetchedAt` через persisted `querySortDate`, список и Reader. Updated-only Atom больше не выглядит заново опубликованным после refresh.

Коммиты `96d5418`, `e4748ab` и `6813074` объединили initial и subsequent refresh через app-level reconciliation, cleanup, badge и reload boundary. Для каждого зафиксированного target существует terminal outcome; повторяются только неуспешные ленты. Sidebar и Articles Screen используют один selection/filter context и не публикуют stale completion в новую область. В `ba25369` пользовательское описание настройки хранения приведено к этой семантике.

## Предсказуемая загрузка изображений

В `16bc962` visible image completion отделён от необязательной disk-cache maintenance, а cancellation и stale completion перестали удерживать актуальную загрузку. `84b3ac0` добавил bounded adjacent prefetch с общими loader/cache budgets и подготовкой следующей materialized page; `e4727e7` устранил ложные cache misses после округления thumbnail и замену большей версии поздним меньшим результатом.

В `6e79f2a` rolling window стал обновляться сразу при переходах между статьями. Его lifecycle принадлежит фактическому reading route, поэтому запоздалое исчезновение старого Reader не отменяет новую работу. `1790e7b` убрал полупрозрачную поверхность при переходе к предыдущей статье: content surfaces получили непрозрачный фон и согласованный направленный переход.

## Семантический Reader вместо потери структуры HTML

Коммиты `889d2ab`, `169eb46`, `e716268`, `98c18e2`, `4718ea3` и `5788527` восстановили безопасное отображение malformed inline HTML, таблиц, вложенных structural containers, definitions, disclosures, asides, расширенной inline-семантики и figure/media. Содержимое сохраняет порядок, подписи и metadata ссылок; неподдерживаемые элементы получают читаемый fallback без WebView и сетевой классификации.

В `d14476a` и `3d89d89` таблицы получили адаптивный выбор cards/grid и ширину столбцов по содержимому. `e9ce674` убрал дублирующего автора из header, `2218e2f` добавил раскрытие распознанных accordion-блоков, `bd910a5` согласовал `mark` с текущей темой, а `ef3e45d` исключил служебные HTML-комментарии из текста и media plan. `870918b` закрепил сохранение буквальных `(c)`, `(C)` и `C(c)`.

Коммит `6e26c4a` сохранил исходные строки и отступы многострочного кода с горизонтальной прокруткой, добавил перенос однострочного кода без изменения копируемого текста и исключил source swipe, начинающийся внутри code block.

## Единая обратная связь списка, Sidebar и настроек

В `79323bd` persisted read/starred snapshot стал синхронно согласовывать Reader, строку и счётчики list session. `c3c441d` объединил анимации изменений текущего snapshot, а `a176458` сохранил согласованный список во время поискового debounce и применяет готовые результаты атомарно, без промежуточного спиннера.

Коммиты `7927b5a` и `b98ce16` согласовали outline/filled state symbols и прозрачные icon-only swipe actions с локализованными accessibility labels. `a0bdbfe` сохранил пользовательское раскрытие папок по устойчивому `Folder.id`, `eb51dde` выровнял форму context-menu preview, `4e0e1ee` перевёл взаимоисключающие настройки на системный `Picker`, а `2fb0906` заменил sidebar-specific empty copy на приглашение добавить первую ленту.

В `88f7b96` и `14b680f` Sidebar и Articles Screen получили общую native collapsing navigation bar. Refresh indicator размещён в native bar, освобождает место в idle и сопровождает refresh/post-refresh query согласованным статусом. Заголовки, search и Back сохраняют системный lifecycle; визуальное acceptance для #843 ограничено согласованными ширинами от 375 pt, отдельная проверка 320 pt остаётся за пределами этой задачи.

## Подписка на Reddit и завершение локализации

В `d25fac5` адрес subreddit преобразуется в прямую Atom-ссылку, ошибки 403/429 получают отдельные сообщения, а initial refresh может использовать свежий validated preview snapshot через обычный refresh lifecycle без немедленного повторного HTTP-запроса. Диагностика сохраняет технический контекст без чувствительного содержимого.

Коммит `6d4410f` завершил локализацию оставшихся действий, состояний и ошибок: user-facing сообщения отделены от технической диагностики, переводы и VoiceOver descriptions согласованы для поддерживаемых языков.

## Публичная документация и локальные рабочие contracts

В `6e79f2a` публичный `README.md` сокращён до описания приложения, а рабочие документы включены в Xcode navigator. Задачи #796–#801 выполнены в локальных git-ignored `AGENTS.md` и `AgentDocs/`: уточнены routing, Git/GitHub lifecycle, безопасный cleanup после squash merge, capability-based validation, localization matrix и data lifecycle boundaries. Аудит дат выделен в non-routed research artifact. Эти локальные contracts присутствуют в filesystem и navigator, но не входят в публикуемый Git diff.

## Итог

Эпик сформировал согласованный behavioral baseline для списка, Reader, Sidebar и refresh/retention lifecycle: пользовательский контекст сохраняется при переходах и асинхронных обновлениях, загрузка изображений ограничена и переиспользуется, HTML остаётся читаемым и структурированным, а системные взаимодействия и локализованная обратная связь следуют общим boundaries. Это основа для следующей архитектурной работы без переноса перечисленных регрессий.

author: jtr860830
body:
`tklab create class --init-cluster VALUE` (class file `init_cluster`) replaces the boolean `--k8s`: the instructor says which cluster every student's VM gets, and can override it per student. tklab passes the value through to tkctl and keeps no list of presets of its own.

## The value

| value | in the VM |
|---|---|
| `default` | `tkctl create cluster tk8s` (what `--k8s` did) |
| a tk8s preset name (`ha`, `lab`, ...) | `tkctl create cluster tk8s --preset <name>` |
| a path ending in `.yaml`/`.yml` | the file is written to `/var/lib/tklab/cluster.yaml` through the guest agent, then `tkctl create cluster -f` |

A preset tkctl does not know is rejected inside the VM and lands in the roster's error column, as before. A cluster.yaml is checked before any VM is cloned: it exists, is at most 60 KiB (the agent file-write limit) and has `name:` directly under `metadata:`; tklab reads that name with a small line parser (no YAML dependency) to run `tkctl use` and `verify`. Class-level `init_cluster` is the default for every student; `[[students_override]]` can set a different one.

## What changed

- `classdef`: `Student.init_cluster` (parsed value or the file's absolute path), `ClassDef.wants_cluster`; `k8s = true` is refused with the new spelling in the message.
- `pve`: `agent_file_write` (`POST .../agent/file-write`).
- `provision`: `k8s_command` builds the in-VM command per student; the agent writes the file 0666, so the root part runs `chmod 0644` before `runuser`. VM tags are `k8s-<value>` / `k8s-file`; a bare `k8s` tag from an existing class still reads as `default`. `describe -o toml` writes `init_cluster` per student, with the placeholder `"cluster.yaml"` and a comment for a file-sourced one.
- Reruns after a `k8s:` roster error rewrite the tag with the current value and prepend `tkctl delete cluster <name> --yes` (tkctl would otherwise resume the old topology). A rerun first checks that the previous attempt is not still running in the VM (a timed-out build keeps going) and only reports that if it is; dropping `init_cluster` for a student on a rerun clears the error and keeps the roster's secrets, which also survive unexpected exceptions now.
- `cli`: `--init-cluster` joins the flags that exclude `-f`; `--k8s` on `create class` is gone (`create template --k8s` is unchanged).
- README rewritten for the three forms; preset values need a template on tk8s v2026.10.12 or newer.

## Verified on the lab

- `uv run pytest -q`: 244 passed; ruff clean.
- `--init-cluster ha` for one student on pve-node7: `create class` to `tk8s cluster ready` in 5 m 20 s (clone and boot included), 5.5 GB used after `tkctl verify` (PASS 17) in the 8-core / 24 GB VM; tag `k8s-ha`, `describe -o toml` round-trips.
- Class file with one `default` student and one override to a cluster.yaml: the file arrived as root 0644, the first attempt failed on purpose (2 control planes, which tkctl refuses), the rerun redid only that student, started with the delete, built `demo` 1+1 (PASS 15), and `describe -o toml` printed the placeholder with its comment.
- Fresh-context review (Opus) and a cold Codex adversarial review; every Important finding fixed with a test that failed first.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: vlastikyoutubeko
body:
**Offline mode:** when app.odjezdy.online (or Transitous) is unreachable, the board keeps showing the timetable it last knew instead of „Nelze načíst odjezdy“. This also works after a reboot without network.
- The last good board (up to 80 departures + alerts) is written to `/var/lib/odjezdy/board-cache.json` (at most every 2 min). It is loaded at start and when switching stops, and is valid for 12 h. Past departures drop off as usual.
- The status line says **BEZ SPOJENÍ · poslední data HH:MM**. The BUSE footer now uses the shared `statusText()`, which also fixes its missing Transitous credit, and turns red when offline.

**/api/v2:** one `GET /api/v2/departures?stopIds=a,b,…` replaces up to 8 parallel `/api/board/:id` calls. The server merges and dedupes the rows, and its alerts are added to the stop notices.
- Detected via `/api/v2/health`, re-checked hourly.
- A server without v2 (404/400) falls back to `/api/board/:id`.

Tested by rendering to PNG:
- v2 against production: Florenc, 120 departures in one request.
- Fallback with a proxy that returns 404 for v2: 1 v2 attempt, then 8 `/api/board` calls, 160 departures.
- Offline with the API pointed at a dead port: 80 cached departures with the notice, in BUSE and DB.

Not tested in a VM. No app/VERSION bump, so merging does not publish a release.

author: adamtaylor152
body:
## Description

The `_frameleaf._tcp` DNS-SD record carried `id`, `name`, `setup`, `linked` and `cloud`, but no scheme. The native apps assume `https` when `scheme` is missing, so a server found on Wi-Fi could not be reached (the server only listens on plain HTTP).

The TXT record now also carries `scheme`:

- `http` by default: the server never terminates TLS itself.
- `https` only when `FRAMELEAF_LOCAL_URL` names the advertised LAN address with `https://` (something in front of the server terminates TLS there). This uses the same `localAddressFor` helper that already picks the advertised SRV port (FL-218), so scheme and port always agree.

The port stays in the SRV record only (DNS-SD convention; no existing TXT key carries it). The `lanDiscovery` setting still gates publishing, the refresh comparison now includes `scheme`, and nothing about users or content is added. The settings doc table lists the new key.

Jira: https://heroit.atlassian.net/browse/FL-435

Jira Smart Commit evidence: pending (commit subject carries FL-435).

## How Has This Been Tested?

Per the owner's no-local-builds rule (2026-10-17), nothing was run locally; remote CI verifies.

- [x] Updated `lan-discovery.service.spec.ts` publish expectation to include `scheme: 'http'`
- [x] New test: `https` `FRAMELEAF_LOCAL_URL` on the LAN address advertises `scheme: 'https'` with its port; no `port` TXT key
- [x] New test: `FRAMELEAF_LOCAL_URL` naming a different host keeps `http` and the bind port

- [x] I have no unrelated changes in the PR.
- [x] I have written tests for new code (if applicable)

Written by an AI coding agent, reviewed against the existing LAN discovery and FL-218 port logic.

author: simontang6868
body:
> **⚠️ 口径更正（后续 commit 已修）**
>
> 本 PR 初版把 `positive_ratio` 说成「参与率」，**这是错的**。
> `positive_ratio` 的语义是**盈利窗口占比**（`return > 0` 的窗口 / 有有效指标的窗口）——
> 见 `parameter_selection.py::summarize_v2` 的 `pos_count = sum(1 for v in returns if v > 0)`。
> 真正的**交易参与率**要按窗口级 `trade_count > 0` 计数，由
> `design_audit.summarize_participation` 计算，**summary JSON 里没有这个字段**。
>
> 已修：`scripts/expansion_report.py` 的表头与键名、`docs/EXPANSION_2026-10-17.md` 第 6 节。
> 数值不变，变的是名称与推论强度 —— 盈利窗口占比高 ≠ 能赚到（本 PR 里 ma 就是占比上去了、中位数更负）。
> 48 只数据的真实参与率本轮**拿不到**，已在文档里写明缺失，没有用别的指标冒充。

叠在 #19 之上（`research.py` / 契约测试同文件改动，先合 #19 再看本 PR 的 diff 才是干净的）。

## 为什么做

`docs/EXTERNAL_VALIDITY_2026-10-17.md` 的结论是：6 只手挑标的支撑不了任何总体结论——
22 只外推样本里 15 只为 0、7 只为负、0 只为正，且「价格→参与率」r=-0.772 全靠茅台单点。
本轮把样本换成**可复现的指数成分抽样**，让「样本太小」这个替代解释彻底失效。

## 做了什么

| 文件 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `data/step75/build_universe.py`（新） | 中证指数官网取沪深300 成分（备源新浪）；代码升序**等距抽样**，无随机种子；meta 落盘**幸存者偏差**与**抽样偏差**声明 |
| `data/step75/universe/csi300_50.json`（新） | 50/298 只的可复现股票池定义（含来源、抽样规则、偏差声明） |
| `data/step75/research.py` | 新增 `DEEPQUANT_UNIVERSE` 支持外部池；输出 JSON 新增 `universe` 字段，偏差随结果落盘 |
| `scripts/expansion_report.py`（新） | 只汇总事实：闸门可用率 / 零中位数率 / 分位数 / 原口径 vs 扩样 / 费率极差。显式不排序、不择优、不下总体结论 |
| `backend/tests/test_research_script_contract.py` | +7 条：等距抽样确定性、覆盖首尾、池子过小全取、腾讯前缀、`DEEPQUANT_UNIVERSE` 存在、输出含 `universe`、偏差声明必须在 meta |

**实现细节**：`select_evenly` 步长用 `(N-1)/(n-1)` 而非 `N/n` —— 后者取到索引 0,k,2k,...
末端够不到最大代码（300 取 50 时末位只到索引 294，最后 5 只永远进不了样本）。

## 实测结果（2017-01-01 ~ 2024-12-31，`min_trades=2`，IS150/OOS50，qfq）

### 1. 闸门可用率 96%（48/50）

拦下 **泸州老窖 000568 / 山西汾酒 600809**（均 `invalid_price`）。核实后确认不是误杀：
泸州老窖 2017-01-16 `low=-0.01`；更严重的是**分段量级不一致** —— 2017-01-03 `close=1.20`，
全表中位 `close=120.27`，次日 `close=2.35`（+95.8%）。
**缺失不是随机的**：可用样本系统性偏掉高分红/高送转标的。

### 2. 零中位数扩样后依然存在

| 策略 | n | 正 | 负 | 零 | 零占比 | 收益中位数 | 盈利窗口占比(中位) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ma_cross` | 48 | 4 | 28 | 16 | **33.3%** | −0.58% | 35.7% |
| `mean_reversion` | 48 | 29 | 5 | 14 | **29.2%** | +0.35% | 51.4% |

6 只池是 60% / 40% 零。**扩到 48 只，零占比降了但没消失** → 是事件稀疏的结构性后果。
`ma_cross` 48 只里只有 4 只（8.3%）中位数为正。

### 3. 手挑池的系统性高估

| 策略 | 6 只池 | 48 只池 | 变化 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ma_cross` | +0.00% | **−0.58%** | 符号翻转 |
| `mean_reversion` | +2.21% | **+0.35%** | **约 1/6** |

### 4. 已排除的混杂

- 窗口数不齐：≥30 窗口的 39 只 ma 中位 −0.49%，全样本 −0.58% → 新股不是替代解释。
- 费率：跨三档极差仅 0.36~0.39pp，小于策略间差异 0.93pp → 不是主因。

## 这些数字不能用来做什么（硬边界）

1. **R12**：全部是窗口收益中位数，不是账户连续收益。
2. **R11**：盈利窗口占比是**方向性**指标、事件密度是**数量**指标，两者都不是可交易性证据，
   都不得用于择优（ma 就是占比上去了、中位数反而更负）。
3. **幸存者偏差**：池子是抓取当日成分股，缺退市样本 → 收益偏乐观。反过来说：
   `ma_cross` 在偏乐观的池里仍为负，这个负结论是稳的；`mr` 的 +0.35% 不可信其上限。
4. 高分红标的缺失（见上）。

## 附带发现（**未改动**，按纪律先提案）

`checks_extended.py::_check_price_jumps` 的 `count` 是**行数**而不是超阈值行数
（泸州老窖报 1942，真实 41）。原因：`price_df = df_sorted[["close"]]` 是单列 DataFrame，
广播比较后 `len(jumps)` 等于行数。`is_valid` 只看 ERROR，**拦截判定不受影响**，
只影响落盘 JSON 里的 WARNING 计数。共享校验模块，未擅自改。

## 测试

- 后端全量：**852 passed, 1 skipped**（845 + 7 条新增）
- 未改动 `requirements.txt`、`engine.py`、风险阈值；未 merge 任何 PR

body:
## Summary

Split out of #5663 at review. An update that changes an `AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer`'s `Subnets` (or `SubnetMappings`) and keeps the balancer used to leave it on its old subnets. It went on listing subnets the template had dropped or replaced, which the update cleanup then deleted. `ElbV2CfnProvisioner` now moves a kept balancer onto the template's subnets in place, as `SetSubnets` does, and a rolled-back update moves it back.

### How

- On an update that reuses the balancer, `moveToTemplateSubnets` calls `SetSubnets` when the template's subnets differ (order does not matter), and keeps the prior list in a hidden `CfnRollback` marker attribute.
- `rollbackUpdate` moves the balancer back to that list. A failed move back propagates, so the stack reports that error rather than an unimplemented rollback, and the list stays for a `ContinueUpdateRollback` retry. A committed or cleared update drops it.
- `SubnetMappings` gives the subnets when `Subnets` is absent, with intrinsics resolved and blank ids skipped.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (`fix:`)
- [ ] New feature (`feat:`)
- [ ] Breaking change (`feat!:` or `fix!:`)
- [ ] Docs / chore

## AWS Compatibility

`Subnets` and `SubnetMappings` on `AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer` are updatable without replacement ([resource reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-elasticloadbalancingv2-loadbalancer.html)), so CloudFormation moves the balancer rather than leaving it where it was. Moving it keeps the subnets only: Floci's `SetSubnets` does not carry a mapping's `AllocationId` or private addresses.

### Tests

`ElbV2CfnProvisionerTest`:
- an update moves a kept balancer onto the template's subnets and a rollback moves it back;
- the same subnets in another order leave it alone;
- a committed update and a cleared update forget the prior subnets, and a later update that leaves the subnets alone drops a stale list;
- a failed move back propagates and keeps the prior subnets for another try;
- a create that finds the name taken leaves that balancer on its subnets;
- `SubnetMappings` gives the subnets when `Subnets` is absent.

Red first: with the tests and the marker constant only, 4 of the 44 `ElbV2CfnProvisionerTest` cases fail on main: the move and move back, a committed update, a failed move back and `SubnetMappings` (`red-C.log`).

## Test results

At `2a74dfcdf` on main `534571b2a`:
- full suite in CI's four shards: 40,266 tests, 2 failures and 1 error, all host-specific ones that also fail on `main` on this machine (Docker loop mounts for `Ec2VolumeBlockDeviceDockerIntegrationTest`, and an x86-only SQL Server image for one `RdsAwsIntegrationTest` case);
- `checkstyle:check`, `make docs-check` and `make partition-check`: pass;
- the commit still applies cleanly to main `a611e9ea6`.

## Checklist

- [x] `./mvnw test` passes locally (see Test results)
- [x] New or updated integration test added
- [x] Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I have no more than 2 open, non-draft pull requests and no more than 4 open pull requests in total (drafts included) in this repository (maintainers and dependency bots are exempt).

## Summary

From walkthrough audit 6. Four places where pasting the guide's commands, in order, still failed or left you stuck:

- **Step 10 had no v2 code.** It now writes `$WORK/hello/v2/worker.js` with a heredoc, the same way step 6 writes v1. It ends with `curl -sS "https://$NAME/"`, which answers `hello from takoserver v2`.
- **The seed variant never stopped the Host,** so the seed command refused ("cannot prove that no Host is running"). It now stops the Host first, seeds in the shell of step 6 with the Host's environment loaded, and then says to start the Host again.
- **The cold snapshot left out `/etc/takoserver`.** That directory holds the cursor key, without which the Host refuses to start, and the v2 config, whose grants are the only way a restored Host serves seeded artifacts.
  - There is now a pasteable block for this guide's layout: `systemctl stop`, `is-active`, `SNAP=/var/backups/takoserver/<UTC>` with mode 0700, then `cp -a` of the data and of etc.
  - The socket sentence no longer contradicts the runtime-only paths list: `/tmp/tw-*` and `$TMPDIR/tactor-*` are not copied, and the root's own `s/` may stay.
- **Step 7 said only "read the startup diagnostics" when the Worker Forms are unsupported,** but the Host logs no reason for most causes. It now gives a block that shows the usual causes:
  - the env vars that must be set;
  - `workerd --version`, where a glibc error means the OS is too old;
  - both `targetKey` values, which must be `selfhost-v2-worker-primary`;
  - the runtime boot keys, which must be `["actor","workflow"]`;
  - the plane keys;
  - a journalctl grep.
  If only WorkerEndpoint is unsupported, it points at step 4's Endpoint settings.

Also:

- **Coming back later** sets `NAME` from the Endpoint's output (`jq -er`), and says seeding needs the Host's environment in that shell.
- **The Docker rollback** writes `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` and `TAKOSERVER_DOCKER_IMAGE` into `.env`. Before, a later `docker compose` command without `-p` acted on the original project, or started the newer image, whose migrations undo the rollback.
- **The site's "Keep it running" backup sentence** names `/etc/takoserver` (EN and JA).

- The 7 test files that read the guides (`landing`, `selfhost-startup-instructions`, `selfhost-v2-ordinary-journey-native`, `v1-installation-upgrade-boundary`, `console-settings`, `console-resource-detail-v2`, `console-resource-mutations`): 112 tests, 0 fail.

Local full gate on one combined candidate holding #449, #450, #451 and #452. Settings: `bun run check`, Bun 1.4.0, `env -i`, private `TMPDIR`, under the shared heavy-work lock, nice 19 on 2 CPUs.

_Requested by **Boss** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Fdi97YyvNbutkphdtRfLg6?thread=cmsg_01Fdi97YyvNbutkphdtRfLg69UZbx2P3CXZDfz4Qiy7NQJ)_

Before: v2.2. Every rise of 10 m or more counted as a climb. Long climbs were split into pieces of at least 1.5 km. Difficulty was shown as words (Easy to Crux). The pace jumped at each gradient band edge. Key zones were listed in both Your route and Your plan. There was one Export A4 button in the top bar.

After: batches 1 and 2 of the v2.2 design review.

**Batch 1 (v2.3, restore branch `restore/v2.2-before-review-batch1`)**
- Brand line "Prep & go" and new intro texts.
- New engine KPIs, and the Your runs block is removed.
- Start time tile, and jump links without boxes.
- Grid tables with mini profiles.
- Best / Balanced / Cautious, with the edelweiss next to the switch.
- Section % on top of the section box, and D+ done under the clock.
- Keep all / Keep none for watch messages.

**Batch 2 (v2.4, restore branch `restore/v2.3-before-review-batch2`)**
- **Climbs and bumps.** A climb gains at least 10% of the race's D+ or 100 m. Smaller rises are bumps (b1, b2...). Bumps are not counted, but they keep their tactic, script cue and watch message.
- **Section split.** Long climbs (3 km or more) split only where the gradient changes by at least 2 points. Each section is at least 15% of the climb.
- **Smoother pace.** Pace is interpolated between band centres.
- **Stars.** Difficulty shows as 1 to 4 coloured stars everywhere. Key zones say "up to X min to gain".
- **Tables.** Columns are #, start km, mini profile with the average % on it, length, gain, steepest 100 m, then stars. Section sparklines are thinner.
- **Your route.** Map and profile fit on one screen. Climb number badges open a pop-up with the climb's figures. Zooming the profile zooms the map and dims the rest of the route. The key zones block is gone.
- **Your plan.** Key zones are star chips. A chip opens the zone's card, shades the zone on the profile and zooms the map on it.
- **Cockpit (all 3 modes).** The profile is on top and 50% taller, with the section bar under it. The race % sits on the km line. The race script is compact, and clicking a moment zooms the map on it.
- **Export A4.** One export per section (Your plan, Your race, Prep my run, Rewind my run, Deep dive), with tick boxes to leave parts out. There is a new race-script part, and the top-bar button is removed.
- **Engine.** The pace values line up in three columns.

How: the climb/bump rule is in `briefCourse`. `splitClimb` uses dynamic programming over 1..k sections and stops adding sections when the gain is under 10% of the one-piece cost or neighbouring sections are too similar. `paceAt` in model.js does the pace interpolation. The map controller has a new `focus(a, b)` method. Print sections carry `data-part`, and `p4Filter` keeps only the ticked parts. All 85 tests pass, including new tests for the split and climb rules. Checked in headless Chromium at 1440×900, 1366×768 and 390×844: the cockpit fits one screen, and the map top plus at least 3 script moments fit one screen.

- `README.md`: what the repo is (website, registry, versioned docs), stack, local commands, planned layout, security stance, independence notice, license.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: ways to contribute, branch model, checks, PR rules, and the widget submission guide (the seven steps from PLAN.md section 9, with manual equivalents for the planned `ow` commands), trust tiers and submission security rules.
- `SECURITY.md`: private reporting, scope, out-of-scope items, and the honest limits (code widgets are not sandboxed; tiers describe review, not isolation).
- `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`: the sibling code repository's version, with URLs pointed at this repository.
- `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/widget_listing.md`: ownership of registry and CI paths, a general PR checklist, and a checklist for listing PRs.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*`: blank issues off, a link to private advisories, bug and feature forms, and a form for authors stuck on submission.
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: bun and GitHub Actions updates into `develop`, weekly, minor and patch grouped.

## Why

Registry PRs come from people we do not know, so the rules for listings, trust tiers and security reporting need to be written down before the first one arrives. The contributor docs also need to match the branch model used in the code repository.

No code, package file, workflow or build config is changed. The planned `bun` scripts and the `ow` commands are marked as planned wherever they appear.

author: modelmirror-agent
body:
## What & why

When the Court reassigned docket number 26-221 to a different petition, an arrival cell's forecast was scored against that other petition. The event has already been voided. This PR adds the detection that the 2026-10-14 void entry committed to, so that this can't happen again silently.

### What changes in outcome resolution
**New rule (`src/fedcourtsai/pipeline/redocket.py`).** A moment counts as opened under a different petition when either of these holds:
- **Petitioner side:** its caption shares no party word with the row's current caption on the petitioner side.
- **Respondent side:** the respondent side is disjoint *and* the moment opened before the row's current docketed date. This arm applies to non-interim moments only, because an application's submission date routinely comes before docketing.

How words are compared:
- Role words are dropped, accents are folded, and apostrophes are removed.
- A prefix or abbreviation match only counts when the shorter word has 4 or more letters. So `Dep't` matches `Department`, but `Lee` does not match `Leeds`.
- A side with no party words on either caption, such as `In re` or a bare docket number, is not compared.

**What the rule reads.** It reads the caption from both the corpus event and the committed `event.yaml`. The committed file keeps the caption the prediction was made under, even after the corpus title has re-tracked. A malformed `event.yaml` simply doesn't count as a witness, so it can't break the poll.

**Where it applies.** `pipeline/outcome.py` `detect_resolution` refuses such a moment with a fixed reason. This covers every refresh channel (the live poll and the pull) and both convergence passes, for SCOTUS only.
- The moment goes to the unrecorded queue.
- Sibling moments on the same case still resolve.
- The lost-outcomes pass marks it `resolved_without_outcome=redocketed`, a new reason in `NO_OUTCOME_REASONS`.

**Docs and the census script**
- New corpus-check script: `scripts/checks/redocketed_numbers.py`.
- Updated: `docs/data-pipeline.md`, `docs/cli.md`, `docs/pipeline.md`, and the void reading rules in `metrics/README.md` and `docs/process-version.md`. Those two previously described the detector as future work.
- New dated `docs/freeze-record.md` entry, framed as an **attribution and membership** change that moves no digest.

**What this serves:** scored outcomes and every figure built on them. A forecast is never again graded against a different petition.

### Census (read-only, prod corpus)
**Vintage**
- Blob `5d4bac58…`, which is `main` `3a77cf324`'s pointer.
- Latest pull 2026-10-17; newest stored snapshot read 2026-10-17.
- Ledger: `main`'s `data/`.

**1. What the rule refuses today**
- Corpus side: 591,662 titled events, of which 33,611 are on captioned rows. 153 of those carry a different caption string, 1 differs in party words, and **1 is refused**.
- Ledger side: of 14,294 `event.yaml`, 12,438 carry a different caption string, 2 differ in party words, and **1 is refused**.
- The refused event is in both cases `scotus/9026000221` `evt-petition-arrival-disposition`, which is already voided.
- **No false positives** among those roughly 12.4k committed captions that no longer match the current one.

**2. Live 25-/26- rows (5,386 of 7,474 have two or more snapshots to compare)**
- 7 numbers were re-docketed: 26-221, 26-246, 26-5334, 26-5502, 26-5569, 26A266 and 26A286. Only 26-221 has any ledger events.
- 4 rows changed only their docketed date, with the same parties: 26-263, 26-354, 26-5442 and 26A290. None has ledger events. These read as date corrections and are not refused, which supersedes the 2026-10-14 entry's date-only definition.

**3. All 306 predicted SCOTUS cases, every consecutive snapshot pair**
- Only 26-221 changes parties.
- **No other affected event, and no further void owed.**

To re-run it, put this in the PR body for the corpus-check lane once the PR is ready (the lane only answers ready, non-draft PRs):
```corpus-check
uv run python scripts/checks/redocketed_numbers.py
```
Until it runs there, these figures are this session's local reading, not lane-verified.

### Limits (all stated in the freeze entry)
- **Permanent:** a refusal leaves the moment with no outcome; nothing relocates it.
- **Who it hits:** refusals lean toward arrival-stage, IFP and application moments, so a forward arrival-stage figure should quote its `redocketed` count beside its n. That lean is reasoned from how re-docketing works, not measured.
- **Missed cases:**
  - an interim re-docketing that keeps the petitioner's words (census: 0 today);
  - shared first names;
  - corporate renames, which refuse by design and would land in triage.
- **Mints that re-fire:** the CVSG and interim-response mints rewrite both witnesses on every poll. So after a re-docketing, neither witness keeps the earlier caption for those moments. Fixing that would change the ledger writer and is your call.
- **Refused but still open:** a refused moment on a still-pending row stays open and forecastable.
- **Still owed by #2422:** relocating Nathan under No. 26-257, and the summary withdrawal.

### Verification
- `scripts/gate.sh lint types schemas docs-tests`: clean.
- Full suite: 7,947 passed, 2 failed. Both failures (the proxy and chmod-as-root tests) also fail on clean `staging` in this container (#2388).
- The new convergence-path test fails if the committed-caption witness line is deleted from `_plan_case`, and passes with it.
- `uv run fedcourts process-digest --all` is unchanged: `proc-v9`, the same six digests.
- No owned path is touched; `voided_events.json` and `voids.py` are unchanged.
- This branch merged `origin/staging` to resolve a freeze-record append conflict. `staging`'s entry stays first and is preserved byte-for-byte.

### Review
- **code-reviewer:** no blockers. Changes made: the respondent arm is restricted to non-interim moments, word matching is tightened (role words, accents, prefixes of 4 or more letters), a malformed witness degrades instead of failing, and convergence-path and non-SCOTUS tests were added.
- **stats-reviewer:** no blockers. Changes made: the entry is labelled as attribution plus membership, the permanent-missing-outcome effect and prevalence are stated, and the denominators are corrected (the script now prints the subcounts).
- **docs-reviewer:** one blocker, the future-tense detector wording in `metrics/README.md` and `docs/process-version.md`. Fixed, and the other recommended items are applied.
- **For you:** this rewrites a reading rule and adds a freeze-record entry, so I'm leaving the merge with you. Fill the entry's `<FILL:>` merge facts at promotion.

author: derwiath
body:
Closes #137.

## Summary

```diff
 run_command
-  jj.operation(ws, ignore=args.ignore_jj, snapshot) as jj_workspace
-  open_backend(ws, jj_workspace) as backend
-  args.jj_workspace = jj_workspace
+  open_backend(ws, args.backend_choice, snapshot, checkouts) as backend
+    selected_backend: --backend, else core.backend (auto = jj in a jj workspace)
+    jj.operation(ws, lock_only=backend is git)     # lock + pinned operation for the whole command
   args.backend = backend

 sync_command
-  if args.jj_workspace: prepare_sync / detach_for_sync / eol / advance_sync
+  backend.prepare_sync(bookmark)  check_sync_clean()  start_sync()  commit_sync(subject)
-  run_hooks(...)
+  run_hooks(..., backend.name)                      # GIT_P4SON_BACKEND=git|jj
```

```text
--backend {git,jj}      replaces the unreleased --ignore-jj; overrides core.backend
core.backend            auto | git | jj; jj without .jj is an error
jj backend              refuses a missing jj or one older than 0.41, pointing to --backend git
git backend in jj       still holds jj's lock, needs no jj; reuses git-p4son's own lock from a hook
completion              follows the setting and a typed --backend, and completes its values
init                    backend.workspace_lock, the lock-only path
```

Commits:

1. **Read the change from one commit and keep the working files**: `GitBackend.revision` is `HEAD`, so the
   `revision is None` index paths in `lib.py` go. Around Perforce reverts the working files are kept for both
   backends, and `restore_files` goes. `TestKeptFileMatchesGitsRestore` checks, with `core.autocrlf` and the
   `ident` attribute, that the kept file equals the one git restores. `writable apply` reads `HEAD` the same way.
2. **Turn the minimal jj support into the backend's jj adapter**: everything else above, plus:
   - `writable` snapshotting on jj
   - "with the jj backend" wording in the help texts, README and skill
   - `on_jj` matching jj's line endings to git's `core.autocrlf` on Windows
   It also holds the cleanups from a `/simplify` review and reviews 4 and 5:
   - one `git.commit_all` behind both sync commits, with `words.tool` as the hook value
   - one lock-only branch in `jj.operation`
   - `--backend` read in completion's word loop
   - snapshotting by default, with `alias`, `sync-split-users` and plain `writable` opting out on their parsers
   - the jj test fixtures built on one `JjTestCase`

Follow-ups opened from that review: #163 (quiet mode leaking out of `run_command`) and #164 (a jj `eol-conversion`
that disagrees with git's `core.autocrlf`).

Outside `backend.py`, `jj.py` and the adapters, jj appears only in help texts and docstrings.

### Command tests on both backends

`on_jj(TestClass)` in `tests/helpers.py` copies a test class:
- its repository is colocated with jj right after `git init`
- its commands run on the jj backend
- it is skipped without jj

`run_command` in the test helpers now opens the backend as `cli.run_command` does. The copies are `TestNew`,
`TestNewAlias`, `TestUpdate`, `TestSync`, `TestSyncLocalChanges`, `TestSyncHooks`, `TestSyncDryRun` and
`TestSyncSplitting`. Two sync tests that leave a stray file only hold for git: jj makes the file part of the
working change, which sync refuses for another reason.

## Evidence

- [CI run](https://github.com/neoboid/git-p4son/actions/runs/39047090076): all six checks pass, Windows included.
- Locally, with jj 0.46: 977 passed, 4 skipped, five runs in a row. With jj hidden from `PATH`: 896 passed and 82
  skipped. `scripts/typecheck.sh` passes for linux and win32.
- New tests:
  - backend choice: the setting, the flag, `jj` without `.jj`, an unknown setting
  - the git backend holding jj's lock and needing no jj
  - missing and old jj pointing to `--backend git`
  - nested runs needing `--backend git`
  - `--backend git` and `core.backend = "git"` following git's detached HEAD in a jj workspace
  - hooks seeing `GIT_P4SON_BACKEND` on both backends
  - `GitBackend`'s sync methods
  - completion of `--backend`

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** every command

- `--ignore-jj` is gone, but it was never released.
- In git workspaces, `new` and `update` now keep the working files around Perforce reverts instead of restoring
  git's index version. In a clean workspace that's the same file.
- `writable apply` now lists the files tracked in `HEAD` rather than in the index, so a file staged but not yet
  committed is left alone.

body:
## Summary

Three CLI bugs found by an end-to-end run of platform frontend builds (`frontend.build`) on a branch preview, released as 3.13.1:

- **`app dev verify` rejected every app whose frontend OpenCloud builds.** It compared the session's server-built artifact with the local bundle digest, which leaves the frontend out, so it failed with `DEV_VERIFICATION_TARGET_CHANGED` before reaching OpenCloud, and the revision could never be promoted. It now expects the server-built artifact that `dev start` and `dev sync` record. On 3.13.0, the hosted Agent only got past this by hand-editing `.opencloud/dev.json`.
- **`app dev` read commands ignored their directory argument when authenticating.** `status`, `request`, `requests`, `receipts`, `evidence`, `email list|get`, `notifications list` and `integration list` authenticated from the working directory. Run from anywhere else, they reported that the directory was not connected.
- **Slow responses failed with `fetch failed`.** Node's fetch gives up on any response whose headers take longer than 300 seconds, whatever the request's timeout. So a validation whose frontend build ran to the platform's five-minute limit, or a long dev verification, failed while OpenCloud finished it. JSON POSTs now go through `node:http(s)` (`src/slow-response-fetch.ts`). Downloads and uploads keep using fetch, and failures keep fetch's error shapes.

## Tests

- New contract coverage for platform-built verify (fails on 3.13.0, passes now).
- New contract coverage for dev reads from another directory, using a real workspace binding and credential (fails before the fix).
- New unit tests for `slowResponseFetch`: the node:http path, delegation, abort reason, and a dropped connection.
- Also run: `npm test` (496), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:contract` (all suites), `npm run test:package`, `npm run verify:version`, and the 3.13.1 command-surface snapshot.
- On a branch preview, the packed candidate ran dev start → verify → promote for platform-built apps. A five-minute build timeout now reports `FRONTEND_BUILD_FAILED … did not finish in time`, and dev requests work from other directories.

The matching platform fixes are in opencloud-ai/platform#390 (merged).

author: xinye1017
body:
## 阶段 5 / 7 · 重做「今日学习节奏」，并重新平衡首页视觉权重

该区块原本是一行说明文字、18 根**固定宽度**的迷你柱和一个箭头。在没有任何专注的一天，那些柱子渲染成等距小点——看起来完全像分页指示器，而且折叠态不携带任何信息。

现在：

- 真正的区块标题，时间窗口移到坐标轴两端（06:00 / 24:00），不再在标题里重复；
- 柱子等分整宽、立在一条 hairline 轴上，空白的一天是一条干净的带标注时间轴，而不是第二排虚线；
- 一句话说明这块在度量什么——已确认总量、覆盖几个小时、最集中在哪个小时。它会明确说出自己的 06:00 窗口，因为时间轴不含更早的记录，不加限定的总量会与同屏的「今日累计专注」矛盾；
- 具名的「展开详情 / 收起详情」控件，而不是光秃秃的箭头。

没有专注的小时不绘制任何东西。当前小时保留一个小刻度，但**仅在时间轴已有柱子可对照时**才画：空白的一天里，那个刻度是一个没有所指的孤立标记——正是这次重做要消除的问题。

几何规则抽成纯函数 `rhythmSlots()`，组件从它渲染。这样「空白日不画任何东西」可以用算术断言，生产代码里不需要任何测试专用 prop。

时间轴范围单独发布为可访问节点：它原先只作为绘制文字存在于 `no-hide-descendants` 子树中，读屏用户完全无法获知。

依赖：阶段 1（与阶段 2–4 完全解耦，可并行）

验证：`tsc` 通过 · 117 测试通过 · 真机截图确认

author: chbauman
body:
Follow-up to #22, part of chbauman/sudoku-ts#47.

**Problem.** The generator removed random digits only until one removal made the solution non-unique, and it recorded every unique puzzle on the way. A check of the collection showed that 4052 of 4053 puzzles in `generated_dat.txt` still had removable digits (about 14 of 33 on average).

**Generator.**
- New `SudokuGenerator::minimize()`: one pass over all digits in random order, removing each one whose removal keeps the solution unique. A digit that cannot be removed at some point never can be later (fewer digits only allow more solutions), so one pass ends in a minimal puzzle.
- Only minimal puzzles are collected, also those from the local search (`--climb-steps`): accepted climb steps are minimized again, and the minimal puzzle is only used if its level did not drop.
- Puzzles have ~24 instead of ~33 digits and come from more varied solution grids. Generation is slower because of the extra solving.

**Data.** `generated_dat.txt` is regenerated from an empty file (`--min-level 0 --max-per-level 200 --climb-steps 2000`, stopped after 400 of 2000 iterations): 200 puzzles each for levels 1-3, 73 for level 4, 4 for level 5 (677 in total, 92 distinct solution grids). All entries are minimal, have consistent descriptors/grids, and a sample was checked with `solve` for unique solutions. Levels 4 and 5 are slow to find; the file can be extended by running `generate --output-path generated_dat.txt` for longer.

**README.** Documents the minimization and the new contents of `generated_dat.txt`.

Builds with `g++ -std=c++20 -O2 -Wall`.

author: patel-om
body:
**Founder class: control plane.** Adds `.claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md`, `scripts/pr_review.py` and `scripts/review_map.py`, edits `.github/review-teams.yml` and `.github/CODEOWNERS` (both scripts join the control-plane class), `tests/test_review_teams.py` and `docs/REVIEW_MECHANISM.md` (still PLANNED). Needs the founder's merge. Council rollout R5; tracker T19 and T20.

## What it does
`python3 scripts/pr_review.py <n>`, started by the `pr-review` skill from a checkout of `origin/main`. Same mechanism as Nirmaan's script (nirmaansoftware/Nirmaan#78), ported to Python:

1. One review at a time, using a lock in `~/.nirmaan/pr-review/review.lock` that Nirmaan's script also uses.
2. Refuses and posts nothing for forks, other authors, a base other than main, or a Claude Code session that has the branch checked out.
3. Clean worktrees of the head and of main, outside the repository. The fetched head must equal the pull request's head.
4. From main's map only (`scripts/review_map.py`, which is the coverage test's loader moved out of the test): owning teams, which lead holds key 1 (a rule's or content rule's `lead`, else the team's first lead), sections (partners), ledger files, content rules and founder classes.
5. CI first: until `test`, `no-tools`, `physical-design`, `test-union` and `dashes` are green, both checks stay pending and no model is called.
6. Key 1 runs once per owning team lead, using the base checklist (council record, "Every key 1 (base)"), the lead's seat file and the members' "In a review" sections. Key 2 runs the chair seat plus every owning lead's seat file, with key 1's results. Each is a fresh `claude -p` with Read, Grep and Glob only, `--safe-mode`, no MCP, `dontAsk`, and no tokens in its environment. The reviewer does not get the PR title, body or commit messages (the IP rule). The diff is passed as untrusted data with a random delimiter.
7. Every verdict is validated: schema, head SHA, and every cited file:line must exist at the head. A pass that contains a blocker or critical finding is recorded as fail. A failed call, timeout or rate limit gets one backoff retry, then the key is "review deferred" (pending). It never passes by default.
8. The head is checked again before every post. The script then posts one comment per key, plus `review/team-lead` and `review/executive`. Executive is success only when key 2 passes, there is no `hold` label, and for any founder class the founder's latest review approves this head SHA.
9. Calls (tokens, duration, outcome) are logged in `~/.nirmaan/pr-review/calls.jsonl`.

**Posting identity.** The App posts when `NIRMAAN_REVIEW_APP_ID` is set together with `NIRMAAN_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` or `NIRMAAN_REVIEW_APP_KEYCHAIN_SERVICE` (optional `NIRMAAN_REVIEW_APP_INSTALLATION_ID`). The JWT is signed with openssl, so there is no Python dependency. Without the App it is a dry run: comments plus `dry-run/review/*` statuses, which are never green.

## Tests
- `tests/test_pr_review.py`: 44 pass against a fake `claude` and a fake GitHub, with no model calls and no network. They cover bad JSON, non-JSON CLI output, a missing citation, a missing file, the wrong SHA, the head moving (before key 1 posts and between keys), timeout, rate limit, pass with a critical finding, CI not green, a missing seat section, founder class by path, content and section (approval on the current head versus an old head), map and seats read from main, ledger files, hold, refusals, dry-run statuses, the shared and stale lock, verdict reuse, the env allowlist and the App JWT.
- Full suite: 2109 passed, 8 skipped, 1 deselected (the documented `test_ai_boundary` one).
- `scripts/check_dashes.py`: clean.

## Not done here
No real review was run on any pull request. The seeded dry run (R6) needs this merged and the App (T21). The security seat still has to review the isolation.

Agent work. Never a person's decision or a release.

﻿## Objective

The deployment wizard hardcoded provider presets, logical models and access groups in `installer/frontend/providers.js` (26 model-name literals in JavaScript). Following the no-hardcoded-model-names rule, the catalog moves to pure data and the code only loads it.

body:
关联 [#257](https://github.com/MyBlackHole/c-logger/issues/257)、[#100](https://github.com/MyBlackHole/c-logger/issues/100)、[#210](https://github.com/MyBlackHole/c-logger/issues/210)、[#218](https://github.com/MyBlackHole/c-logger/issues/218)、[#221](https://github.com/MyBlackHole/c-logger/issues/221)。基线 main `db0410e83f1476bea83db0258b87d54603cc147c`；当前head `b4cd9cd30f6ff5653953127ed76a7a204e02ba4e`。

## 安全缺口与修复范围
现有 `release-publish` 的 `prepare/gate` 只有标签、VERSION、ABI/符号清单和精确提交身份约束；**没有 A–F、D1–D6 签收就推送合法 `v2.*` 标签仍可能进入正式打包和发布**。本PR在绑定选定标签源码之后、`authorized=true`之前增加纯Python3标准库的`scripts/check_release_signoff.py`。没有改变标签路由、真实打包/发布命令、远端标签复核或资产验收的已有规则。

- 新版本化 `validation/release_signoff_v2.json` 的**12项默认全部 pending**，冻结基线 `null`。准确最新main在未实际批准前必须**拒绝发布**，本PR**绝无人为风险接受签署**。
- 有界批准时逐项必须有 approved/accepted_with_risk、明确GitHub维护者、UTC时间、对应固定Issue的实际决策评论链接、工程证据URL、具体残余风险；12项必须完整，不允许加/丢条目、占位字符串或缺决策。
- 最后冻结的受测代码Git SHA必须是实际标签提交的祖先；从冻结SHA至最终标签提交的**唯一允许变化为签收JSON**，任何生产源码、公开ABI、测试、CI定义或打包内容变化都被拒绝，必须重新冻结并重新验收。避免自引用SHA，签收记录必须在冻结代码之后单独提交。
- 沿用原有 `tests/test_release_gate.py` 真正从工作流提取shell、使用本地临时Git/轻量及附注标签+假`gh`的隔离验证。正向测试仅构造标注为“**本地夹具模拟签收**”的完整字段；另有待决策/缺文件/错误版本/错误Issue/伪签署人/无证据/风险简写/冻结后源码ABI漂移/未提交签收等独立负例。无一次真实 GitHub Tag/Release操作。
- 保留 `docs/v2/RELEASE_PREFLIGHT.md` 和 `docs/RELEASE_SAFETY.md` 的危险边界：**机器解析不能认证GitHub评论真实身份或取代分支/标签保护与人工复核**。D1–D6未被自动视为后续增强，#218/#221/业务SLO没有被批准。

## 验收
当前为草稿，尚待本**精确head**的Xmake完整正确性、`release-gate`本地正反、静态/共享包、发布安全门禁、源码格式及其他所有适用CI实际通过。即使这些测试绿色，真实签收仍是pending、正式`v2.0.0`标签和Release**禁止创建**。

Students sign in with a one-time link emailed through Resend from `login@dolphub.tech`. Also adds a local development mode that needs no Neon, Resend or R2 account.

## How sign-in works

1. A student enters their PCU email at `/login`.
2. Resend emails a link to `https://dolphub.tech/auth/verify`.
3. The link opens a page with a "Continue" button. Only the button press uses the link, so mail scanners that open links early cannot use it up.
4. The student lands on `/dashboard`, signed in for 30 days. Sign-out ends the session.

## Changes

- **New tables.** `login_tokens` and `sessions`, stored as hashes only.
- **Sign-in service.** `requestSignInLink`, `consumeSignInLink`, `getSessionUser`, `signOut` and `purgeExpiredAuthRecords`.
- **Limits.** Links expire after 15 minutes and work once. Each address gets 3 links per 15 minutes. The site stops at `DAILY_EMAIL_CAP`, 90 by default, under Resend's free tier of 100 a day.
- **Existing rules kept.** Only PCU addresses can create accounts. The signup freeze still lets existing users in. Deleting an account ends its sessions.
- **Pages.** `/login`, `/auth/verify`, a placeholder `/dashboard`, and a simple home page. All are plain and phone-first, for the frontend to restyle.
- **Session cookie.** httpOnly, SameSite Lax, and `__Host-` prefixed in production.
- **Local development.** `DATABASE_URL=pglite:./.data/pglite` runs Postgres inside Node. Without `RESEND_API_KEY`, sign-in links print to the terminal.
- **Production checks.** The app refuses to start without Neon, Resend, R2 and an https `APP_URL`.
- **Docs.** README local and production setup, plus backend reference, decision log and plan updates.

## Testing

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | 61 passed |
| Browser test of the full flow at phone width | 15 of 15 passed |
| `npm run typecheck` | Passed |
| `npm run lint` | Passed |
| `next build` | Passed |

The browser test covered refusing a Gmail address, a scanner opening the link first, reusing a link, the dashboard redirect when signed out, sign-out, and the rate limit.

Not yet tested against real Resend, Neon or R2, because those accounts are not set up.

## Before sign-in works on dolphub.tech

- Verify `dolphub.tech` in Resend and create an API key.
- Set the production variables on Vercel, as listed in the README.
- Run `db:migrate` and `db:seed` against Neon.
- Send one real sign-in link to a PCU address and check inbox versus spam.

## Known risk

Anyone can request links for made-up `@pcu.edu.ph` addresses and use up the daily email cap. Freezing signups stops links to new addresses. A per-IP limit or a form challenge is the follow-up if it happens.

body:
## What and why

Before: `web/package.json` pinned `overrides.sharp` to an exact version. metron-PR344 added that pin at 0.35.0, when `next` required `^0.34.x`. Dependabot reads an exact override as the requirement, so every sharp advisory has been reported as `security_update_not_possible` and needed a manual bump: aac4fe0 → 0.35.4, then #540 → 0.35.5. The latest red `/web` sharp job, run 37784424206 on 10-08, failed with "next@15.5.26 requires sharp@0.35.4". The lockfile was fixed by #540 (689324c, sharp 0.35.5), so that alert self-clears. The pin itself was still in place.

After: the pin is gone. `next@15.5.27` already declares `sharp: ^0.34.3 || ^0.35.4`, so npm resolves the same sharp 0.35.5. `package-lock.json` is **byte-identical**, so `npm ci` installs the same tree. The next sharp security update can now land through Dependabot without a manual bump. This is the same fix crucible-dashboard#947 made for dash-web.

How: deleted one key from `overrides` and ran `npm install --package-lock-only` (npm 11.20.0); the lockfile did not change.

Other `/web` Dependabot red: nanoid (run 31617802201, 08-12). It failed with `security_update_not_possible` because postcss `^3.3.16` was blocking. It was fixed long ago: nanoid is 3.3.20 in the lock. Self-clears.

Not fixed here (not lock-fixable): `npm audit` still reports 5 high findings, all one dev-only chain: `eslint-config-next` → `@next/eslint-plugin-next` → `fast-glob@3.3.1` → `micromatch` → `braces@3.0.3` (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm, `<=3.0.3`). No patched `braces` has been published (3.0.3 is the latest, from 2024-05). npm's only suggested fix is a semver-major downgrade to `eslint-config-next@14.2.35`. It is a lint-time dependency, so it is not in the served app.

**Deploy on merge:** `deploy.yml` sends an SSM command to the Metron box (`METRON_INSTANCE_ID`). The command resets `/home/ec2-user/metron` to the merge SHA and `metron-ops` to `origin/main`, then runs `infrastructure/deploy-on-merge.sh`. That script runs `npm install` in `web/`, rebuilds the `/dash` Next.js variant, and restarts `metron-api` and `metron-dash-web` with health checks. The lockfile is unchanged, so the installed tree is the same. Not a red line.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added/updated for the behavior change: n/a, no behavior change (identical lockfile)
- [x] `pytest` passes locally: n/a, no Python touched
- [x] `ruff check api portfolio_analytics tests` is clean for files I touched: n/a
- [x] No secrets, proprietary prompt templates, or private signal feeds committed
- [x] Fail-loud preserved

## Test plan

Ran the `web` job from `ci.yml` locally on Node 22 (v22.22.2): `npm ci`, `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean), `npx next lint` (no warnings or errors), `npm test` (71 files / 425 tests passed). `npm ls sharp` shows sharp@0.35.5. `npm audit --package-lock-only` is unchanged from main: 5 high, all the braces chain above.

author: pvd232
body:
# RGP-PB-06: Compare the original and additional publications

Context: a copied graph can pass ordinary validation while pointing to a different valid input. This check compares each saved source relationship with its recorded destination copy.

## Implementation

`GraphComparison` reads the journal's file mappings and compares original and destination files through separate caches. It checks complete snapshot membership, selected roots, required inventory entries, payload hashes, and the exact destination repository.

For saved protocol documents, it derives the permitted location and hash changes from the original record. The check preserves parameters, measurements, source commits, input names, and list membership. It also checks the derived stage-plan hashes, reuse keys, and download-source receipt identifiers. The comparison code runs independently of the promoter's rewrite methods.

An operation can use the same working-space limit for its separate source and destination check caches. Verified temporary downloads are removed after each comparison; original files remain intact.

## Checks

20 focused cases passed in 20.69 seconds. Pyright, docstring checks, formatting and lint checks passed. Exact commands and hashes are recorded in [review-checks.json](review-checks.json).

The new cases cover a complete mixed-cloud graph, an altered seed, a missing required file, and substitution of a separately valid plan. The substituted plan passes the ordinary graph verifier and fails this source-to-destination comparison.

## Size and review

Production grows by 297 lines and tests by 183 lines. The comparison owns the required independent check; it consumes the existing file references, manifests, journal, and source readers. Git records the implementation directly. Independent review is pending.
