body:
## Summary

- While the app is keeping the Mac awake with the lid closed, it sets the built-in display's brightness to 0. It restores the saved brightness when the lid opens, which is checked every 0.5 s while the screen is off.
- It does nothing when an external display is attached, because macOS already turns the built-in panel off in clamshell mode.
- Brightness uses the private `DisplayServices` framework, because Apple silicon has no public API for it. If the framework is missing, the screen is left alone and the log says "Could not turn the display off".
- Crash and quit safety:
  - Quitting always restores the brightness.
  - The saved brightness is kept in `~/Library/Application Support/ClaudeLidClosed/dimmed-brightness`, so a restarted app puts the screen back after a crash.
  - Brightness is never restored below 10%, so a 0 reading taken while the backlight was already off can't leave a black screen.
- Added a **Turn Display Off When Lid Closed** menu switch, on by default. The menu detail shows "display off" while the screen is dark.
- Dry-run mode (`CLAUDE_LID_DRY_RUN=1`) now logs brightness changes instead of applying them. The pretend lid opens when a `lid-open` file appears in the state directory.
- README updated: feature list, architecture diagram, safety section, menu, limitations and development notes.
- If the Mac goes to sleep with the lid still closed, the brightness stays at 0 until the lid is opened. This is intended and documented.

## Testing

- Not run: no build or test results are available for this change.
- Not run: dry run with `CLAUDE_LID_DRY_RUN=1 CLAUDE_LID_FAKE_LID=closed`. Expected: the log shows brightness going to 0%, then back after `touch <state dir>/lid-open`.
- Not run on a real MacBook: lid closed during a Claude Code task should turn the display off, and opening the lid should restore the previous brightness.
- Not run: killing the app while the display is off, then relaunching, should restore the brightness from `dimmed-brightness`.
- Not run: with an external display attached, the brightness should not be changed.
- Not run: turning the **Turn Display Off When Lid Closed** switch off should leave the screen alone.

author: mnemonik-dev
body:
## Summary
Two changes so that a buyer can use the Arc mainnet transcription seller without contacting the operator.

### 1. The seller needs no shared password
The password sits in the proxy in front of `seller.mnemonik.xyz`, not in the seller code. Removing it as is would have let a stranger read the `worker_token` of any task and use a paying buyer's GPU container. `get_deployment_status` with no `task_id` also returned the latest session, token included. This PR ties the risky calls to the customer of the task.

- `deploy_with_escrow` and `get_deployment_status` need `request_signature` and `request_timestamp`. The signature (EIP-191) binds the chain, the escrow, the task and the action. The seller accepts it only from the customer address of that task, and only within 5 minutes. An unknown task and a wrong signer give the same error.
- `get_deployment_status` needs a `task_id`. The latest-session fallback is gone in signed mode.
- New guardrail tool `warrant_sign_request`. It signs only for tasks that this guardrail funded itself, so a prompt injection cannot make it sign for another task.
- The seller limits proposals (120 an hour in all, 10 an hour for each customer address), caches the io.net hardware lookup for 20 seconds, deletes unused proposals older than 24 hours and refuses new ones when 2,000 are stored.
- `WARRANT_REQUIRE_REQUEST_SIGNATURE=0` switches signatures off for local tests only.
- `buyer_init`, the README, the agent skill (`SKILL.md`) and the demo agent no longer mention a credential.

### 2. One-command buyer setup, and a `warrant-buyer` package
- `buyer_init.py` makes a new burner wallet and an acceptance key in `~/.warrant-buyer` (mode 0600), writes the manifest and public keys file with the mainnet values, and prints the MCP configuration. A rerun reuses the keys. `--status` shows the USDC balance.
- `cli.py`, `scripts/build-buyer-wheel.sh`, `packaging/warrant-buyer/` and `.github/workflows/release-buyer.yml` build wheels for Linux x86-64 and ARM64 and macOS arm64 and x86-64. The workflow publishes to PyPI on a `buyer-v*` tag with trusted publishing.

## Verified
- Full showcase suite with `warrant-host` built: 141 tests pass, 1 skipped. 16 of them are new: 12 seller tests (a stranger, a wrong action, a wrong task, a wrong escrow and a stale signature are refused; the customer gets the token; rate limit, store cap, pruning and cache) and 4 guardrail tests.
- `ruff check` is clean.
- The Linux x86-64 wheel, installed in a clean environment with no repository and no Rust: `init` runs, the guardrail starts over stdio and signs.

## Not verified
- A live seller with signatures on, or a real mainnet purchase. The mainnet purchase path has not run with money yet.
- The macOS wheels, the Linux ARM64 wheel and the PyPI publish step.
- The in-process limits are global. One client can use them up. Limit requests for each IP address at the proxy.

## Before this goes live
1. Merge, then redeploy the seller. A seller that runs the old code with the password removed leaks worker tokens.
2. Remove the basic auth at the proxy only after the redeploy, and add a per-IP rate limit there.

author: arsfeld
body:
## Problem

A show you are binging sinks on the player's Continue Watching rail. The server ranks the rail correctly (newest watch across the whole show first), but the player re-sorts every card by its own `lastPlayedAt`, with undated cards last. For a "next episode" card that date was the named episode's own progress, and that episode has never been played. So the card had no date and fell behind every half-watched title, however stale.

## Change

- `ContinueWatchingItem.lastActivityAt` (nullable `DateTime`): when the viewer last watched the title; for an episode, the newest watch across its show. It is the key the server already orders the rail by (`OnDeckEntry.sort_at`).
- Exported SDL updated, and the Rust `mydia-api` struct gains the field for `sdl_parity`.
- Player: `MydiaContinueWatching` selects it, and `continueWatchingSummary` uses it for `lastPlayedAt`, falling back to the episode's progress date.

## Compatibility

Older servers reject the new field, and the player falls back to `MydiaContinueWatchingNoIds` as before, keeping today's ordering. 0.17 betas, which have catalogue ids but not this field, also take that fallback, so their rail loses ids (used only for cross-server dedupe).

## Tests

- Elixir: a next card's `lastActivityAt` equals the finished episode's watch time; a movie's equals its own progress time.
- Dart: mapping precedence and fallback; a next card for a show watched today outranks a stale half-watched card through `buildHomeRows`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Continue Watching items now include the latest watch activity time and a state describing why they appear in the rail.
  * Episode activity times reflect the show’s most recent watch, while movies use their own latest watch time.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Continue Watching dates now prioritize the item’s latest activity, falling back to saved progress when activity time is unavailable.
  * Recently watched episodes rank ahead of stale, partially watched movies while preserving the server-provided row order.

author: olibrowne
body:
Before: two overnight bug hunts found nine problems.

**Local UI and network code:**
- Any web page could frame the local UI (`127.0.0.1:8765`) and steer clicks into Approve, Fill or an A365 push (clickjacking).
- A deeply nested JSON body crashed into the "unexpected error" path.
- A failed Mouser request could leave a few characters of the API key in `http.log`, which feeds the triage report.

**BOM intake:**
- "Total parts | 3" footers and quantity-only rows became parts, one of them with an empty name.
- `DNP` / `10k (DNF)` written in the Value or MPN cell didn't mark the line as not fitted, so it was looked up and costed.
- The European quantity `1,0` was counted as 10.
- A UTF-8 CSV containing one stray cp1252 byte was decoded entirely as cp1252, turning `10µF` into `10ÂµF`, which parses as 10 F.
- `C1~C4` ranges counted 0 designators.
- An MPN that Excel had turned into `5.30E+08` was searched with no warning.

After: each case behaves as expected. The local UI sends `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`. Nested JSON gets a plain 400. Secret query parameters are redacted before error text is cut. The BOM fixes don't change any part names, so existing DbLib rows are unaffected.

How: `ui/server.py` (local headers, the `_json` RecursionError), `httpcache.py` (`SECRET_Q` redaction) and `bom_triage.read_bom`/`count_refs`/notes. Each fix is a separate commit with a failing-first test in `tests/test_review_1018_ui_mcp.py` or `tests/test_review_1018_bom_intake.py`.

Tested locally: the full suite passed on each branch (1191 and 1194). The combined touched modules pass 122/122 on 3.11, and the accuracy gate is 327/331, the same as the baseline.

Design questions found but not changed are in the overnight test report: approvals lost when a second process runs the librarian, no login in local mode, and naming changes that would rename existing rows.

author: dailyxplorer
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the 7 confirmed bugs from the second full audit of the meetings feature (audited code: `main` at b755fa1).

1. **A microphone lost mid-meeting is now reported.** If the only input (a USB or Bluetooth headset) drops out and doesn't come back, the meeting shows a new notification: "The microphone stopped recording. Murmur keeps trying to bring it back; check that it's still connected." Before, the user's voice went missing from the rest of the recording without a word.
2. **A lasting rate limit no longer fails every queued meeting.** When a meeting ends rate limited, the queue waits before starting the next one. Before, each queued meeting spent about 30 minutes retrying and then failed.
3. **The meeting's "Me" track records the input channel chosen in Settings**, as dictation does. Before, it averaged every input of a multi-input interface.
4. **A title being typed is kept** when the summary (or a retry) saves its own title at the same moment.
5. **A stale meeting folder that can't be deleted no longer blocks every future meeting.** It is moved aside and the new meeting starts.
6. **A meeting with a recorded track that can't be read no longer ends Ready.** The readable side stays on screen, the meeting fails with "The recording couldn't be read.", and no summary is written from half of it.
7. **The last two pieces of a long track are cut in a pause**, not at the exact midpoint, so no word is split.

## Design choices

- **Lost microphone (#1).** One `Heard` clock records when audio last arrived, across every reopen. The stall detector keeps its 3 s threshold, measured from the later of the last audio and the reopen. `interrupted()` turns true after 6 s without audio (3 s stall + 1 s reopen delay + margin), so a reopen that works stays silent. The coordinator now knows which source each track is and raises one alert per source per loss, with the same pattern as the existing `SystemAudioInterrupted`. The new tray string is translated in all 24 locales.
- **Rate-limit hold (#2).** I looked at how rate limits work in practice: the ChatGPT/Codex usage cap frees up over a sliding five-hour window, and the usual advice is exponential backoff, because retrying sooner prolongs the problem. After a meeting that ends `rate_limited`, the worker sleeps for 30 min, doubling for each such meeting in a row up to 4 h, and resets after a meeting that isn't rate limited. Queued meetings keep their state ("Waiting to be processed…") instead of failing. The worker reads the outcome from the stored meeting, so `Processor` is unchanged.
- **Channel (#3).** This mirrors dictation exactly: the chosen channel is used when the device has it, otherwise all channels are averaged. The same rule applies on every reopen.
- **Title (#4).** A ref holds the title as it was when editing began. The field re-syncs only while it is not focused. On blur it saves only if the draft differs from that starting title. Escape resets the starting title, so a revert never saves.
- **Stale folder (#5).** If the folder can't be deleted, it is renamed to `<id>.stale-<ms>`. Nothing reads that name, and the corrupt-library sweep skips it because it isn't a number. Under a symlinked meetings root, the start still fails, because a rename would then act outside the app's data. I did not switch the table to AUTOINCREMENT: that needs a table rebuild with cascading foreign keys inside a migration transaction, and a failed migration resets `meetings.db`. That risk is too high for this fix.
- **Unreadable track (#6).** I reused the existing `NoAudio` error, so no new strings were needed. A sign-out still takes priority, because it is the error the user can act on.
- **Balanced cut (#7).** This reuses `split_chunk`: the quietest moment in the middle half, which is how refused pieces are already cut.

## Tests

Each fix has a regression test, written first. The new tests were run before the fixes, with compile stubs, and all failed as expected:

```
test result: FAILED. 208 passed; 8 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 386 filtered out
```

The 8 failing tests were the 7 new or updated tests plus `user_alert::every_meeting_alert_has_its_own_message_in_a_notification`, which covers the new alert.

New or updated tests:
- `capture::mic::a_microphone_silent_past_a_reopen_counts_as_lost`
- `capture::mic::the_input_channel_chosen_in_settings_records_the_meeting`
- `coordinator::a_lost_microphone_warns_once_and_the_meeting_keeps_recording`
- `coordinator::a_stale_folder_that_cannot_be_deleted_never_blocks_a_new_meeting`
- `processor::a_recorded_track_that_cannot_be_read_fails_the_meeting_and_keeps_the_other`
- `meetings::the_queue_waits_longer_after_each_rate_limited_meeting_in_a_row`
- `chunking::a_short_tail_is_balanced_with_the_piece_before_and_still_cut_in_a_pause` (replaces the test that asserted the exact midpoint)

Results after the fixes, run on macOS (Apple Silicon):

- `cargo test --lib -- meetings:: user_alert:: tray_i18n`: `test result: ok. 217 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 385 filtered out`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `bun run lint`: clean
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `bun run check:translations`: `All 23 languages have complete translations!`
- `bun run format:check`: clean
- I also ran `cargo check --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` on every intermediate commit. Each one builds.

## Known limits

- **#1:** the mic alert fires only once audio has been missing for 6 s. Nothing tells the user when the mic comes back, which matches system audio. If both sources drop, the system-audio message still says "your microphone is still recorded".
- **#2:**
  - Codex's `Retry-After` or reset time is not read, because the error type doesn't carry it yet. The wait is a fixed backoff.
  - A manual "Retry" during the hold also waits.
  - The UI doesn't say why queued meetings are waiting.
  - In-flight pieces of a run still stop only at their next gate wake-up, up to 4 min later. This was the audit's optional item, and I didn't do it.
- **#4:** there is no frontend unit-test runner, so the title fix is checked by lint and tsc only. A rejected rename still leaves the rejected text in the field. That is a separate, minor issue.
- **#5:** the folder moved aside is left on disk, and only a log line mentions it.
- **#6:** the error says "The recording couldn't be read." even though one side is shown. A retry doesn't help when the file is really gone.

## Manual checks for the owner

1. **Lost microphone:** start a meeting with a USB or Bluetooth headset as the only input. Unplug it, or turn it off, and leave it off. Within about 6–10 s a notification should say the microphone stopped recording. Plug it back in: recording goes on, and there is no second alert unless it drops again.
2. **Channel:** on a multi-input interface, pick input 1 in Settings → Microphone channel, record a short meeting, and check that the Me track carries only that input. It should not be quieter than dictation.
3. **Title:** on an unnamed meeting, click the title while the summary is being written and type. When the summary finishes, your text should stay, and leaving the field should save it. Escape should revert without saving.
4. **Rate limit (optional, hard to trigger on purpose):** in the log, look for `holding the queue for 1800s` after a meeting fails with "Codex is limiting requests". The next queued meeting should stay "Waiting to be processed…" instead of failing.
5. **Everyday use:** record and process one normal meeting with both tracks and confirm the transcript, summary and compression still work.

author: janttsu
body:
Work package 10a of `docs/spec/format-3-design.md` (section 13): replicas, pools, transferrers, data moves, drains and quota usage on the pack-level ledger. Behind the `format3` feature; engine-independent functions for the integration (WP12) to wire. Based on `f3-blockmap` (#81, which carries #75 ledger3 and #78 pack size classes) with `main` merged (record, ledger3, membership3, manifest3, trash3).

New module `crates/varsto-core/src/storages3/`:

- `copies`: copies of a block = storages holding a live place of it (pack held there, place not dead or lost through the map table). `block_copies`, `file_copies(chunks)`, `block_facts` / `file_facts` (the input of `policy::evaluate`, with per-disk copies of pools and carriers left out), `block_copy_details` (independent verification and first-stored time per storage).
- `replica`: `replicate(src, tgt, storage, claimed)` copies packs whole (size class and id checked, read back from the target), claims them with `pack_stored` (zero folder, map_seq 0) and `pack_verified`, copies records and maps as they are, skips junk. `check_replica_events` refuses anything a replica may not say.
- `pools`: `pack_referenced` / `tidy_disk_packs` (disk insert tidy follows the ledger), `check_disk_packs` (hash every pack against its id, `pack_verified` / `pack_dropped` events), `book_sets` (the pool's `BookInput` from pack copies, for `disk_suggestions` and the next disk to dock), `group_rule_met` (disk group rule counted by the places holding the pack), `pool_pack_copies`.
- `moves`: `plan_move`, `run_move`, `run_drain`, `leftovers`. A pack whose live members are all in scope is copied whole; otherwise the members in scope go into new packs (first fit decreasing, smallest class) and the others into a remainder pack on the source. The source is dropped only after the destination is read back; the caller deletes after the batch is pushed (`MoveRun::delete_dropped`). Staged moves to pools wait for room or for a second place, and halve a pack a disk has no room for.
- `drain`: `drain_plan` (copy rules capped at what was met before, never the last live place, refusal text), `storage_usage` (quota usage in pack classes).
- `carriers`: transferrer targeting and emptying from `held` (`manifest3::HeldIndex` or any callback), pack-level emptying.

Small changes elsewhere: `packs::first_fit_decreasing` factored out of `PackStore::write_packs` (same behaviour), `Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq` on `policy::ChunkFacts`.

Tests (14 in `storages3::tests`): replica copies packs and claims them without keys; a replica cannot claim a folder, drop or announce a record; a pool disk lists packs from the ledger and tidies unknown ones; a staged move across two disks counts a group rule by places (waits with one place, drops the source with two); a policy with 2 copies is met by a pack on two storages and violated when a member is dead in one of them; a folder move keeps every block readable through the map (whole pack, rebuilt pack and remainder, `find_block` after deleting the source packs); a damaged pack is never copied; keep-source and run limits; pool without room takes members in smaller packs; a drain refuses while a place is the only live one, copies whole packs, and counts min copies and per-place rules; quota usage; transferrers with a callback and with a real `HeldIndex`.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` with and without `--features varsto-core/format3`; `cargo test -p varsto-core --features format3 --lib` (467 passed); default `-p varsto-core` (651), `-p varsto-cli` (122), `-p varsto-ffi` (88).

Noticed, not fixed:
- `PoolStorage::tidy_disk` only removes unindexed files; an indexed pack the ledger no longer names stays until the pool deletes it (as before). `book_sets` shows it as reclaimable.
- The spec text for these functions (a numbered section in `alpha-0-format.md`) belongs to WP11.

author: aelhamah
body:
The tile proxy landed in #80; this is the half that makes it do anything.

Until now the key was still a string in the web bundle and in `MapTilerConfig`, so anybody could download the `.ipa`, read it out, and spend the account. **The Worker was deployed and unused.**

## What the proxy needed before a browser could be one of its clients

**CORS.** A browser discards any response that does not say it may be read, so without `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` the tile is fetched, dropped, and the map is blank. Echoed for a *verified* origin, never `*` — a wildcard would make the proxy readable by every page on the internet, which is the opposite of an origin allowlist. Refusals carry the header too, because a browser cannot otherwise read the `429 quota_exceeded` that explains what happened. `Vary: Origin` on every response, since a shared cache in front of this Worker must not hand one allowlisted origin's response to another.

**A browser identity.** A page cannot set `User-Agent` — it is a forbidden header name — so `Origin` is the only thing a browser can be judged on. The native app uses `User-Agent` and can. Both leave upstream wearing the same `User-Agent`, because the MapTiler key's own allowlist is one exact string and keeping it that way is what lets the key stay out of every client.

**A separate web quota.** Every browser user of a deployment shares one bucket, since there is no stable per-visitor identity a browser can be asked for, and one map view is a few hundred requests. `WEB_DAILY_QUOTA` is its own, much larger number; sharing the native figure would be gone in minutes.

**Key stripping.** `sanitizeUpstreamResponse` cannot do this alone: the key in a style is in the *body*, as URLs inside the JSON, and has to be rewritten back to the proxy's own address so that following a rewritten source URL still works and still reveals nothing.

## Two deployment traps, both of which fail silently

**xcconfig reads `//` as the start of a comment.** So `TILE_PROXY_BASE_URL = https://host` resolves to `https:`, and the app quietly falls back to MapLibre's demo basemap with nothing on screen to explain why. Quoting does not help, and `\/` lands in the Info.plist as literal backslashes. The native side therefore splits it into `TILE_PROXY_SCHEME` and `TILE_PROXY_HOST`, and `project.yml` rejoins the halves where no `//` is ever adjacent.

**`serviceStatus.ts` now classifies failures against the *proxy's* host**, not MapTiler's, since the proxy is now the only host this app talks to. Matching the old one would classify every real failure as "not ours" and show no banner at all — including for the blank map that this whole PR exists to prevent. An empty `TILE_PROXY_HOST` (no proxy configured) is guarded separately, because `includes('')` is true and would report every unconfigured deployment as a basemap outage.

## Also

- `web/vitest.config.ts` — `src/config.ts` reads the base URL at module load, so without this every URL under test is built from an empty base string and the suite passes for the wrong reason: `'/maps/outdoor-v2/style.json'` contains `/maps/outdoor-v2/`, and a relative path is exactly what an unconfigured deployment produces. Separate from `vite.config.ts` so it can never affect a production build.
- `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is matched exactly, never by prefix — `https://aelhamah.github.io.evil.test` starts with an allowlisted value and is a different site.

## Verified

| | |
| --- | --- |
| proxy | 90 tests, `tsc --noEmit` clean |
| web | 336 tests, `tsc -b` clean, production build contains no `key=` and no `MAPTILER_API_KEY` |
| iOS | `swift build` clean, 181 tests, 0 failures |

## Required before this does anything

Three repo secrets, all currently unset:

- `VITE_TILE_PROXY_BASE_URL` — the Worker's URL, for both the site deploy and PR previews
- `TILE_PROXY_HOST` — the same host, for the iOS preview captures
- `MAPTILER_KEY` — already set on the Worker; only needed if you redeploy it

Without them the builds fall back to a keyless basemap and say so on screen, which is the existing designed behaviour rather than a build break.

---

Not included: #81, the map loading indicator. It touches the same three web files and will need a rebase once this lands.

author: anchit-tandon
body:
## Why
The first scheduled autopilot run in production (14:48 UTC) worked 2 tasks, and both came back "needs you" within about 3 s. At that moment every free AI provider was in quota cooldown, so chat replied with its text-only fallback. That run was judged "needs you", and "needs you" is never retried, so the tasks were stuck for good. The batch loop also only looked at `todo` tasks, so in-progress tasks were never picked up.

## Changes
- `judgeRun`: a `fallback` reply with no checklist and no confirms is now `failed` and its report starts with `NO_PROVIDER`. The update log reads "waiting for a free AI provider", which does not count toward the 3-attempt limit.
- `dueForRun`:
  - takes both `todo` and `in_progress` tasks;
  - retries outage runs on the next run;
  - re-works "needs you" runs where nothing was verified, up to 3 times.
- `/api/cron/autopilot`: works nothing while `llmStatus()` reports "down", and returns `waiting` when a run hits an outage. `scheduled-jobs.yml` stops the batch loop on `waiting`.

## Tests
New unit and route tests were added first and failed before the fix. The full vitest suite passes: 1271 passed. `tsc` is clean.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01Db5jPAyARFzweH9A3TRYP6)_

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes scheduled autopilot task selection, retry semantics, and cron batching behavior; mistakes could skip work or over-retry tasks, but scope is limited to autopilot paths with new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes task autopilot getting **stuck in `needs_you`** when chat returns a text-only **`fallback`** because no AI provider can run tools—those runs are now treated as **provider outages** to retry, not user work.
> 
> **`judgeRun`** classifies empty `fallback` replies as **`failed`** with a report prefixed by **`NO_PROVIDER`**. **`recordRun`** logs *"waiting for a free AI provider"* for those cases so they **do not count** toward the three-attempt **`couldn't work on it`** limit. **`dueForRun`** now picks **`todo` and `in_progress`** tasks, **retries outage failures on the next run**, and can **re-run empty `needs_you`** outcomes (nothing verified) up to the attempt cap.
> 
> The **cron autopilot** route checks **`llmStatus()`** and returns **`{ worked: [], waiting }`** when all providers are down (no task claims). When a batch hits an outage mid-run it surfaces **`waiting`** so **GitHub Actions** stops the multi-batch loop (not only when **`worked`** is empty). Tests cover outage wait, fallback handling, and eligibility rules.
>

author: akasa-bit
body:
## 変えたこと

### 星系マップの背景
- カリーナ星雲を、北アメリカ星雲に差し替えた。
  - 元画像: NASA/JPL-Caltech、PIA13845。可視光とスピッツァーの赤外線を合成したもの。
  - 2560px に縮め、彩度 55%・明るさ 72% に落とした。上にかぶせる暗さも 0.58 から 0.5 にした。
- ≡ メニューの出典と README を更新した。

### AI の恒星への入植
- 住める惑星のない星系にも、主星を回る宇宙ステーションで入植する。適性の低い惑星より 6 光年以上近いときだけ選ぶ。
- 星系内の拡張でも、空いている恒星に宇宙ステーションを建てる。資源の多い天体が先。

### 交易路の自動拡張
- 片道の輸送量が容量の 9 割を超えると、知らせ (新しい種類「交易路」・普通の段) を出す。
  - 対象は地球の国の星系がかかわる交易路だけ。
  - 8 割を下回るまでは 1 回だけ。
- 端の星系 (A) の政府が自動で拡張する。資金が費用の 1.5 倍以上あるとき。
- 太陽系と直轄の星系の交易路は、帝国 → 交易路タブの切り替えに従う (既定はオン)。
- 稼働率を星系の欄に出した。一覧で赤にする境目は 95% から 90% に変えた。

### 兵站
- 1 艦隊は年に燃料 2・金属 1 を使う。
  - 駐留艦隊はその星系の備蓄から出す。
  - 攻撃中の艦隊と、入植していない星系の艦隊は、その国の最も近い入植星系から出す。
  - この消費は需要に数えるので、交易路で運ばれてくる。
- 備蓄で足りないぶんは、基準価格の 2 倍の資金で現地調達する。
  - 駐留艦隊は拠点の政府、攻撃中の艦隊は首都の政府が払う。
  - 資金も尽きると補給不足になる。
- 戦力の倍率 = 補給線の効き × (0.5 + 0.5 × 充足率)。
  - 補給線の効きは、拠点から 6 光年までは 1、30 光年で 0.5。
  - 艦隊戦・攻囲・海賊の撃退に効く。
- 戦力が 6 割を切った攻囲艦隊は、年に 5% ずつ脱落する。
- 補給の状態は次の場所に出す。
  - 星系の欄の軍事: 充足率
  - 帝国 → 政治タブの艦隊戦・攻囲: 両軍の戦力

### 一括建艦
- 星系の欄で 1・5・10・20 艦隊、帝国 → 軍事タブで 1・5・10 艦隊を、まとめて編成できる。
- 費用は数の倍。指令の政治力は 1 回ぶん。

## 確かめたこと
- 観戦モードで 300 年進めた (シード 3 / 7 / 11)。
  - 恒星の入植地は 22〜34 か所。入植星系は 37 / 34 / 30 から 42 / 48 / 44 に増えた。
  - 拡張された交易路は 15 / 18 本。稼働率 9 割超の交易路は 5 / 9 本から 1 / 2 本に減った。
  - 艦隊の数で重みをつけた補給の充足率は約 0.8。補給不足は、資金も収入もマイナスの小さな星系だけ。
  - 工業の稼働率と人口は、変更前とほぼ同じ。
- 戦争を直接試した。
  - 拠点まで 3 光年の攻囲は戦力 100%、12 光年の攻囲は 87% で、どちらも降伏させた。
  - 遠征の買い付けを前線の小さな星系に払わせると戦力が 43% まで落ちたので、首都が払うように直した。
- 一括編成: ボタンを押すと駐留艦隊が 3 → 8 に増えた。画面を撮影して表示を確認した。
- 回帰テストはすべてエラーなし。数値の差は、仕組みを変えたことによるもの。
  - t76・t78 は手元にテスト用データがないので走らせていない。
- ゲームの仕組みを変えたので、等価性のハッシュは変わる。

author: olety
body:
## Rows / FIX lines

- FIX-LIST 2572 (OF-535): two refusal cases left no mesh path receipt. Built.
- FIX-LIST 997 (OF-535), the L03 half: a mesh sync request now carries the machine its mesh connection proved. The comparison against the HTTP machine proof is L02's half.
- FIX-LIST 996 (OF-535): nothing built. No production device host in this repo constructs a SyncConnection or a SyncClientConfig, so there is no place to assign MeshSyncDialer. Evidence is under "New FIX lines".

## What now works, and where

- crates/oneiron-mesh-transport/src/iroh_transport.rs: the transport runs its own accept loop in place of iroh's Router. iroh's Router only logged and dropped an attempt that failed before a protocol handler saw it. Now an inbound attempt whose QUIC accept, TLS handshake or ALPN negotiation fails leaves a path receipt with no endpoint key (outcome Failed), so do an ALPN no gate serves (outcome Refused) and a TLS failure after the ALPN is known, in the gate's on_accepting. These receipts fold with the other attempts from keys no MACHINE names.
- crates/oneiron-mesh-transport/src/iroh_transport.rs: refusals folded into a machine's 60 s window are no longer lost when no later refusal comes. The tally keeps the newest folded refusal, counting them all. A timer armed by the window's first folded refusal writes it when the window ends. IrohTransport::shutdown writes every pending tally after it closes the endpoint. The timer holds the sink weakly, so it never keeps a dropped transport's vault open. A refusal after the window still writes at once and counts any tail the timer has not written yet. The fresh close row after a failed open write is unchanged.
- crates/oneiron-server/src/handler/mesh.rs: new `crate::handler::mesh::MeshProvedMachine(pub(crate) oneiron::EntityId)`, pub(crate). SyncRoute::serve inserts it as a request extension holding `connection.machine()` on every request a mesh stream carries, beside the synthetic ConnectInfo. A TCP request never has it. It is `#[allow(dead_code)]` until admission reads it.

## Outside hunks

None. Both files are L03-owned.

## Calls

- No new constant. The window-end flush uses the existing REFUSAL_RECEIPT_WINDOW (60 s). The receipt the flush writes opens the machine's next window, so a key still writes at most one refusal row a window.

## Check

`cargo check --locked --workspace --all-features` rc=0 on gce-grad at 1ff9195526638b0eaede2044eb451e292232e347 (fleet job 1017-234634-0c5e, after a signed merge of origin/main at b77764ee5). No warnings in the changed files.

author: piemh
body:
## What

CCWrapper becomes downloadable: a per-user `Setup.exe` from GitHub Releases (no admin, no .NET needed), with updates and the documents a public release needs.

- **Installer and updates (Velopack 1.2.161).** An installed copy asks once before any network request. It then checks GitHub, downloads quietly and shows **Update X ready** in the bottom bar. The update installs when the last CCWrapper window closes, or on **Restart now** (confirmed first; the same account reopens). Velopack's apply force-stops every process in the install folder, so auto-apply on start is off and the hand-off on exit happens only from the last window. A new **About** window (sidebar) has the version, the update switch and the policy links.
- **Status relay** publishes NativeAOT (1.1 MB, no runtime). A relay path with a space, `'`, `&`, non-ASCII or another shell-unsafe character uses its 8.3 short path, or the session starts without the relay. This removes README's "no spaces in the path" limit.
- **Pipeline.** `ci.yml` builds and tests PRs. `release.yml` runs on a `v*` tag: tests, self-contained publish, `vpk pack`, build attestation, `SHA256SUMS.txt`, then a **draft** release that you publish. The SignPath signing steps run only once its secrets exist. Actions are SHA-pinned, and secrets are scoped to the steps that use them. `scripts/pack.ps1` builds the same installer locally (`vpk` pinned in `.config/dotnet-tools.json`).
- **Policies:** PRIVACY, TERMS (individual publisher, Spain), CODE_SIGNING_POLICY (SignPath Foundation's required wording), SECURITY, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES (licenses checked against the actual packages). They were drafted, then reviewed with the legal plugin (compliance-check, legal-risk-assessment, review-contract). Not legal advice.

## Before the first tag

- Fill `[LEGAL NAME]` and `[CONTACT EMAIL]` in PRIVACY.md, TERMS.md, SECURITY.md and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt.

- `dotnet test -c Release`: 289/289. Build: 0 warnings. `--smoke`: exit 0, both from bin and from a self-contained publish.
- `pack.ps1 -Stage all` locally: Setup.exe 90 MB. The nupkg holds the native relay, LICENSE and notices, and no .pdb.
- Two QA rounds (Opus). Round 1 found that Velopack's default auto-apply on start would close other account windows, plus 8 smaller issues; all are fixed. Round 2: ship.

body:
### Purpose

Fix pure Python VARIANT shredding silently changing scalar types (for example, `0` to `0.0` or `2.5` to `2`) and dropping explicit JSON null fields.

Check the original Variant type and integer bounds before using typed columns. Keep incompatible values and JSON null in residual bytes, distinct from missing fields and SQL NULL. Only decimal/timestamp values retain Arrow round-trip validation for precision and overflow.

### Validation

- Variant and Variant path suites: 169 passed, 70 subtests passed (PyArrow 19.0.1, pypaimon-rust 0.4.0).
- Multi-batch Python/native and plain/shredded table comparisons check types and physical Parquet residuals. The original eight-row probe now passes 8/8 on all three paths.
- Flake8 and `git diff --check` pass.

### Benchmark

20,000 rows × 10 matching DOUBLE fields; shredding plus in-memory Zstd Parquet serialization. Python 3.11.13 / PyArrow 19.0.1; one warmup, five measured runs, rotating implementation order. All outputs are byte-identical (601,068 bytes).

| Implementation | Median |
| --- | ---: |
| Original, without correctness checks | 1.401 s |
| Previous per-scalar Arrow round trip | 3.679 s |
| Type-checked fast path | 1.425 s |

Reproduce from `paimon-python`:

```bash
git show f3f1f951db:paimon-python/pypaimon/data/variant_shredding.py > /tmp/variant-original.py
git show 88acffa0d7a2:paimon-python/pypaimon/data/variant_shredding.py > /tmp/variant-roundtrip.py
python -m pypaimon.benchmark.variant_shredding \
  --reference original=/tmp/variant-original.py \
  --reference roundtrip=/tmp/variant-roundtrip.py
```

The benchmark emits individual timings and source/output hashes. Decimal/timestamp throughput and remote table ingestion are not covered by this benchmark.

author: waledev1
body:
## Overview

This PR adds an in-memory sequential transaction queue to `Web3Context` so rapid conversions no longer collide on sequence numbers, with optimistic local sequence tracking, automatic Horizon resync + single retry on `txBAD_SEQ`, and queue status surfaced to the user.

## Related Issue


## Changes

### 🔁 Sequential Transaction Queue

* **[MODIFY]** `src/context/Web3Context.tsx`
  * Adds an in-memory FIFO queue that serializes transaction submission so rapid button presses are processed one at a time instead of racing on the same sequence number.
  * Tracks optimistic local sequence numbers per account, advancing on each queued submission and falling back to a server resync from Horizon when a sequence error is detected.
  * On `txBAD_SEQ`, resyncs the sequence from Horizon and retries the failed transaction once with the corrected sequence number.
  * Exposes queue status (pending / processing / idle) through context for consumers.

* **[MODIFY]** `src/hooks/useWeb3.ts`
  * Surfaces the queue status and submission helpers from `Web3Context` so components can reflect in-flight state.

* **[MODIFY]** `src/components/shared/Header.tsx`
  * Displays the current queue status to the user so in-flight submissions are visible.

## Verification Results

```
npm run build
✅ Type-check and build pass

Manual check:
✅ Rapid submissions queue instead of throwing collision errors
✅ txBAD_SEQ triggers Horizon resync + single retry
✅ Queue status visible in the header
```

| Acceptance Criteria | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Rapid button submissions queue gracefully instead of throwing collision errors | ✅ FIFO queue serializes submissions in `Web3Context` |
| Failed sequence errors trigger automatic resync from Horizon and single retry | ✅ `txBAD_SEQ` handler resyncs and retries once |
| Clear queue status displayed to the user | ✅ Queue status surfaced via `useWeb3` and shown in `Header` |

Closes #130

author: nikhil-sharma-b
body:
Studio UI fixes, and an SVG export that other editors can edit.

## SVG export

- **Erasing cuts the shapes** instead of nesting one mask per eraser stroke. A shape no eraser touches is written as before. A shape an eraser covers is dropped, and a hole comes out as a ring. A partly transparent eraser keeps a single mask, one level deep.
- **Each stroke is one outline** instead of one sliver per mesh triangle. Seams under 0.02 px between a stroke's pieces are closed, and points within 0.05 px of a straight line are dropped.
- **Brush art is rounded** to 2 decimals, or more when the transform stretches it, and points on a straight run are merged.
- **Brush data is left out** unless the export dialog's option keeps it.
- Polygon booleans use `@countertype/clipper2-ts` (a port of Clipper2 1.5.4, no dependencies), allowed in the engine through `.oxlintrc.json`. `clipper2-js` was tried first and looped forever on a dense eraser stroke.

On the 404 illustration:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Masks | 77, nested 73 deep | 0 |
| Path data | 933 KB | 196 KB |

Rendered in Chromium, each step stays within anti-aliasing of the export before it. Opened in Figma, the paths select and resize directly, with no masks or stray shapes (checked by hand).

## Studio

- Brush sets: one set is open at a time, the built-in set by default, and a new set opens when it is made.
- The vector brush list opens one group, on the brush in hand. It can be searched, and custom brush cards are tidier.
- The vector brush form uses the settings field layout, and the brush panels line up with the rail card at one shared height.
- Clicking a popover's trigger again closes the popover. The popover parts share its dismissal through functions rather than refs in context, which the React lint rules reject.
- Dialogs have rounded corners and popover-style scrollbars, and button focus rings are even.

## Tests

- New unit tests: `svg-erase-cut`, `svg-stroke-outline`, and pattern and scatter art rounding.
- New browser test: an erased scene renders as the masked export did.
- Locally, all 1564 unit tests and all 890 browser tests pass. One fluid painting test passed on retry; it flakes in earlier runs too.

author: delllatitude7490
body:
## Summary
- Add native Iced **Pause** controls for running/queued direct downloads, a dedicated **Paused** section, and **Resume** / Remove controls.
- Add `rdm jobs pause INSTANCE:ID`; the existing `jobs resume` alias now resumes deliberately paused work through the explicit retry path.
- Keep one active managed worker, the existing Rust service and Iced software renderer. No React/webview, new runtime service, idle-hold polling timer, managed parallelism or legacy queue migration.

## State-machine guarantees
- Commit running pause intent (`pausing: true`) BEFORE signalling the engine. Request acceptance means Pausing, not a completed drain.
- Report **Paused** only after the worker and range/checkpoint helpers have drained and the result is committed. Only then start the next FIFO job. Queued jobs pause immediately without network or output work.
- Preserve Paused across shutdown/restart/crash; committed pause intent also recovers as Paused. Never resume held work automatically.
- Resume revalidates current policy and creates a **distinct new attempt/handle at the FIFO tail**, retaining saved destination/connections/private opt-in. The old record links to the new ID; old handles and waiters cannot cancel or claim the new attempt. Duplicate resume is rejected.
- Paused/Interrupted held jobs cannot be silently evicted at the 64-record bound. Remove dismisses a hold into Cancelled history without deleting partials.
- Repeat Pause is idempotent. Explicit Cancel can override Pausing; shutdown preserves an existing pause request. Cancellation already in progress cannot become a pause. Real completed/failed outcomes racing Pause remain truthful.
- Attached CLI callers exit nonzero with a Paused message rather than claiming completion or following a new attempt automatically.

## Integrity fixes required by pause testing
- Typed engine cancellation distinguishes an intentionally drained transfer from real network/flush/sync/checkpoint errors. A set token alone no longer hides an error as Cancelled/Paused. Real sibling errors found during range drain take precedence over cancellation. Streaming cancellation flushes and syncs partial bytes before confirmation.
- Fixed the existing non-overwrite `Reuse` path: an existing final file is protected even beside valid partial/manifest state. Propagate this protection through ranged, streaming and empty-file publication, including a final file arriving during inspection. Explicit legacy interactive/overwrite behavior is otherwise unchanged; partials without a final file still resume normally.
- Actual Range resume produces exact bytes. No-range servers safely restart from zero rather than append a full response. Existing final output is not replaced. A failed final checkpoint during Pause reports Failed, not clean Paused.

## Compatibility / privacy
- Internal Rust IPC **v5**: rebuild matching CLI/service/GUI/native host together. External Firefox Native Messaging **v1** and permissions remain unchanged; no browser-side pause/resume capability added.
- SQLite **schema 2**. Existing schema-1 images are validated and migrated in place, preserving IDs, records and private inputs. Older service binaries refuse schema 2; downgrade is unsupported. Back up state while the service is stopped if needed.
- Paused jobs retain URL-bearing retry input under the same existing owner-private, **plaintext local storage** model. Not encryption or protection from same-user processes; public snapshots/logs remain URL-free. Successful/retired attempts clear private input.
- Scope remains shared-service direct HTTP/HTTPS jobs. Provider/SFTP/listing/sync and legacy `rdm queue` workflows remain separate.

## Validation completed locally
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --locked -j2`: **673 passed, 0 failed, 1 existing ignored**.
- Workspace locked build and all-target Clippy with `-D warnings`: passed.
- **10 Firefox JavaScript tests** passed.

PlantIt previously required a shared FastAPI/SQLite backend, while its placeholder authentication and unscoped records were unsuitable for public personal accounts. This change makes the frontend a static, local-first PWA: each browser profile saves its own plants, villages, photos, activity, and watering history in IndexedDB, with no data API or required login.

Changes:
- Transactional local CRUD, conflict detection, derived watering tasks, and atomic backups/restores with validation and replacement confirmation.
- Install manifest/icons, complete offline app-shell caching, user-controlled updates, storage persistence request, and backup reminders.
- Markdown imports into the real collection, one-time migration of legacy browser records, and a read-only SQLite exporter for existing server data.
- Reject remote photo URLs; add CSP and hosting header templates. Build only the static frontend for deployment, excluding the legacy backend and SQLite files.
- Add hosting/recovery instructions for plantit.guitartabsync.com and CI that produces a static build artifact.

Validation: 10 local data tests, 2 SQLite exporter tests, and 8 real Chromium browser tests passed locally. Browser checks cover UI creation/reload, offline navigation/writes/export, backup transfer with photos/history into a separate profile, invalid/cancelled restores, Markdown import, unavailable storage, legacy migration, and a mobile viewport. The offline check also passed after the final worker-cache change. git diff --check passed.

Deployment limits: not deployed to Hostinger. Test an actual Safari/iPhone installation and verify HTTPS/headers on the selected static host before public launch. Collections are per browser and origin, with no automatic sync or app-level encryption; backups are unencrypted. The legacy Python backend remains in the repository for recovery and must not be exposed publicly.

author: brunoboto96
body:
Part of #556

## What
`scout_attach` with a saved sign-in decides whether it landed on a sign-in page (`⚠ AUTH FAILED`) by watching the address until it holds still for 400 ms. An app that sends a signed-out visitor to sign-in from its scripts some time after load, or whose sign-in page answers slowly, was read before the address changed. A stale profile then passed as signed in, and the run tested a signed-out app. A Windows CI failure of `auth loss: attach detects a storage state that did not sign in` on #599 had this shape.

- `settle.ts`: `stableUrlOf` takes a quiet window and a `navigating()` check. `InFlightRequests.navigating(frame)` is true while the frame's latest navigation request is open. It stays true for up to `NAVIGATION_COMMIT_GRACE_MS` (500 ms) after that request finishes without failing, until the frame commits it. A failed or aborted navigation clears at once. A 204 or a download clears after the grace. A new redirect hop counts as on its way.
- An attach with a storage state watches with `ATTACH_URL_QUIET_MS` (1000 ms) instead of 400 ms. Every `stableUrl` caller waits while a main-frame navigation is on its way, up to the existing 3 s cap. Those callers are the attach verdict, a navigation's bounce verdict, and the check after a submit-style click that sent nothing.
- The Signing-in guide and a changeset describe the change.

## Cost
An attach with a saved sign-in on a page that stays put takes about 0.6 s more: the quiet window is 1000 ms instead of 400 ms. Locally, chromium measured 750 ms on main and about 1350 ms with this change. An attach without a sign-in is unchanged, and so is a page with nothing on its way. A wait of close to zero is not possible here: no signal tells a page that is stable apart from one whose guard fires 600 ms after load, short of waiting that long.

## Tests
- Smoke `auth loss`, contrastive pairs. `gated-late.html` redirects to sign-in 600 ms after load: a stale profile gives AUTH FAILED, and a profile that signs in (same page) attaches cleanly. `gated-slow-login.html` redirects at once to a sign-in page the server answers after 3.5 s: AUTH FAILED when stale, clean when signed in. On main, three checks fail: both stale cases are passed as signed in, plus the landed-on wording. Ran on chromium, firefox and webkit after merging main, 18/18 each. The `action results` suite also passed on chromium (25/25).
- `settle-test`: `keepWatchingUrl` with `navigating` and with `quietMs`, as contrastive pairs. `stableUrlOf` waits out a navigation in flight and takes the quiet window it is given. `InFlightRequests.navigating` covers in flight, committed, finished but not committed (within the grace), a 204 after the grace, aborted, and redirect hops.
- `npm run build`, `typecheck:scripts`, `format`, `guide-test`, `hygiene-test`.

author: sumansaurabh
body:
## Summary

Until now the server had one coarse rule: the shared server token could do anything, and any other signed-in caller could do everything to its own sandboxes. This PR gives every API route a named permission (read, read secrets, write, exec, audit, metrics, fleet admin, cluster internal) and gives the four built-in roles (viewer, runner, auditor, admin) their permission sets, so a read-only token really is read-only. Nothing an existing caller sees changes: the shared server token and the managed control plane keep exactly today's access and today's error bodies, and tests pin those bodies byte for byte.

This is task **T2** of the identity-and-access stack (plan PR #734, `plans/identity-and-access.md` §7). It sits on T1, identity/01-principal-authenticate (PR #739), which sits on T0b (PR #738) and the plan branch. No credential that can hold a non-default role exists yet (T3 adds `avm_` tokens, T6 adds SSO), so the role behaviour here is exercised through test authenticators; with identity off this PR changes no response for any caller.

## Repo impact map (mandatory)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    API["HTTP API + facades: v1, Daytona, E2B, Runloop, /mcp, dashboard (pkg/api)"] -->|"changed: every route registered through Route(perm, h)"| ROUTE["Route + 403 writers (pkg/api/apihttp)"]
    ROUTE -->|"new: Permission, role table, Can, HostCapable, DenyHint"| CP["controlplane seam (pkg/controlplane)"]
    ROUTE -->|"new: ErrorResponse.required_permission, role"| MODELS["Wire types (pkg/models)"]
    API -->|"unchanged calls"| SVC["Service layer (internal/service)"]
    SVC -->|"changed: four gates ask hostCapable, not !scoped"| CP

    classDef touched fill:#ffd54f,stroke:#f57f17,color:#000;
    class API,ROUTE,CP,MODELS,SVC touched
```

## What changed

- `pkg/controlplane/permission.go` (new) — the §5.3 permission set (`Permission`, `PermSandboxRead` … `PermClusterInternal`, pseudo-permission `PermAuthenticated`), the role table, `Access.Can`, `Access.HostCapable` / `HostCapable(ctx)`, `LeastRoleFor`, and the D9 hint `DenyHint`.
- `pkg/api/apihttp/route.go` (new) — `Router.Route(perm, h)` / `RouteBy(tag, classify, h)`: authenticate → authorize → audit seam (`AuditHook`, for T5). `RouteHandler` carries its permission so a test can find untagged routes. `WriteForbidden` and `Denial.Message` are the 403 text for every surface. `apihttp.RequireOperator` is removed.
- `pkg/api/v1/routes.go`, `pkg/api/daytona/routes.go`, `pkg/api/e2b/routes.go`, `pkg/api/runloop/routes.go`, `pkg/api/server.go`, `pkg/api/dashboard.go` — all 141 non-public routes now go through `d.Route(perm, …)` (or the server's `route` for `/mcp` and the dashboard metrics). `withAuthOperator` and its file are deleted. Runloop classifies each call from the same `devboxActions` table its hand router dispatches on.
- `pkg/api/v1/handlers.go`, `pkg/api/v1/cluster_handler.go`, `pkg/api/v1/audit_limit.go`, `pkg/api/e2b/handlers.go` — the places that read `Access.Fleet` but meant "operator power" now ask a permission: capacity inventories and storage retirement need `fleet.admin`; a fleet-wide non-operator gets its own audit-read rate bucket; the E2B detail hides the envd token from a caller without `sandbox.exec`.
- `internal/service/owner_scope.go`, `service.go`, `isolate.go`, `custom_domains.go`, `dns_verify.go` — `hostCapable(ctx)` replaces `!scoped` on exactly the four D3/D7 gates; `requireVisibleSnapshot` stays on fleet visibility.
- `pkg/models/types.go` — `ErrorResponse` gains `required_permission` and `role` (`omitempty`, set only for token and OIDC callers).
- Tests: the registry test (`pkg/api/route_registry_test.go`), the per-role matrix over every route, per-surface 403 hint and L8 byte tests (`pkg/api/route_hint_test.go`), the `hostCapable` gate table and the `ownerScope` call-site test (`internal/service/host_capable_test.go`, `internal/service/owner_scope_callsites_test.go`).

## How to review

### ✅ Quick start (≈ 97 min)

| # | Commit | What it does (plain words) | Review with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `6ac33fae` | The permission list, which role holds what, the "may use host powers" rule, and the wording of the "ask an admin for…" hint | Part 3 · Steps 1, 2 |
| 2 | `56d8d460` | Every route now declares its permission and checks it after sign-in; the operator-only wrapper is gone; the registry, matrix and 403-body tests | Part 3 · Steps 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 |
| 3 | `c3db18cf` | The four host-level powers ask the new rule instead of "is this caller scoped?" | Part 3 · Steps 8, 9 |
| 4 | `a025a65c` | A benchmark of the per-request cost of the permission check | Part 0 |

Start with Step 3 (⭐): it is the one function every request passes through. The long `routePermissions` map in `pkg/api/route_registry_test.go` is the route → permission table to check against §5.3; it is pinned on purpose. This PR's base is T1's branch identity/01-principal-authenticate (PR #739), not `main`.

### Part 0: The change in one picture

Think of the building pass again. T1 printed the holder's name and role on every pass. This PR puts a sign on every door saying which role may open it, and the guard now reads the sign. The master key (server token) still opens every door except the machine room, which only the cluster's own nodes enter, exactly as before.

| | Before (base fe956aeec418e4e88a0498da5016c52a57441acb) | After (this branch) |
|---|---|---|
| Routes that declare what they need | 0 of 146 (only "signed in" or "operator") | 141 of 146; the 5 others are the public allowlist (GET /health, GET /ui, GET /ui/, and the E2B runtime proxy /e2b/runtime and /e2b/runtime/) |
| A route registered without auth | silently fleet-wide (H4) | `TestRouteRegistry` fails |
| Refused cells in `TestRolePermissionMatrixOverRoutes` (route × sample request) | n/a | viewer on a team 129, runner on a team 54, viewer on every team 128, runner on every team 53, auditor 127, admin 29 (only `cluster.internal`), managed runner 54, managed viewer 129, server token 29 (only `cluster.internal`, as before) |
| 403 body, managed caller on `GET /v1/templates` | `{"error":"operator authorization required"}` | identical bytes |
| 403 body, server token on `POST /v1/cluster/internal/apply` without a peer certificate | `cluster internal endpoint requires mTLS` (text/plain) | identical bytes |
| Added cost per request (`BenchmarkRouteAuthorize`, Apple M1 Max, `-benchtime 2s -count 3`) | — | 46.1–46.6 ns/op, 0 allocs |

### Part 1: Dictionary

- **Permission:** the verb a route needs, e.g. `sandbox.exec` (§5.3 permissions table).
- **Role:** viewer, runner, auditor or admin; a fixed set of permissions (§5.3 roles table).
- **Binding / team:** which owners a role reaches: one team (`team:payments`) or every team (`*`, `Access.Fleet`).
- **Fleet scope:** `Access.Fleet`: the caller sees every owner. After this PR it means only that, never "operator".
- **Host-capable:** may use host-level powers (raw host mounts, `file://` bundle refs, trusted DNS path). Operator, node, internal calls and admin only.
- **Principal kind:** `operator` (server token), `node` (a cluster peer), `controlplane` (managed), `token` (T3), `oidc` (T6), `system`.
- **D9 hint:** the 403 text "role viewer on team payments cannot sandbox.exec; ask an admin for role runner on team payments", for token and OIDC callers only.
- **L8:** founder rule: identity off, the server token and managed callers behave exactly as today.
- **Registry test:** registers every route into a recording mux and fails on any route without a permission tag.
- **Audit seam:** `apihttp.AuditHook` / `Server.audit`, the hook T5 fills with per-call audit records.

### Part 2: How the request flows

```
client → loggingMiddleware → clusterControlHeaderGuard → mux
  → RouteHandler (Router.build)                       ← NEW: the only way a route is mounted
      → withAuth / authenticate (T1)                    unchanged: 401s
      → authorize(perm)                                 ← NEW: 403 via the

author: gafferongames
body:
Glenn (2026-10-17): "What can we do to stop this repeated cards getting stuck?" Fixed at the source, so the coordinator stops releasing these by hand.

## 1. Rule 2 broken by the machine itself
**Cause:** `internal/sprint/seat_answers.go:457` (TickDecisionDefaults, "hold with cause"). When a bound judgment went unanswered for twice its deadline, the server moved a **ready** primary to waiting. A ready primary at its bound usually has a withdrawn work card, so `check.go:124` broke rule 2 on the machine's own step. After every manual release the bound was raised again and parked again 20 minutes later. This hit a11-defs-worker-answers, a13-models-tablemodel-dual-read, rocketnet-loopback-driver-backend and roadmap-tables-ideas-script. The log line "waits: a sentinel was put in front of it by the machine" was this move to waiting.
**Fix:** a ready primary is now held in place. It stays ready, and the hold keeps it out of every deal (dealPlan and TickDeal both check IsHeld). Release clears the hold where the card stands. `lifecycle.go` now treats an in-place release as exact, and `DefaultHeldDecisions` and the where frame list ready holds too. A review primary is still parked in waiting.
**Model:** `tla/SprintTables.tla`. A new invariant `Rule2Withdrawn` says a withdrawn work card's primary is ready, or waiting on an unlanded need, or resolvable by the tick's resolve. `DecisionParkStep` now holds a ready primary in place. There is a new reversed witness `parkmoves` (`MCSprintTablesBrokenParkMoves.cfg`), and TLC finds its counterexample in 4 states: withdraw, then park. `AddMove` now matches `steps_work.go:493`: a ready card with a withdrawn work card is never pulled behind a stop. Rule2Withdrawn was also added to `MCSprintTables.cfg` and `MCSprintTablesDecisionParking.cfg`.

## 2. Stale gate-needs judgment
**Cause:** the deal raised "no member up satisfies a card's GATE-NEEDS" as a note in its own plan (`steps_work.go:1238`, `deal.go` gateNeedsJudgment). That note was outside the tick's `notify`, so nothing ever closed it. During the v1.5.0 restart at 13:37Z, all members went down when their beats lapsed, and studio beat first. It stayed open for 35+ minutes after the Linux members came back, holding 4 cards and 25 behind them.
**Fix:** `TickDeal` now judges this as a `notify` cond (`gateNeedsNow`, which uses the same pool as dealPlan). It is raised while no pool member carries the need, closed in the same tick one does, and its text is updated in place. The open judgments already in the live store close on the first tick after deploy.
**Model:** `tla/JudgmentRetire.tla` has `GateClosedAfterTick` and `GateRaisedAfterTick`, with reversed witness `gate_stays`.

## 3. Mixed-version fleet
There is no wire or record change. No beat or facts code changed between v1.4.8 and main (`git diff v1.4.8 main` shows nothing in `presence.go`, `store/presence.go` or `live.go`). The v1.5.0 server read the v1.4.8 members' facts: the 13:40:11Z judgment lists every Linux member with `linux` in its facts. That judgment read "no member up satisfies GATE-NEEDS linux" because `gateNeedsWhy` always named `needs[0]`. The card (f3dl-perf-scalar-oracle-regen) needs `linux, x86-64`, and members carry `amd64`. The why now names the need no member carries, or the needs together.

## Tests (red on base, green here)
- `TestDecisionDefaultHoldsAWithdrawnReadyPrimaryInPlace`: red on base with the production text "rule 2: s1-1.w1 is withdrawn and its primary s1-1 is waiting, not ready or waiting on an unlanded need".
- `TestAGateJudgmentClosesInTheTickItsCauseEnds` and `TestGateNeedsWhyNamesTheNeedNoMemberCarries`: red on base.
- `TestDecisionDefaultParksBoundAtTwiceDeadline` and `TestABoundJudgmentUnansweredRaisesTheSeatNotAnsweringOnce` were updated to expect a ready primary held in place.
- `make test` is green on hulk. All tests use the in-memory store with time passed as an argument.

## TLC (hulk)
judgment-retire group: 4/4 pass (bounded). sprinttables group: 33/33 pass, recorded with `--manual`. `MCSprintTables.cfg` already times out at the 110s budget in the nightly run on main (run 39002863199). The new model is smaller than the old: 1,151,546 distinct states against 1,277,746, and 278s against 299s with 2 workers, timed side by side.

author: jeremyung
body:
Restructures the engine and web code in response to the 2026-10-16 architecture review, before parallel work starts. Item-by-item status is in `specs/architecture-refactor-plan.md`.

## What changed

**Engine**
- `lib.rs` goes from 22,944 to 87 lines. Code moves into `core/`, `world/`, `infrastructure/`, `population/`, `transit/` and `persistence/`; unit tests move to `src/tests/`, experiments to `src/experiments/`.
- Retired planners move to `src/legacy/` and compile only with the new `legacy` feature (master-plan acceptance hasn't passed). **Behaviour change:** production builds reject saves that have no master plan.
- `WorldState` is split into `network`, `land`, `construction`, `people`, `transit` and `legacy` sub-states, flattened into saves so existing saves and fixtures still load.
- String kinds and stages are enums, including traveler/resident activity, routine and transfer.
- Cargo workspace: a pure `city-plan` crate and a thin `city-wasm` bindings crate.
- `step_one()` runs a declared system registry (`core/systems.rs`).

**Web**
- `render/city.ts` goes from 3,025 to 1,455 lines: roads, landscape and actors layers, plus a `RenderLayer` registry (`render/layers.ts`).
- `kit.ts` is split by building family; anchor building and framing move out of `director.ts`.
- `main.tsx` passes the renderer a `CameraRig`. Audio scene assembly moves to `app/` and optics math to `optics/`, so `render/` no longer imports `camera/` or `audio/`.
- Snapshot types and movement-buffer constants are generated from Rust (`npm run types`, written to `web/src/generated`).
- The architecture review route is dev-only and absent from production builds.

**Repo and CI**
- New docs: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `validation/STATUS.md`. Dated notes move from the specs and README to `validation/spec-notes/` and `validation/archive/`.
- One-off rustfmt and Prettier passes, listed in `.git-blame-ignore-revs`.
- CI now runs the format check, an import-boundary lint (dependency-cruiser), a 1,500-line file limit, a generated-type drift check, and a legacy WASM build for the tests that need it.
- `scripts/` is sorted into folders; test inputs move to `tests/fixtures/validation/`.
- 841 bulk evidence files under `validation/` are no longer tracked. No history rewrite.

## Validation
- After each engine refactor: saves, snapshots and movement buffers matched main's WASM over 120,000 ticks on seeds 87231, 5 and 0 (saves compared as canonical JSON once flattening reordered keys), and saves round-trip unchanged.
- 504 engine tests pass (76 in `city-plan`); 731 web tests pass.
- After each renderer change: a WebGL screenshot in headless Chromium matched main.
- A clean checkout passes the full CI sequence and leaves the tree unchanged.

## Not in this PR
- **Typed IDs (#9):** typing `Road.id` alone causes 153 cascading errors. Adopt one ID type at a time. Generation counters aren't needed because IDs come from one counter and are never reused.
- **Owner-only state APIs (#6/#7):** sub-state fields are still `pub(crate)` and domain code is still `impl Engine`.
- **Splitting `director.ts` by mode (#22).**
- **Behaviour changes (#12–#16, #18):** bucketing, the structural commit point, the event queue, data definitions, the routing service, snapshot deltas.
- **CODEOWNERS (#28):** waits for a second contributor.

## Merge notes
- Open branches will conflict heavily. Run `npm run format` on each before rebasing.
- The local tag `evidence-2026-10-16` keeps the untracked evidence and is not pushed.

## What changed
- **Market Street (Game mode):** the Marketplace is a painted street instead of a card grid. Skyline behind, fountain square with Sal's counter and a new Hype tent, stalls standing in districts (In range, Near your price, Further off, The fog lane for stores with no price of yours), lamps, trees, crates and a bench between districts, a gate at the bottom. Each stall is a real link with a printed plate: name, ticker, tone flag plus word and signed gap, price against yours, the five gate pips, verdict. `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint` (0 errors), `vitest` (92 files, 884 tests) and a production build, all on Faiz's folder before rebasing onto main. author: its-applekid
body:
Closes #4950

#### Context

A shared GitHub budget hold can prevent the main-CI fixer from filing a ticket, leaving a red main run without an automated repair task.

#### TL;DR

A shared-budget hold returns without sleeping; the next MainWatch poll retries under the same dedup key.

#### Summary

- Retry a held create on the next MainWatch poll without blocking the current poll.
- Report holds through `system.main.fixer.held`; ordinary create errors use `system.main.fixer.failed`.
- Verify a hold followed by a later successful poll files exactly one ticket.

#### Alternatives

- MainWatch already polls periodically, so a timer or in-call wait is unnecessary. The existing dedup key is reused on each poll and its receipt is written only after successful creation.

#### Complexity routing

- Signal: untagged, initially treated as complexity:3
- Skills used: `aiur-agent`; `ce-code-review` self-review before handoff
- Rationale: the issue has no complexity label, but the change is contained to one existing subsystem and its mirror test.
- Adjustment: treated as complexity:2 after inspecting the implementation surface; skipped planning overhead.

#### Docs

- [x] Docs not required — this restores the already-documented behavior that dispatch retries shared-budget holds.

Closes #656

## 変更内容
- `backend/app/services/weapon_master_sync_service.py` を追加しました。`sync_weapon_master` が武器マスターの値をコピー先へ反映し、変わった値を集計して返します。commit はしません。
- `backend/scripts/maintenance/sync_weapon_master.py` を追加しました（CLI）。既定は読み取りのみで、`--apply` を付けたときだけ書き込みます。`--weapon-id` / `--fields` で対象を絞れます。

| 同期先 | 同期のしかた |
|---|---|
| `player_weapons.base_snapshot` | マスターの値で上書きする。`custom_stats` は触らない |
| `mobile_suits.weapons`（購入した武器のスロット） | `resync_mobile_suit_weapons` で作り直す |
| `mobile_suits.weapons`（初期装備のスロット） | `power` を含めてマスターの値で上書きする |
| `master_mobile_suits.specs.weapons` | マスターの値で上書きする |
| `ace_pilots` | 更新しない。差分の件数だけを表示する |

- 読み取りのみの実行では `no_autoflush` の中で変更を作って rollback するので、DB に書き込みません。
- `base_snapshot` の description と docs（`weapon-data-model.md`、`backend/CLAUDE.md`、`scripts/maintenance/README.md`）を「武器マスターに追従するスペック」に直しました。

- 購入した武器のスロットは、バトルエントリー時と同じ resync で作り直します。`--fields` で絞っても、未反映だった値は変わることがあります（出力に出ます）。#657 のバグにより、そのスロットに機体強化（`weapon_power`）で足した威力もここで消えます。この挙動はエントリー時と同じです。
- 初期装備のスロットに機体強化で足した威力も消えます（#656 で決めた方針）。`weapon_power` の扱いは #657 で直します。
- `base_snapshot.power` が変わると、武器改造の上限（base 値に対する倍率）も新しい値を基準にします。

## 確認
- `tests/unit/test_weapon_master_sync.py`（8件）: 読み取りのみで DB が変わらないこと、`--apply` 相当で4つの同期先が直ること、`custom_stats` が保たれること、2回目は差分なしになること、フィールドの絞り込み、エースパイロットは数えるだけで更新しないこと、不正な ID・フィールドのエラー
- `tests/unit` 全体: 1352 passed, 1 xfailed, 1 xpassed
- ruff / mypy: エラーなし
- 本番 DB には未実行です。実行するときは、読み取りのみの実行結果を確認していただいてから `--apply` します。

body:
## G5b: source-first Gefest document persistence (stacked on #34)

Implements a bounded, versioned **G5ProjectArchive v1** for the real four-shell Box-minus-upright-Cylinder family:

- Persist only canonical primitive source parameters, complete current/Undo/Redo state records and G4c result volume evidence. No unserialized B-rep graph or render mesh is trusted.
- Restore all historical committed B-reps by re-running G4b2b3b source intersections and **independent G4c certification** before reopening the document. Old scoped handles are never serialized or revived.
- Explicit typed feature DAG (`source_a`, `source_b`, `difference`) with 177 output semantic topology names and producing-operation references; validated on load even when the output exists only in a Redo state.
- Versioned, size-bounded JSON schema and strict rejection of unknown fields, corrupted provenance or altered source material evidence.
- `save_atomic` writes a temporary file in the destination directory, fsyncs it and renames only after full archive/source validation; `load_file` performs bounded read and independent reconstruction.
- New stateless `geometry.v1` `g5_project` CLI operation accepts either new source operands or a returned project archive; supports commit/undo/redo/reopen/source-replace actions. Results return the entire archive for a later separate-process request.
- Integration tests cover real file replacement and error-preserving paths, archive tampering, source changes, Undo/Redo after reopen, regenerated scoped handles, feature DAG and cross-process CLI JSON handoff.

**Scope:** bounded original analytic four-corner Boolean; not a general Gefest UI integration, arbitrary NURBS support, crash-durable multi-file transaction or distributed locking.

**CI status:** verified, see below. No changes to `main`, G5a PR #34 or previous WAI project checkouts.

## Verification — G5b

- [RustSolid CI run 39043359389](https://github.com/boltholds/rustsolid/actions/runs/39043359389): **SUCCESS** at commit `8149f819a03c3be73cae55c11f72c810bfb0357b`.
- **7/7 project archive integration tests** passed: versioned source-rebuilt snapshots, real disk file rename and load, 177 semantic DAG bindings, historic Undo/Redo after reopen, input edit replay, corrupt schema/graph/mass and write error rejection.
- **3/3 separate-process geometry.v1 CLI integration tests** passed: project JSON handoff, Undo/Reopen/Redo persistence, malformed provenance failure without partial geometry disclosure.
- Existing RustSolid regression, release compilation and CLI smoke suite all pass.
- G5b contract: `docs/gefest-g5b-persistent-document-v041.md`.
- Scope explicitly excludes crash-durable cross-platform replacement guarantees, database ACID, distributed locking, and the separate Gefest UI's feature-graph integration.

## Summary

```diff
 Project::load(judged)
   parse the judged files, keep them
-  parse every other file, keep it
+  for every other file: cache.found(language, source, || rules::find(parse(file)))   # then let the file go

 duplicate::judge(node)
-  shape(node) again, look the shape up
+  the group the index gave the function starting at this byte
```

.git/orcrist-cache/<16 hex>.json    # one file's findings: key = its content, language, `smallest`, the binary
```

- Only a real folder is used: none where `orcrist-cache` is a link or a file. Only plain files named `<16 hex>.json` or `.<pid>.writing` are read, written (`create_new`, then renamed) or let go.
- A function's shape is kept as a 64-bit hash: alike by chance one in 2^64; a function written to collide costs a wrong finding.
- `restating-comment` finds the code's line from where the code starts, not by counting lines from the top.

## Evidence

Django, 559,000 lines, judging one file:

| | Before | Cache cold | Cache warm |
|---|---|---|---|
| release | 3.9 s, 805 MB | 2.2 s, 150 MB | 0.49 s, 72 MB |
| debug | 5.1 s | 3.2 s | 0.89 s |

Findings byte for byte the same on this repository, on Django whole, and on the four projects of `precision/check.sh` (exit 0). Tests: a file changed since is read again; an entry that cannot be read is found again; entries unused for a week are let go; nothing is kept or let go through a link, nor anything orcrist did not write (against the cache before that fix, the test's `precious.txt` was deleted).

`cargo test`: 55 passed; clippy and fmt clean. Argonath: 0 of 19 kept runs changed, as a change that keeps every finding should; `/code-review medium` and `/security-review` pass.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** `.git`

Every run in a repository now writes `.git/orcrist-cache`; deleting it costs one slower run.

Known gaps, minor, left for #76: an `orcrist-cache` that already exists is used without checking its owner or mode, and entries are written with the default umask, so the README's "its owner's alone" holds only when orcrist made the folder; no kept run can see the cache, its output being the same by design.

## Purpose
Improve genuine reader value in the AdSense quality-repair workstream; no automatic review flags are forcibly cleared and no new doorway pages are published.

## Original editorial work
- 42 separately written problem/decision/verification examples across **14 high-intent existing service guides**: NIS passport renewal/tracking, NIMC DOB amendment/SIM linkage/slip reissue, JAMB profile code/CAPS, WAEC/NECO results, BVN retrieval, CAC business-name/company registration, and NYSC Senate list/call-up letters.

- The content is not presented as interviews, first-hand tests, a new agency verification date, or a promise that fees/forms/approvals are current.
- Preserves official source citations and date from the underlying guide. Readers are explicitly directed to the original issuer for current requirements.

## Surface changes
- Server-side source-aware component renders only on these 14 guides, with conditional quick navigation and accessible, mobile-first layout.
- Tests assert 14 authentic records, 42 complete, distinct decisions and valid next-guide routes; CI invokes the focused checks.

## Checks / approval
Run `npx tsx --test tests/service-original-decisions-20261017.test.ts`, TypeScript / content / publication audits and browser/Cloudflare smoke in CI. This is a first scoped batch of original material, not a claim that all ~1,300 indexable pages have been individually evaluated or that Google has approved AdSense.

author: kingyx3
body:
## What changed
- **#116 retrieval permissions (source level).** The owner's `classification` now limits who a Tier 0 text source may answer. `public` and `internal` (the default for an unlabelled source, and what the reference rules use) ground any answer, so existing workspaces are unchanged. `confidential` grounds only a verified, mapped team member; a public caller, a customer's email or a call with no attributed person gets no documents and the reason `source-members-only`. `restricted` is not served by the built-in store to anyone (`source-restricted`), because Tier 0 has no document-level permissions. The asker's standing comes from the sidecar's own principal, never from an argument (`kb_search` has no parameter that asks for more), and an unattributed call counts as public (fail closed).
- **#116 locale and freshness.** A `text-file` source may carry `locale`; `kb.search` takes an optional `locale` (matched on the language part; an unlabelled source matches every request). Each returned section carries `freshness` (effective date, `reviewBy`, `reviewInDays`, `reviewSoon` within 14 days) and its locale.
- **#111 readiness.** A Skill whose only knowledge source is `restricted` reports `no-content` with a specific remediation (connect a provider with document-level permissions, or lower the classification after review). `knowledge-check.py --classification` warns at upload who a source could not answer.
- **#117 Scenario A** gains the "restricted page" case: a confidential or restricted source never grounds a reply to a customer's email; the sender is handed to a person and no draft is written.
- Schema (`locale`), capability catalogue (`kb.search` `locale`), `docs/contracts.md`; `VERSION` 0.8.30.

## Validation
- `make contracts tests` (1735 tests OK, incl. new `tests/test_knowledge_permissions.py`: access matrix, readiness agreement, freshness boundaries, locale, sidecar principal handling, no access-widening argument, schema/catalogue), receptionist evals PASS, `py_compile`, `bash -n scripts/*.sh`, bandit `-ll` clean. `make hermes` needs network and was not run locally; CI covers it.

## Compatibility
- Additive for existing workspaces: the default classification (`internal`) behaves as before, and the optional `locale` argument and `freshness` field are new. A client that already labels a text source `confidential` or `restricted` will see it stop answering public callers; that is the point of the label.
- Not done: per-document permissions, cache/index invalidation on revocation, external knowledge providers, semantic conflicts, live evidence. Freshness reports declared dates only.
