author: teemow
body:
Fixes https://github.com/giantswarm/giantswarm-repo-manager/issues/234

## Problem

The release step reported `red-release` when the only failed job of a tag pipeline was `publish-github-release`, although the GitHub release and the gsoci image existed (app-catalog-cleanup-tool `v0.3.0`). auto-release creates the GitHub release before the pipeline runs, so that job fails because the release is already there. It runs after every artifact is pushed, so the failure leaves nothing unpublished.

## Solution

- Bump devctl to v8.140.0, which exports this rule as `reconcile.UnpublishedJobs` (https://github.com/giantswarm/devctl/pull/2800, the fix for https://github.com/giantswarm/devctl/issues/2798).
- `statusesReleaseStep` (the release step from the tag commit's statuses) drops the failed contexts whose job leaves nothing unpublished. A release red only in `publish-github-release` reads built and names the job: `…; publish-github-release failed, the GitHub release it publishes exists`.
- The release watch (`ReadTagPipeline`) follows a repository's latest GitHub release, so the same rule applies there: a failed workflow whose failed jobs are only `publish-github-release` counts as green. Without this, the watch would still settle such a release red and tell the team.
- A red artifact job (`push-to-registries-release`), with or without `publish-github-release`, is still `red-release`. A tag with no pipeline or no status is still `missed-tag-build`.
- devctl v8.140.0 also changed `reposetup.Remote.Person`: it now checks only the teams it is given and no longer lists the caller's teams. The server called it without teams, so after the bump every caller would have had no teams, which breaks scope `mine` and the team guards (the e2e suite fails on the bump alone). `person` now lists the caller's org teams itself, as devctl did before. The login was already verified on the request.

## Proof

- New cases in `TestStatusesReleaseStep`: the app-catalog-cleanup-tool v0.3.0 shape (red only in `publish-github-release`, image job green) reads `ok` / built with no finding. Red in `push-to-registries-release` plus `publish-github-release` is still `red-release`, naming the artifact job.
- New cases in `TestReadReleaseDecidesFromTheTagPipeline`: the watch settles the v0.3.0 shape `built`. A red artifact job beside it settles `red`.
- `go test ./...` passes, including `internal/e2e`, which fails on the devctl bump without the `person` change. `golangci-lint run` reports 0 issues.
- Live: v0.3.0 is no longer app-catalog-cleanup-tool's latest release (v0.4.1 is, and it reads `release ok … built`), so v0.3.0 cannot be read live again. The test cases above reproduce it. After the roll, `devctl repo status` is checked to still read the release step correctly, and the team guards (scope `mine`) are checked to still resolve the caller's teams.

author: pedrolucas167
body:
## Objetivo

O README, o `BASELINE_CONCURRENCY.md` e o `SCALE_ANALYSIS.md` publicavam números de desempenho. Eles **não são reproduzíveis**, e a medição que os alimentava tem um erro aritmético. Este PR remove as afirmações que não se sustentam e corrige a medição.

Um comprador que tentar reproduzir os números falha por um fator de 106× — e depois desconfia do resto. Melhor não afirmar do que afirmar errado.

## Medição

### O throughput estava errado por 2×

Em `ScaleTest`, cada iteração envia **duas** ordens:

\\\java
Order buy  = orderService.createOrder(...); matchingEngine.submitOrder(buy);
Order sell = orderService.createOrder(...); matchingEngine.submitOrder(sell);
completedOrders.addAndGet(2);
\\\

mas o cálculo usava `totalOrders = numThreads * ordersPerThread`. A asserção do próprio teste entrega o erro:

\\\java
assertEquals(numThreads * ordersPerThread * 2, completedOrders.get());
\\\

O autor contava 200 ordens na asserção e 100 no throughput. **Todo número publicado era metade do real.**

### O cronômetro media a orquestração, não a carga

`System.currentTimeMillis()` envolvia criação do `ExecutorService`, `latch.await`, `shutdown` e `awaitTermination`. Agora mede apenas a janela de processamento, com `System.nanoTime()`.

Também corrigi os rótulos (diziam "100 ordens" onde eram 200) e removi campo/imports não usados.

## Os números não reproduzem

Medido na mesma máquina, com o código atual:

| Cenário | Publicado | Medido (4 execuções) |
|---|---|---|
| 10 threads / 200 ordens | < 100ms | 36ms–107ms |
| **50 threads / 1.000 ordens** | **50ms / 10.000 ordens/seg** | **5.063ms–5.810ms / 86–98 ordens/seg** |
| 100 threads / 2.000 ordens | < 500ms | 60ms–95ms |
| 200 threads / 4.000 ordens | 5.133ms | 5.758ms–8.724ms |
| 100 contas / 2.000 ordens | 701ms | 761ms–1.132ms |
| 1.000 contas / 20.000 ordens | 30.690ms | 23.011ms–45.592ms |

E o mesmo cenário, mesmo código, muda 8× conforme o contexto de execução:

| Cenário | Dentro da suíte | Isolado (JVM nova) |
|---|---|---|
| 50 threads / 1.000 ordens | 5.063–5.810ms | **567–779ms** |
| 10 threads / 200 ordens | 36–107ms | **292–612ms** (mais lento) |

A carga é idêntica nos dois casos; o que muda é o estado da JVM (JIT, GC). Somando: resultados não monotônicos, variância de até 3× entre execuções, e medições feitas em um processador de **4 núcleos físicos / 8 lógicos** com pools de 50 a 1.000 threads — acima de 8 threads mede-se o escalonador.

## Documentos

**`BASELINE_CONCURRENCY.md`** — foco em corretude, e correções de fatos que não batiam com o código:

- `Order` **tem** `ReentrantLock` próprio (aqui o documento acertava) ✔
- trades ficam em `ConcurrentLinkedQueue`, não `CopyOnWriteArrayList` ✘
- eram **6** testes de contas, não 5 — e `shouldMaintainConsistencyWithConcurrentMixedOperations`, citado no documento, **não existe** ✘
- "⚠️ Sem Persistência: estado não persistido entre execuções" — falso desde o journal ✘
- "1.460 operações" não corresponde ao que os testes enviam (2.600 ordens só nos cenários de trading)

**`SCALE_ANALYSIS.md`** — retira a curva de escala e o diagnóstico de gargalos. O gargalo apontado era **impossível**: o documento atribuía a lentidão das 1.000 contas a "contenção de locks" nas `Position`, mas `runConcurrentOrdersWithManyAccounts` submete uma tarefa por conta, então cada posição é tocada por uma única thread. Sem compartilhamento não há contenção. O que de fato difere nesses cenários é que todas as ordens compartilham um único símbolo (um único lock).

**`README.md`** — números removidos, aponta para os documentos. O bullet "métricas documentadas em cada experimento" virou "métricas instrumentadas", que é o que de fato existe (`MetricsCollector`, `LoadTestResult` com p50/p95/p99).

## O que NÃO mudou

- Nenhuma asserção de conclusão foi removida ou enfraquecida
- As garantias de corretude continuam publicadas, porque **são** válidas: atomicidade, consistência do book, isolamento de saldos/posições, ausência de deadlock
- Price-time priority segue documentada como validada pelos testes de domínio e pelo replay do journal, não pelos testes de concorrência (que não a assertavam)

## Validação

- `./mvnw -Pall-tests verify` → **76/76, BUILD SUCCESS**

## Próximo passo

Medição de desempenho com JMH (warmup, forks, repetições, mediana e dispersão) — PR seguinte, encadeado neste.

author: mazino2d
body:
## Summary

This is M6 phase P3. Until now, a dropped room socket ended the call. A dropped socket happens on a network blip, a tab in the background, or a phone screen that turns off briefly. With this change, the call keeps playing, other players see the seat as reconnecting (⏳), and the device takes its seat back when the socket returns.

Closes #56

## How it works

- **Socket drops.** Audio goes straight to the SFU, not through the socket, so the device keeps its connection.
  - The RoomDO marks the seat `reconnecting`. That happens when the socket closes, or when a new socket opens for the same player.
  - When the socket is back, the device sends `voice.resume { key }` with its own track name. The seat comes back with the same session and the same mute state, so there is no new join.
  - A seat that is not resumed within **30 s** is swept by the room alarm. The alarm is shared with the M4 timer and the idle close.
- **Media path fails** (`connectionState = failed`, for example switching from Wi-Fi to 4G). The device joins again with a new session and keeps its mute state. Other devices pull the new track because its key changes. A refused resume does the same.
- **Another tab takes the seat, or the room closes.** This device leaves the call.
- **Talking mark.** The threshold is now 0.01 (about −40 dBov), with a 600 ms hold. In the production run of #60, a fake microphone at about 0.016 never showed 🗣 under the old 0.03 threshold.
- **TURN is deferred.** Home Wi-Fi and 4G pass UDP. The plan now lists this as a risk to revisit if someone cannot connect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC18 Others see ⏳, and the device resumes with the same seat and mute state. A seat that never comes back leaves after 30 s. (integration: resume, stale key, alarm sweep; unit: `markLost`, `sweep`, `nextSweep`)
- [x] AC19 The game goes on while a player's voice is reconnecting. (integration)
- [x] AC20 After a reload, the player is back in their seat and taps **Vào voice** to rejoin. The seat waits as reconnecting in the meantime.
- [x] AC21 Leaving the room or the room closing removes the player from the call. (P2 tests)

The "within 10 s" part of AC18 is measured after deploy with the headless Chromium run.

## Tests

`npm run check` passes: 211 tests.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: frank-reichenbach
body:
## Summary

The routing evaluation ran once, 486 sessions across Claude Code and Codex. Two Codex reads of the candidate skill reported not-run because the model read it with one `cat` of several files, and checking a fix to the observer would otherwise need another live run. This branch counts such reads, adds an offline re-judging of recorded routing runs, and records the evaluation.

## Changes

- Runtime: a Codex read counts when one `cat` names the candidate's `SKILL.md` as its first file and the output starts with that file's whole text. Option-like words after the first file, standard input, pipes, redirections and other readers still report not-run. README's Codex gap entry says so.
- Runtime: `judge_run` holds `activation_case`'s verdict on a finished run, unchanged, so a recorded run can be judged again under its own workspace path.
- Tools: `live_runs.rescore` and `tools/rescore_routing.py` re-judge a recorded routing or routing-smoke run without launching anything. Recorded case streams bind to the results in launch order; a run whose streams do not bind one to one is refused. The output, `rescored.json`, keeps each recorded result and names the scorer revision and the hash of the skill files matched.
- Evals: `evals/canaries/results/routing-2026-10-17.md` and its index record the evaluation: results re-judged at `430582c`, the misses and their causes, the observability limits, measured tokens and quota windows, and hashes of the private evidence with the recipe for the streams manifest hash.

## Decisions

- Only `cat` with the candidate first: cat prints its files in order, so the output's start is the first file's own text. A candidate later in the list, or a reader that can stop early, leaves the attribution open, as the existing single-file rule's tests require.
- Routing expectations and skill descriptions are unchanged. Codex reading harness-intake before harness-research in a workspace without a decision follows the research skill's own procedure, and Claude Code's six misses do not point at missing description wording. Changing expectations after seeing the results would change the measured question.
- Explicit `/name` and `$name` invocations stay not-run when the stream shows nothing; no trace marker is invented.
- Re-judging instead of re-running: the 243 recorded Claude Code verdicts reproduce unchanged, and four Codex verdicts change from not-run to pass.

## Tests

New tests cover multi-file `cat` reads (candidate first, a reference or another skill after it, numbered output, the shell wrapper Codex uses) and the reads that still report not-run (another skill first, a cut-off start, standard input, pipes, redirections, partial readers), re-judging a recorded run (a changed verdict, untouched recorded files, rates, scorer and skills hash), and refusing a run with a case that never launched.

author: bot-reno[bot]
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [docker.io/freikin/dawarich](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich) | minor | `1.15.3` → `1.16.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>Freika/dawarich (docker.io/freikin/dawarich)</summary>

### [`v1.16.0`](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1160---2026-10-17-Berlin)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/compare/1.15.3...1.16.0)

##### Added

- Self-hosted users with an active Pro purchase in the Dawarich mobile app now get the supporter badge. The app reports the purchase to your instance automatically; Dawarich Cloud ignores it.
- `POST /api/v1/visits` accepts an optional `address` (street, house number, postcode, city, country). A newly created place stores it, and visit responses include the place's formatted `address`, so apps can keep a visit's name and address separately.
- A visit created without an address (for example from the map's visit form) gets its place address and city looked up in the background when reverse geocoding is enabled; the name you gave is kept.
- Visit cards in the map's visit list show the place address under the visit name.
- Insights show route maps on the year cards. Pro and self-hosted instances also get a year calendar coloured by country, a country timeline and a race against the previous year's distance; Cloud Lite shows a plain activity calendar and a preview of the race.
- Search trips by name, description, places and notes; sort them and filter by year, month and country.
- A Family tab on the map (`F`) holds the family layer, the member list with each member's last known address, and a link to the family page.

##### Changed

- Achievements no longer credit any country or region for time spent in territories claimed by more than one state (Natural Earth disputed areas), and achievement cards leave those areas out; statistics, the scratch map and country attribution are unchanged. Regions lying almost entirely in such territories are no longer part of their country's set. Existing progress is recalculated in the background without notifications, and achievements already earned are kept. The upgrade loads the disputed-area boundaries and recalculates achievements once in the background; on large instances this can take a while.
- Stats and Insights are now one page at /insights; /stats and /stats/:year redirect there.
- Visitors opening `/` go to the sign-in page; the landing page is removed. Sign-in and sign-up pages are redesigned. Uptime checks that probe `/` now get a redirect; point them at `/api/v1/health`.
- The map Layers tab shows layers as tiles, with options for enabled layers below them. Anomalies show only while Points are on, and the Create button is now Tools.
- Buttons are raised and form fields recessed across the app.

##### Fixed

- Stop the onboarding and other closed modals from flashing on page load in Firefox.
- Changing the theme with a missing or unknown value now returns an error instead of crashing or saving an invalid theme.
- Merge duplicate legacy points before coordinate backfill so upgrades complete without unique constraint errors ([#​3200](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/3200)). On large instances still carrying legacy coordinates this step can take several minutes; let it finish.
- Keep MapLibre toast notifications within narrow viewports and allow map controls beneath messages to remain clickable.
- Bundled country boundaries now match their ISO 3166-2 subdivisions: achievement cards, the scratch map and country attribution follow, and affected existing points are reassigned in the background.
- Count briefly visited countries consistently in Insights, statistics, the stats API and digests even when no city meets the minimum stay threshold. ([#​3290](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/3290))
- Refresh import statuses after the live stream subscribes or reconnects, recovering updates missed before connection ([#​3174](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/3174)).
- Emoji in place, area, visit and family member names now render correctly on the map instead of a placeholder glyph ([#​2365](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/2365)).
- Update both mobile and desktop family-sharing indicators after changing location-sharing settings.
- Keep signed storage capabilities and private filenames out of request path logs.
- Prevent legacy or restored export URLs from deleting unrelated files; retain unproven legacy files after export removal or migration.
- Refuse location-sharing consent when family access expires while waiting for the request lock.
- Keep saved ZIP member imports processing when a later archive member fails validation.
- Keep notification badges, read states and deleted items current in other open tabs.
- Use safe defaults for missing user settings and refuse unsupported settings writes without replacing malformed data.
- Shared tracks hide their map and route coordinates when the owner disables route sharing, while enabled statistics remain visible.
- Only administrators can request test email, and queued test messages are discarded after the recipient loses administrator access.
- Calendar activity and status counts refresh after demo visit edits and deletion, including restored visits removed by null-island cleanup.
- Achievement sharing returns only to same-host HTTP(S) or safe relative pages and falls back for non-HTTP return URLs.
- Concurrent Cloud family invitations can no longer reserve the same final available seat; self-hosted families remain unlimited.
- Public-share unlock phrases are filtered from request parameters and query-string logs.
- Keep tied transportation modes, visit and country rankings, location-search coordinates, and Immich GPS matches deterministic.
- Clear pending two-factor challenges after successful authentication, preventing a stale challenge from switching accounts.
- Reserve transportation reclassification while its worker is queued, preventing duplicate runs from repeated requests and allowing retry after enqueue failure.
- Import progress no longer moves backwards when an older Google Takeout continuation finishes late or publishes a stale status.
- Public monthly statistics and yearly digest links show an unavailable-share message after their owner is deleted.
- Area creation and editing reject unsupported response formats before saving changes or scheduling visit relabeling.
- Account deletion confirmation can be requested again immediately if token generation or email enqueueing fails.
- Partnero signup failure diagnostics and Immich enrichment errors exclude provider-supplied credentials and customer details.
- Propagate failed monthly statistics calculations so background jobs can retry, without repeating an unread failure notification on every retry of statistics or data recalculation; digest jobs report a failed month with a single digest failure notice.
- Achievement backfills now restore historical visit dates, including previously earned regions and countries ([#​3728](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/3728)).
- Timeline calendar activity and status counts refresh after confirming or declining visits in bulk.
- Shared photo thumbnails lose their old authorization immediately when the trip dates or shared resource change.
- Protect the acting and last active administrator from deletion, and serialize administrator deletion and role changes to retain administration access.
- Prometheus metrics from web and Sidekiq no longer produce duplicate series when label order differs ([#​3769](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/3769)).
- KMZ imports no longer repeatedly re-import their own archive and fill the import queue and storage ([#​3766](https://redirect.github.com/Freika/dawarich/issues/3766)).

</details>

author: vladyslavgul-stack
body:
## Goal

After a user opens trial/plan selection from onboarding step 2, confirmed trial activation or payment now returns to the original video tab and preserves the current tour step. Cancelled/unconfirmed checkout, a closed tour/tab, another video or account leaves the user on the website with a return fallback.

## Changed Areas / Affected Planes

- [x] Web / site: checkout/login/pricing continuation and verified success UI
- [x] Extension: one-time tab/document/owner-bound navigation bridge
- [x] Shared protocol: additive navigation-only message schemas
- [x] Docs: active trial-flow stability plan
- No Worker, room events, media, database or entitlement-policy changes.

## Risk Class / Quality Gate

- High: cross-plane extension/billing navigation.
- `pnpm dev:check` passed. Generic protocol detection recommends room/P2P harnesses; those are excluded here because no room/media contract or Worker implementation changes. All consumer type checks and API/protocol unit suites pass.
- Live staging trial/payment acceptance remains required before promotion to main.

## Verification

- `pnpm check`: all six tasks passed.
- Web: 1,246 passed, six existing skips; focused checkout/pricing/trial/return suites passed.
- Extension: 2,434 passed across 149 files (`vitest run --maxWorkers=2`). A concurrent broad run exposed an existing Watch History timing-sensitive assertion; the full reduced-concurrency run passed. One intermediate run intentionally observed the new owner-race regression before the final fix.
- Protocol: 245 passed; API: 272 passed.
- Staging 0.1.3 build and artifact validator passed; narrow permissions unchanged.
- Loaded package in disposable real Chrome, offline fixtures: successful cross-origin external-port round trip focused the original video on the same step; replay, closed tour/tab, changed video and changed owner did not focus it. This is browser integration evidence, not live billing acceptance.
- Independent read-only review: owner race during storage/tab checks and stale same-URL website document were found, regression-tested and fixed; final review has no remaining important findings.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Staging / Release Notes

- Target: staging only. Main/production/Chrome Store publication excluded.
- Updated matching staging and local Store ZIPs will be recorded after deployment.
- Mixed versions fall back to existing Billing/success behavior. No automatic room creation or entitlement grant.

## Docs / Graphify

- [x] Active plan updated with the navigation contract, lifetime, fallback and rollout boundaries.
- Graphify queried before cross-plane work: `Trace checkout continuation trial activation success return extension onboarding auth handoff`.
- Full changed-plan semantic extraction completed with its source SHA; safe adapter attempted. Publication stopped before writing due to existing `Unresolved cross-source AST node: storage (wxt/utils/storage)`. Curated graph/report/manifest remain untouched; fragment/log retained locally for the graph repair.

## Security / Env Impact

- [x] No new secrets, env variables, database migration, host permissions or OAuth allowlist.
- Exact configured website origin, top frame and current owner are checked. A short external port ties the request to the live website document; abort/unload disconnects it. The source document/frame and unchanged video must still acknowledge an active tour.
- UUID is single-use, bounded to 20 session records and one hour; no video URL or account credentials leave the extension.
- Paid return requires a tab-local owner/session receipt and server confirmation of the exact completed/paid Checkout and its active subscription. Response fields are additive; no extra Stripe calls.
- Anti-abuse cookie/installation proof, atomic trial reservation, Stripe idempotency/schedules and existing auth remain authoritative.

## AI Contribution Notes

Codex implementation plus independent correctness/security review. Read operating manual, current state, architecture, plane contracts, quality gates and active trial plan. Real-account staging trial/payment round trip is still a user acceptance step before production.

## Rollback

Revert this PR on staging and reload the prior extension. No data migration rollback is needed. Keep trial/anti-abuse infrastructure unchanged; additive response fields tolerate mixed versions and absent bridges fall back on the website.

## Delivered staging evidence

Merged as `2be7000553e9a0c5510c349c20989d3f819cd339`; its tree equals tested source `acdeb8b29c3a44142e2627482a2c19eef0ad09b9`. Vercel deployment `dpl_4dqS4Y7Up6avjLUhhAR9Sn724UrR` is READY with `staging.anidachi.app` assigned. Deployment smokes passed; unauthenticated checkout remains password-gated and `noindex, nofollow`. Main remains `a8aee4641ab74bd8b7992217fdcc4302543b7d54`; promotion PR #402 stays open without auto-merge.

Both immutable 0.1.3 ZIPs passed five real-Chrome fixture cases after extraction (success/same step, closed tour, changed video, closed tab, changed owner; success also rejects replay):

- Staging SHA-256: `bff41959181988680103e8dc492dffe6b27fd08382b7d1372fc7f3ed8a29ee65`.
- Local Store candidate SHA-256: `98b44f2634af5cde40e5c3a1a32aa6571ad61a2bfaf6d7c1e63e34ba14c316c0`.

body:
Editor stili, PR 6 di 6, sopra la #582. **Solo i file della migration (due): non applicata.** Si applica su staging insieme a Lorenzo, dopo l'unione delle PR 1-5.

**Cosa fa** `20261017200000_system_style_editor_stili.sql`
1. Gli stili di sistema **mai ritoccati** (versione in uso con config identica alla predefinita di `20260408320000`, viola `#6366f1` su bianco) ricevono una versione nuova (`version` + 1) con la config dello stile pronto «CataloGlobe»; `current_version_id` punta alla nuova. La vecchia resta in «Versioni di prima». Gli stili ritoccati dal locale non si toccano (D128 per Lorenzo).
2. `handle_new_tenant_system_group()` crea lo stile di sistema dei tenant nuovi con la config nuova. `REVOKE EXECUTE` da `PUBLIC`, `anon`, `authenticated` come nelle migration di aprile, in un file a parte (`20261017200100_system_style_editor_stili_grants.sql`): `db push` non accetta funzione e REVOKE nello stesso file (42601).

La config è l'uscita di `serializeTokens(cleanLook(applyPreset(DEFAULT_STYLE_TOKENS, "cg")))`, riletta con `parseTokens`: identica.

**Prove SQL da lanciare in Studio, prima** (quanti cambierebbero)
```sql
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE sv.config = jsonb_build_object(
    'colors', jsonb_build_object(
      'pageBackground',   '#FFFFFF',
      'primary',          '#6366f1',
      'headerBackground', '#6366f1',
      'textPrimary',      '#1a1a2e',
      'textSecondary',    '#6b7280',
      'surface',          '#FFFFFF',
      'border',           '#f1f5f9'
    ),
    'typography', jsonb_build_object('fontFamily', 'inter'),
    'header', jsonb_build_object('imageBorderRadiusPx', 12),
    'navigation', jsonb_build_object('style', 'pill'),
    'card', jsonb_build_object(
      'layout', 'list',
      'radius', 'rounded',
      'image', jsonb_build_object('mode', 'show', 'position', 'left')
    )
  )) AS da_cambiare,
       count(*) AS stili_di_sistema
FROM public.styles s
JOIN public.style_versions sv ON sv.id = s.current_version_id
WHERE s.is_system;
```

**Dopo**
```sql
-- nessuno stile di sistema mai ritoccato rimasto sulla config vecchia
SELECT count(*) FROM public.styles s
JOIN public.style_versions sv ON sv.id = s.current_version_id
WHERE s.is_system AND sv.config = jsonb_build_object(
    'colors', jsonb_build_object(
      'pageBackground',   '#FFFFFF',
      'primary',          '#6366f1',
      'headerBackground', '#6366f1',
      'textPrimary',      '#1a1a2e',
      'textSecondary',    '#6b7280',
      'surface',          '#FFFFFF',
      'border',           '#f1f5f9'
    ),
    'typography', jsonb_build_object('fontFamily', 'inter'),
    'header', jsonb_build_object('imageBorderRadiusPx', 12),
    'navigation', jsonb_build_object('style', 'pill'),
    'card', jsonb_build_object(
      'layout', 'list',
      'radius', 'rounded',
      'image', jsonb_build_object('mode', 'show', 'position', 'left')
    )
  );
-- versione nuova in uso, vecchia ancora presente
SELECT s.id, sv.version, sv.config->'meta'->>'preset' AS preset,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM public.style_versions v WHERE v.style_id = s.id) AS versioni
FROM public.styles s JOIN public.style_versions sv ON sv.id = s.current_version_id
WHERE s.is_system ORDER BY sv.created_at DESC LIMIT 5;
-- funzione non chiamabile dai ruoli dell'app
SELECT has_function_privilege('authenticated', 'public.handle_new_tenant_system_group()', 'EXECUTE');
```
Tenant nuovo di prova su staging: la pagina pubblica deve uscire col vetro, l'alone e la foto a destra.

**Annullare**: rimettere `current_version_id` sulla versione precedente degli stili toccati (quelli con una versione nuova creata all'ora della migration) e ripristinare la funzione da `20260408320000`. Le righe nuove restano in `style_versions` come versioni di prima: non fanno danno.

author: stefanmuellerai
body:
## Zusammenfassung

Betrieb auf dem Applikationsserver des BLfD (`zrz-ux-vm19027`): Podman rootless, keine Root-Rechte, keine Ports unter 1024, kein öffentliches DNS (kein Let's Encrypt), Internet nur über den Behörden-Proxy, auf dem `files.pythonhosted.org` gesperrt ist. Deshalb wird auf dem Server nichts gebaut: GitHub Actions baut die Images und legt sie in ghcr.io ab.

### Images (`.github/workflows/images.yml`)
- Baut `ludwigone-backend`, `-frontend`, `-dashboard` bei jedem Push auf `main` (`:latest`, `:sha-…`) und bei Tags `v*`.
- Spiegelt Postgres 16, Redis 7, Temporal 1.24.2 (+ UI), Caddy 2.8 und ClamAV 1.4 nach ghcr.io: Der Server braucht nur ghcr.io (kein Docker-Hub-Limit über die gemeinsame Proxy-IP).
- Dashboard mit `VITE_API_BASE_URL=/`: Login/BFF über denselben Host wie das Dashboard, das Image passt auf jeden Server.

### `docker-compose.intranet.yml`
- Eigenständig (ohne `!reset`/`!override`), läuft mit `docker-compose` über den Podman-Socket oder mit `podman-compose`.
- Ports: Portal **3000**, Dashboard inkl. Login-API **5173** (Caddy, ohne HTTPS). Die interne API wird nicht veröffentlicht.
- Proxy-Variablen in den Containern geleert: Ollama (`10.1.216.70`) und Temporal würden sonst über den Web-Proxy angesprochen.
- Rootless-tauglich: keine Speicherlimits, keine Start-Bedingungen über Healthchecks, `restart: always` (für `podman-restart.service`), SELinux-Labels an Bind-Mounts, kein Healthcheck für die Worker.
- KI über Ollama, Modelle per `.env`; Bilderkennung abschaltbar (`VISION_ENABLED`, `CLASSIFICATION_USE_VISION`) für Ollama-Server ohne Vision-Modell.
- ClamAV optional (Profil `virenscan`, Signatur-Updates über den Proxy, `deploy/clamav/freshclam.conf`), Temporal-UI optional (Profil `tools`, nur lokal).
- Vorlage `deploy/intranet.env.example`, Caddy-Konfiguration `deploy/Caddyfile.intranet`.

### Portal
- „Wechsel zum Admin-Dashboard“ öffnete fest `http://localhost:5173`. Jetzt der aktuelle Host auf Port 5173; `NEXT_PUBLIC_DASHBOARD_URL` hat Vorrang (z.B. für die Domain-Variante).

### Doku
- `docs/INTRANET-PODMAN.md`: Podman-Speicher nach `/srv`, Registry-Login, `.env`, Images laden, Start, erster Test, Betrieb (Logs, Update, Backup, Neustart der VM).
- Verweise in `README.md` und `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`.

## Tests
- `docker compose config` für die Intranet-Datei (mit allen Profilen) und `caddy validate` für `Caddyfile.intranet` – jetzt auch in der CI.
- Frontend und Dashboard: `lint`, `typecheck`, `test` grün (neue Tests für die Dashboard-Adresse und für `VITE_API_BASE_URL=/`).
- Ein Start der Container war in der Entwicklungsumgebung nicht möglich (kein Container-Dienst); der erste echte Lauf erfolgt auf dem Server.

## Hinweise
- Die Images sind privat: Auf dem Server `podman login ghcr.io` mit einem Token mit `read:packages`.
- Rootless Container laufen nach dem Abmelden bzw. nach einem Neustart der VM nur weiter, wenn für den Benutzer „Linger“ aktiv ist (`loginctl enable-linger`, ggf. durch den Serverbetrieb).

body:
## Description

Closes #1807 (`[ROCK8]`, epic #1799). Implements `QD16`.

**The popup** is built to prototype D: an on/off switch, "Show videos older than" (6 months, 1 year by default, 2 years), and Diagnostics. It has no counts and no history. The languages setting is left out, per the owner's decision on #1807.

**The settings** are one schema-versioned record in `storage.local`: `{ v: 1, boundary, enabled }` (`src/lib/settings/settings.ts`).
- The popup is the only writer. Its saves run one at a time, and each click is applied to what is stored.
- The popup and the content script both read through `followSettings`:
  - It reads the record once, then follows `storage.onChanged`.
  - A first read that a change overtook is dropped.
  - A failed read applies the defaults.
- An unreadable field falls back to its default, so a bad record never admits more than a fresh install does.
- The boundary values are 182, 365 and 730 days. 6 months is 182 because the estimator reads "1 year ago" as 182 days, and a test pins that no offered boundary plates a younger label while holding an older one.

**The boundary is a Core input** (R7):
- `start` carries `boundaryDays`.
- `boundary` re-decides every card in place, at the `t` it was last seen. Only a card whose view moved is re-rendered, and it goes straight from one stamp to the other.
- `fsm.ts`'s `decide` takes the boundary as an argument instead of the constant.

**Off is plain YouTube:**
- Every static pre-mask rule is keyed to `:root:not([data-boyo-off])`.
- The content script stops the runtime and sets that attribute, in one task, only when the owner switches off. It writes it through the Actuator's `switch.ts`.
- A content script that never runs leaves the pre-mask on, so fail-closed is unchanged.

**Boundary changes** are appended to `boundaryChanges` in `storage.local`. Only the Diagnostics page reads it, in a "Boundary changes" section that its Refresh button rereads. The doctrine's §9 falsifier ("`B` keeps getting lowered") needs that history. The log is append-only, and entries a build can't read are kept rather than dropped.

**Docs:**
- `QD16`, `absent-plated-heard.md` §1 and §7, and the QD5 status are amended.
- QD15 and §6 note the owner's 2026-10-17 lane decision as a pending amendment for #1806.
- §5's "no production path stores `B`" paragraph is replaced.
- `amo-notes.md` now describes the real permissions, storage and network use (#1780).

### Not met as written: "No manifest requests `contextMenus`"

The issue assumed the permission existed only for the whitelist's right-click item. That item and its `confirm()` already went in #1803.

Today `contextMenus` serves one thing: the "Open diagnostics" tab menu item, shared with the sibling extensions (`@some-extension/common/lib/diagnostics`). I kept it. If the owner wants the permission gone, the follow-up is small: remove the menu, and the background script then has nothing left to do.

`rg -i whitelist extensions/some-censor` still matches the doctrine's history (`quarantine-capsule.md` §2, `QD5`, §6), which the amendment protocol keeps in place. No code, test, type or manifest mentions it.

## Superseded

Removed:
- `src/lib/background/{api-client,message-handler,index}.ts`:
  - `ApiClient`, the dev-only localhost client;
  - the handler for `IS_WHITELISTED`, `GET_WHITELIST`, `ADD_WHITELIST`, `REMOVE_WHITELIST`, `GET_ENABLED` and `SET_ENABLED`.
- `src/types/messages.ts` and `src/types/api.ts`. `messages.ts` held `WhitelistEntry`, `BgRequest`, `BgResponse` and `BgBroadcast`, including `ENABLED_CHANGED` and `CHANNEL_WHITELISTED`.
- The controller's `GET_ENABLED` bootstrap and its `ENABLED_CHANGED` listener.
- The popup's tagline.
- The e2e fixture's page-level `chrome.runtime` stub, which no fixture page used.
- The stale comments in `vite.config.ts`, `popup.css` and `popup.ts`.

Changed rather than duplicated:
- Core's "lets no input change a card's view" test is now "no input but the boundary".
- The replay-determinism log includes a `boundary` event.
- The pre-mask selectors are extended with the off gate. They are not duplicated.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] This change requires a documentation update

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings (the 2 eslint warnings predate this)
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
- [x] Any dependent changes have been merged and published in downstream modules

**Run locally in `extensions/some-censor`:**
- `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint src tests`, `stylelint`, `prettier --check`, `knip` and root `check:test-layout`: all clean.
- `vitest`: 292 tests pass.
- `pnpm test:e2e`: 36 tests pass, including `settings.spec.ts`:
  - **S1** clicks the real popup and watches an open fixture tab re-decide. It records the value each `data-boyo` write replaced, which is never empty, and checks the final stamp.
  - **S2** checks that off stops the tab and lifts the blur, and that on restarts it.

**Mutation checks.** Each of these was confirmed to fail its test:
- `setBoundary` not dispatching fails S1.
- A strip before each restamp in `rebound` fails S1.
- Off without the attribute write fails S2.
- The controller's stale-read guard removed fails its unit test.
- The popup without serialized saves fails `popup.test.ts`.
- 6 months at 183 days fails the ordering test.
- Refresh without the log reread fails its render test.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [x] A setting persists in `storage.local` (a production build no longer routes through `ApiClient`), and the content script reads it on the next load (controller test).
- [x] Unreadable or invalid storage yields the defaults (`settings.test.ts`, controller test).
- [ ] `rg -i whitelist` returns nothing outside the doctrine's history, and `contextMenus` stays for Diagnostics. See above.
- [x] The popup shows no number other than the boundary options.
- [x] Changing the boundary updates an open tab without a reload, and never passes through a state where a held card is visible (S1).

## Screenshots

The built popup, on and off, matches prototype D's popup without the languages block. The screenshots were taken locally from `dist/` in Chromium.

body: **Source and licence** [flag-icons](https://github.com/lipis/flag-icons) 7.5.0 (MIT, published May 2025). 7.6.0 came out two days ago, so I took the newest release that's at least two weeks old. I read the licence from the npm tarball itself: MIT, "Copyright (c) 2013 Panayiotis Lipiridis". The one obligation is to keep the notice with the copies, so it ships as `flags/LICENSE.txt` next to the SVGs. No visible attribution is required. Documented under "Third-party assets" in architecture.md. **Sanitising** (`apps/public/flags.sanitize`, run by `manage.py import_flags`) - Refused: DOCTYPE/ENTITY/processing instructions (checked before parsing), any element outside an SVG shape/gradient/clip allowlist (`script`, `foreignObject`, `image`, `animate`…), `href` not starting with `#`, `url()` other than `url(#id)`. - Dropped: every attribute outside the allowlist (all `on*`, `class`, fonts), unsafe `style` declarations, the root `id`. - All 250 flags passed; nothing in the package needed refusing. - Tests re-run the sanitiser over the committed files (output must equal input) and throw 11 hostile inputs at it. - Defence in depth: WhiteNoise answers before the CSP middleware, so static files had no CSP at all. In production WhiteNoise serves them content-hashed, brotli/gzip-compressed and cached for a year. **UI** `{% flag code %}` tag: `` (decorative, the name is always next to it), explicit width/height (no layout shift), lazy on the list (250 flags) and eager in the country page heading. author: 0xb1ob
body:
Job cp-cp-ci-actions-read-retry-xaj2: make the Actions CI read robust against the "not JSON" stalls.

## What changed
- `src/actions-ci.ts` `get()`: one attempt is classified (JSON body / denied / rate-limited / retryable). A non-JSON body on gh exit 0, an HTML 403/404, a 5xx or a transport fault retries after 250 ms and 750 ms (`ACTIONS_RETRY_DELAYS_MS`) while the observation budget lasts. A persisting fault is one named `ActionsCiError` with category, endpoint, gh's status, a 60-byte token-redacted body preview and the attempt count.
- Status wording: `HTTP 403/404` only for a JSON (real GitHub) denial; `status <n>` / `gh exit 0` otherwise, because `ciReadDenied` treats any `HTTP 403` as "token lacks Actions read".
- `runCommand` (merge-ask.ts) and `statusRunner` attach `stdout` to the thrown Error so the body of a failed gh call reaches the fault.
- docs/contracts.md: new paragraph under "CI evidence is GitHub Actions and nothing else".

## Cause
Not reproducible from here: `gh api` without `-i` exposes no status for an exit-0 body, so the root cause (truncated body vs. HTML/proxy page) could not be confirmed. The fault now records the evidence needed to confirm it next time.

## Dropped: the `gh pr checks` / check-runs fallback (task item 3)
Dropped by main-session decision: "CI evidence is GitHub Actions only" is a deliberate contract (cp-ci-actions-only; docs/contracts.md, pinned by `tests/actions-ci-policy.test.ts`; `gh pr checks` 403s in this home). Retry with backoff plus the named fault is the fix; the "fallback success/failure" tests are the accepted "retry recovers" / "retry persists" tests.

## Tests
`tests/actions-ci.test.ts`: truncated body recovers on retry; persisting HTML body is one malformed fault with status + redacted preview; HTML 403 is transport (not denied) while JSON 403 stays denied; no retry past the budget or for structurally wrong JSON.
Ran: typecheck, actions-ci, actions-ci-policy, main-ci, foreign-ci-watch, ci-watch, integrate, integrate-held-ci, ci-access, merge-ask, awaiting-merge(-tick), contract, contracts-exports.
No agent runs, no agent directory used.

- **Ejercicios:**
  - Cada renglón muestra las series en línea y cómo le fue frente a la última vez: `récord 20 kg` con trofeo, `↗ 1 rep`, `↘ 152 kg en total`, `=` o `primera vez`.

author: hatamnya-afk
body:
## Scope
Resolve the static contract mismatch between Dynamic Decision and CP49 authoritative Decision Birth, and make multi-Birth SQLite persistence atomic at the caller-owned transaction boundary.

## Changes
- Extract `build_decision_semantics()` so validation and semantic determination run once without issuing identity.
- Let the dynamic boundary return `SEMANTIC_READY` when no canonical ID is supplied; retain the existing `READY` path when an ID is explicitly supplied.
- Keep UUIDv4 issuance and persistence owned by the CP49 integration boundary.
- Reject attempts to issue a second identity for a Decision that already contains `decision_id`.
- Promote `SEMANTIC_READY` to `READY` only after Birth persistence returns the expected ID.
- Remove per-record commit from `persist_authoritative_birth()` so the producer's caller-owned transaction can commit or roll back a complete batch atomically.
- Document transaction ownership explicitly: schema setup is committed separately; callers must wrap a complete Birth operation/batch in a transaction; successful return is not durable until caller commit; duplicate collision rolls back the active transaction.
- Add focused tests for semantic preservation, no-ID and explicit-ID paths, invalid IDs/scores, duplicate issuance prevention, persistence failure, SQLite reopen durability, duplicate-ID protection, batch rollback, and caller-owned commit/rollback visibility.

## Verification
- User-reported focused test run at prior code head `9bd38481f84ae1854724e0d38ac50b786905987b`:
  `python -m pytest -q test_dynamic_decision_birth_order_v0_1.py test_mcp01_main_integration_boundary_v0_1.py`
- Result: **15 passed in 0.29s**. This is a focused local run, not the full suite or CI.
- Independent temporary SQLite verification previously showed persistence after reopen and preservation of the original duplicate-ID row; the initial batch-atomicity check failed, motivating the caller-owned transaction fix. The new focused regression test covers rollback of the first row when a later duplicate fails.
- PR #52 is merged (`bbe1679e86f5d4abad5041d6f3db4d29807055ee`). After the trigger was enabled, this PR's head was updated with a caller-owned transaction regression test. CI run `39062552049` passed: compile-only pipeline check, focused contract tests, dependency installation, and full regression suite (**500 passed in 3.47s**).

## Status / safety
- Draft PR; not merged into an operational branch.
- The full regression CI passed for the current head; final code review and managerial decision to merge remain outstanding.
- No pipeline invocation, exchange calls, order submission, execution activation, or production database access was performed.
- Execution authorization remains FALSE.

## What this changes
- `std::optional<ToneProcessor> tone_`, built with `emplace` in `doInitHal()` once the config is loaded. `ToneProcessor` has no default constructor, which is why it's an `optional`.

Fixes #97

- Local ESP-IDF v5.3 firmware build is clean. Host tests and `clang-format` pass.

3. If the tone is noticeably quieter than in the bring-up app (#52), the likely cause is that the driver configures TX for the left slot only, while the amp plays the average of left and right. That fix would go in the HAL, which is outside this issue.

author: jovidecroock
body:
## Summary

- Audit finding **DX-8** (P3), the packaging part.
- **Before:** 11 packages hard-depended on `@pracht/core` (`workspace:^`, published as `^0.20.0`). Under 0.x a caret stops at the minor, so upgrading `@pracht/core` alone to 0.21 nested a second core under every adapter and satellite. Core keeps request state in module scope, so the second copy splits it.
- **After:** `@pracht/vite-plugin`, `@pracht/adapter-{cloudflare,netlify,node,static,vercel}`, `@pracht/session`, `@pracht/i18n`, `@pracht/query` and `@pracht/test` take `@pracht/core` as a `peerDependency`, plus a `devDependency` for the workspace link. Upgrading core alone now gives a peer warning and no second copy. The repo already releases `@pracht/openapi` this way, and changesets keeps such peers as patch re-releases (`onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange`), so release cadence is unchanged. Built output still imports `@pracht/core` externally, which I checked in the `dist/` of adapter-node, session and test.
- **Non-breaking:** every scaffold (`packages/start`) and every example lists `@pracht/core` directly, and npm 7+ and pnpm install peers automatically.
- **Left as a hard dependency on purpose:** `@pracht/cli`. It is a 1.x dev tool that may run without an app install, and I did not want to risk a missing-peer failure for `pnpm dlx`/`npx` users. `@pracht/vite-plugin` became a peer too after review (see below). That is compatible with #447's `fixed` group: the plugin and core still release at one version.
- **`@pracht/query`'s `preact` peer stays `^10.0.0`.** The audit suggested widening it. `packages/query/test/package.test.ts` pins it to `@tanstack/preact-query`'s own peer (`^10.0.0`) on purpose, so widening it would promise an install npm cannot resolve. That limit comes from TanStack, not from pracht.
- **Skill:** `skills/upgrade-pracht/SKILL.md` said internal dependencies are "pinned exact". npm shows `^0.20.0`, so the skill now describes caret ranges and which packages peer core. **Coordination with #447:** #447 rewrites the paragraph directly above this bullet. Whichever PR lands second needs a trivial rebase of adjacent lines; the two texts do not contradict each other.
- `docs/WORKSPACE.md` records the convention.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm run verify` (build, format, lint, typecheck, test, e2e)
- [x] New `packages/framework/test/satellite-manifests.test.ts` asserts that core is a peer, not a dependency, of all 10 packages. It fails on main for all 10.
- [x] `pnpm install` updated the lockfile (core moved to `devDependencies` in 10 importers). `pnpm peers check` shows no new issue; the remaining ones are third-party `preact ^10` peers that predate this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Docs updated if needed (`docs/WORKSPACE.md`; no public site page describes package manifests)
- [x] Skills updated if needed (`skills/upgrade-pracht/SKILL.md`)
- [x] Concise, user-facing changeset added if published packages changed (patch for the 10 packages and for `create-pracht`, because the bundled skill changed)

Verify note: all steps pass except the two `e2e/capabilities.test.ts` WebMCP/eval specs. Those also fail on main with the local Chrome WebMCP build and are unrelated to this change.

## Adversarial review

Cross-model review: NEEDS-CHANGES (3 findings). All were accepted and fixed in c439191fc7, and verify was re-run.

- **485-1 (P2), accepted and fixed.** With `@pracht/vite-plugin` still hard-depending on core, upgrading core alone made npm nest `adapter-node` (now a core peer) under the plugin, beside the plugin's old core. The generated server entry then could not resolve `@pracht/adapter-node` from the app root. Scaffolded apps list their adapter directly and get a loud `ERESOLVE` instead, but an app that relies on the default adapter would fail at build. `@pracht/vite-plugin` now peers core as well, so nothing nests, and the manifest test covers it.
- **485-2 (P3), accepted and fixed.** The skill said a newer core only produces a peer warning. Under npm it fails with `ERESOLVE`. The skill now says so, and warns that forcing past it can install a second core.
- **485-3 (P3), accepted and fixed.** The skill's rollback section still said "exact-pinned". It now describes the actual ranges.

**Owner note:** upgrading `@pracht/core` alone past the family's minor now fails loudly under npm (`ERESOLVE`) and warns under pnpm. Before, it silently installed a second core. The upgrade skill and the changesets fixed-group policy already tell users to upgrade the family together.

author: mrashid2206-ai
body:
**Stack 2 of 7.** Merge after the audit PR (stack 1). **This PR's own changes:** https://github.com/mrashid2206-ai/employees-leave-management/compare/audit-and-admin-safety...portal-flows

## Why
The employee portal hid things employees need and showed wrong times on phones set to another time zone.

## What changes
- **Correction requests are visible.** The Requests tab lists them with status, times and reason. A **"Request correction" button works for any day**, including one with no attendance row, which covers the most common case: "I forgot to check in". Correction messages are now bilingual, and future dates are refused.
- **Missed check-out prompt:** if the last working day has a check-in and no real check-out, the attendance tab offers to file a correction. The automation is unchanged.
- **Session expiry:** a 401 now shows a toast and returns to login. Every tab has an error state with retry, instead of looking like "no data".
- **Oman time everywhere:** the clock ticks and is formatted in Asia/Muscat. **Permission date/leave time and return time are stamped by the server**, and an employee can no longer send their own.
- **Check-in feedback:** toasts for a cancelled-and-refunded leave, holiday work, and overtime. `confirm()` is replaced by the app's confirm dialog, and cancelling a leave now asks first.
- **Monthly summary:** a month picker with present/absent/leave days, hours, overtime and lateness. There's no 30-row cap, and the employee's own schedule is shown ("starts 07:30, Sun–Thu, 8h"). Schedule resolution is shared with the server (`schedule-core.ts`).
- A signed-in employee opening `/employee-login` goes to `/check-in`, and RTL margins are fixed on the portal.

## Bug found while checking it in a browser
**An admin who is also an employee got the portal's "my" requests answered as the admin** when both sessions were in the same browser. The bell came back empty, and "my" tardiness/permissions/corrections came back as everyone's. The portal now sends `x-auth-context: employee`, and `verifyAnyAuth` then authenticates the employee only. The header can only narrow access: an admin session alone with the header gets 401. Tests cover all three cases.

## Tests
Unit: `schedule-core`, `portal-summary`, Oman-time helpers. Integration: `permission-times.itest.ts`, plus more cases in the corrections and authorization tests. **Checked in a real browser** (Arabic):
- the ticking clock, the missed check-out card, the corrections list;
- the monthly summary;
- the schedule line;
- the bell count.

author: pierremesure
body:
Arbetsförmedlingen loads its “Upphävda” records through a separate public JSON request. The harvester reads only the initial current list, so it misses 72 archived records (32 AFFS and 40 AMSFS).

Read the archive after the current records and derive its endpoint from the official page identifiers. Keep each record under its own series. Sort the current records numerically so incremental runs can stop correctly.

Request pacing: add a pause using the existing `POLITENESS` constant (0.3 seconds) after the initial listing GET and archive POST. This adds at most 0.6 seconds per complete enumeration, not per archive record. It follows the existing listing helpers’ pacing convention. The HTTP layer still enforces any robots.txt `Crawl-delay` separately. These pauses are an incidental change; archive discovery does not depend on them.

Validation: 378 föreskrift tests pass, including six new fixture tests for first, incremental, deep and forced harvests. Ruff, ty and diff checks pass. Fixtures freeze the official current list and complete archive response.

After merge, run `lagen foreskrift download affs --deep`, then the normal downstream rebuild. This PR changes discovery; it does not update the live lagen.nu dataset.

Fixes #132

author: yicheng0608
body:
Closes #181

## 做了什麼

依 #181 的[評分提案](https://github.com/YiCheng0608/stock-lab/issues/181#issuecomment-6237884037)與[統籌核可](https://github.com/YiCheng0608/stock-lab/issues/181#issuecomment-6237895647)實作 `candidate_score_v1`（評分只用於排序，不代表勝率或預期報酬，不改變策略判定）。

- **設定** `backend/app/domain.py`：`CANDIDATE_SCORE_V1`（權重 technical 0.35／chips 0.30／group 0.20／news_sentiment 0.15；RR 權重 0 只顯示；`minimum_weight_coverage` 0.65；名單上限 20）＋`weighted_available_mean`（只對有值項加權並回傳覆蓋權重，缺資料不補 0）。設定快照由 `test_config_snapshot_is_pinned_and_weights_sum_to_one` 釘住，改設定未升版會讓測試失敗。不放進 `CANONICAL_CONFIGS`（那份快照識別策略列）。
- **評分** `backend/worker/candidates.py`：候選池（T 日 conditional、現行公式、active stock／ipo、價位合法、非停牌；ETF 與指數排除）→ 四分項 → 總分重新正規化＋覆蓋門檻 → 同股只留高分策略 → 固定排序鍵 → 前 20 → 規則式理由（每個分項先取 1 條，最多 4 條）。籌碼與策略同一套交易日與公式（測試對照 `_strategy_institutional_flow_to_average_volume_ratio`／`_margin_change_ratio`），且最後一根必須是 T；族群只取 T 日分數列，條件同 `_qualified_groups_for_instrument`；新聞是 3 個台北日曆日、規則關聯、LLM `news_v1` 方向，unknown 與未判讀不計分，窗口內沒有 news 收集 run 時整日 null。
- **保存** migration `0013_candidates`（接在 `0012_news_llm` 之後，additive、forward-only）：`candidate_runs`（交易日×版本唯一；零候選也寫一列並記原因、排除計數、設定快照、摘要）與 `daily_candidates`（交易日×標的×版本唯一）。同日同版本重跑回 `already_complete`，不新增、不改寫。`daily_candidates.instrument_id` 外鍵指向 instruments，因此照 #151 的 `technical_indicators` 前例加入 `instrument_identity_migration._CHILDREN`；fallback 升級補 `0013` marker；各測試的 head 常數由 0012 改成 0013。
- **排程** `worker/schedule_runs.py`：`DAILY_STEPS` 改為 collect → analyze → evaluate → **candidates** → indicators。依賴改成明確表（evaluate、candidates 依賴 analyze；indicators 只依賴 collect），evaluate 失敗不擋 candidates，candidates 失敗不擋 indicators。CLI 新增 `python -m worker.cli candidates [--date]`。
- **API**：`GET /api/candidates?date=&limit=`（1～20，預設 20，不帶 date 取最新 run）與 `GET /api/stocks/{exchange}/{symbol}` 的 `candidate`。組裝放在新模組 `app/candidate_view.py`，`api.py` 只加一個端點與一行。每列有 `weight_coverage`／`partial_components`、四分項（子項值、percentile、`inference`、`null_reason`／`null_explanation`）、進場區／停損／目標／RR、理由、族群、資料日期與來源；未計算的日期回 `status=not_computed`。
- **文件**：V1_SPEC 新增 [`candidate_score_v1`](docs/V1_SPEC.md#candidate_score_v1) 節（開頭聲明、RR 權重 0 的原因、percentile、null、族群榜別／排名記錄、理由排序）；OPERATIONS §3 新增 CLI 列、daily 順序，§6.3 加 candidates 步驟與失敗處置；UI_COPY_SPEC 新增 §10 理由碼與文案；ROADMAP 目前產品能力。

**exit code 影響**：candidates 步驟失敗（例外或非 success／no_data）時該 daily run 記為 `failed`，`worker.cli daily` 的 exit code 是 1（工作排程器「上次執行結果」= 1），錯誤欄寫 `candidates: …`。這時行情、訊號、追蹤與指標都已寫入；只要重跑候選，執行 `python -m worker.cli candidates --date YYYY-MM-DD` 即可，不需要 `daily --force`。T 日沒有訊號時 candidates 回 `no_data`，不影響 run 狀態，也不寫列。單獨跑的 `worker.cli candidates` 在 success／no_data 以外的狀態都 exit 1。

## 怎麼驗證

- [x] 後端 pytest／ruff：全套 `python -m pytest backend/tests -q` → **2737 passed**（8 分 8 秒；HEAD 的上一個 commit 有 1 項失敗，原因是 candidates 步驟沒走 `pipeline.SessionLocal`，已在下一個 commit 修正）（本機 Windows，Desktop `.venv` python 3.12.14）。`tools/ci/checks.py repository --base 611b416e…` 與 `lint` 都通過；新檔已 `ruff format`；改動的既有檔，ruff 違規數與 base 相同（`ruff format --check backend` 在 master 本來就不乾淨，沒有改既有檔的排版）。
- [ ] 前端 test／build：本 PR 沒有前端變更。
- [x] AC 逐條結果：
  - **AC-1**（記憶體 DB，`backend/tests/test_candidates.py` 16 項）：分項 percentile（含較低為佳的子項）、null 不補零（籌碼母體排除無資料股、group null 時總分以 0.80 重新正規化、新聞無收集 run 時 null）、`weighted_available_mean`、權重加總與設定快照、同分以 `exchange`／`symbol` 固定排序、ETF／不合法價位／RR<1.5／observation 排除並計數、technical 缺時被覆蓋門檻排除、同股兩策略留高分、上限 20、零候選原因（`no_actionable_signals`、`all_excluded`）、沒有訊號時 `no_data` 且不寫列。
  - **AC-2**：`test_rerun_is_idempotent_and_a_new_version_keeps_old_rows`：重跑回 `already_complete`；新增新聞後重跑，列 id、分數、排名、分項與理由全部不變；換版本設定另存新 run 與新列，舊列逐欄不變。真實副本重跑也回 `already_complete`，`candidate_runs` 1 列、`daily_candidates` 20 列不變。
  - **AC-3** 真實資料：見下節。
  - **AC-4**：`test_api_returns_ranked_fields_inference_and_null_explanations`：欄位齊全、`news_sentiment.inference=true`、`technical.inference=false`、null 分項有 `null_explanation`、`limit` 上限 20（21 → 422）、未計算日期 `not_computed`、個股 API 的 `candidate`（有／無）；`test_api_reports_the_zero_reason`。真實副本的 API 輸出也確認過（下節）。
  - **AC-5**：V1_SPEC、OPERATIONS、UI_COPY_SPEC、ROADMAP 同批更新。
  - daily 掛點：`test_daily_schedule.py` 新增 evaluate 失敗仍跑 candidates、candidates 失敗讓 run 變 failed 但不擋 indicators、candidates `no_data` 時 run 仍是 success；既有測試的步驟清單加上 candidates。

### AC-3 真實資料執行

- 資料：2026-10-18 02:00（台北）以 SQLite backup API 把正式 `C:/Users/YiCheng/stock-lab-data/stock.db`（唯讀開啟，0011，2026-10-16 daily 已 success）複製到 `C:/s181/stock.db`，只在副本上 `init-db` 升到 0013（2 分 42 秒）。正式 DB 沒有寫入。

- 新聞分項全部 null（`news_collection_missing`）：正式 DB 還沒有任何 `run_type=news` 的收集 run，也還沒有 `news_llm_results`。族群分項全部 null：正式 DB 當日只有 5 個有排名的產業群組、沒有題材榜，前 20 檔的所屬產業都不在其中。所以每檔的 `weight_coverage` 都是 0.65（技術＋籌碼），照實記錄。

| 排名 | 標的 | 策略 | 總分 | technical | chips | 理由 |

author: 1994akh
body:
Adds the 17 Oct probe note under art decision 4 (the boy hero's body); the other two decisions already carry theirs.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## 背景
原工单 290063（id=39）在管理端显示执行动作 #28、#29 的状态是 `completed`，但 `team_ok=false`，侦查、修复、验证三个角色都失败。
- #28：只出报告的 executor
- #29：执行端 git clone 出错（根因见下）

后来真正给出结论的是 Grok Bot 云端执行器的重派（Para 6d45fe28、1dd961b7）。20:50 那次重派回写时覆盖了 #28，22:59 那次没有记成执行动作。

## 根因
`modstore_server/customer_service_orchestrator_part05.py::apply_customer_ticket_incident_progress`
1. 无条件写 `action.status = "completed"`、`action.error = ""`，不管 `team_ok` 和各角色结果是什么。
2. 调用 `build_action` 时 `target_id=str(event_id)`，幂等键是 `ticket:employee.dispatch:incident_team:event_id`。同一事件再派一次（重派或外部执行器）会拿到原来那条动作并覆盖它，不会新记一条。

## 修改
- 动作状态按角色结果判定：
  - `completed`：team_ok
  - `failed`：有角色失败，或者没有任何角色结果
  - `manual_review` / `pending`：角色待人工核对 / Para 任务还在跑
  - `partial`：已有角色都成功，但团队不完整，比如只出报告的重派
- `error` 写“未成功角色：…”。`request` 和 `result` 记 `para_task_ids`、`tools`（来自 handler 的 tool_name，比如 grok_bot）、`executor`。

author: karangoel59-dev
body:
CoinDCX accepted and filled an entry, but its position appeared after the old five-second confirmation window. The bot latched an entry failure and then repeatedly retried the blocked signal. Delayed exits also caused repeated exit/protection requests.

- Confirm entries, TP/SL and exits for up to 60 seconds, retrying failed reads. Query order-specific fills for better timeout diagnostics; require verified position protection before releasing the entry journal.
- Consume blocked entry signals before sizing and report the block once. Keep exits available.
- Coalesce exit requests and retain pending confirmation after acceptance, an uncertain response or “already in progress”; avoid duplicate exits and TP/SL changes while pending. Pending exit state is in memory; unresolved exits require venue inspection.
- Add a service-lock-protected recovery CLI that defaults to inspection. Explicit `--confirm` clears only the matching account/instrument journal after terminal filled-order evidence, complete matching fills, and two flat/no-working-order checks. Dry-run cannot clear it. Document the procedure.

Validation: typecheck, build and all 99 tests pass locally and in an isolated Azure checkout. Regression coverage includes 17-second position delays, transient read failures, uncertain/concurrent exits, blocked signal handling and recovery refusal cases. Read-only validation against the affected live submission confirmed its 0.15 SOL fill and closed/idle state; the journal was retained. The recovery CLI correctly refuses an active service. No production deployment or recovery has been performed.

body:
Adds a scheduled workflow that validates the live MTA-STS/TLS-RPT configuration of `westphalia-kn.de` every Monday at 06:00 UTC, using [ThorstenSauter/mta-sts-check-action](https://github.com/ThorstenSauter/mta-sts-check-action) v1.0.0.

It checks:
- the `_mta-sts` and `_smtp._tls` TXT records
- the policy file at `https://mta-sts.westphalia-kn.de/.well-known/mta-sts.txt`, its certificate and its syntax
- that every MX host is covered by the policy

Results go to the job summary. A failing scheduled or manual run opens an issue labelled `mta-sts-check` (or comments on the open one), and the next passing run closes it. No secrets are needed. The workflow also runs on PRs that change it (for example, Renovate bumps), but doesn't touch issues there.

author: damaged-soda
body:
## 背景

Coda 资源页新增「全部」一组视图（coda-console/coda#1350 第 2 个 PR）：面板卡片可以带 `identity`，身份相同的卡片在一组视图里合并成一张，写明在哪几台；卡片里的额度条当作属于这个身份，只显示一份。核心只比较字符串，不认识账号。

## 改动

| 插件 | 身份 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude | `claude:<邮箱哈希>` | 会话启动时 SDK 初始化结果里的账号（`initializationResult().account.email`），存进 `limits.json` 的是哈希；换账号时旧账号的额度窗口作废。用 API key、云服务商或拿不到邮箱时不标 |
| Codex | `codex:<小写邮箱>` | 本机 ChatGPT 登录的邮箱（卡片标题本来就显示它） |
| Codex 多账号 | `codex-account:<管理器身份>` | 管理器给每个账号的身份（ChatGPT 账号 ID 的哈希），各台相同 |
| Kimi | `kimi:<用户 ID>` | `userinfo` 的 `userId`；照旧不显示手机号、邮箱 |
| Grok | `grok:<邮箱哈希>` | 照旧不显示、也不送出邮箱 |

- 契约检查包（`check/panel.mjs`、`check/coda.mjs`）接受卡片的 `identity`：一行、不超过 200 字，与 Coda 后端的面板规则一致。
- 五个插件按约定升版本（`scripts/check-versions.mjs` 通过）。

## 验证

- `npm test`：253 项全过。新增：Claude 记账号存哈希、文件里没有邮箱、换账号清窗口；Grok 哈希、无邮箱不带；Kimi 用户 ID；Codex、Codex 多账号卡片身份。
- 未验证：真机上 Claude SDK 初始化结果里是否给出邮箱（setup token 没有 profile 权限时可能不给，那样卡片不标身份、在一组视图里按台显示）。

## 合并顺序

先合这个，再在 Coda 的 PR 里同步插件副本（`scripts/sync-plugins.mjs`）。Kimi 记住账号的缓存是按登录文件变化才刷新的，旧缓存里没有用户 ID，下次登录文件变化后才带上身份。

author: alejoamiras
body:
## What changed and why

Arc 1 of `implementations-plan/service-structure-1` (decision page 37, P37-09, option A).

- **Popup import waits through the shared activation waiter.** `popup/pages/import.vue` passes `awaitProfileActivation` (`composables/unlockWait.ts`) to `completeImportWithRecovery`, as unlock and create already do. `composables/waitForProfileActive.ts` and its test are deleted (`unlockWait.test.ts` already covers each of its cases), and the build regenerated the two auto-import files. A bootstrap failure the shell records for the imported profile now ends the wait at once and reaches recovery. Before, import waited out its 30 s backstop.
- **A new activation retires its profile's earlier failure record.** `runFencedBootstrap` (`popup/profile-bootstrap.ts`) clears a record that names its own profile before the bootstrap's first await, and only while its run is current. Restore keeps a free backup id and passkey import uses the credential's userHandle, so an imported id can repeat. Without the clear, a wait that started after a same-id re-import could act on a predecessor's failure.
- The planning plan for all four arcs lands with this PR (`implementations-plan/service-structure-1/`).

**UI impact.** No screen, copy or row changes. The one difference a person can notice: after a recorded bootstrap failure, import reaches recovery at once, not after up to 30 s. P37-09 signs it: "Build: import goes through the shared waiter and the copy is deleted; a test proves import stops at once on a recorded failure."

**Known limit.** #700 (filed and closed): on full-backup import only, a stale record can still race recovery after a same-id re-restore. Full-backup import finalizes on its own port, so the shell's retirement may not run first. Its reopening condition is in the issue.

## Tests

- `popup/pages/import.test.ts` drives the page's real `completeImport`, the real `completeImportWithRecovery` and the real waiter, under fake timers:
  - a failure for another profile routes nothing, and a failure for the imported profile reaches recovery and `/popup/auth` with no timer advanced;
  - a healthy activation shows the wallet with no recovery;
  - with no signal, nothing routes before 30 s, and recovery runs at 30 s.
- `popup/profile-bootstrap.test.ts`:
  - a run retires its own profile's record before the bootstrap starts;
  - a superseded run clears nothing;
  - another profile's record stays.
- Red proofs, taken from the base copies at 0fe841be: the failure case fails on base, and the retirement case fails with the clear removed.

## Validation

All on the merged head (dev at e6a3b098 plus this branch), local:

- `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck:all`: green.
- The four phase files (`import.test.ts`, `profile-bootstrap.test.ts`, `unlockWait.test.ts`, `completeImportWithRecovery.test.ts`): green.
- `bun run test:all`: green, twice (extension 13,447 passed on the merged head).
- `bun run build`: the regenerated auto-import files are committed, and a rebuild leaves the tree clean.
- `grep -rn waitForProfileActive apps/extension/src`: empty.
- `bun run check:plans`: 0 findings.
- Smoke e2e, Chrome, armed dist, retry 0: `import-paths.test.ts` + `import-dead-rpc.test.ts`, 10 passed in 122 s. No e2e scenario is added or removed, so the suite's wall-clock is unchanged by design.
- Codex review: round 1 minor findings fixed, round 2 clean. An Opus review's minor findings were folded into the same fix.

Closes #521

author: onemen
body: Fixes #555 ## Problem On Windows every `profiles.ini` candidate was built as `\`, with `IsRelative=` never read. A portable install's absolute profile path (`IsRelative=0`, e.g. `E:\x2wg22ar.test_scripts`) collapsed into `...\Mozilla\Firefox\E:\...`, a string that is not a directory, so: - the browser card showed `(not detected)` and the folder button did nothing - the installer tab opened in the default browser instead of the detected profile - with two instances running, the round-robin handed a card another install's profile ## Fix - One section-buffering walker (`profiles_ini_foreach()` + `resolve_profile_path()`) replaces both line-streaming parsers: `IsRelative=0` paths are kept verbatim, and the key order inside a section no longer matters. - `find_active_profile_readonly()` prefers the locked profile whose `compatibility.ini` names this binary; the first locked profile stays the fallback, so a profile without `compatibility.ini` still detects. - `collect_locked_profiles()` skips duplicate paths: `profiles.ini` repeats them in its `[Install...]` section, and a doubled pool entry let the round-robin assign the same profile to two running instances. ## Test `installer/test/test_profiles_ini.mjs` drives the new hidden `--test-profiles-ini` CLI mode (relative join, absolute path kept verbatim, reversed `Path=`/`IsRelative=` order, `[Install...]` section, missing-ini exit code) and is wired into `pnpm test:hash`, which the Windows publish gate runs against a freshly built binary. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

author: tonykoop
body:
Refs #660 (part of #648).

## What
- `CadamConfig`: optional `bot_email` / `bot_password` / `anon_key` (env `CADAM_BOT_EMAIL`, `CADAM_BOT_PASSWORD`, `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`); all secret fields are `repr=False`.
- `generate()` signs in (`POST {supabase_url}/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password`, anon key) before any row is written or paid call is made; static `CADAM_ACCESS_TOKEN` is used only when no bot credentials are set. `validate()` accepts bot creds in place of a static token.
- Sign-in errors are fixed messages (HTTP status at most), raised outside the `except` so no chained context can echo a credential or token.
- Reference image is now optional (needed for the text-only smoke).
- `_cadam_config` reads the new env names. `arena preflight`, when bot credentials are configured, requires the bot keys instead of the static token, probes `CADAM_BASE_URL` and the sign-in, and prints a clear redacted FAIL (server-down message names `npm install && npm run dev`). Static-token mode makes no network probe.

Note: sign-in happens at the point of a new dispatch (not on pure `resume_only` recovery of an already-persisted result), so recovery is never blocked by auth.

## Tests
Fake-transport tests: sign-in path and ordering, re-sign-in per generate, static-token fallback, validate, redaction (message, repr, `__cause__`/`__context__`, config repr), malformed replies, preflight GO / server down / 404-is-up / sign-in rejected / output redaction / URL sources / static-mode no-probe. 103 targeted tests, ruff and `check_public_terms.py` pass.

Local CADAM app (`npm run dev` under Node 22 — Node 20 fails on missing native WebSocket), model `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1`, prompt "a simple 3-hole wooden whistle, 150 mm long", no image. body:
Two bugs found while using these actions in kmctl's CI.

**prek and pre_commit were swapped.** 586f8f4 ("build: add prek") copied `pre_commit` to `prek`, then edited `pre_commit` instead of the copy. Since v1.1.0, `actions/prek` has run pre-commit and `actions/pre_commit` has run prek, each with the other's inputs. This swaps the two `action.yaml` files back, so each runs the tool its name and README say, and fixes the prek README's `prek_version` default (it said 4.2.0, pre-commit's; it is 0.2.25).

This is breaking for anyone who relied on the swapped behaviour or input names, so it wants a major tag (v2.0.0).

**pytest ran every tier by default.** With `markers: ""` (the default) the action ran `pytest -m ""`, which clears the project's own `-m` from `addopts` and runs tiers the project leaves out, such as integration tests. It now passes `-m` only when `markers` is set, and reads its inputs from `env`. Checked on kmctl: with no `markers` the run gives `710 passed, 8 deselected`, the project's own default.

A caller after this change:

```yaml
prek:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6  # when hooks call uv run
    - uses: JasperHG90/toiminnot/actions/prek@v2.0.0
      with:
        prek_version: "0.5.5"
        python_version: "3.12"

tests:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: JasperHG90/toiminnot/actions/pytest@v2.0.0
      with:
        directory: tests
        python_version: "3.12"
```

Left as they are: inner actions pinned by major tag (as AGENTS.md asks), the caches, and the 3.11 Python defaults.
