author: kilbot
body:
## Why

Owner rule (2026-10-17): a merchant-visible log row or toast that says there is a problem when there isn't one, or gives no clear instruction, scares merchants. The demo SYNC221 story (#2663) — a completed order reading "a change clashed with an edit in your store" — is the pattern; this PR applies the same rule to the app's own (non-sync) rows on the money path:

- benign, user-cancelled or self-healing → `debug`/`info`, no code;
- one incident → ONE coded row. If the sync observer or a lower layer already wrote it, the caller shows the toast only (`markErrorReported` / `isErrorReported`, or a debug-level log with `showToast`);
- a real problem carries the code whose summary and hint are true, and the store's / gateway's own sentence is the toast title;
- the level follows the code's registry severity where the call site can.

Audit input: the app-rows audit, systemic S1–S5 and sections A0–A3, plus `use-mutation.ts` / `use-local-mutation.ts`. Error copy is #2669 (open); codes below were picked against its copy.

## Machinery (small)

- `LoggerOptions.toast.type` — the toast variant can differ from the level, so an already-reported incident can log at `debug` and still show an error toast, and an `info` row can show a warning toast. Default unchanged (follows the level).
- `resolveMerchantToastText` (S4) — an explicit `toast.title` now keeps the code's action hint as the description (unless the call site passes `toast.text2`). "Checkout failed" now says what to do. This reverses an earlier deliberate choice that `apps/main/__tests__/toast-merchant-sentence.test.ts` pinned ("an explicit title is complete"). That test now pins the S4 rule. About 33 call sites set an explicit title together with a code, and each now gets its code's hint as a second line.
- `reportPushFailure` (`screens/main/contexts/push-failure-code.ts`) — the one report for `engine.write` + `awaitWriteOutcome`: engine-reported refusal/clash/401 → toast only; timeout → warning SYNC191 "still sending"; anything else → the caller's one error row. `pushFailureCode` now returns SYNC201 / SYNC221 for a rejection / clash (the codes the observer stamped).
- The core jest logger mock's `markErrorReported` / `isErrorReported` are now stateful (a WeakSet, like the real one).

## Call sites

| Call site | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hooks/use-http-client.tsx` transport row (S1) | error (warn if `quietErrors`), network → CLIENT999 | debug, `outcome: failed`; reply-less axios error → SYNC121 | Transport can't see the ending (queued email, local receipt, image placeholder); callers own the row. Network is "store unreachable", not "report this bug". |
| `contexts/merchant-toast.ts` (S4) | explicit title drops the hint | title + code's action hint | Toasts like "Checkout failed" had no next step. |
| `pos/cart/buttons/pay.tsx` "Checkout failed" | error CHECKOUT101 for every push failure | refusal/clash/401: toast only (store sentence, SYNC201/SYNC221/AUTH101); timeout: warn SYNC191 "still on its way — wait, then press Checkout again"; local failure: error CHECKOUT101 | S2 double report; the store's own reason was dropped; a timed-out push reads as a failure while it can still land (server dedupes on uuid). |
| `pos/cart/buttons/save-order.tsx`, `orders/edit/form.tsx` "Failed to save order" | error SYNC999 ("re-enter and save") | as Pay; timeout → "still on its way — don't enter it again" | Same; SYNC999's re-enter advice is a duplicate-order risk. |
| `orders/edit/form.tsx` localPatch undefined | threw "Local patch failed" → 2nd row + toast | return (localPatch already reported) | S3 double report. |
| `orders/edit/form.tsx` customer not on device | error SYNC999, no toast | info + warning toast "That customer isn't on this device yet…" | Not an error; the cashier saw nothing happen. |
| `hooks/mutations/use-mutation.ts` create (`awaitRemoteId`) timeout | error SYNC999 "re-enter and save" | warn SYNC191 "{Customer} still on its way to your store… don't enter it again" | Owner call: a re-entered customer is a duplicate. |
| `use-mutation.ts` create rejection | error row (doubles the observer's) | debug + toast (store sentence, SYNC201 hint) | S2. |
| `use-mutation.ts` `patch` undefined result | 2nd error row + toast | silent (already reported) | S3. |
| `hooks/mutations/use-local-mutation.ts` | toast "There was an error: rxdb CONFLICT" | SYNC101's own summary + hint; raw message in context; rethrow marked reported | No instruction; callers double-reported the rethrow. |
| `pos/cart/add-customer.tsx`, `pos/cart/cells/actions.tsx`, `pos/cart/edit-cart-customer.tsx` (catch) | 2nd row for localPatch's rethrow | skip when `isErrorReported` | A2#24 double report. |
| `pos/cart/edit-cart-customer.tsx` profile not on device | error SYNC999 "No customer found" | info + warning toast "Saved to the order. The customer's profile isn't on this device, so it wasn't updated." | The order was saved; nothing is broken. |
| `pos/hooks/use-add-coupon.ts` rejection | warn, raw title | info | A store rule doing its job; shown inline. |
| `use-add-coupon.ts` throw | "There was an error: {raw}" | `pos_cart.coupon_apply_failed` (CHECKOUT111); skipped if already reported | No instruction; double report. |
| `pos/hooks/cart-failure.ts` `reportStaleCartLine` (remove / fee / shipping) | warn | info + info toast | Multi-tab is first-class; the cart already shows the other tab's change. |
| `pos/hooks/use-cart-stock-guard.ts` insufficient / backorder | warn rows | info rows, warning toasts | Store's overselling rule working as designed. |
| `use-cart-stock-guard.ts` missing stock record | warn "{name} is out of stock" | info + "Stock for {name} hasn't loaded on this device yet. Try again in a moment." | It isn't out of stock; the record hasn't synced. |
| `pos/hooks/use-cart-settlement.ts` :472/:548 | error CHECKOUT999 "Do not re-charge", message `String(error)` | error CLIENT999, readable message | A background recalculation is no checkout. |
| `pos/contexts/current-order/use-new-order.ts` | error CHECKOUT999 | template replaced (`!patched`) → debug; write failure → SYNC101 | Benign race; non-money local write. |
| `pos/hooks/utils.ts` lineItems invariant | CHECKOUT999 | CLIENT999 | Invariant, not a checkout outcome. |
| `checkout/components/payment-webview.tsx` :789 gateway decline (S5) | error PAYMENT999 "Confirm whether the payment went through" | warn CHECKOUT101, toast = gateway's sentence (fallback "The payment didn't go through, so this sale is not paid") | Owner call. |
| `payment-webview.tsx` :562 PAYMENT101 | error, red toast | warn, warning toast | Owner call: payment taken, don't charge again. |
| `payment-webview.tsx` :305 / :313 | warn | debug | Catch-up after a routed paid sale; `protected` snapshot is expected. |
| `payment-webview.tsx` :486 / :502 | warn | info | Both arm the server-truth poll that completes the sale. |
| `payment-webview.tsx` :738 auto-reload | warn | debug | An automatic retry; :744 still reports if it fails too. |
| `checkout/hooks/use-checkout-session.ts` :295 (S5) | every failure CHECKOUT201 | offline before start → warn SYNC121 "You're offline, so nothing was charged" + "Reconnect…, then try again"; bootstrap / 4xx refusal of start → CHECKOUT101 + store sentence; `failed`/`cancelled` → warn CHECKOUT101 + provider sentence; paid but the post-payment step threw → warn PAYMENT101; lost reply / 5xx / 409 / poll timeout / offline mid-poll → CHECKOUT201 | Owner call; only a sent start can leave the outcome unknown. |
| `orders/refund/form.tsx` :393 (S5) | PAYMENT999, server text hidden by the code summary | offline → warn SYNC121 "no refund was made"; 4xx refusal → store sentence (SYNC211 / AUTH201); lost reply, 5xx, 408/409/429 → PAYMENT311 "WCPOS couldn't confirm whether this refund went through." + "Open the order and check its refunds before trying again — a retry could refund twice." | Owner call: each retry mints a new idempotency key. |

author: mrashid2206-ai
body:
**Stack 3 of 7.** Merge after the portal-flows PR (stack 2). **This PR's own changes:** https://github.com/mrashid2206-ai/employees-leave-management/compare/portal-flows...portal-a11y-pwa

## Why
**The PWA never actually worked.** The proxy redirected `/sw.js`, the manifest and the icons to the login page, and browsers refuse a service worker behind a redirect, so the portal couldn't be installed and push reminders couldn't register. The bell and login also weren't usable with a keyboard or screen reader.

## What changes
- **Proxy:** an exact allow-list for the PWA files. It is not "anything with an extension", so no route can skip auth by accident.
- **PWA:**
  - the service worker is registered from the portal layout and the login page;
  - offline page loads get a small bilingual offline page, and nothing else is cached;
  - PNG icons at 192 and 512 px, a maskable icon and an apple-touch icon, all generated by `scripts/generate-icons.mjs`.
- **Bell:**
  - an aria-label with the unread count, `aria-expanded`, and keyboard-operable rows;
  - **mark all as read** (server side, scoped to the caller);
  - it closes on Escape or an outside click, shows dates in the chosen language, and polls every 60 s while visible.
- **Login:** real labels, `autocomplete` for password managers, a labelled show/hide toggle with pressed state, and the language toggle placed on the start side for RTL.
- **Bottom nav:** a `<nav>` with `aria-current="page"`. The smallest text sizes are raised.
- **Logout unsubscribes this device's push**, so a shared phone stops getting the previous employee's reminders.
- **Reminders:** the check-in reminder now respects each employee's own days off. **New check-out reminder** (`/api/cron/checkout-reminder`, scheduled hourly 14:15–22:15 Oman time): it nudges people still checked in after their own end of day, at most once a day, via migration `0022_push_reminder_log`. It does nothing when VAPID keys are unset.
- **Fix:** six audit-log headings were stored as escaped text (`ا…`) and displayed as codes in Arabic. They're decoded, and the translations test now rejects escaped Arabic.

## Tests
`portal-push.itest.ts` (14 tests), plus the translations guard. Checked in a browser: the service worker controls the page, the bell label reads "2 unread", and `aria-current` is set.

author: copilot
body:
This PR introduces a full `vanilla-enterprise-shop` implementation aligned with the issue’s educational objective: a production-grade, framework-free storefront/editorial SPA in pure HTML/CSS/ES modules. It establishes explicit architecture patterns (Proxy store + Pub/Sub, service/repository layering, guarded router, modular components) with strict frontend tooling.

- **Architecture foundation (Core + DI wiring)**
  - Added `EventBus` (Observer/Pub-Sub), `Store` (Proxy-based reactive state), `Router` (hash routing with dynamic params + guard middleware), and `Component` lifecycle base (`render/mount/bindEvents/destroy`).
  - Wired app bootstrap in `src/js/app.js` with dependency-injected services/components/pages and event-driven state updates.

- **Domain/data layer (Repository/Service pattern)**
  - Added `StorageService` localStorage adapter with seed initialization and JSON recovery.
  - Implemented `AuthService`, `ProductService`, `OrderService`, `ArticleService`, and `FeedbackService`, including simulated async latency and role/auth checks for protected flows.

- **RTL Persian UI system + design primitives**
  - Added semantic RTL shell (`lang="fa-IR"`, `dir="rtl"`) and Vazirmatn font setup.
  - Implemented layered CSS architecture (`@layer reset,tokens,base,layout,components,utilities`) with theme tokens, light/dark mode support, logical properties, bento/grid layout primitives, and component styles.

- **Feature modules and routed pages**
  - Implemented reusable UI modules: `Header`, `Footer` (embedded feedback form), `CartDrawer`, `QuickViewModal`, `Toast`.
  - Implemented SPA pages: storefront, auth (including demo login shortcuts), checkout (promo support), gateway simulator (OTP + success/failure + receipt), articles (listing + reader + related products), contact (validation + FAQ), admin (product CRUD/order status/feedback inbox), and profile.

- **Educational/type/tooling contract**
  - Added `// @ts-check` and `@fileoverview` headers across modules with architecture rationale and data-flow notes.
  - Added `jsconfig.json`, flat ESLint config, Stylelint/HTMLHint/Prettier/EditorConfig, and npm scripts for linting/format/typecheck.

```js
// Core reactive write path (Proxy + Pub/Sub)
this.state = new Proxy({ ...initial }, {
  set: (target, prop, value) => {
    Reflect.set(target, prop, value);
    if (typeof prop === 'symbol') return true;
    this.bus.emit(`state:${String(prop)}`, value);
    this.bus.emit('state:changed', { key: String(prop), value });
    return true;
  }
});
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

# Role & Objective
Act as a Principal Frontend Architect and Senior Educator. Build a complete, production-grade, highly modular **E-Commerce & Editorial Web Application** using **100% Pure Vanilla HTML5, CSS3, and Modern ES6+ JavaScript** (Zero runtime frameworks, zero external UI libraries).

The primary goal of this codebase is **educational mastery**: a developer reading the source code must learn enterprise-level vanilla web architecture, GoF/Frontend Design Patterns, clean code practices, state management, DOM performance optimization, and strict linter/tooling setups.

---

## 1. Localization, Aesthetic & UI Direction
- **Language & Direction:** Full RTL (`dir="rtl"`, `lang="fa-IR"`) interface in fluent, natural Persian.
- **Typography:** Load and configure `Vazirmatn` (via Google Fonts/CDN) with Persian numeric variants (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` / Persian digits helper).
- **Niche Design System ("Editorial Tech-Luxury & Bento Grid"):**
  - Avoid generic Bootstrap-like templates. Use a refined, high-contrast **Bento-grid & Neo-Brutalist/Minimalist hybrid** aesthetic with subtle glassmorphism, crisp `1px` structural borders, tactile micro-interactions, and smooth view transitions.
  - **Theming:** Built-in Light/Dark mode using CSS Custom Properties (`--color-surface`, `--color-text`, etc.) persisted in `localStorage` and respecting `prefers-color-scheme`.
  - **CSS Architecture:** Follow **CUBE CSS / ITCSS** principles utilizing native `@layer` (`@layer reset, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities;`), CSS Nesting, Logical Properties (`margin-inline`, `padding-block` for native RTL fidelity), and fluid `clamp()` typography.

---

## 2. Software Architecture & Design Patterns (Strictly Enforced)
Do NOT write spaghetti DOM scripts. Implement the following patterns explicitly and document them in code comments:
1. **Reactive State Management (Proxy + Observer/Pub-Sub Pattern):**
   - Build a central `Store` class using ES6 `Proxy` to trap state mutations and an `EventBus` (`Pub/Sub`) to notify subscribed UI components selectively without full-page reloads.
2. **Component Architecture (Modular View / Web Component Pattern):**
   - Every UI block must be an encapsulated ES Module class or factory with a deterministic lifecycle: `render()`, `mount()`, `bindEvents()`, and `destroy()` (to prevent memory leaks).
   - Use **Event Delegation** on parent containers instead of attaching listeners to individual product cards.
3. **Repository & Service Layer Pattern (Simulated Async Backend):**
   - Separate UI from data access. Create a `StorageService` wrapping `localStorage` with initial seed data (`seed.js`), and `ProductRepository`, `AuthService`, `OrderRepository`, `ArticleRepository`, and `FeedbackRepository`.
   - Simulate realistic network latency (`150ms–400ms` via `Promise`) to demonstrate proper **Skeleton Loaders** and async error handling (`try/catch/finally`).
4. **SPA Client-Side Router with Route Guards (Strategy & Middleware Pattern):**
   - Hash or History API router supporting dynamic params (e.g., `#/products`, `#/product/:id`, `#/articles`, `#/article/:id`, `#/checkout`, `#/gateway`, `#/login`, `#/admin`, `#/contact`).
   - Implement **Route Guards** to protect `#/admin` (Admin role only) and `#/checkout` (Authenticated users).

---

author: zeiado
body:
## What

`GET /api/v1/reminders/due`: open applications you should follow up on (US-08).

```
GET /api/v1/reminders/due?tz=Africa/Cairo&within_days=3
```

```json
{
  "items": [
    { "application_id": "…", "company": "Acme", "role_title": "Backend Engineer",
      "status": "applied", "follow_up_on": "2026-10-10", "days_overdue": 7 }
  ],
  "total": 1, "limit": 20, "offset": 0, "today": "2026-10-17"
}
```

Closes #10

## Design notes

- **Whose "today"?** At 23:30 UTC on Oct 17 it's already Oct 18 in Tokyo. `tz` (IANA name, default UTC) decides the date, and the response echoes the `today` it used. Unknown or malformed names (`../../etc/passwd`) return 422.
- **Most overdue first**, then company name. `days_overdue` is 0 for today and negative for upcoming items when `within_days` is set.
- **Final statuses are excluded** (accepted, rejected, withdrawn), reusing `FINAL_STATUSES` from the workflow module, so the rule lives in one place.
- **Time is injected.** Routes get the time from a `get_now` dependency. Tests freeze it with `app.dependency_overrides`: no mocking libraries, no flaky tests around midnight.
- **Index** `(user_id, follow_up_on)` replaces the single-column one (new index created before the old is dropped).
- **Windows:** added `tzdata`, because Python's `zoneinfo` has no timezone database on Windows without it.

## How to test

```bash
make check   # 239 tests (1 PostgreSQL-only), 100% coverage; also run on PostgreSQL 16
```

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] `make check` passes locally
- [x] Docs / ADR updated if behavior or design changed (design doc: Reminders)
- [x] Migration added if the schema changed (index)

body:
## Quoi

La page **Connecteurs** gagne une section **Serveurs MCP** :

- **Catalogue de 44 serveurs MCP officiels**, tous interrogés en direct (octobre 2026). Ils sont classés par catégorie, avec une recherche :
  - Productivité : Notion, Asana, monday, ClickUp, Todoist, Airtable, Miro, Box, Dropbox, Google Drive
  - Développement : Linear, GitHub, GitLab, Jira/Confluence, Sentry, PagerDuty, Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare, Supabase, Neon, Sanity, Hugging Face
  - CRM et support : HubSpot, Attio, Close, Intercom
  - Finance : Stripe, PayPal, Square, Qonto, Pennylane, Ramp
  - Design et sites : Figma, Canva, Webflow, Wix
  - Communication : Slack, Gmail, Google Calendar
  - Automatisation : Zapier, Jotform
  - Documentation publique : Cloudflare Docs, Microsoft Learn
- **On peut aussi ajouter n'importe quel serveur MCP.** Le mode de connexion est détecté tout seul (OAuth ou serveur public), sinon on fournit un jeton.
- **Logos** : les vrais logos de marque (Simple Icons, CC0) sont intégrés dans le code, en couleur sur une tuile blanche. 32 marques ont leur logo, les autres un monogramme à leur couleur.
- **« Se connecter » ouvre la page de connexion du fournisseur**, puis revient sur `/api/connectors/mcp/callback` et `/connecteurs` avec un message.
  - Autorisation OAuth 2.1 selon la spec MCP 2025-06-18 :
    - découverte via `WWW-Authenticate`, RFC 9728 et RFC 8414 / OpenID ;
    - enregistrement dynamique du client (RFC 7591) ;
    - PKCE S256 et paramètre `resource`.
  - L'état anti-CSRF est lié à l'admin qui a lancé la connexion et expire en 15 minutes.
  - On ne demande que des portées raisonnables : celles du défi, ou la liste annoncée si elle est courte.
- **Fournisseurs sans enregistrement dynamique** (Asana, Box, Google, GitHub, PagerDuty, HubSpot, Slack) : un formulaire donne le lien pour créer l'application OAuth, l'adresse de retour à déclarer (avec un bouton Copier), et les champs client_id et secret. GitHub accepte aussi un jeton personnel.
- **Bouton « Tester »** : il appelle le serveur en Streamable HTTP (réponse JSON ou SSE, session, pagination) et affiche la liste de ses outils. Le jeton est rafraîchi s'il expire ou s'il est refusé une fois.
- **Sécurité** :
  - toutes les requêtes passent par la protection SSRF de l'onboarding, maintenant aussi en POST ;
  - jetons, secrets et vérificateurs PKCE restent côté serveur (réglage `mcp_connectors`) ;
  - les routes sont réservées aux admins.
- Interface en FR et EN.

Les imports par jeton existants (Notion, Linear, Todoist, ICS) ne changent pas. Ils sont maintenant sous le titre « Imports par jeton ».

## Pas encore fait

Une fois branché, un serveur MCP est seulement connecté et testé. Le cerveau ne s'en sert pas encore : ni pour exposer ses outils aux agents de l'équipe via le MCP du cerveau, ni pour importer ses contenus. Ce sera une PR séparée.

## Vérifications

- CI GitHub verte sur `c5d7745` : typecheck et tests, sous Linux et Windows.
- Session de vérification sur un clone propre :
  - typecheck sans erreur ;
  - tests : core 101/101, client 214 réussis (0 échec, 9 ignorés hors réseau ou Windows), web 5/5 ;
  - build de production OK ;
  - smoke tout vert, en stockage fichier et sur Postgres 16, y compris la nouvelle section « API : serveurs MCP » (10 vérifications).
- Tests ajoutés :
  - `packages/core/src/remote-mcp.test.ts` : partie pure de l'autorisation et cohérence du catalogue ;
  - `apps/web/scripts/remote-mcp.test.ts` : parcours complet contre un faux fournisseur local (découverte, enregistrement, page de connexion, échange du code avec PKCE et refus d'un mauvais vérificateur, outils en SSE sur deux pages, jeton révoqué puis rafraîchi), plus le refus des adresses internes (SSRF) et le choix des portées.
- Découverte en direct contre les 44 vrais fournisseurs :
  - les 33 en connexion en un clic ont un serveur d'autorisation avec enregistrement dynamique ;
  - les 9 à application OAuth ont leur serveur d'autorisation, sans enregistrement dynamique ;
  - les 2 publics renvoient leurs outils.
- Captures à 1440 px et 390 px :
  - logos nets, pas de débordement ni de texte coupé ;
  - ouvrir « Configurer » n'étire plus les cartes voisines ;
  - l'adresse de retour est lisible en entier ;
  - le catalogue s'ouvre sur un aperçu de 9 serveurs avec « Voir les 35 autres serveurs ».

## À configurer

`BRAIN_PUBLIC_URL=https://www.nos-brainer.tech` sur Vercel. L'adresse de retour à déclarer chez les fournisseurs à application manuelle est alors `https://www.nos-brainer.tech/api/connectors/mcp/callback`.

author: dirkwa
body:
The runtime stage installs four packages on top of `node:24-trixie-slim` and leaves the rest of the base exactly as the Node image built it. So a release can ship Debian packages that already have a security fix, until the Node image is rebuilt and a later release happens to pick that up. Observed here: the weekly Trivy scan flagged `liblzma5 5.8.1-1+deb13u1` (DSA-6549-1) in a fresh build on 2026-10-12, while Debian already shipped `deb13u2`.

The runtime stage now runs `apt-get upgrade --with-new-pkgs` before installing its packages, so a release ships the Debian fixes available on the day it is built. `--with-new-pkgs` keeps a security update that needs a new dependency from being held back.

`publish-image.yml` builds that stage without the layer cache (`no-cache-filters: runtime`). With `cache-from: type=gha` and `mode=max`, the upgrade layer is keyed on the base image and the command text, so it would replay the package set of an earlier build until the base moved. The build and deps stages keep their cache.

The base stays a floating tag on purpose: upstream rebuilds are taken at the next release.

## Tested

- CI does not build the image, so the publish workflow is the first real build of this Dockerfile.
- On a Pi, I ran `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get upgrade --with-new-pkgs -s -y` in a container of the published updater 1.1.2 image (same base). It ran clean: 0 upgrades, since 1.1.2 was built after the base picked up `deb13u2`.
- `cr review --agent`: 2 findings, both taken. `--with-new-pkgs` was added, and the Dockerfile detail was dropped from the AGENTS.md file map.
- `no-cache-filters` checked against `docker/build-push-action` v7's `action.yml`. Prettier and YAML parse clean.

author: hgopalan
body:
Related to development plan rev. 6, sub-phase 1.7 (surface layer and wall treatment).

## Summary

This PR adds the wall model the steady residual needs at the ground.

- **Surface layer per ground column.** A friction velocity u* comes from Monin–Obukhov similarity (MOST) at a reference height: the log law, or MOST with a surface heat flux. The stability functions are ERF's, copied unchanged.
- **What crosses the ground** in the residual (#9):
  - the wall stress, on the u and v control volumes;
  - the surface heat flux, on θ;
  - nothing, for k.
- **Wall k.** The wall value of k (Axell and Liungman), held in the first cell as a Dirichlet row, or added as a relaxation source.
- **Implicit side.** `line_jacobian` gets the matching first-cell rows: no ground neighbour, the wall-stress coefficient for u and v, and the wall-k rows.

**ERF#3982**, the reference-height fix the plan names (your September fix), is already in the pinned ERF commit, so the copy needs no local change.

**Where this differs from ERF's MOST**, so that the wall law matches the closure that will use it (sub-phase 1.9):
- the log law is written in d + z0;
- the distance is normal to the ground;
- with a heat flux, u* is solved to round-off rather than to an absolute 1e-5.

The Theory section explains each choice.

**Bit-identity.** Without a wall model (`ResidualInputs::surface == nullptr`) the residual is unchanged: diffusion is now assembled from its face fluxes, which is what the diffusion functions already did. All golds and regression tests pass unchanged.

## Theory

**Friction velocity.**

$$
u_* = \frac{\kappa U}{\max\!\left(\ln\dfrac{d+z_0}{z_0} - \psi_m(d/L),\ 1\right)},\qquad \frac1L = -\frac{\kappa g q}{u_*^3\theta_0}
$$

- $U = \max(|\mathbf U_t|, 0.1)$ m/s is the wind parallel to the ground at the reference height.
- $d = h/|A|$ is the distance normal to the ground of a point at vertical height $h$; $|A| = \sqrt{1+z_x^2+z_y^2}$ from the column's ground slopes.
- $z_0$ is the roughness, $q$ the kinematic surface heat flux, $g$ and $\theta_0$ the buoyancy options', and $\psi_m$ ERF's Businger–Dyer function.
- **Why $d + z_0$:** the closure's mixing length is $\kappa(d+z_0)$ (plan 1.9), and ERF's own neutral check tests $u = (u_*/\kappa)\ln((z+z_0)/z_0)$. With $\ln(z/z_0)$, the review's 1-D steady column misses the log law in the first cells by 7–22 %.
- **Why normal distance:** on a slope the wall distance is $h/|A|$. Vertical heights would overstate u* by 2 % at slope 0.3 and 15 % at 0.9.
- **Why the denominator floor and Newton:**
  - Under strong convection at low wind, the relation clamped at $z/L = -100$ has only a negative root (331 of 5525 swept cases).
  - ERF's relaxed iteration to an absolute 1e-5 makes u* a step function of the wind, which spoils a finite-difference Jacobian.
  - Newton to round-off keeps the residual smooth.

**Ground fluxes** (per unit horizontal index area):

$$
G_{u,v} = u_*^2\,\frac{\mathbf U_t}{U}\,|A|,\qquad G_\theta = -q\,|A|,\qquad G_k = 0 .
$$

- **What is dropped:** the stress has no component across the ground. Its vertical component acts on the half control volume of w at the ground, a boundary row, and is dropped. ERF's MOST stress likewise enters only the u and v rows.

**Wall k.**

$$
k_w = \frac{(u_*^3 + \kappa B d_0)^{2/3}}{C_{\mu0}^2},\qquad B = \frac{gq}{\theta_0}\ (q>0),\qquad R_k = a\,(k - k_w),\quad a = \frac{\max(u_*,0.01)}{d_0}.
$$

$d_0$ is the first cell centre's normal distance. The Dirichlet mode replaces the row; the source mode adds the term. The wall eddy viscosity consistent with this log law is $\kappa u_*(d+z_0)$.

## Changes

1. **`extern_erf/ERF_MOSTUtils.H` (copied, unchanged)** and its row in `EXTRACTED.md`: `similarity_funs`.
2. **`Source/SurfaceLayer.{H,cpp}` (new):**
   - `SurfaceLayerOptions` with range checks;
   - `SurfaceState`, per column on the ground slab;
   - `compute_surface_state`, `reference_interval`, `set_ground_fluxes`, `apply_wall_k`, `apply_wall_to_implicit`, `apply_wall_k_line`, `wall_eddy_viscosity`.

   | Option (C++ struct, no input key yet) | Default | Effect |
   |---|---|---|
   | `z0` | 0.1 m | Roughness, > 0 |
   | `zref` | 0 | ≤ 0: each column's first cell centre; else a vertical height inside every column |
   | `stability` | `neutral` | `neutral` or `heat_flux` |
   | `heat_flux` | 0 K m/s | Finite; `heat_flux` only (refused with `neutral`) |
   | `wall_k` | `dirichlet` | `dirichlet` or `source` |
   | `Cmu0`, `kappa` | 0.5562, 0.41 | > 0, ERF's defaults |

   Gravity and θ0 come from `BuoyancyOptions` (#9).

3. **`Source/Residual.{H,cpp}`:**
   - `ResidualInputs::surface`;
   - diffusion is built from face fluxes, so the wall model sets the ground faces;
   - the wall-k rows;
   - `line_jacobian` applies the wall rows (its precomputed-flux overload takes the `SurfaceState`).
4. **Tests.** `Tests/Unit/test_SurfaceLayer.cpp` (new).
5. **Docs.** New `docs/surface.rst`; rows UT-1.7.1 to UT-1.7.5 in `docs/testing.rst`; `docs/extraction.rst`; `docs/residual.rst`.

## Results

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| **u* from a log-law state on the ERF#3982 column** (dz0 10 m, ratio 1.1): first centre, 10 m face, 55.3 m, a centre | **within 2e-5** (linear interpolation would miss by 3.5 % at 10 m) |
| u* with a heat flux against an independent bisection (unstable, stable, low-wind convective) | within 1e-10, positive |
| Wall k, neutral | u*²/Cmu0² exactly |
| Wall stress over the 120 m hill | along the ground (normal component 1e-14 of its size), magnitude u*²\|A\| |
| R_u, R_v, R_θ with and without the wall model | differ only in the first cells, by (wall flux − interior flux)/(J Δζ), to 1e-12 |

## Test(s)

`ctest -L unit` passes on 1, 2 and 4 ranks and with tiling off, in double and single precision. Also:
- under the invalid, zero and overflow traps on 1, 3 and 4 ranks, one box per rank (120 tests), except the `PoissonB*` tests (the AMReX traps from #7);
- with GCC 16, except `Reference.NaNSnapshotIsRefused`, which traps only on arm64 GCC;
- the extern_erf drift check;
- all regression and smoke tests and their golds, unchanged.

The nine abort tests were not run locally (macOS `atos` hang); this PR does not touch them.

| Test | Plan ID | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| `SimilarityFunctions.MatchTheReferenceTable` | UT-1.7.1 | ERF's ψ, φ (Businger–Dyer, Jimenez) against a Python table, z/L −5 to 5, to 1e-14; dψ/dζ = (1−φ)/ζ |
| `SurfaceLayer.ReferenceIntervalIsHalfOpen` | UT-1.7.2 | Centres, faces (10 m), last centre; below/above refused |
| `SurfaceLayer.LogLawFrictionVelocityOnAStretchedColumn` | UT-1.7.3 | u* within 2e-5 at four reference heights |
| `SurfaceLayer.MostFrictionVelocityWithAHeatFlux` | beyond | Against bisection to 1e-10; 1/L |
| `SurfaceLayer.WallKAndWallViscosity` | UT-1.7.4 | k_w exact (neutral), Axell form (heat flux), wall ν_t |
| `SurfaceLayer.ColumnsOverTheHill` | beyond | d0, \|A\|, u* per column from the nodes; stress along the ground, magnitude u*²\|A\|; drag |
| `SurfaceLayer.WallModelInTheResidual` | beyond | R changes only in the first cells, by the independently written wall flux minus the interior flux; wall-k rows in both modes (k varying, its ground flux removed) |
| `SurfaceLayer.WallRowsOfTheLineJacobian` | beyond | Ground neighbour removed, wall drag on u and v, wall-k rows |
| `SurfaceLayer.WallKRowAtLowWind` | beyond | The row uses u* ≥ 0.01 m/s |
| `SurfaceLayer.InvalidOptionsAreRefused` | beyond | Every option named; z_ref outside the columns; bad buoyancy options; missing surface state |

- **Mutation check.** 20 one-line mutants are each killed by at least one test. Examples: ln(z/z0) instead of ln((z+z0)/z0), vertical instead of normal distance, linear interpolation, no denominator floor, the Newton sign, no tangential projection, no |A|, a wrong stress component or neighbour, the heat-flux sign, the k_w buoyancy sign, the u* floor in the wall-k row, the source sign, the ground link kept, no wall drag, the ground taken at one node, the wall

Two YouTube videos, one commit each, plus a skill update. The uxpeak video was matched against the Mobbin rules, so the two don't overlap.

| Rule | Action | Confidence | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Show value before asking for an account](rules/show-value-before-asking-for-an-account.md) | new | established | NN/g's login-wall research. |
| [Teach in context, not up front](rules/teach-in-context-not-up-front.md) | new | established | NN/g tested tutorials with 70 people: readers did no better and rated tasks harder. |
| [Ask for permissions when they are needed](rules/ask-for-permissions-when-they-are-needed.md) | new | established | App Review Guideline 5.1.1(iv). One unconfirmed report of a rejection over a "Not now" button is noted. |
| [Only ask questions that change the experience](rules/only-ask-questions-that-change-the-experience.md) | new | single-source | The only evidence is one Headspace anecdote with no sample size. |
| [Show input rules before people type](rules/show-input-rules-before-people-type.md) | new | established | WCAG 3.3.2. |
| [Start with one question per page](rules/start-with-one-question-per-page.md) | new | established | GOV.UK service manual. |
| [Show fewer options up front](rules/show-fewer-options-up-front.md) | reinforced | disputed | The Grammarly example is added. The video misquotes its lift as about 20%; the sources say 10%+ or 10–20%. |

### uxpeak, "The UX Psychology Behind Apps People Can't Stop Using" ([source note](sources/yt-2TlIg3VokY8.md))

| Rule | Action | Confidence | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Preselect the most likely choice](rules/preselect-the-most-likely-choice.md) | new | established | A meta-analysis of 58 studies supports it. The rule never preselects anything that costs money or gives consent. |
| [Count only real progress](rules/count-only-real-progress.md) | new | **disputed** | One field study (Nunes and Drèze) supports a head start, but a 32-experiment meta-analysis found progress bars don't reduce drop-off. The video's "even a fake one works" is reversed. |
| [State the real cost of declining, without shaming](rules/state-the-real-cost-without-shaming.md) | new | established | The video's "I'll Risk It" is confirmshaming, and framing meta-analyses show no reliable advantage for loss framing. The example is reversed. |
| [Compare prices in the same units](rules/compare-prices-in-the-same-units.md) | new | **disputed** | The video's "just 2.6%" compares a monthly fee with a one-off price. A year of the plan is 31% of the laptop. |

Skipped claims and the reasons are listed in each source note.

`ux-ingest` now:
- runs several videos on one branch, one commit per video, so each is checked against the rules the previous one added;

author: mrashid2206-ai
body:
**Stack 4 of 7.** Merge after the PWA PR (stack 3). **This PR's own changes:** https://github.com/mrashid2206-ai/employees-leave-management/compare/portal-a11y-pwa...platform-hardening

## What changes
- **Security headers on every response** (`next.config.ts`):
  - **CSP** that blocks every other origin for scripts, connections, frames and objects;
  - **HSTS** in production;
  - **Permissions-Policy**: geolocation for this site only, camera/microphone/etc. off;
  - nosniff, Referrer-Policy, COOP and `frame-ancestors 'none'`;
  - no `X-Powered-By`;
  - X-XSS-Protection removed, since it's deprecated.
  - Known limitation: `'unsafe-inline'` stays in `script-src`, because Next's prerendered pages need it. A nonce-based CSP would mean rendering every page dynamically, which could be a follow-up.
- **xlsx 0.18.5 → SheetJS 0.20.3** from the official tarball. Same API, and it fixes the prototype-pollution and ReDoS advisories that have no npm fix.
- **Node 22** in CI and e2e, with `engines` and `.nvmrc`, so Railway and CI agree. Node 20 reached end of life in April 2026.
- **Retention**, run by the nightly cron after the catch-up and never failing it:
  - expired `rate_limits`;
  - `error_log` older than 90 days;
  - automation runs older than 400 days.
- **The cron secret is accepted in the header only.** `?key=` put it in access logs.
- `logger.error` now includes stack traces.
- **Removed `/api/cleanup`**: a one-off destructive endpoint, unaudited and made obsolete by migration 0009.
- Removed the stale `railway-migration.sql`, and untracked personal tool state and Playwright artifacts.
- **Session revocation can't silently fail.** `bumpTokenVersion` now throws and runs inside the caller's transaction, so a failed revocation rolls back the deactivation or password change instead of reporting success.
- **A failed boot migration now makes `/api/health` return 503.** Before, it still said "ok" while serving a partly migrated schema.
  - **Heads-up:** if Railway's health check points there, a deploy whose migration fails won't go live. That's intended.

## Tests
`retention.itest.ts` and `platform.itest.ts` (17), plus unit tests for `cron-auth` and `log`. The CSP was checked in a real browser (login pages, dashboard, recharts, fonts, service worker), with no violations.

author: razzleberrytt
body:
## Lane 5 reliability repair (research-only, owner #6743)

**Red physical proof:** an ordinary mono PCM16 24 kHz RIFF/WAVE header can declare 24,000 samples although the file physically contains 120 samples (240 bytes). Python's `wave.getnframes()` returns the header count; the current candidate scorecard only used that header, allowing `originalWavSamplesAt24000Hz` to be wrong even for exactly hash-pinned WAV bytes.

**Bounded fix:** for each source WAV, strictly verify PCM16 mono/24 kHz, stream-read *every declared sample* in 16,384-frame pieces, reject a partial/empty WAV, then rehash the exact physical source after reading. No source WAV, renderer, encoding, published film, science claims, production workflow, R-version or release permission changes. The scorecard's already mandatory science/voice/craft/phone/cross-lane holds remain.

**Negative regression:** valid full 24,000-frame source passes; unchanged header with only 120 physical frames, empty source, and mismatched pinned SHA each HOLD. A separate local isolated standard-library physical proof reproduced the same valid/truncated/empty behavior before this PR; final branch full-suite/hosted CI remains to be checked.

**Safety:** `mayPublish=false`; no accepted first excellent render or five-render streak; no new /1590 workcard credit. Existing 3-slot D/R/A WIP unaffected. Merge only through serialized trusted controller with exact-head green checks and review; do not relabel synthetic/local tests as real-film or external review.

**Scope:** exactly two files under `research/evidencemotion-director/` (`lane5_candidate_scorecard.py` + `test_lane5_candidate_scorecard.py`).

body:
Fixes #94. Two commits.

`list`, `inbox`, `status`, `latency`, `show` and `verify` read a mailbox directory this account cannot list
(for example mode 000) as an empty one and exit 0. A reader then concludes there is no mail, which is the
failure PROTOCOL section 15 warns about. They now print `UNREADABLE MAILBOX at <path>` and a `hint:` on stderr,
nothing on stdout, and exit 2, the status a missing store already had. A readable empty mailbox is unchanged.

The second commit closes the race after that check: `Path.glob` swallows listing errors, so a mailbox that
becomes unlistable between the readability check and the load still read as empty. `load_messages` now lists
with `os.scandir` and reports a failure as a `REJECT ... mailbox cannot be listed` line, so `list` and `inbox`
exit 2.

author: dirkwa
body:
The weekly Trivy scan built a fresh image and scanned that, so an alert described a build that never shipped. On the updater, a `liblzma5` alert from the 2026-10-12 fresh build stayed open while the 1.1.2 release, built on 2026-10-16, already carried the fixed `deb13u2`. The reverse happens too: a release that ships a vulnerable package goes unflagged once the base image is fixed.

The scan now pulls the published `:latest` and scans that, with no build step, so an open alert means the released image is affected, and it closes when a release ships the fix. It scans each published architecture, amd64 and arm64, as a matrix: the Node base image is built per architecture upstream, so their packages can differ. amd64 keeps the `trivy-docker` category so existing alerts update in place, and arm64 uploads as `trivy-docker-arm64`. The action has no platform input, so the step sets `TRIVY_PLATFORM`, which Trivy binds to `--platform` (checked in its `pkg/flag/options.go`).

The severity filter is dropped:
- **It never applied.** `trivy-action` runs `unset TRIVY_SEVERITY` for SARIF output unless `limit-severities-for-sarif` is set; checked in its `entrypoint.sh` at v0.36.0. So the HIGH,CRITICAL filter the comment described did nothing.
- **Turning it on would hide the important findings.** Debian advisories usually carry no severity, so that filter would drop exactly the base-image fixes.

Every fixable finding is now treated as actionable, and the workflow comment says what fixes each kind:
- **Debian package:** the next release, once the runtime stage upgrades them (the companion `fix(image)` PR).
- **npm package:** the next release when the fix is inside the `package.json` range (no lockfile is committed, so the build resolves fresh); otherwise a dependency bump.
- **Node runtime:** a release after the `node:24` base is rebuilt upstream.

Neither Dependabot nor any workflow trigger reacts to a code-scanning alert; an open alert here is the cue to cut a release.

## Tested

- YAML parses and Prettier is clean. `cr review` not run on this branch: the CLI's free allowance is used up.
- Dispatched on this branch ([run](https://github.com/dirkwa/signalk-updater-server/actions/runs/39061104824)): both the amd64 and arm64 jobs pulled `:latest`, detected Debian 13.7 with 92 packages, and uploaded. The log doesn't name the platform scanned; that `TRIVY_PLATFORM` selects it comes from Trivy's source.

body:
Adds merged test-coverage measurement to the observatory.

```
rustup component add llvm-tools-preview && cargo install cargo-llvm-cov   # once
make coverage
# open observatory/coverage.html
```

One command instruments the whole workspace, runs the cargo suite, the datatest corpus (675 assertions), the stages corpus and the tests/cli probes through the instrumented binaries, and merges everything into per-crate / per-phase-folder / per-file line coverage, plus an lcov file and the llvm-cov HTML report under `observatory/coverage/`. The atlas phase cards pick the numbers up when present. First measurement on this tree: 87.6% of 330k lines, with P5 (76%) and P2 (78%) the weakest phases and a 745-file lowest-coverage-first list to mine.

- The instrumented build lives in its own `decompiler/target/llvm-cov` tree: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is pre-set before `cargo llvm-cov show-env`, which otherwise instruments (and its clean step wipes) the normal target dir.
- `KUNA_DECOMP_TEST` is pinned so the corpus runs cannot silently fall back to an uninstrumented `decomp_test_dbg`; probes get the instrumented binary via `REPIPE_KUNA`.
- Profile output is pool-merged (`%16m`, directly in the target dir — `report` does not scan subdirs), so thousands of spawned processes produced 180 files, not thousands.
- Suite failures never abort the measurement; they surface as a banner (`meta.runsFailed`) and the report covers what ran.

Tests: `test_observatory_coverage.py` covers the rollup math, path bucketing and the runsFailed flag from a canned llvm-cov summary (`make test-tools`). Caveats and knobs: `docs/observatory.md`.

author: krishna-1812
body:
## What this adds

**Buyer Radar** is a new agent, shown as Building, at `/strategic-agents/buyer-radar`. It also opens inside every workspace at `/<account>/agents/buyer-radar`.

It searches LinkedIn posts for people asking for what we sell:
- **CallVibe:** call analytics, call audit and QA, conversation intelligence, alternatives to Gong.
- **Markify:** a marketing, SEO or Google Ads agency, or a marketing RFP.

For each search it:
1. **Keeps the real buyers.** Claude Haiku reads every post and scores it 0 to 100. Vendors promoting their own products and job seekers are capped at a score of 10, whatever the model says.
2. **Writes the messages.** Each lead gets an email, a LinkedIn connection note and a message for existing connections, all built on the person's own post.
3. **Saves the leads to one list.** Newest first, with filters: strong, new, contacted, replied, not a fit, and by offer.
4. **Sends them.**
   - From the page, by the team, after a confirm.
   - Or automatically, for a workspace that switches it on, only to leads at or above the send score, within daily caps.
5. **Posts strong leads to Slack**, if a channel is set.
6. **Runs every day**, if switched on.
   - `.github/workflows/buyer-radar-daily.yml` runs at 06:47 India time.
   - It is off until `BUYER_RADAR_CRON_TOKEN` is set.
   - It skips a workspace once that workspace reaches its monthly cap.

## Guard rails on sending (`tracker/buyer_radar_send.py`)

- **Off switch:** `BUYER_RADAR_SEND=off` stops every send.
- **Opt-outs hold everywhere:** anyone who opts out is never written to again, from any workspace (`br_suppress`).
- **Once per person:** nobody is written to twice on the same channel, from any workspace.
- **Daily caps:**
  - per workspace: 20 emails and 15 LinkedIn sends by default;
  - across all workspaces: at most 60 LinkedIn sends a day, because there is one connected account.
- **Every email** carries a one-click opt-out link (`List-Unsubscribe`, RFC 8058) and the workspace's postal address.

## How it sends

- **Search:** Apify's HarvestAPI LinkedIn Post Search, which needs no LinkedIn login. Each run's charge is capped with `maxTotalChargeUsd`. `run_actor_collect` now takes that cap and returns what Apify reports the run cost.
- **Email:** the existing Gmail sender. `send_email` now takes a sender, a display name and headers.
- **LinkedIn:** Unipile, via two new functions, `send_invitation` and `start_chat`.
  - An existing connection gets a message.
  - Anyone else gets a connection request with the note.
  - Neither route is confirmed against a live response yet.

## Costs

- **Typical run:** about $0.40 to $0.70, which is up to 325 posts a day with the default 13 searches.
- **Run cap:** $2 by default.
- **Monthly cap:** $40 by default.
- **Where it's recorded:** every call goes to `br_spend`, with who ran it and the workspace. The admin panel reads it through two new `SOURCES` entries: "Buyer Radar" in dollars and "Buyer Radar (Saleshandy)" in credits.

## In every workspace (`CLAUDE.md`)

- `ACCT_AGENTS` entry, the workspace's own space (`_mr_email`), a History reader, client routes and run routes.
- A client the workspace shares it with can search and read the leads.
- A client sees no settings, drafts or costs.
- A client's search never sends, never finds emails and never posts to Slack.

## Checks

- **Tests added:**
  - `tests/test_buyer_radar.py`: 62 tests covering the engine, sending rules, routes, the workspace and its client, and the page script under Node with hostile strings.
  - `tests/test_buyer_radar_store.py`: the store on a real Postgres.
  - Buyer Radar's two ledgers seeded in `tests/test_admin_spend.py`.
- **Full suite:** 7,473 passed, 0 failed. The Postgres tests ran separately as a non-root user, and all 71 of those touched here passed.
- **Browser check:** the page at 1440px and 390px wide, with no horizontal overflow and no JavaScript errors.

Plan and setup: `docs/buyer-radar-plan.md`.

author: hahfyeex
body:
## What

Four bug fixes across the contract test suite, frontend, and backend.

## Changes

### #1147 — Contract: multisig module integration tests

`src/multisig.rs` was imported for its types in `tests/integration_test.rs` but
its public functions (`verify_m_of_n`, `threshold_met`) were never exercised
through the contract client at the integration level.

Added 8 integration tests that call `set_admins`, `propose_operation`, and
`approve_operation` through the Soroban SDK test harness and assert M-of-N
behaviour end-to-end:

- Exact threshold met (1-of-1 executes immediately on propose)
- Below threshold (2-of-2 does not execute after only 1 approval)
- Surplus approvers (2-of-3 executes on 2nd; 3rd blocked with `ProposalAlreadyExecuted`)
- Zero threshold rejected by `set_admins` (false-positive guard)
- Threshold > admin count rejected at `set_admins`
- Proposal snapshots threshold at creation; lowering it later does not retroactively execute
- Full `SetRoyaltyRate` propose → approve round-trip with side-effect assertion
- Non-admin proposer rejected with `UnauthorizedEmergencySigner`
- Duplicate approval rejected with `AlreadyVoted`

**File:** `tests/integration_test.rs`

---

### #1172 — Frontend: export progress feedback

`handleExport` issued a single `getTransactionHistory(contractId, 10_000, 0)`
request with no user feedback — the button froze for the entire wait.

- Replaced with a paginated loop (`EXPORT_PAGE_SIZE = 500`) that collects rows
  incrementally across as many pages as needed.
- Added `exportProgress` state `{ fetched, total }` updated after each page.
- Rendered a native `<progress>` bar and `Fetching N / M transactions…` label
  inside the export panel while the export is running; both disappear on
  completion or error.
- Progress region uses `role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"` for screen-reader
  compatibility.

**File:** `frontend/src/components/TransactionHistory.tsx`

---

### #1173 — Backend: webhook HMAC signature header

Subscribers had no way to verify delivery authenticity because webhooks were
posted without a signature header.

`postWebhook` now serialises the body once and, when `webhook.secret` is set,
attaches `X-Webhook-Signature: sha256=<hex>` (GitHub / Stripe convention) via
`computeWebhookSignature`. Legacy webhook rows with no stored secret are
unaffected.

**File:** `backend/src/webhook-delivery.js`

---

### #1175 — Backend: earnings-history cache key normalisation

The cache key included the raw `contracts` query string, so `?contracts=B,A`
and `?contracts=A,B` produced different cache entries for the same logical
query, doubling cache misses on any reordering or whitespace variation.

The key segment is now built from the already-parsed `contractIds` array after
deduplication and sorting: `[...new Set(contractIds)].sort().join(",")`,
falling back to `"all"` when no contracts are supplied.

**File:** `backend/src/routes/earnings-history.js`

---

## Closes

Closes #1147
Closes #1172
Closes #1173
Closes #1175

It is replaced by two behaviour tests in `test_an_invite_code_is_a_registration_credential.py`: a signed-in stranger gets 403 and no code value in the body, and a platform admin gets 200 with the issued code in the list. author: nephlonor
body:
## Daily challenge
- One round a day on the course of the day (rotates GCC Basel, Alsace, Augusta), with the same pins, wind and weather for everyone. One chance, finished before 11:59 pm Zurich time. Found on the start screen and in the menu.
- Each finished hole goes out live (MQTT, retained). While playing, the board shows everyone's score after the same number of holes you have finished, so a round posted hours ago replays hole by hole and someone still playing can be seen climbing. A small live panel shows the top three and you; tapping it opens the board.
- The full board opens when your round is done. Before you start it is locked. Yesterday's final board can be viewed by anyone for 24 hours.
- Results are also filed in the repository (`leaderboard/daily-<day>.json`) by the workflow, which checks the day, the course of the day, that the holes add up and one result per player and device.
- The daily round has its own save slot: it waits while you play another course, and ordinary rounds wait while you play it.

## Best shots
- Every shot is logged and rated by strokes gained (expected strokes from where it started less where it ended, less the stroke and any penalty), plus strike quality, smash factor and putt break. A holed shot from off the green or a long breaking putt beats a perfect drive. The three best shots show on the scorecard.

## Player profiles
- Tapping a name on a leaderboard (course boards and the daily board) opens that player's stats and the best shots of that round. Posted rounds carry a compact stats profile and best shots; the workflow keeps profiles in `leaderboard/players.json`.

## Menu
- Settings is now a menu with a daily challenge card, round in play with course switcher, tiles (leaderboard, stats, scorecard, replay) and grouped rows opening sub pages: Player and golfer, Sound and music, Live play, Practice.
- All sheets use the translucent glass theme. The start screen's tutorial cards shrink on short phones to make room for the daily card.

Tested in a browser against a local broker: two players on the daily challenge (same pins and weather, live board by hole, full board after finishing, profile sheet), resume of the daily round after a reload, switching between daily and ordinary rounds, the workflow script against mock issues (accepted, duplicate, wrong course, wrong day, bad sum), and the earlier multiplayer and resume tests.

author: rayoplateado
body:
## What and why

Before: `--pages` followed only `rel="next"` or a page number (`?page=2`). A shop category paged with `?offset=24` was read only to its first page: 8 of 68 items.

After: when a listing has neither of those, jurl also follows a number that steps regularly between the page's links to the same listing. That number can be a query parameter or the end of the path. jurl follows it only when the step fits the page: the step must be between half the page's record count and the full count, so tiles beside the grid still let it match. A lone "next" link is followed only when its value is exactly the current value plus the page's record count. When the page has no numbered records, the step must instead come from three positions in a row.

Some things never count as positions:
- page-size selectors (`items`, `ipp`, `show`, `limit`, `top`...), ids, prices, years, sorts and radius filters;
- values of 10,000,000 or more, such as dates.

The existing stop rules still apply: a repeated page, nothing new, and the page cap. `rel="next"` and `?page=` still win when they are present.

No rule names a site.

## How it looks

Tests in `src/paging.rs` and `src/extract/html.rs`:
- **Followed:** a 68-item list at 24 per page from its first, middle and last page; `start`, `skip` and `from`; a path tail; a prev/next-only pager from page 1; a grid with tiles beside it.
- **Not followed:** page-size pairs, weekly date steps, radius-like steps, ids, years, prices, a single numeric link that doesn't match, and step 1.
- **Precedence:** `rel="next"` and `?page=2` win over an offset pager on the same page.

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` pass (672 passed, 1 ignored)
- [x] Everything jurl prints still comes verbatim from the page
- [x] Reviewed independently; the blocking findings (page-size selectors, date steps, prev/next-only pagers) are fixed. `--pages` help and the README are updated.

author: davis-matthew
body:
Optimized loops that took the sum over binomial coefficients. Originally found by comparing values to OEIS A000225.

Exploits the fact that
$$\sum_{k=1}^{n} C(n,k) = 2^n - 1$$

I also removed the loop counter and a factorial function because they were used only to compute these binomial coefficients. This closed-form also does not encounter overflow issues as early as the factorial function.

author: jeffmalone
body: Gabe’s iPhone upload (`IMG_1006.mov`) failed because the TUS client posted to the JWT-auth endpoint and sent a bearer that is not a compact JWS. **What happened** The guest page already minted `createSignedUploadUrl` on the server (`POST /film/upload-token`, team-code cookie). Tus then posted to: `https://.storage.supabase.co/storage/v1/upload/resumable` and sent `apikey: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` plus `x-signature`. `/upload/resumable` requires a JWT (`Authorization` / `apikey`). The publishable `sb_publishable_…` anon key is not a JWT, so Storage returned `400` wrapping `403 AccessDenied` / `Invalid Compact JWS`. Guests are code-gated, not signed in, so there is no user session JWT to send instead. **Fix** - Server still validates the team-code session, MIME (including iPhone `.mov` / HEVC), 20 GB, name, and rate limit, then mints `createSignedUploadUrl` with the service role. That key never reaches the browser. - Tus now uses `/storage/v1/upload/resumable/sign` and sends only `x-signature` + `x-upsert`. No `apikey`, no `Authorization` bearer. - 20 GB limit and iPhone `.mov` accept list are unchanged. **Checks** - `npx tsc --noEmit` passes - `npm test` (Node 22 with type stripping, same suite as CI): 577 pass, 82 skipped, 0 fail - New/updated unit tests: signed TUS endpoint, headers never include a JWT bearer or `apikey`, guest client source does not send `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, iPhone `.mov` + 20 GB still accepted - A real iPhone upload was not re-run here (no production Storage / team code in this environment) **What Jeff must do by hand** OLB has no auto-migrations. **No new SQL** in this PR. If `0142_game_film.sql` is not on the project yet, run that in the Supabase SQL editor (creates `game_film_uploads`, `game_film_managers`, film columns on `olb_teams`, and the private `game-film` bucket at 20 GB). Still required from #196 (no new env vars or Storage settings in this fix): 1. Project Settings → Storage: raise the project file-size limit to at least 20 GB if it is still the default (often 50 MB). 2. Vercel env: `FILM_SESSION_SECRET` (unlock cookie). Existing `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` mint the signed token on the server. The guest TUS client no longer sends `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. 3. Redeploy this branch so phones pick up the signed TUS path. No Storage RLS change: the signed token is the upload grant. The bucket stays private.

body:
## Incident and objective
On Oct 17, 2026 the operator ran the exact `fc501feb...` read-only + authorized schema-only shadow rehearsal: `119 source / 112 complete / 7 pending / 2 historical rollbacks` PASS, then shadow restore succeeded but the **production-vs-restored schema digest differed** and the tool stopped *before any Satchel SQL was executed*. Cause unknown; do not assume `pg_dump` nondeterminism or waive equality.

Adds a bounded, opt-in `--explain-schema-mismatch` operator diagnostic **only alongside** `--rehearse --authorize-shadow-database`, which reports up to six SHA-identified diff hunks, line ranges and SQL-verb categories without printing raw production schema, function bodies, comments, identifiers, secrets or table rows. Protects the original source-vs-shadow equality check, retains random scratch database creation and cleanup on all normal mismatch failures, and does not change any migrations, signer, wallet, database production objects or release authority. Opt-in is required because even a temporary schema-only clone creates/drops a shadow DB; default `--check` remains read-only. Large dumps fall back to limited line counts. Added tests for redaction, hard STOP, no migration execution, enforced scratch DB cleanup and refusal of opt-in without authorized rehearsal.

Documentation index resealed to pre-doc implementation commit; use merge commit into the funded HD feature branch, not protected main. **No live schema dump or production code deployment has occurred in this PR; the new diagnostic must be executed by an operator and its fingerprints interpreted before changing comparison rules.** [HD #634](https://github.com/Emaren/app-prodn/issues/634), [WoloBridge PR #29](https://github.com/Emaren/wolochain/pull/29) remains NONCREDITING.

author: davidschachteradfa
body:
[ADFA-6597](https://appdevforall.atlassian.net/browse/ADFA-6597)

Showing a tooltip no longer scans the whole Tooltips table.

## Cause
`QUERY_TOOLTIP` joined Tooltips and TooltipCategories. `documentation.db` has no `ANALYZE` statistics, so SQLite's planner chose to scan all of Tooltips (46,128 rows, 13 MB) and look up each row's category. `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` showed `SCAN T`.

## Change
The query looks the category's id up first:

```sql
SELECT T.rowid, T.id, T.summary, T.detail
FROM Tooltips AS T
WHERE T.categoryId IN (SELECT id FROM TooltipCategories WHERE category = ?)
AND T.tag = ?
```

- **Plan:** `SEARCH T USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_Tooltips_1 (categoryId=? AND tag=?)`, using the table's existing `UNIQUE (categoryId, tag)` index.
- **Speed:** on a desktop against the real database, a lookup goes from 6.2 ms to 0.004 ms and returns the same rows.
- **Why `IN`, not `=`:** if two categories ever shared a name, both rows would still come back, so `getTooltip` keeps reporting the duplicate as before.
- The arguments are now `(category, tag)`, to match the new order. The query and its binding live in `queryTooltip`, in a new `TooltipQuery.kt`; `getTooltip` calls it with named arguments, and the test calls it too, so the test covers the order the app binds.
- **Why a new file:** ktlint leaves `ToolTipManager.kt` unformatted while its only top-level declaration, `object TooltipManager`, doesn't match the file name. Top-level code added there makes Spotless reformat the whole file, about 380 lines.
- `QUERY_TOOLTIP` is `@VisibleForTesting`, since only the plan test reads it. It is still a public static field in bytecode, as it was inside `TooltipManager`, so it is still in the plugin-api fat jar.

**Not in this PR:** the buttons query still scans TooltipButtons (54,799 rows, 5.4 MB), because that table has no index on `tooltipId`. The index has to be built into the database, which appdevforall/OfflineDocumentationTools#39 does. Measured: 2.4 ms -> 0.004 ms, for 696,320 bytes installed and 220,515 bytes of `.br`. Each PR helps on its own.

## Testing
- New `TooltipQueryTest` (Robolectric, documentation.db's own Tooltips schema), three cases: the right row for a category and tag; two same-named categories still return both rows; the query plan uses the `(categoryId, tag)` index and doesn't scan Tooltips.
- Mutation checks: the old join fails the plan test (`[SCAN T, SEARCH TC USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid=?)]`), `=` instead of `IN` fails the duplicate test, and swapping the arguments in `queryTooltip` fails both row tests (0 rows found).
- `:idetooltips:testV8DebugUnitTest` passes: 7 tests.
- `idetooltips` gains `testImplementation(libs.tests.robolectric)`, the catalog entry other modules use.
- `docs/documentation-database.md` is updated.
- No screen changed, so there was no font-scale check. Not yet timed on a phone.

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
[XLA:GPU] Avoid linking StreamExecutor GPU PJRT client in non-GPU builds.

Multi-backend binaries and tools depend on `//xla/pjrt/plugin/xla_gpu:xla_gpu_pjrt_client` to dispatch client creation by device type, even when built for CPU-only or non-GPU targets without `--config=cuda`, `--config=rocm`, or `--config=sycl`. Because `xla_gpu_pjrt_client` unconditionally depended on `//xla/pjrt/gpu:se_gpu_pjrt_client` and called `GetStreamExecutorGpuClient`, non-GPU builds compiled and linked the full `StreamExecutorGpuClient`, GPU collectives (`GpuCliques`), and cross-host transfer implementation even though `se_gpu_pjrt_client` cannot create a working GPU runtime client without `GOOGLE_CUDA`, `TENSORFLOW_USE_ROCM`, or `TENSORFLOW_USE_SYCL` defined.

Guard the `se_gpu_pjrt_client` dependency on `xla_gpu_pjrt_client` with `if_cuda_or_rocm` and `if_sycl` (matching `se_gpu_pjrt_client_impl` in `xla/pjrt/gpu/BUILD`) and return `absl::UnimplementedError` from `GetXlaPjrtGpuClient` when built without CUDA, ROCm, or SYCL support. This has zero runtime or memory impact on GPU builds while avoiding unnecessary compilation and linking of the GPU PJRT runtime client and GPU collectives in non-GPU builds.

author: lesomnus
body:
`cxz self-update` has been silently refusing to roll out. The update helper on the installation exits 1 with:

```
maintenance: project 0994d89407f46adeb66cb8b1: session ca6f584c93b4a20c7454c7d6: agent child processes running or unknown (protocol 1)
```

`processesQuiet` treats every child of the agent, and every process in the agent's process group, as agent work. But cxz asks the agent to spawn its MCP servers, so claude holds two `cxz _mcp-bridge <session> <name>` children open for the entire session:

```
  367   367   357  claude -p --mcp-config {...cxz_memory...cxz_tasks...}
  393   367   367  cxz --state /cxz/state/data _mcp-bridge ca6f584c93b4a20c7454c7d6 cxz_memory
  394   367   367  cxz --state /cxz/state/data _mcp-bridge ca6f584c93b4a20c7454c7d6 cxz_tasks
```

So the session is never quiet, and an installation that always has a session open can never update -- which matches the only updates that have landed being the ones taken right after a full restart.

Skip those bridges, matched on the argv cxz spawns them with, and skip processes that have already exited: a zombie is not work, and nothing reaps it, because PID 1 of a session container is `sleep infinity` (51-151 of them were sitting in live session containers).

Deploying this still needs one restart: the supervisor binary is pinned when a session starts, so the sessions running now keep the old check. After that, updates land without one.

body: What's new: none Card: https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-7105/bureau-pipeline-the-lane-contract-declares-how-a-build-starts-the **What it does.** The lane contract now says how a build starts. It names the lane a writer puts a card in to start its build (Todo), the lane whose entry is the dispatch (In Progress), the lanes that dispatch comes from, and the 15-minute start window. Todo's entry gains a forward `replaced_by: In Progress` and stays live. No card lands anywhere different. Every other card of the Todo retirement reads these names, and one later card (the flip) turns them. **Why.** It's the same two-halves cutover the queue rename used. Readers learn the new names before any writer moves, so the flip is a one-line change. **The changes.** - `config/lane-contract.json`: a `build_start` block, exactly as the card's contract gives it, with `why` lines saying what each field means. Todo gains `"replaced_by": "In Progress"`. - `scripts/lane_contract.py`: `start_lane()`/`START_LANE`, `dispatch_lane()`/`DISPATCH_LANE`, `dispatch_from()`/`DISPATCH_FROM`, `start_lanes()`/`START_LANES`, `start_minutes()`/`START_MINUTES` and `is_build_dispatch(from_lane, to_lane)`. Each has a docstring saying what the name means. `check()` refuses a malformed `build_start` by field, with ids and messages like `build_start.start_minutes`: a dispatch lane that is not a live work lane; a start lane that is neither the dispatch lane nor a lane it replaces; a `dispatch_from` that names a missing lane, Hand-work, In Review, Done or the dispatch lane, or is not a list; and a `start_minutes` that is not a positive integer (bools and floats count as not). - `docs/lane-contract.md`: re-rendered, with a new "How a build starts" section after the off-flow table. **One decision to flag.** The card says `DISPATCH_FROM` is `dispatch_from` plus every alias that maps into one of those lanes. Its acceptance criterion says the set is the five lanes and the queue's old name, "and nothing else". Read literally, the alias rule would also pull in the Green Light rename alias, whose state is no longer on the board. Those two statements can't both hold, so I followed the acceptance criterion. An alias name counts only while the contract still carries it as a lane, of any status. The contract names every state on the board (`board.every_state_is_named`), so a name it no longer carries is one no card can be moved out of. This is still derived from the file: when the queue's old alias or its retiring entry is deleted, it drops out with no code edit. `is_build_dispatch` resolves both names through `aliases()`, exactly as the card says. **Proof.** - 52 new tests in `tests/test_build_start.py` cover the shipped values, the dispatch table from the card plus Intake and Planning, the flipped contract and the deleted Todo entry, and 18 malformed fixtures, one per refusal. One test in `tests/test_lane_contract.py` pins that Todo stays live and names its replacement. All green locally. - I also ran the 43 test files that read the contract or its rendered doc directly, one by one. 42 are green. `tests/test_green_light_rows.py` stalls at the same test on unmodified `main` in this runner, so that stall is the environment and not this change. CI runs it. - `python3 scripts/lane_contract.py check` with the board readable: 17 asserted, 0 failed, exit 0. Offline (no Linear key), the only failures are the three board rules that need the board. They fail the same way on `main`. The new `build_start` check passes offline, and `test_the_offline_check_raises_nothing_against_build_start` pins that. - `check_tdd_commits.py origin/main HEAD`: exit 0. The test commit comes before the implementation commit. **Risk.** Low. Nothing writes these names yet. `replaced_by` on a live lane is ignored by the drain and every other reader, all of which filter to retiring lanes. A contract with no `build_start` block (the hand-built fixtures and older contracts the history tests render) is neither checked nor rendered, so those stay as they were. The shipped file can't lose the block without anyone noticing, because the module reads its constants off it at import. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? author: h11t-labs
body:
## Wat was het probleem

Een applicatie met een eigen router wisselt van weergave zonder een nieuwe pagina te laden. Lintje laat dat toe, maar zei een host niet wat hij daarna moet doen, en de voorbeelden deden het niet goed: de focus viel bij zo'n wissel naar `body`, een schermlezer zei niets en het tabblad hield de titel van de vorige weergave (WCAG 2.4.3 en 2.4.2). Er was ook geen openbare manier om de focus op de inhoud van de shell te zetten: `<main>` staat in haar shadow root. Daarnaast misten de sjablonen in de handleidingen een `<title>` en de viewport-regel, stond "Op deze pagina" in de broncode na de tekst, en werden een host zes dingen niet verteld (de taal van een vertaling, de strook van de chat, menu-items zonder pagina, de contrasteis van een eigen thema, afspelen vanaf een tijdcode, het foutenoverzicht op een serverpagina).

## Wat er nu is

- **`lintje-shell` heeft `focusContent()`.** Het zet de focus op de inhoud en schuift die onder de vaste balken, precies zoals de skiplink (die het nu zelf aanroept). Het staat met zijn uitleg in de referentie van de shell.
- **Het routerrecept** in de handleiding over events zegt wat een host na een wissel doet: `document.title` als "Paginatitel — Naam van de applicatie", `focusContent()` bij een nieuwe pagina of het eerste veld bij een nieuwe stap, en een buur die blijft vóór hij iets verbergt dat de focus had.
- **De sjablonen** in "Een eerste pagina" en de dashboardhandleiding hebben de viewport-regel en een `<title>`. "Een eerste pagina" toont ook hoe een serverpagina na een geweigerde verzending `lintje-error-summary` boven het formulier zet en het bij het laden de focus geeft.
- **"Op deze pagina"** staat in de broncode vóór de tekst, in de handleiding en in de stijlgids; vanaf 1024 px zet `order` het rechts ernaast. Onder 1024 px bereikt Tab de lijst nu waar je haar ziet.
- **De zes hiaten** staan waar een host ze leest: de koppen van `lintje-translator` (`lang` op de vertaling), `lintje-chat` (een keuze in de strook beantwoord je ter plekke, in `ready`) en `lintje-transcript` (na `lintje-seek` roept de host `play()` aan), de handleiding over events, de contrasteis van 4,5:1 voor `--primary` in de themahandleiding, en het foutenoverzicht in "Een eerste pagina".
- **De voorbeelden** doen het: Transcriptie, Meldingen, Datacatalogus, het dashboard en de stijlgids zetten na elke wissel de titel en de focus, en geven de focus door vóór ze een knop verbergen (zoekveld, transcript, "Opname starten", de paginakop of "AI-bewerkingen"). Meldingen opent de lade pas als de zoekfunctie de focus heeft losgelaten en geeft de upload van stap 1 `name="bijlagen"`, zodat "Wijzigen" bij Bijlagen het veld vindt. Het dashboard markeert geen menu-items meer die het niet tekent. Vertalen en de stijlgids zetten `lang` op de vertaling, en een tijdcode speelt nu echt af. Een nieuwe toast neemt de focus van de oude over.
- Onderweg hersteld: in Transcriptie opende een opname uit "Recente opnames" de pagina Opnames in plaats van de opname, omdat de hero elk `lintje-navigate` van binnenuit afving.

## Hoe ik het heb gecontroleerd

- Unittest voor `focusContent()`: de focus staat daarna op `<main>`, in beide indelingen en op 390 px; de test van de skiplink slaagt.
- Met het toetsenbord nagelopen in Chromium, op `main` en op deze branch, voor elke plek uit de tabel van het issue: na elke wissel staat de focus op de genoemde plek en niet op `body`, en het tabblad draagt de titel van de weergave (bijvoorbeeld "Teamoverleg 2 oktober — Transcriptie", "Nieuwe melding, stap 2 van 3: Opvolging — Meldingen"). Op `main` viel de focus op al die plekken naar `body` of bleef hij in het menu.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run test:unit`, de browsertests van de shell en de specimens van vertaler, transcript en spelers.

## Wat nog open is

Keuzes die het issue niet letterlijk vastlegt:

- Een startpagina zonder paginakop heet "Start — Transcriptie" en "Start — Datacatalogus", naar het menu-item.
- `focusContent()` scrolt de inhoud onder de balken, ook na een routewissel; in de bovenindeling schuift de logobalk daarmee uit beeld, zoals bij de skiplink.
- Op de controlestap van Meldingen gaat de focus naar de eerste "Wijzigen", het begin van wat nieuw is.
- Na "Alle filters wissen" in de Datacatalogus gaat de focus naar het eerste filter; staan de filters ingeklapt, dan naar de balk die ze openklapt.
- "Paginakop" als doel in Transcriptie ("Stoppen en bewaren", "Wijzigen", "Opnieuw verwerken") is de inhoud van de shell, waar de paginakop bovenaan staat: de kop zelf neemt geen focus.

Closes #250
