author: shiny-code-app[bot]
body:
## Why

On October 17 a Supervisor-launched Claude worker (ENTDOCKER56-C1, claude-info) sat on Claude Code's "Is this a project you created or one you trust?" dialog for `~/Developer/odoo-enterprise-docker` while the launcher reported success. Chris decided: "trust, everything under ~/Developer should be trusted" (#2100). He later added the default Claude home (Q471).

Claude Code keeps folder trust per home in `.claude.json`, as `projects["<root>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted`. The root is the repository root, or the main checkout's root for a linked worktree ([permissions docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#what-runs-before-you-trust-a-folder)). Trust on a parent folder does not cover a repository nested inside it. That is why the stop happened: the info home trusted `~/Developer` itself but had no entry for the repository.

## What changed

New `skills/supervisor/scripts/claude_trust.py`. Before any tab, receipt or daemon step, `iterm_tab.py new --account-provider anthropic` plans the trust writes for each launch:

- **Scope.** A root under `~/Developer`, or a linked worktree in the configured worktree root (`~/.config/codex-skills/worktrees.json`, read through `dev_worktree.configuration()`) whose main checkout is under `~/Developer`. Both the launch folder and the main root from the worktree's Git pointer are resolved first, so a symlink pointing out of `~/Developer` is out of scope. A worktree records both its main checkout's root and its own root, because Claude's docs describe both.
- **Homes.** Every configured Claude account home, plus the default `~/.claude.json` when it exists. The default home is never created. A configured home without `.claude.json` refuses before anything is written. A home with no `projects` object gets one.
- **Outside scope.** The launch goes ahead only when the selected home already trusts the root. Otherwise it refuses and names the home and the folder.
- **Writes.** Only `hasTrustDialogAccepted` changes. The new file is swapped in with an atomic exchange (macOS `renamex_np` `RENAME_SWAP`, Linux `renameat2` `RENAME_EXCHANGE`), and the displaced file comes back. If a running Claude session saved in between, that content is carried forward and swapped in again, so its save is never discarded. A save after the swap replaces the file whole; the readback sees the key missing and applies it again. This relies on Claude Code saving by renaming a new file over `.claude.json`, which its leftover `.claude.json.tmp.*` files show. Claude documents no lock.
- **Launch form.** Claude launches need a literal `cd /absolute/repository && exec claude ...`, the form helpers.md already documents.
- **Docs.** helpers.md and SKILL.md describe the behavior.

## Verification

- `ClaudeTrustTests` in `test_supervisor.py` (8 tests, fixture homes only, with `Path.home`, the worktree root and the account config patched). They cover:
  - the October 17 case, in every home including the default one, with the login and other entry keys kept;
  - a worktree getting both roots;
  - refusals with no writes and no launch step: a folder outside, a foreign worktree, a symlink escape, a worktree whose Git pointer goes through a symlink, a plain folder in the worktree root, and the home folder;
  - an outside folder that is already trusted;
  - a missing `cd`, and a missing configured home config;
  - an absent default home that stays absent;
  - a session save just before and just after the swap.
- Each behavior fails without its change:
  - With origin/main's `iterm_tab.py`, every test errors.
  - With `claude_trust.py` from cd380f08, the symlinked-pointer, missing-`projects` and concurrent-save tests fail.
  - From 0f9a5872, the swap tests fail, and a scratch reproduction showed that version silently losing a session's refreshed login.
  - From 5ade286f, the default-home assertions fail.
- Existing launch fixtures carry a trust record (tmux) or patch the planner (TerminalTests), so no test reads or writes a real home.
- Locally: `test_supervisor.py`, `test_tmux_terminal.py`, `test_provider_launch.py` and `test_launcher_startup.py` pass, as do `validate-skill-repo`, `validate-public-safety`, the PEP 723 check and `compileall`. CI's Ubuntu job runs the same modules through the `renameat2` path.
- Read-only plan against the real homes: `odoo-enterprise-docker` plans writes to the cbusillo home and `~/.claude.json`, and `/private/tmp` and the home folder refuse.
- PyCharm inspection: `claude_trust.py` was GREEN at 0f9a5872. The later revisions are UNKNOWN (`inspection_inputs_changed`, retry not allowed), recorded on #2133.
- OpenAI review of record, run by the Supervisor:
  - [cd380f08](https://github.com/cbusillo/codex-skills/pull/2126#issuecomment-6241854687): three findings, all fixed ([disposition](https://github.com/cbusillo/codex-skills/pull/2126#issuecomment-6242012490)).
  - [0f9a5872](https://github.com/cbusillo/codex-skills/pull/2126#issuecomment-6242147784): one finding, fixed ([disposition](https://github.com/cbusillo/codex-skills/pull/2126#issuecomment-6242371830)).
  - [88440ab9](https://github.com/cbusillo/codex-skills/pull/2126#issuecomment-6242920801): none.

Refs #2100

author: yeraze
body:
Closes #5866
Closes #5868
Closes #5867

## Protocol: the issue was wrong
#5866 proposed `CMD_SEND_TXT_MSG` + `TXT_TYPE_CLI_DATA` addressed to the companion's own key. The `companion-v1.18.0` source does something else:

- **Local CLI** is `CMD_RUN_CLI_COMMAND` (66) → `RESP_CODE_CLI_REPLY` (29), synchronous, no RF (`examples/companion_radio/MyMesh.cpp:1118`).
- It arrived with companion protocol **v14** (`FIRMWARE_VER_CODE`); 1.16 and 1.17 report 13. That is DeviceInfo's `fw ver` byte, so it is the gate.
- The over-the-air CLI is `TXT_TYPE_CLI_COMMAND` (3), run only when the target's contact for us has flag `0x10`. That is #5867, not this PR.
- The firmware verbs (`MyMesh::handleCommand`, `CommonRadioPrefs`, board hooks) are config get/set, `ver`, `board`, `reboot`, `poweroff`/`shutdown`. There is **no** `stats`, `clock`, `advert` or `neighbors`.

## What changed
- `run_cli` bridge command in the native backend (raw frame on the `rx` tap, under the radio-op lock, since the reply has no tag). Classified serial-only.
- `sendLocalCliCommand` on a Companion with protocol 14+ sends every line to the firmware, except `stats`/`clock`/`advert`/`advert.zerohop`/`help`/`version`, which stay on the shim. It reads the protocol byte once if the poller hasn't. Strips the firmware's `> ` value marker, caps lines at 170 bytes (frame size), and reads a timeout on `reboot`/`poweroff` as sent (they never answer).
- `poweroff` and `shutdown` join `DANGER_COMMAND_PATTERN` on both server and client.
- #5868: on protocol 14+ the Local Console shows Version, Stats, Clock, Radio, TX power, Time zone, Zero-hop advert, Help and a danger Reboot. WiFi verbs exist only on WiFi builds, so they are in the placeholder rather than buttons.
- Dev notes updated.

## Mesh impact
No new transmissions. None of the firmware CLI verbs transmit; `advert` still goes through the existing shim and floor. Receive-only mode still blocks only `advert`/`advert.zerohop`.

## #5867: Companion-to-Companion remote CLI
- **Permission toggle** in the contact panel (Companion contacts, `configuration:write`): sets ContactInfo.flags `0x10` via `set_contact_remote_cli`, read-modify-write keeping the other bits, then a read-back. `POST /nodes/:publicKey/remote-cli`. Disabled with a tooltip below protocol 14 or when the radio doesn't hold the contact. The flag isn't stored; it comes from the device contact table.
- **Remote console** for Companion contacts (`MeshCoreCompanionRemoteConsole`): `send_cli` sends `TXT_TYPE_CLI_COMMAND (3)`; repeaters keep CliData. There's no login; a target that hasn't allowed us stays silent, and the timeout message says so. Same `remote_admin:write`, danger guard, `meshcoreDeviceLimiter` and receive-only gate as `/admin/cli`.
- **Bug fix:** on 1.18, a CLI command from a peer we haven't allowed reaches us as ContactMsgRecv `txtType 3`. It fell through to `contact_message`, so it was stored as a DM that auto-ack/auto-responders could answer over the air. Now it's logged and dropped.

### Mesh impact (#5867)
- Sending: one DM plus one reply per command (times hops), user-initiated, under the existing 10/min limiter (agreed: no new cap).
- Granting: allowing a contact lets it make this radio run commands and reply over the air. The firmware does that without MeshMonitor seeing it, so nothing here can cap it. The panel warns next to the toggle.

## Testing
- New: `meshcoreNativeBackend.runCli.test.ts`, native block in `meshcoreManager.localCli.test.ts`, `MeshCoreLocalConsole.catalog.test.tsx`, danger-pattern cases, `meshcoreNativeBackend.remoteCli.test.ts`, `meshcoreRemoteCliRoutes.test.ts` (harness), `MeshCoreContactDetailPanel.remoteCli.test.tsx`.
- Full suite: 31,810 passed, 0 failed (PG/MySQL skipped; no schema change). `tsc` both configs clean, `lint:ci` OK.
- Not tested on hardware: no 1.18.0 Companion to hand.

body:
Part of the robustness batch (next/robustness)

Validate captured frame dimensions, format, row layout and byte counts against the take and the native destination buffer before copying. Refuse and count incompatible frames, with one Warning per take, and continue recording at the take's fixed size. The counter supports live monitoring and resets on open().

Apply the checks across native recorder paths, including synchronous and asynchronous CoreVideo copies. Accept complete NV12 images when unused padding after the final UV row is absent. Emit recorder diagnostics after releasing the writer mutex.

Document both counters in English, Japanese and Korean and regenerate the reference outputs. Add coverage for capture and destination layouts, NV12 byte spans, mismatch reporting and continued encoding.

Usage:

```cpp
if (recorder.getRejectedFrameCount() > 0) {
    // some frames did not match the take size and were skipped
}
```

Validation (Linux):

- Recorder headless suites (recorderFrameSize, saveContract, frameTiming, audioListenerTeardown, videoFrameRate, videoAudioStream), normally and under ASan/UBSan.
- Recorder display check with taller and wider resizes mid-take: 12 checks. Fbo display check: 144 checks.
- Strict en/ja/ko reference check and header-state check pass.

- Device mode `recorderFrameSize --device-check` (a real recording resized taller, wider and back, plus matching and mismatched Fbo frames): 19 checks on Linux, where the resize part is skipped; see core/tests/recorderFrameSize/README.md.

Apple, Android and Web paths are covered by device checks or code trace.

Carries forward @JaumeAP's fix from #294 — maintainer edits weren't enabled on the fork — plus the 2.20.15 bump, CHANGELOG heading, README section and rebuilt bundle.

**Review changes on top of #294:**
1. **Sender read-back.** Same contract as `send-email` since 2.20.13: after `set sender`, read it back; on mismatch delete the compose and return an error.
2. **A message you sent keeps its own From.** Candidates are to/cc first, then the original's own sender (`extract address from`). **Live verification (robs-shop-mbpro, built server via disclaim + node-pinned, `send: false` only, probe drafts trashed after):** reply and forward of iCloud message 32 both drafted from `dansville.rob@icloud.com`. body:
## Problem
Der Release `d34121d` (Merkliste je Kunde) wurde nach dem Einspielen als fehlerhaft gemeldet und automatisch zurückgesetzt. Danach meldete der Server zusätzlich „Seite antwortet aber nicht“.

Die Ursache liegt nicht im Release, sondern in der Prüfung danach. Das Wochenangebot ist inzwischen auf „nur für angemeldete Kunden“ gestellt. Deshalb antwortet `?action=offer` ohne Anmeldung korrekt mit **401 „Bitte anmelden“**. Die Prüfung in `deploy/freigabe-einspielen.sh` verlangte aber `"ok":true` und schlug deshalb immer fehl, für den neuen Stand genauso wie für die Vorversion.

Die Seite selbst war die ganze Zeit erreichbar; von außen geprüft: Startseite 200, Eingabebereich 200, Angebots-API 401.

## Lösung
Die Prüfung akzeptiert jetzt beim Angebot **200 mit ok:true oder 401 mit gültiger API-Antwort**. Startseite, Eingabebereich und Status-API werden unverändert geprüft.

## Test
Neuer Fall im Release-Test (`tests/deploy/test_freigabe.sh`): Wochenangebot nicht öffentlich, der Release muss live gehen.
- Mit der alten Prüfung schlägt der Test fehl (11/12), genau wie auf dem Server.
- Mit der neuen Prüfung besteht er (12/12).

## Wichtig beim Einspielen
Das Einspielskript läuft beim nächsten Release noch in der **alten** Fassung, die auf dem Server installiert ist. Für genau diesen einen Release muss das Wochenangebot vorübergehend wieder öffentlich sein: Angebot bearbeiten → Angebote verwalten → „Öffentlich ohne Anmeldung sichtbar“. Ab dann gilt die neue Prüfung, und die Einstellung kann wieder ausgeschaltet werden.

author: jatassi
body:
## Summary

PR 4 of S15 (Nodes, Pairing and Roles): one Apply for every Role change, with the plan and board ops.

**Before.** An Admin changed a Node's Roles through `PUT /nodes/{id}/roles`, which replaced that Node's rows outright. Nothing planned the change first. Nothing stopped a second Node from taking a Role whose `Max` is one, and nothing handed a Role SlipStream always needs back to the Controller when its last holder let it go. Two Admins editing at once overwrote each other. `node.roles` was a list of names, with no word on whether the Node was holding them, away or lapsed. The Fake world gave each joined Node its Roles one call at a time.

**After.** `GET /nodes/roles` (`getRoleBoard`) answers a `basis`, each Node with `assigned` and its `roles`, and `gestures`, which holds the plan's verdict on every move and add. `POST /nodes/roles/plan` (`planRoles`) answers the Outcome of a set in words and stores nothing. `PUT /nodes/roles` (`setRoles`) takes `{basis, set: [{nodeId, roles}]}`, stores the Outcome and answers once the Nodes in step that it changed hold their new Roles. A set planned on an old `basis` answers 409 `roles_stale`, and a set a guardrail blocks answers 409 `roles_blocked`. Both carry `outcome`, the same change planned on the rows now. A set naming an unknown Node answers 404, and a set naming one Node twice answers 422. `node.roles` is now a list of `{role, state, held?}`. `PUT /nodes/{id}/roles` and the old `SetRoles` write path are deleted. Fake world setup claims the Controller, joins every Worker, then applies one set.

**How.**

```
Apply(ctx, Change)                       Change = SetRoles | WriteOff (PR 5) | Remove (PR 9)
  Library.Write
    plan: situation(board) ─▶ unknown id? ErrNotFound ─▶ Plan ─▶ Basis differs? StaleError{Outcome}
    Blocked()? BlockedError{Outcome}
    store: per seat, delete/insert Role rows and forfeits; per Moves effect, owner.Unassigned(node, heir)
  nothing touched? answer
  reload (serialized) ─▶ publish nodes.changed ─▶ Touch(touched) ─▶ AwaitDelivery each, bounded by ctx
Preview(ctx, Change) = plan in a Read
RoleBoard(ctx)       = situation + board + Gestures
nodesapi: StaleError ─▶ roles_stale · BlockedError ─▶ first Block reason's code (blockedAs) · ErrNotFound ─▶ 404
```

`api.NewCarrying[T]` declares a problem code that carries one more member. The router documents that member's schema beside the code, so the generated web types know `outcome` exists. `set` and `next` are lists of `{nodeId, roles}` rather than maps, because a map's values can't carry the Role enum. `nodes.Owner` gains `Unassigned`, which a Portable Role's owner must have. `indexers.SearchingOwner` uses it to rehome a Node's Indexers on the heir in the same Write. Reloads now run one at a time, so the last reload to run has read the last commit. `web/openapi.json` and the web client are regenerated, and the web fixtures use role objects.

**Tests.** `apply_test.go` covers five cases:

- A stale basis is refused by Preview and by Apply, each with the fresh plan, and the rows stay put. A set naming an unknown Node answers `ErrNotFound`.
- A second relay is blocked with `box already relays. Drag Relaying to move it.`, and nothing is stored.
- The same set on the current basis plans nothing and doesn't change the roster.
- Unticking the last Downloading holder hands Downloading back to home.
- When Apply answers, a Node in session already reports the new node-scope version as applied.

`situation_test.go` checks that a Moves effect makes the owner move work from seedbox to home. `indexers/owner_test.go` checks that every Indexer homed on the Node is rehomed. `nodesapi_test.go` runs the board, plan, blocked, unknown 404, set, stale 409 and duplicate 422 cases through the API. It also checks that every `role` enum in the document lists the Role names. `api_test.go` checks a carrying code's body and its documented `$ref`. In the world tiers, `CheckHome` sets seedbox to Searching alone and asserts the handback words and both Nodes' Roles. The partition test checks that a set naming a down Node answers at once. `walk_test.go` now tests creating an Indexer while no Node that searches is in step. Searching is Always now, so it can no longer be removed from every Node.

### Deviations

- `set`, `next` and `forfeit` are lists of `{nodeId, roles}`, not maps keyed by Node id.

body:
## What this does not show

- No real Claude Code run was made with the instance default; the tests use a recording adapter. The flag itself (`--allowed-tools`) is unchanged in `cliagent/claude.go`.
- The check runs when the action executes, not when the plan is drafted, so a plan without the list still reaches its checkpoint. With the instance default set it then runs normally; without it each action fails at once, before any agent or credential is started. A plan-time check would put software nouns into the core loop, which Phase 39 rules out.

## Summary

Two delivery plans in a row on 2026-10-17 came without `params.allowed_tools`. Claude Code runs headless and denies every tool not listed, so each such action would have spent its whole 30-minute limit unable to edit, commit or push. Nothing told the planner the field exists; plans had it only when a brief said so.

This PR makes the failure impossible to miss and cheap to prevent:

- **Instance default.** A `cli_agents` instance takes `allowed_tools`; a delegation whose action names none gets it. The action's own list still wins, so a plan can narrow it for one task.
- **Refusal.** With no list anywhere and no Karakuri tools, a `claude_code` delegation is refused before the agent starts or a credential is issued, with an error that names the missing field (AGENTS.md rule 10). Headless Claude Code would still read files but deny every edit, shell command and web fetch. A delegation that asks only for Karakuri MCP tools (Phase 34) still runs, since the agent then has exactly those tools. Cursor, Gemini and Copilot apply their own defaults or ignore the list, so they are unchanged.
- **Options for every CLI type.** `buildCLIAgentSlot` kept instance options only for `claude_code`. So `timeout_seconds` (#183), and now `allowed_tools`, were accepted for `cursor_cli`, `gemini_cli` and `copilot_cli` instances but never applied. Every type now keeps its options.
- **Planner hint.** The write-action hint now names `params.allowed_tools`.

## Evidence

- `go vet ./domains/software/`: OK
- `go test -count=1 ./domains/software/ ./config/`: ok
- `scripts/check_langchaingo_imports.sh`: OK
- New tests:
  - `TestActionToolListWinsOverTheInstanceDefault`
  - `TestInstanceToolListAppliesWhenTheActionNamesNone`
  - `TestClaudeCodeWithNoToolListIsRefusedBeforeItStarts`: no adapter call, no credential issued
  - `TestKarakuriToolsAloneAreNotRefused`
  - `TestInstanceToolListIsNotSharedBetweenDelegations`: the instance list is cloned per delegation
  - `TestOtherAdaptersRunWithoutAToolList`
  - `TestCLIEnvReadsToolsAndTimeoutFromTheInstance`: builds the environment from a config-built registry for each of the four CLI types. It also covers #183's `timeout_seconds`, which had no build-path test.
  - `TestWriteActionHintNamesAllowedTools`
- I checked that the refusal, Karakuri-tools, clone and wiring tests each fail when their code is reverted.
- `go test -count=1 ./internal/platform/tools/...`: ok

## What changed

- `domains/software/environments.go`:
  - `cliEnv.allowedTools`, read from the instance at build time.
  - The cloned fallback in `Act`, and the refusal after `karakuri_tools` is read.
  - `deniesUnlistedTools`.
- `domains/software/hints.go`: the write-action hint.
- `internal/platform/tools/registry.go`: every CLI type keeps its instance options.
- `config/default.yaml`: documents `allowed_tools` in the `cli_agents` example.

## Summary

The device relay for WiFi OTA and serial over WiFi (ticket #41, map #1, plan Track D): a standalone Node 22 + TypeScript + Hono service in `server/relay/` that implements protocol v1 from `_config/architecture.md` → "Track D" → "Relay service" (including the #49 fixups: same-token re-register always accepted, `previousToken` rotation, terminal states, `GET /v1/builds/{id}`, `DELETE /v1/devices/{id}`). Not deployed: `fly.toml` only.

## What changed

- `server/relay/src/app.ts`: all v1 routes in `createRelay({ store?, now?, config?, logger? })`.
  - Device: `register` (create / same token / matching `previousToken` → 204, otherwise 409), `next?wait=` long-poll (≤ 25 s, 204 or `{buildId,size,sha256}`), `builds/{id}/image` (pull-based stream, `Content-Length`), `status`, `serial` (≤ 50 lines / 8 kB), `input?wait=` long-poll.
  - Editor: `GET /v1/devices/{id}`, `POST …/builds` (raw octet-stream, `X-Image-Sha256` checked server-side → 201; one pending build, a queued one is replaced → `failed`/`replaced`), `GET …/events` (SSE: `online`/`offline`/`status`/`serial`, 15 s heartbeat comments, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, `Last-Event-ID` replay from the serial ring), `POST …/input`, `GET /v1/builds/{id}` → `{state}` | 404, `DELETE /v1/devices/{id}`.
  - Sweep: `offline` events after 60 s without calls, TTLs for builds (10 min), devices (24 h), and rate-limit keys.
- `src/store.ts`: a `Store` interface + `MemoryStore` (device records, builds, 500-line serial ring, input queue). `src/hub.ts`: in-process long-poll wake-ups (one waiter per device and kind, released on timeout, abort, supersede or delete) and SSE fan-out.
- `src/auth.ts`: bearer tokens ≥ 32 hex chars, stored as sha256, `timingSafeEqual`. `src/rate-limit.ts`: per device, counted only after the token checks out: control 60/min, serial 150/min, builds 10/h → 429 + `Retry-After`. `src/body.ts`: 2 MB image limit taken from `Content-Length` before reading, and chunked bodies are cancelled once they cross it.
- CORS from `RELAY_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (default `*`), allowing `Authorization`, `X-Image-Sha256` and `Last-Event-ID`. JSON logs to stdout (method/path/status/ms/ids). Tokens, headers and bodies are never logged, and a test checks this.
- `scripts/fake-device.ts`: a firmware stand-in (register → long-poll → download + sha check → status progression → serial batches, input echoed).
- `Dockerfile` (node:22-alpine, two stages, prod deps only, `USER node`), `fly.toml` (`som-relay`, `gru`, `auto_stop_machines = "off"`, `min_machines_running = 1`, port 8080, `GET /healthz`), `README.md` (run, test, fake device, deploy, env, behaviour notes).
- `.github/workflows/relay.yml`: install, typecheck, lint, format, test, build and hadolint on PRs touching `server/relay/**`.
- Root untouched: `server/` was already excluded from the root eslint, prettier, tsc and vitest configs.

## Test plan + evidence

**Relay** (`server/relay`): `pnpm install && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check && pnpm test && pnpm build`

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  41 passed (41)
```

Coverage:
- Auth: missing or wrong token → 401. Same-token re-register → 204. A different token without `previousToken` (or with a wrong one) → 409. With a matching `previousToken` → 204, and the old token then gets 401. Only the sha256 is stored.
- Long-poll: 204 at the 25 s deadline (fake timers). 200 right away when a build is queued mid-wait. `wait` is clamped to 25 s. A second poll supersedes the first. An aborted request leaves 0 waiters and 0 timers.
- Builds: sha mismatch → 400, missing header → 400, wrong content type → 415, declared and chunked bodies over 2 MB → 413. A newer upload replaces the pending one. The image streams with `Content-Length`. Status moves the build to `running`/`failed` (terminal; the image then returns 410). `GET /v1/builds/{id}` returns 404 after the 10 min TTL (injected clock). Another device's token cannot read a build.
- Device TTL: the record is dropped after 24 h, and DELETE resets it so a new token can register.
- Serial: batches over 50 lines or 8 kB are rejected, and the ring keeps the last 500 lines. Input round trip: an editor POST wakes the device long-poll.
- SSE: online → status queued → status downloading → serial (id) → heartbeat → offline → online, in that order. `Last-Event-ID` replay works, and DELETE ends the stream.
- Rate limits: control, serial and builds each answer 429 with `Retry-After` when exceeded. Wrong-token floods do not use up the device's budget.
- CORS: only allow-listed origins are accepted.
- Over a real socket (`test/server.test.ts`): a disconnected long-poll client and a disconnected SSE client are released. A stalled 2 MB download does not delay another request (< 500 ms), and it still completes intact.
- Races (`test/races.test.ts`, added in review): rotation ends old-token SSE streams and long-polls (the old poll gets 401). An upload held open across DELETE + re-pair gets 401 and is not queued. A serial batch landing after DELETE gets 404 and does not bring the record back. Concurrent uploads reserve memory before reading, so the cap holds and reservations are released. Late status reports for a terminal build are ignored. A stalled SSE reader is dropped when its backlog overflows, and its stream ends.
- Mutation check: with the abort listener in `Hub.wait` removed, both disconnect tests fail.

**Root**: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check && pnpm test && pnpm build` are all green (49 files / 553 tests).

**Docker**: `docker build` OK. The container answers `GET /healthz` → `{"ok":true} 200`, and `id` → `uid=1000(node)`.

author: bubbafat
body:
An account admin can now have keys stop working once nobody has used them for a set number of days, so a key left in an old script or on a lost laptop ends on its own.

- `tenants.key_idle_days` (control migration `c9e5a7b3d1f4`): off until set, 1–3,650 days.
- Upkeep ends each key a person made that has gone unused that long (made that long ago, if never used). It runs every 5 minutes, even while Upkeep is paused, since this is about who gets in, not the machine's work.
- Never ended: a key nobody made (the scheduler's, or one the server admin's API made), a device's key (the Devices API ends those), or the account's last admin key.
- `PATCH /v1/tenant/settings` takes `key_idle_days`. Fewer days, or turning it on, answers 409 `keys_would_end` naming the keys that would end at once, until `confirm_end_keys` is true.
- `GET /v1/keys` gives each key's `ends_at`.
- Web: Settings › API Keys gets an "Unused keys" setting (admins), and each key's end date appears under Last used. CLI: `lumiverb settings key-idle-days <days>|off [--yes]`; `settings show` reports it.

Tests: `tests/test_key_idle_days.py` (what ends and what doesn't, the 409, upkeep, the last admin key), the CLI's and the migration's, and web component tests. Python 4,659 passed; web 622 passed; `tsc` clean. Checked in a browser on a throwaway install: the setting saves, and a new key shows its end date.

author: czpython
body:
A chat agent asked "remind me in 5 minutes" had no clock. It guessed a time with no offset, probed with reminders it created and cancelled, and saved one about 20 minutes out. This gives the agent the time and a relative mode, so the request is one call.

- **The time on every turn.** `get_turn_content` opens each turn with `[Internal: The time is 2026-10-17T23:14:57+02:00 (Europe/Madrid).]` (`TIME_MESSAGE`), in the installation `timezone`. A resumed session gets it on its next turn, so the clock never goes stale.
- **`delay_seconds`.** `chat_create_reminder` takes `delay_seconds`, and `Reminder.create` resolves it against Druks's clock when it saves the reminder. The tool takes exactly one of `delay_seconds`, `send_at`, and `cron`. A zero or negative delay, a past time, two modes, or none are refused with 422, and nothing is saved.
- **This chat by default.** `conversation_id` is optional. Without it, the reminder sends in the conversation the call comes from. An explicit conversation still has to be the caller's own. A call from no chat without one gets 422.
- **Local time back.** `ReminderResponse.nextSendAt` is in the installation timezone (`Reminder.local_next_send_at`). The tool tells the agent to report that time as it is, to ask the person rather than pick another time when Druks refuses one, and never to make a reminder to test the clock. Delivery stays on the minute check, and the docs say a reminder sends up to a minute after its time.
- **Prompt and docs.** The admin prompt calls `chat_create_reminder` directly for this chat. The Reminders section of `docs/chat.md` has a table of the three modes.

## Verification

```
uv run ruff check backend druks-calls
uv run ruff format --check backend druks-calls
uv run pytest backend/tests/test_whatsapp.py backend/tests/test_chat.py   # 92 passed
```

CI runs the full suite.

New tests: in Europe/Madrid, a delay sends 300 seconds after saving, a time with no offset reads as local, an offset time stays exact, and a Monday 9:00 cron stays at 9:00 local across the October daylight-saving change. Each bad combination of modes, a negative delay, and a past time are refused. Without `conversation_id`, a reminder sends in the calling chat, a call from no chat gets 422, an explicit own conversation works, and `nextSendAt` carries Madrid's offset. Each turn opens with the local time.

author: jfbosch
body:
## Summary

Each model in the Models list on the AI assistance settings page now has a button that shows which reasoning levels are ticked for it, such as "Reasoning levels: Low to Max", "Reasoning levels: Off, Low, High" or "Reasoning levels: none". Pressing it opens a small picker with one check box for each level in the model's provider list, lightest first, plus OK and Cancel; only OK saves. The picker is a flyout rather than a ContentDialog, because the Settings window is itself a ContentDialog and WinUI allows only one open at a time. The temperature help now says temperature is not sent while a level other than Off or None is on, and the user guide explains all of it.

## Changes

- `ReasoningLevelSummary` (CognitiveSupport) turns ticked levels into the button's words: runs of three or more neighbouring levels become "first to last", others are listed with commas, and "none" when nothing the provider offers is ticked.
- `ReasoningLevelCatalog.InServiceOrder` gives the ticked levels the provider accepts, lightest first, each once; the resolver now uses it instead of its own copy of that filter.
- `LlmModelEntry` exposes the button text, an accessible name that includes the model name ("Reasoning levels for gpt-5: None, Low, High", or "unnamed model" when the name is blank), the picker heading, the choices for the current provider, and `SetReasoningLevels`, which saves in provider order and drops levels the provider does not offer. Renaming the model or changing its provider refreshes the button text and accessible name.
- New `ReasoningLevelsPicker` control: heading, a one-line explanation, one check box per level (accessible name is the level name), OK and Cancel. Tab cycles inside it, Enter on a check box means OK, and Escape or a click outside cancels.
- `LlmSettingsPage`: a "Reasoning" column with the button after the temperature box. On open, focus goes to the first check box; on close, by any route, focus returns to the button.
- Help text: temperature note, plus help text for the new button. The temperature box tooltip carries the same note.
- User guide `settings.md`: a "Reasoning levels" section covering the button, the keyboard flow, the levels for each provider, the fallback rule and the temperature note. HTML rebuilt.

## Test plan

- `dotnet test --configuration Release`: 2707 passed, 0 failed. The WinUI project compiles, XAML included.
- New `ReasoningLevelSummaryTests` cover ranges, comma lists, two-neighbour lists, mixed runs, order and duplicates, and levels from the other provider.
- New `LlmModelEntryReasoningLevelsTests` cover the button text and accessible name, the choices for each provider and after a provider change, saving (order, duplicates, foreign levels, empty), change notifications for the button bindings, and that saved levels survive repeated JSON copies of the settings without duplicates.
- Not verified: the app was not run, so the flyout's focus behaviour, the Enter and Escape keys inside the Settings dialog, and what a screen reader and ZoomText announce were not checked by hand.

Closes #420

bizpower
body:
## Cosa è successo davvero

La generazione delle email non partiva. Cinque errori in fila, ognuno misurato con una sonda temporanea (deposta e richiusa ogni volta, mai restituisce la chiave):

| | messaggio di Google | significato vero |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `403 project has been denied access` | mancava la **fatturazione** sul progetto |
| 2 | `403 Agent Platform API is disabled` | altra porta (Vertex), altra API |
| 3 | `403 requires billing to be enabled` | fatturazione poi collegata ✅ |
| 4 | `403 requests to this API are blocked` | la chiave **non può** usare `aiplatform`: nelle sue restrizioni quell'API è grigia |
| 5 | `402 prepayment credits are depleted` | **porta AI Studio, chiave `AQ.`, dopo la fatturazione** |

Cioè: la chiave `AQ.` passa dall'indirizzo di sempre. Il 403 iniziale non voleva dire «porta sbagliata», voleva dire «progetto senza fatturazione» — e lo diceva male.

## Cosa cambia nel codice

- **Rettifica**: il commit `2bc6d86` instradava le chiavi `AQ.` su Vertex. La misura dice che è sbagliato e unirlo avrebbe rotto la generazione; l'instradamento se ne va, e al suo posto resta un commento che racconta la strada sbagliata.
- **Il 402 ha un ramo suo**: era il numero meno riconoscibile, finiva nel generico «errore (402)». Ora dice che il credito prepagato è esaurito e dove si ricarica.
- **I quattro 403 sono distinti**: porta, API spenta, fatturazione, restrizioni della chiave — ognuno col suo rimedio, e il messaggio di Google riportato per intero, perché è lì che sta l'indirizzo da aprire. Prima, per qualunque 403, si diceva «controlla che la chiave sia valida e attiva»: la frase che ha fatto rifare due volte una chiave che non aveva niente che non andasse.

Stessa cosa in `qf-chat`: la chiave è una sola.

`tsc` invariato: qf-mm-ai 0, qf-chat 0.

author: nickysemenza
body:
## Summary

`entity_read` `compact` and `fields` reads (added in #2623) failed for several entity kinds. Both causes are fixed generically.

```diff
 selectListReadRows(entity, rows, fields)
-  every requested key must be loaded
+  an optional list key the complete list also omits may stay absent
+  (defaulted keys still must load, so a missed load can't hide behind a default)

 projectSelection(result, selection)
-  published.partial()            // throws on schemas with object-level refinements
+  z.object(shape → each key .optional())   // refinements check whole records, not selections
```

## Evidence

New integration test: seeds one record of every kind the reference fixture creates, then runs list and get with `resultDetail: "compact"` and with `fields` for every list-capable kind through the MCP client, which validates each result against the published outputSchema.

- **Before:** fails for financialTransaction (compact: "Requested record field was not loaded"; fields: ".partial() cannot be used on object schemas containing refinements"), vendor (compact, fields), financialAccount, image, productCategory and spendingCategory (compact).
- **After:** passes for every kind. Cookbook, run, email and imageJob have no seeded record, so only their list output schemas are exercised. `test:postgres src/server/mcp …list-read…` 127/127; `test:file src/server/generic/list src/server/mcp` 279/279; `pnpm typecheck` clean.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** MCP reads

Only selected (`compact`/`fields`) reads change; summary and full reads are untouched.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes MCP selected-read validation and list row field requirements; blast radius is MCP compact/fields reads only, but touches generic list-read paths used by many entities.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`entity_read`** **`compact`** and **`fields`** selections for entity kinds that previously failed in two generic ways.
> 
> **List read finalization** (`selectListReadRows`) now treats **declared-optional** list schema keys as legitimately absent when the complete list would also omit them (detail-only fields shared with the output schema). **Defaulted** keys still must be present on the raw row before projection, so a missed load cannot hide behind a default. This is driven by a new **`omittable`** set on compiled list read schemas (keys whose shape is `ZodOptional`).
> 
> **MCP field projection** (`projectSelection`) no longer uses **`published.partial()`**, which throws on refined Zod objects. It rebuilds a row parser by marking each published shape key **`.optional()`**, then pipes to **`listReadRowSchema`**, so partial selections validate without running whole-record refinements.
> 
> Adds a **regression integration test** that seeds the reference universe and exercises **list/get** with **`resultDetail: "compact"`** and **`fields`** across every MCP list-capable entity, with the MCP client validating against published **outputSchema**. Docs note the optional-key behavior for progressive list reads.
>

author: walle-codes721
body:
## What happened
At about 23:30 on 17 Oct, eco.linolabs.co started returning error 1101 for every room, for `/api/stats` and for a signed-in `/api/me`. `wrangler tail`:

> Exceeded allowed rows read in Durable Objects free tier.

The account is on the Workers free plan, which caps Durable Object rows read per day. The cap resets at 00:00 UTC, which is 02:00 Italy. No data was lost.

## Why
- **Every call:** `Budget.acquire()` ran `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM calls WHERE t >= ?` before each call. There was no index and the log is never pruned, so each call read every call ever logged.
- **Stats polling:** the speaker page polls `/api/stats` every 15 s, and each poll was a full scan too.
- **Tonight's prep:** it made thousands of voice calls, including 429 retries, each with a full scan.

## Fix (`src/budget.ts` only)
- `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS calls_t ON calls (t)`, so a range read touches only matching rows.
- No count at all when `ECO_MAX_CALLS` is 0 (Seb turned the ceiling off on 17 Oct).
- `stats()` reads the day's figures at most once a minute. `live`, `tripped`, `retryAt` and `lastError` stay current.

## Tests
`npx vitest run` gives 611 passed. The 2 failures are the ones already failing on main. Typecheck shows nothing new.

Merge before reopening the speaker page after 02:00. Otherwise the remaining prep uses up the cap again.

body:
## P255: fix the missing App-to-descendant paint publication

P255's attached-only condition incorrectly treated the App (the declared DOM root, with no parent) as a detached widget. App styles already had the real foreground `Color(224,224,224)` and background `Color(18,18,18)`, but its stored paint stayed EMPTY_PAINT, so Labels and Checkbox labels inherited a transparent foreground. This was a bug in my merged change, not a Toad styling problem.

`PaintNode._update_paint_state` now resolves the declared root from its own paint layer against EMPTY_PAINT and publishes to its existing linked children. Truly detached non-root widgets still remain empty, preserving constructor safety. EMPTY_PAINT is unchanged; there are no fallback colours, widget overrides, ancestor walks, new stores or per-render checks.

### Verification
- New actual Textual `App.run_test`/Pilot regression: uncoloured Vertical containing Label, Checkbox and Collapsible title.
- Before on `66d67b58`: Label/Checkbox foreground `Color(255,255,255,a=0)`; App styles foreground `Color(224,224,224)` but stored App foreground transparent. The regression fails.
- After: App/Label/Checkbox/CollapsibleTitle foreground `Color(224,224,224)`; respective backgrounds `Color(18,18,18)` / `Color(30,30,30)`. Assertions require positive alpha and foreground != background.
- Also proves a raw App foreground rule change immediately updates already attached Label and Checkbox paint without a frame-time repair.
- New regression plus all 104 earlier paint/styles cases: **105 passed in 3.24s**. No existing tests changed/deleted.
- Source **+2/-2**, tests +41. Read-only existing shared core-check interpreter plus immutable installed dependencies; `PYTHONPATH=src`. No environment/build/install/recording.

### Owner / consumer source evidence
Existing refactor-audit `Package.load` parsed all **254 Textual production modules**, omissions `()`. The inventory enumerates declarations/inheritance and relevant writes, checks, calls and imports for `_paint_state`, `_update_paint_state`, `is_dom_root`, `paint_layer`, `_style_rules_updated` and `_parent_changed`. App owns its true `is_dom_root` declaration and real CSS defaults; MessagePump supplies the false default; PaintNode owns the single stored-paint publication and linked-child propagation. No new owner/store/algorithm was introduced. Native/dependency input and consumer APIs are unchanged; this inventory is explicitly Textual production only, not a claimed dependency-wide scan. AST does not prove dynamic getattr/callback/MRO mutation. Source and before/after pilot confirm the changed root path.

Proof and exact command: `/home/ts/.cache/agent-scratch/core-runtime-location/p255/labels-proof.txt`.

The finished P248 checkout was transferred by its owner and moved, not newly created under low disk space. Historical tracked .artifacts deletions were preserved, not restored or staged. Installed-default rollout remains Codex-owned.

author: fastner
body:
`effective-flow pr` now drafts the PR body on the `mechanical` model tier instead of the orchestrator's own tier. The draft is read-only and returns text only, and the orchestrator checks it before creating the PR. The change also defines when a spawn site qualifies as `mechanical`.

A site is `mechanical` only when all five conditions hold:
- The spawn is read-only and returns only a draft or facts.
- Its inputs are bounded and named in the brief.
- The orchestrator checks the output before any effect.
- It makes no safety, classification, judgment or approval decision and asks the user nothing.
- The orchestrator does not read the bulk input itself, so the work actually moves down.

## Changes
- `pr` step 9: the orchestrator reads commit messages, `--stat` and the changed-file list. On the delegated path it no longer reads the full diff or plan content.
- New `pr/body-draft` spawn site with a bounded brief, and a body check before step 10. The check strips effectful tokens and enforces the supplied issue references.
- Hidden mode: the body draft receives no plan path.
- The title type and description are derived from the commit subjects and the stat.
- The `pr` tool includes the delegation mandate.
- Documentation: the per-spawn tier ADR, the build-system eligibility criteria, the architecture guide and the user guide.
- Build: the `pr` context budget is updated.

author: alex
body:
Bug fix. For a key of at most a block, `vg_hmac_<hash>_init` ran `init_scratch` in a frame of its own that it never wiped (the AnyKey docs said so: "smaller and not wiped"). The compression function's message schedule of the padded keys, `K₀ ⊕ ipad` and `K₀ ⊕ opad`, stayed in the dead stack after it returned. The path for a longer key already wiped its larger frame.

This affects every Merkle–Damgård HMAC (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-512/224, SHA-512/256) on all four targets, wherever the compression function keeps its schedule in scratch. The ChaCha session found it on x86-64 HMAC-SHA-256.

## The fix

The short path now zeroes the start of its working space, where the compression function leaves the schedule. The size is per implementation of the compression function, justified in a comment by that implementation's scratch layout:

| Target | Implementation | Zeroed | What it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| x86-64 | scalar SHA-1/224/256 | 4 × 16 B | the 16-word window, `scratch[0..64)` |
| x86-64 | AVX2 SHA-224/256 | 32 × 16 B | `Wₜ + Kₜ` for all 64 rounds, `scratch[0..512)` |
| x86-64 | scalar SHA-384/512 family | 8 × 16 B | the 16-word window, `scratch[0..128)` |
| x86-64 | AVX2 SHA-384/512 family | 80 × 16 B | `Wₜ + Kₜ` of both blocks, `scratch[0..1280)` |
| x86-64 | SHA-NI (SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512), MD5 | none | schedule in registers (SHA-256's SHA-NI stores only the constants) |
| AArch64 | scalar SHA-1/224/256 | 8 × 8 B | the window, `scratch[0..64)` |
| AArch64 | scalar SHA-384/512 family | 16 × 8 B | the window, `scratch[0..128)` |
| AArch64 | `_sha2`, `_sha3`, MD5 | none | scratch unused |
| x86 | scalar SHA-1 | 16 × 4 B | the window |
| x86 | scalar SHA-224/256 | 24 × 4 B | the window and the working variables, `scratch[0..96)` |
| x86 | SHA-NI SHA-1 / SHA-256 | 8 / 16 × 4 B | the saved hash value (and, for SHA-256, the endian mask), `scratch[0..32)` / `[16..64)` |
| x86 | SHA-384/512 family | 50 × 4 B | the working variables and the window, `scratch[0..200)` |
| Arm | SHA-1 / SHA-224/256 / SHA-384/512 family | 16 / 17 / 48 × 4 B | the window (and SHA-256's intermediate sum; SHA-512's working variables) |
| x86, Arm | MD5 | none | — |

- **Size 0:** an implementation that leaves nothing keeps the plain frame, with no wipe at all, so its emitted code is unchanged: MD5 everywhere and the x86-64 SHA-NI functions are byte-identical to `main`.
- **x86-64 wipe:** 16 bytes at a time (`pxor`/`movdqu`). Measured in TSC cycles, 16-byte stores were a third of the cost of 8-byte ones, and 32-byte stores were no faster.
- **Code:**
  - `Impl/StackScratch/X86_64/WipedX.lean` (new): `withStackScratchWipedX`.
  - `Proof/Framework/X86_64/StackScratchWipeX.lean` (new): `Verified.stackScratchWipedBy`, for any `Wiper`, and `Verified.stackScratchWipedX`. These are the register-scratch counterparts of `stackArgScratchWipedBy`.
  - `Proof/Pbkdf2/Md/{X86_64,AArch64}/Variant.lean`: `shortCode` and `initCode H I w`. `MdHash` gains `wipe` and `wipe_le`, from `Compress.wipe`.
  - `Proof/Pbkdf2/Whole/{X86,Arm}/AnyKeyCT.lean`: `shortCode`, `initFramedW` and `shortFramed`. The sizes of the single-implementation hashes are named and documented there and in `AnyKeyInstances.lean`: `md5Wipe`, `sha512Wipe`, …
  - The `wipe` field is added to the `Compress`/`Backend` structures on each target, and every instance sets it with a comment.
  - The registrations bind `v.wipe` or the named sizes.
- **Trust:** no change to `TCB/` or `Spec/`. The contracts are unchanged; the wipe is outside what they state.

## Dead-stack harness

A test program dirties 64 KiB of stack and calls `Hmac::<H>::new(key)`. It does this four times from the same stack:
- once to warm up (CPU detection, first-call paths);
- then with key A, key B and key A again (32-byte keys in the same buffer).

It then counts the bytes of the dead stack that are equal in both runs with key A and different in the run with key B. Those bytes depend on the key. Run-to-run noise (A against A) is at most 5 bytes. It runs on x86-64 natively and on AArch64 under qemu.

| Key-dependent dead-stack bytes after `new` | `main` | this PR |
|---|--:|--:|
| x86-64 AVX2 (`avx,avx2,bmi1,bmi2`), HMAC-SHA-256 / -SHA-512 | 574 / 1273 | 128 / 191 |
| x86-64 `none`, HMAC-SHA-1 / -SHA-256 / -SHA-512 | 168 / 191 / 319 | 104 / 128 / 191 |
| x86-64 SHA-NI (`sha,ssse3`), HMAC-SHA-1 / -SHA-256 (scratch unused) | 104 / 128 | 104 / 128 |
| AArch64 `none`, HMAC-SHA-1 / -SHA-256 / -SHA-512 | 164 / 191 / 319 | 100 / 128 / 191 |
| AArch64 `_sha2`/`_sha3`, HMAC-SHA-256 / -SHA-512 (scratch unused) | 128 / 191 | 128 / 191 |
| a 200-byte key (the long path, already wiped), HMAC-SHA-256 / -SHA-512 | 128 / 255 | 128 / 255 |

- **What this PR removes:** the remainder is the same in every configuration of a target. It equals what `main` already leaves on the implementations that never used scratch.
- **What it leaves:** that remainder is the Rust wrapper's copies of the keyed state. `hmac_init` returns `StreamingHmacState` by value, and `new` returns it again; each move leaves a copy that nothing wipes. HMAC-MD5, whose compression function uses no scratch, leaves 96 bytes. The follow-up Rust PR keys the state in place, and with both PRs `new` leaves **0** key-dependent bytes for every hash, configuration and key length, on both targets.
- **Raw-pattern scan:** a second check looks for the padded keys in the dead stack, as bytes or as 4- and 8-byte words in either order. It found them for AVX2 SHA-256 and the AVX2 SHA-512 family on `main`, and finds none with this PR.
- **Correction:** an earlier version of this table had larger numbers (e.g. HMAC-MD5 450). The harness then compared the first call with the second, and so also counted what only the first call writes.

## Rows over 0.7%

From this PR's Benchmarks run [39071070039](https://github.com/pyca/verified-garbage/actions/runs/39071070039), counting only rows whose code changes.

**What changes:** only the `vg_hmac_<hash>_init` entry functions of the implementations that store their schedule:
- x86-64 scalar and AVX2;
- AArch64 scalar;
- x86 and Arm, all but MD5.

MD5, the x86-64 SHA-NI functions, the AArch64 `_sha2`/`_sha3` functions, `init_scratch`, `finalize`, PBKDF2 and ECDSA's RFC 6979 are byte-identical.

**What the wipe costs:** a fixed handful of stores per `init`, the same at every message size, so the changed implementations' 64-byte rows are 0.8–3.8% slower. By job:

| Job (CPU) | Changed-code rows over 0.7% |

| x86-64 default (EPYC 7763, Zen 3; SHA-384/512 AVX2) | `hmac-sha384/64` +3.4%, `/1024` +1.5%; `hmac-sha512-256/64` +1.4%, `/1024` +1.0%, `-verify/1024` +1.0% |
| x86-64 `avx,avx2,bmi1,bmi2` (EPYC 9V45, Zen 5) | `hmac-sha1/64` +1.6%, `-verify/64` +2.8%; `hmac-sha256-verify/64` +1.0%, `hmac-sha256/1024` +0.9%; `hmac-sha384/64` +2.0%, `-verify/64` +2.6%, `-verify/1024` +0.9%; `hmac-sha512/64` +2.5%, `-verify/64` +1.8%, `-verify/1024` +1.3% |

| x86-64 `avx,avx2,bmi2,adx` (Zen 3; scalar SHA-512) | `hmac-sha384/64` +1.3%, `-verify/64` +2.5%; `hmac-sha512/64` +1.3%; `hmac-sha512-224/64` +1.8%, `/1024` +1.1%, `-verify/1024` +0.8%; `hmac-sha512-256/64` +1.8% |

author: barrydeen
body:
## Summary

Adds **NIP-F5: Relay-Set Communities** — a standard for private communities defined by owner-signed events and served by a *set* of independent relays.

Key properties, contrasted with NIP-29:

- **Portable rosters.** The community is defined by a kind `33500` parameterized-replaceable event (name, relay list, join policy). All membership state is expressed as user-signed control events (kinds `9500`–`9513`: grant, remove, ban, unban, invite, claim, leave, invite revoke), and the roster is a deterministic fold over those events. Relays keep no member tables, so no single relay is load-bearing.
- **No relay-to-relay replication.** Relays are independent; clients fan writes out to the whole set, merge reads, and *backfill* — carry a member's event to a relay missing it, gated by the fold's membership timeline. A community survives the loss of any relay without operator coordination.
- **NIP-70 is intentionally not used** for community content: author-only publishing is incompatible with member-carried replication. Instead, relays enforce authorship directly (direct submission by the author, or member-carried with the author verifiably a member at `created_at`).
- **One-time invites with ephemeral keys.** Invites (9510) bind an ephemeral public key; the claim (9511) proves knowledge of the secret with a BIP-340 signature over `sha256("circlets-claim:" + invite_id + ":" + joiner_pk)`. The secret never touches a relay. Joiners may bootstrap a missing invite themselves.
- **Pyramid join mode** with depth and per-member invite quotas, `reparent`/`cascade` removal modes, ban precedence, and re-join support — all derived in the fold, so every relay and client agrees without a sync protocol.

## Kind numbers

- `33500` (community definition) — verified unclaimed against the kind registry in this repo.
- `9500`–`9513` (control events) — verified free; deliberately outside NIP-29's relay-signed `9000`–`9030` range.

## Cross-implementation conformance

A Go relay and a Flutter client implement this NIP and pass an identical suite of conformance vectors (grants/role transitions, pyramid depth+quota, reparent/cascade, ban precedence, re-join, fold ordering, membership-timeline backfill checks), including an integration test where a community is served by three relays, one is killed and revived, and the set converges purely by client backfill. Happy to share the vectors.

## Notes

- The definition event is publicly readable so joiners can discover the relay set and name before authenticating.
- Direct submissions of control events are freshness-limited (±10 min) to blunt backdated-grant attacks; the owner's ban always overrides, which bounds the residual risk documented in the NIP.

Draft + optional (`relay` scope). README updated with the list entry and the kind rows.

author: enzopinotti
body:
## B102 — S3 CompleteMultipartUpload HTTP 200 bound to private object identity

**Base:** `main@7076c0a5a971d1088b5357b5ae1f74b78ac6cf6f` (B101). **18 atomic commits, 13 changed files**; `[skip ci]`, no manual CI or deployment.

### Confirmed production issue

B100 validated Bucket/Key in **initiation** XML; B99 validated only structure and ETag in **completion** XML. A well-formed `<CompleteMultipartUploadResult>` with HTTP 200, but a foreign `<Bucket>` or `<Key>`, could incorrectly mark the local multipart writer `completed=true`. B90 readback SHA-256 remained a separate publication barrier, but should not be used in place of binding the completion ACK.

### Changes

- `isConfirmedS3MultipartCompletion(xml, {bucket,objectKey})` now compares decoded XML Bucket/Key (if present) to the **actual signed destination** before clearing uploadId or completing the writer.
- Supports escaped `&` and numeric XML entities for legitimate object keys. Preserves B96 embedded errors, B97 64-KiB read, B99 structure/unique ETag and B86 self-closing simulator compatibility.
- Production writer now passes `options.bucket` / `input.objectKey` to the completion parser.
- New B102 standalone Node test suite (five groups with positive, negative, cross-owner, escapes, compatibility and duplicate/Error vectors).
- Jest adapter tests and local signed HTTP simulation explicitly reject HTTP 200 ACK for a foreign bucket/key *after simulated provider commit*, preserving uploadId-only abort and **no DELETE Object** of a private generation.
- Corrected B99 signed HTTP positive fixture that previously claimed `Bucket= bucket, Key= key` irrespective of the actual signed upload target.
- Reconciled B96/B97/B99/B100 source guards with changed signature; new B102 source guard and lifecycle scripts; documentation/runbook.

### Evidence executed (carefully scoped)

- **20/20 V8 isolated test callbacks PASS**: 10 from B96, five from B99 and five new B102, evaluating GitHub blob source after erasing TypeScript type annotations. Parser blob `05a10b9f4da503d57005a7e5dbd486b1a41a5f99`, B102 test blob `6aa522302a19c5531949f8bea256695193fbc57f`.
- **10/10 GitHub cross-source assertions PASS**, including ordering, destination values, tests present, abort fencing and release HOLD.
- **Not executed:** complete Node24/pnpm9 checkout, real Nest/Jest adapter, 23 signed TCP/SigV4 B86–B102 tests, B94 Mongo replica and AWS/MinIO provider acceptance/IAM/lifecycle; browser/backup and audits #133/#141. No approval inferred from static source tests.

**Release #353 OPEN/HOLD** and `STUDY_PROGRESS_ENABLED=false` remain mandatory. Exact-head merge `[skip ci]`; postmerge blob verification.

author: mmontes11
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the llama.cpp `full-cuda13-b11706` upgrade (LAB-243). The llamacpp server now logs four distinct warnings on startup/requests; this PR addresses the one that is actionable from `k8s-ai`.

## What this PR does

Adds `--cors-origins ""` to the `llama-server` args in `infrastructure/llamacpp/llamacpp-statefulset.yaml`.

All llamacpp clients are server-side (multica, opencode, open-webui) — there are no browser consumers — so CORS headers are not needed. An empty value makes the server set `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` to an empty header (browsers ignore it; `tools/server/server-http.cpp:344` in `b11706`), which also silences the `security: no API key is set and CORS allows all origins` warning (triggered by `cors_origins == "*" && api_keys.empty()` in `tools/server/server.cpp`). This avoids introducing API-key auth that every client would then have to configure.

## Other observed warnings (no change needed here)

- `security: router mode enabled` — informational; router + presets mode is intentional.
- `chat template supports preserving reasoning` — per-model init; default (preserve) is kept intentionally, since multica is an agent that benefits from reasoning traces.
- `WARNING: JSON schema conversion was incomplete` — by far the noisiest (once per tool-calling request). Root cause: the n8n MCP tool schemas proxied by multica contain patterns the llama.cpp grammar builder cannot express:
  - `^[a-z0-9-]+\/(?:[a-z0-9._:@-]+\/)*[a-z0-9._:@-]+$` — uses the `\/` escape, unsupported by `gbnf_escape_length()` in `common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp`;
  - `^=\s*\S` — missing the trailing `$` anchor that `_pattern_to_rule()` requires.

  There is no server flag to disable tool-call grammar (it is enabled whenever tools are present and `tool_choice != none`, see `common/parsers/qwen3-coder.cpp`), and this is not fixed upstream as of `b11706`. The fix belongs upstream (llama.cpp grammar builder) or client-side (schema sanitization in multica) — tracked separately, not something `k8s-ai` can configure.

Closes LAB-243

author: antsok
body:
## Summary

Compaction reserves each outgoing call's instructions and tool schemas, can summarize an oversized user band in bounded chunks, and recovers from malformed or timed-out forced recall. Internal recall guidance and targeted re-asks distinguish a compaction record from the user's requested reply format.

## Related issue

Fixes #1995
Fixes #1996
Fixes #1997
Fixes #2005

## Changes

- Apply per-call request overhead and optional estimate margin to the composed sending ceiling, including the wait cutoff and shortening target before a recall record exists, while retaining the configured history-storage budget. Cache schema token counts by serialized contents.
- Keep recall pending when tools are disabled; validate forced arguments before returning a response; support a deadline around the complete forced attempt and one unpinned retry.
- Add opt-in whole-turn chunking across the eligible text and described-media band, bounded summary merges, persisted chunk-answer reuse, and one deadline/cooldown event for the full pass. Optional summary chat options can be retired after a failed attempt and one retry without them.
- Advertise missed result identities in a per-call recall description without adding a message or changing the registered tool. Expose records_without_values on the record strategy and composition.

## Verification

- Full repository pytest: 20,485 passed, 925 skipped. Coverage includes streamed/non-streamed recall, cancellation, tools-disabled deferral, schema mutation, chunk growth/replay, bounded merges and summary-option recovery.
- Review regressions failed before the fixes and passed afterward: no-record fallback preserves a shortenable result under both overflow policies with a reduced sending budget, and all 20 individually fitting media turns reach bounded summary requests. Request and media test files: 93 passed, including failed/oversized descriptions under both input policies.
- All local gate checks passed: lint, formatting, strict pyright for every package, root pyright, documentation paths and implicit concatenation. Commit and push hooks passed.
- Rebuilt the wheel and source distribution, installed the wheel in an isolated environment, and exercised request budgets, chunked summaries, deferred recall, malformed-response retry and record guidance from that installation.
- Markdown example checks and GitHub-backed documentation tracker checks passed during the initial implementation; this review fix changes no Markdown examples or tracker rows.

## Notes for reviewers

The default summary input policy retains the existing bounded-prefix behavior. Chunking does not split an oversized individual turn and leaves the source intact when a reducing merge cannot fit. Record merges and standing-summary folds retain their existing input policies. Request overhead is an estimate of instructions and supported tool schemas; provider-specific framing and other request fields still need separate allowance.

Live model/provider behavior and recall quality were not verified. Local checks and the installed-wheel smoke do not establish hosted CI, publication or production acceptance.

author: jgoneit
body:
## Purpose and changes

`ha status` had two gaps in its human-readable output:

- A completion record that had stopped counting showed as `none`. Finding out why meant reading the record by hand.
- A failed `ha check` ended with the placeholder `see output with: ha log <goal> <seq>`.

This PR puts what remains first.

- **`### Unmet`** before the condition table: each unmet condition with its reason and classification, the seq of the fresh records used, and the exact `ha log` command. When no output is stored it says `no stored output`; when there is no fresh record it says `no fresh record`.
- **Completion line**: the latest `done` with its seq, commit and state. A completion that stopped counting shows its seq, commit and reason (broken chain, code change, goal documents, command change, `reopen`, unmet `/3` conditions, in the order of `contracts/run-record.md` §5.1).
- **Failed `ha check`**: one line per failed target, `output for AC-n: ha log <goal> <seq>`. These lines remain when a later target is refused and the run ends early.
- **Paths**: a goal path that needs quoting is single-quoted in commands. Absolute path arguments are shown repository-relative, so no absolute path appears in human output.
- **`ha done` output is unchanged.** The summary and done information appear only in `ha status`.
- **Docs**: `contracts/run-record.md` and the Seal `ha` reference.
- **Tests**: `internal/status/render_unmet_test.go`, `cmd/ha/preflight_test.go`, scenarios `completion-invalidated` (five invalidation reasons) and `done-output-kept`. The existing `defect-caught` scenario now expects the per-target log line instead of the placeholder, and the existing `cmd/ha/preflight_test.go` gains one assertion that an early-ended `ha check` keeps the failed target's log line. Goal checks are in `tools/goal-checks/status-delta-first/`.

## Design decisions

- The new information lives in `ha status` only, because the goal requires `ha done` output to stay as it is.
- The goal's scenario observation reuses the goal producer's Go result rules (`go_events`, `go_facts`) instead of its own classifier. When one Go run has both an assertion failure and an execution error, it keeps both facts, as `contracts/repository-producers.md` requires.

## Validation

- `python3 tools/verify.py` passed locally on the pushed head (`fbdb3f5`), run directly. Under the recorder's fixed 900-second command limit the same run would time out in the public-copy step, which the verify-nested-independence PR (#95) shortens.
- The goal checks build `ha` from the checked tree and run the real CLI on synthetic Git repositories (25 tests). On the base commit, all five change conditions fail with their declared violation.

## Check boundaries

- The checks observe `ha status` and `ha check` output and exit codes on synthetic repositories. The scenario observation classifies Go results only through the producer's rules: build failures, panics, time-outs and unfinished tests are errors, and other failures stay unclassified unless declared.
- They do not judge wording beyond the fixed tokens and commands listed above.

## Deferred findings

author: le03nava
body:
## Linked Issue

Closes #375

## PR Type

- [ ] Bug fix (`type:bug`)
- [ ] New feature (`type:feature`)
- [x] Documentation only (`type:docs`)
- [ ] Code refactoring (`type:refactor`)
- [ ] Maintenance / tooling (`type:chore`)
- [ ] Breaking change (`type:breaking-change`)

## Summary

- **Cierra el registro con su evidencia de entrega**, que es lo que la convención de `odd/tasks/` pide: el header de `odd/tasks/access-provisioning-enqueue-race.md` pasa a la forma mergeada — `merged — PR #374, merge commit 9436817`, 2026-10-17, cerrando el issue #373 — y el log suma `L10` con el detalle.
- **La prueba que este merge necesitaba es la de contenido, y está dicha**: `main` **se movió bajo el corte** porque la unidad paralela de cache Redis mergeó su propio registro antes (**#372** → `944c964`), así que los padres son `944c964` + `8a71d82` y la identidad de árbol **no** se sostiene — se declara en vez de insinuarse. Lo que sí se sostiene es el contenido: `git diff --shortstat 944c964 9436817` = **9 archivos / +664 −21**, igual a lo que reportaba el pull request.
- **Y se chequeó lo que ese escenario puede romper en silencio**: que el trabajo de la otra unidad sobreviviera al merge — `StatusTypeCatalog`, `StatusTypePage` y su registro están en `main`, y su selección de caché por propiedad quedó intacta. Dos unidades el mismo día en el mismo módulo es donde un revert no visto se esconde.
- **La última frase de `L9`** («Delivery is not this record's decision») queda **superada en el lugar**, no borrada: ese es el estilo de este repo para no reescribir narrativa congelada.
- **No toca código**: es markdown bajo `odd/tasks/`. Ningún comportamiento, ninguna configuración, ningún workflow.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `odd/tasks/access-provisioning-enqueue-race.md` | Header a la forma mergeada con PR, merge commit e issue; `L10` con la evidencia de entrega |

## Test Plan

Ningún test automático aplica: el diff es markdown y no cambia comportamiento. La verificación es de **exactitud del hecho**, y esto es lo que corrí:

| Control | Comando | Resultado |
| --- | --- | --- |
| El merge commit citado es el del PR | `gh pr view 374 --json state,mergeCommit` | `state=MERGED`, `mergeCommit=9436817fd58e26ef4d306a7915474d62475a65f2` |
| Los padres del merge | `git log -1 --format='%h parents=%p' origin/main` | `9436817` ← `944c964` + `8a71d82` — `main` se había movido |
| La prueba de contenido | `git diff --shortstat 944c964 9436817` | `9 files changed, 664 insertions(+), 21 deletions(-)` — idéntico al PR |
| El trabajo de la otra unidad sobrevivió | `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main` + `git show origin/main:…/CacheConfig.java` | `StatusTypeCatalog`, `StatusTypePage` y su registro presentes; su `ConditionalOnProperty` intacto (4) |
| El CI del head, antes del merge | `gh pr checks 374 --watch` | `Check` (API CI) pass 4m57s; `Exactly one type:* label` pass 9s |
| El CI de `main` | `gh run list --commit 9436817` | Docker Build Integrity, Gateway CI y API CI **success**; Angular CI seguía corriendo al escribirse |
| El header no afirma estado vivo | lectura del archivo | `merged — PR #374, merge commit 9436817` + lo que queda abierto, sin «sin pushear» ni «no hay PR» |

Sobre Angular CI: se nombra sin cerrarlo a propósito. Su resultado es una propiedad de `main`, no de este slice, que no toca nada de Angular — y queda dicho así para que el próximo lector no tenga que adivinar si la omisión fue medida u olvidada.

## Contributor Checklist

- [x] The linked issue is approved (`status:approved`).
- [x] The PR carries exactly one `type:*` label, matching the box above.
- [ ] Tests cover the changed behavior, and they were run. → **N/A**: sólo markdown, sin comportamiento que cubrir; los controles de exactitud están en el Test Plan.
- [ ] Shellcheck passes on modified scripts (when any `.sh` changed). → **N/A**: ningún `.sh` tocado.
- [x] Docs updated when behavior, options or messages changed. → Este slice **es** la documentación: la entrega entra en el log fechado del registro y el header pasa a su forma terminal.
- [x] Commits follow conventional commits, with no `Co-Authored-By` trailers.

author: danielalamerata
body:
Descripción:
Se agregan los endpoints de autenticación que reemplazan la validación de credenciales que antes hacía React contra localStorage. El backend ahora valida las credenciales y emite un token de Sanctum que el front envía en cada pedido. Closes #N. Relacionado con gym-frontend #N.

Cambios:

AuthController@login (POST /api/login): valida login y password, busca el usuario por email (sin distinguir mayúsculas) o por DNI, verifica la contraseña con Hash::check y responde { token, user } sin la contraseña. Para credenciales inválidas responde 422 con el mismo mensaje sin importar si el usuario existe, para no revelar qué emails o DNIs están registrados.
AuthController@me (GET /api/me): devuelve el usuario autenticado a partir del token. Lo usa el front para restaurar la sesión al recargar.
AuthController@logout (POST /api/logout): revoca el token actual en el servidor.
routes/api.php: login queda público; me y logout van dentro del grupo auth:sanctum (sin token válido responden 401).

⚠️ Limitación conocida:

Los tokens no tienen vencimiento configurado (sanctum.expiration en null): duran hasta que se hace logout.
POST /api/login todavía no tiene límite de intentos (throttle).
La autorización por rol (403) se implementa en los módulos siguientes (Socios, Clases), que son los primeros con acciones exclusivas de admin.

Verificación:

 Login válido con email → 200 con token y usuario
 Login válido con DNI → 200
 Contraseña incorrecta / usuario inexistente → 422 “Credenciales inválidas”
 Campos faltantes → 422
 GET /api/me con token → 200; sin token → 401
 POST /api/logout → el token deja de funcionar (/api/me responde 401 después)

Close #39

body:
## Why

On October 17 the Supervisor closed odoo-tenant-cm#160 without reading a Client's correction on the linked cm#159. The watcher had surfaced the URL, but its notices omit the comment text, and `gh-plan.py close` never ran the unanswered-comments check that the skills tell agents to run. Nothing forced a read before closing.

## What changed

- `gh-plan.py close` and `gh-issue close` run the existing comment radar on the issue and the threads it links. Linked means native blockers, dependents, sub-issues, parent, and same-owner issues or PRs referenced in the body. They refuse before any write, naming each comment with its link and excerpt, when an outside person's comment has no reply from the Director or an agent since its latest version, or when coverage is degraded.
- The only override is `--unanswered-decision COMMENT_URL`. It accepts a repository-owner comment on the issue posted after the newest such comment, or an unedited `Director decision:` record there that the owner approved with a thumbs-up. Already-closed issues skip the check, including landing reconciliation (`--only-closed`).
- The radar (`github_unanswered_comments.py`) adds `later_reply_url`, the first later Director or agent reply. Planning records and Director question or decision records do not count as replies. Its existing attention states are unchanged.
- Foreign-watch notices carry a one-line `excerpt` of up to 240 characters, still marked untrusted. The supervisor procedure lists each new notice with its excerpt, and the Lessons section records this once, linking #2111.

## Verification

- The check reads through the same `gh` route as the close it guards (`GH_ISSUE_GH`, gh-plan's route), including the radar subprocess. `validate-gh-issue.sh` runs every close case through the real radar against its fake `gh`, and a new end-to-end case refuses a close over an unanswered Client comment with no write.

author: anvme
body:
Closes #64.

## What
An opt-in flag that brings in the brand logos the icon packs already contain. It is **off by default**.

- **Manifest:** `naming` now has a `brand` regex next to `skip`.
  - The Tabler (`^brand-`), Phosphor (`-logo(?:-simple)?$`), Bootstrap (`facebook`, `github`, …) and Material (`google_*`, `nest_*`, `youtube_*`, `android`, …) patterns move from `skip` to `brand`.
  - Noto and Fluent keep their skin-tone patterns in `skip`, so the flag can't bring in duplicate emoji.
- **Env / setting:** `DOORY_ELEMENTS_BRAND_LOGOS=false` in `.env.example` and `settings.base`.
  - `sync_element_packs --brand-logos` / `--no-brand-logos` overrides it.
  - `--list` reports against the chosen mode.
- **Sync:** when the flag is on, elements matching `brand` are kept and tagged `brand` and `logo`, so "facebook" now finds them.
- **Fingerprint:** `PackSpec.fingerprint_for(brand_logos)`.
  - It changes only for packs that have a `brand` pattern. Turning the flag on resyncs exactly those 10 packs, and the others stay up to date.
- **Turning it off again:** logos are reported as stale, and `sync_element_packs --prune` unpublishes them. Designs that already use one keep their copy. This is documented in `.env.example` and `THIRD_PARTY.md`.
- **Notice:** with the flag on, the attribution of those packs ends with "Logos are trademarks of their respective owners; use them according to their brand guidelines." It's served through the existing `attribution` field of `GET /api/v1/elements/packs/`. With the flag off, the attribution goes back to the plain one.

## Notes
- Renaming `skip` to `brand` in 10 manifest entries changes their fingerprint. So the first sync after upgrading re-checks those 10 packs once, with no change in content.
- The Stickers panel doesn't show pack attribution today. Showing the notice there can follow in a frontend PR (#63's pack chips would be a natural place).

## Tests
- `test_no_downloaded_pack_ships_brand_logos` is replaced by checks that:
  - logos sit only in `brand`;
  - `skip` no longer matches them;
  - skin tones stay in `skip`;
  - only packs with logos get a different fingerprint.
- New sync tests:
  - flag off: no logos;
  - flag on: the logos come in, tagged and with the notice;
  - flag off again: they are stale, and `--prune` unpublishes them;
  - packs without logos aren't resynced.
- Command test: the setting is the default and the CLI option overrides it.
- `pytest apps/elements` passes, and `ruff check` / `ruff format` are clean.

author: effortlesssteven
body:
Closes #18108

Stacked on #18107 (uses `CompletionContext::suffix_end` added there). Merge after #18107; this branch will be rebased onto `main` once #18107 lands so the final diff is only the commits below.

## Problem

Builtin, keyword, and package-member completions emitted cursor-bounded text edits, so accepting one mid-token duplicated the suffix after the cursor (`pri|nt` → `printnt`). Same defect class as #17935/#18009/#18105; this covers the remaining filed families.

## Fix

Point `text_edit_range` end at `context.suffix_end` instead of `context.position` in:

- `builtins.rs` (1 site)
- `keywords.rs` (1 site)
- `packages.rs` (4 sites: core-module members, local package members, nested packages, workspace members)

`word_suffix_end` scans identifier characters only, so package ranges stop at `::` boundaries: completing `Foo::B|ar::Baz` replaces `Foo::Bar` and preserves `::Baz`. Filtering still uses the typed prefix; end-of-token ranges are unchanged because `suffix_end == position` there.

Remaining cursor-only producers (variables, workspace symbols, snippets, test frameworks) stay per-family and are not touched here.

## Proof

- New `test_builtin_keyword_package_completion_mid_token_replaces_whole_token`: builtin (`pri|nt`), keyword (`whi|le`), and package member (`Foo::bar|ley` via workspace index) ranges each cover the whole token; applied edits produce no duplicated suffix.
- Mutation falsifier: reverting all six sites to `context.position` makes the new test fail (`builtin edit must cover the whole token`).
- Broader suite: `providers::completion` in perl-lsp-rs-core — 755 passed, 0 failed.
